title: Accountants and auditors
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Predominantly knowledge work involving financial records, tax preparation, auditing, and advisory — almost entirely digital. AI copilots by 2028 handle routine analysis, report drafting, and compliance checks, yielding 2-3x productivity gains. However, client advisory, fraud detection, and complex judgment calls still require experienced human professionals.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Core duties—examining financial statements, computing taxes, analyzing records—are heavily digital and largely automatable by 2031 AI agents. Human role shifts to advisory, client relationships, and complex judgment on risk; team sizes shrink significantly.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: By 2036, AI autonomously handles audit procedures, tax preparation, compliance checking, and financial statement analysis. The remaining human role is concentrated in advisory relationships, novel strategic financial guidance, and situations requiring professional judgment in ambiguous ethical or regulatory territory.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Accountants perform financial analysis, tax preparation, and auditing. This is entirely desk-based knowledge work with no physical labor component.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Purely knowledge-based office work involving financial analysis, tax preparation, and auditing. No meaningful physical component that robots would automate.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Purely digital/office knowledge work with no physical component for robots to automate. Work involves examining financial records, computing taxes, and advising clients—all cognitive tasks.
adoption_friction_rationale: Mid-size and large firms dominate (Big 4, regional firms), with clear ROI for AI in audit and tax. Some regulatory oversight from AICPA and state boards, but no direct patient/client safety risk. Fragmented small-practice segment slows universal adoption.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Much accounting work (audits, compliance) is fixed in volume—companies need one annual audit regardless of speed. Some expansion in advisory services, but core demand is relatively inelastic. Automation historically reduced bookkeeping roles while shifting accountants toward advisory.

title: Actors
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Core work is physical human performance — auditions, rehearsals, live and filmed acting — which AI cannot replicate for most contexts by 2028. However, AI-generated synthetic media is beginning to displace voiceover work, background extras, and some digital character work. BLS itself notes AI may replace actors in certain subfields.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Acting is fundamentally a physical, embodied performance art requiring human presence, emotion, and creativity. AI may assist with script analysis or generate synthetic voiceovers, but live and filmed human performances remain the core product.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Acting is fundamentally a physical and interpersonal performance art where human embodiment and emotional authenticity are the product. AI can generate synthetic performances and deepfakes, but live theater, on-set collaboration, and the cultural value of human authorship preserve most of the role. Some voiceover and background work is displaced.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Actors perform dramatic roles. Creative human performance that robots cannot meaningfully replicate.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Performance is fundamentally human—audiences value human emotional expression and physicality. Some CGI/motion-capture technology exists but live performance and on-camera acting remain human domains requiring constant creative improvisation.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Acting is fundamentally about human embodied performance, emotional expression, and creative interpretation. While CGI and digital doubles exist, the core value is human physical and emotional presence. Robots cannot replace the artistic craft.
adoption_friction_rationale: Highly individualized creative work with strong union protections (SAG-AFTRA) and deep social attachment to human performance. AI-generated performances face legal, ethical, and audience acceptance barriers. Fragmented employer base of studios, theaters, and independent productions.
demand_elasticity_rationale: If AI makes production cheaper, far more content gets created (streaming, games, ads), expanding demand for human performers. Historical pattern: cheaper production tech (digital cameras, streaming) massively increased content volume and acting jobs.

title: Actuaries
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Almost entirely digital work: statistical modeling, risk analysis, financial forecasting, and report writing. AI excels at data analysis and pattern recognition in structured datasets. By 2028, AI copilots significantly accelerate routine modeling and analysis, but deep domain expertise, certification requirements, and regulatory judgment provide meaningful insulation for experienced practitioners.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Statistical modeling, risk probability calculation, and report generation are highly digital tasks that AI agents can largely automate by 2031. Senior actuaries remain for novel product design and strategic judgment, but routine actuarial work is heavily displaced.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Actuarial modeling, risk calculation, data analysis, and regulatory reporting are fully automatable digital tasks by 2036. The remaining human role is in novel product design, interpreting ambiguous regulatory environments, and communicating complex risk trade-offs to executive stakeholders.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Actuaries analyze risk using mathematics and statistics. This is purely computational and analytical knowledge work with no physical component.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Entirely desk-based analytical work using mathematics, statistics, and financial modeling. No physical component to automate.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Entirely analytical and computational work involving mathematics, statistics, and financial modeling. No physical component whatsoever for robotic automation.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large insurance companies and consulting firms are primary employers with strong tech adoption culture. Work is highly quantitative and suited to AI augmentation. Professional credentialing (SOA/CAS exams) creates some friction but employers are motivated by efficiency gains.
demand_elasticity_rationale: The number of insurance products and risk assessments is somewhat fixed by the number of insurers and regulations. AI may enable more granular risk modeling, but the profession is small and demand won't explode. Roughly neutral.

title: Administrative services and facilities managers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: A mix of digital knowledge work (records management, procurement, scheduling, reporting) and physical facility oversight (building inspections, maintenance supervision, staff management). AI meaningfully assists administrative and records functions by 2028, but facilities management requires physical presence, interpersonal leadership, and real-time judgment about building operations.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Administrative coordination, recordkeeping, and supply management are significantly automatable. However, facilities oversight requires physical presence and human judgment on maintenance, safety, and staff supervision, moderating overall exposure.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: The administrative coordination, records management, supply chain ordering, and scheduling components are fully automated by AI agents. However, the facilities management side involving physical building oversight, vendor relationship management, and on-site problem-solving retains a meaningful human role.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Administrative services managers coordinate office operations and facilities. While they oversee physical facilities, their work is managerial with no direct physical labor.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Primarily office-based management and coordination work. Some facility oversight involves physical inspection, but the role is fundamentally about planning, directing, and supervising rather than physical labor.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Primarily office-based management and coordination work. Minor physical component in facilities inspection, but core role is planning, directing, and decision-making—cognitive tasks with negligible physical automation potential.
adoption_friction_rationale: Employed across all sectors including large corporations and government. Role involves coordination and judgment that benefits from but isn't easily fully replaced by AI. Moderate institutional inertia in government and education settings.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Facilities and administrative management is tied to the number of physical offices and organizations, which is relatively fixed. AI efficiency gains likely reduce headcount slightly rather than creating new demand for management oversight.

title: Adult basic and secondary education and ESL teachers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Core work is face-to-face instruction with adult learners from diverse backgrounds, requiring cultural sensitivity, patience, and adaptive teaching methods. AI tutoring tools assist with lesson planning and content delivery by 2028, but the interpersonal relationship, in-person assessment of learning disabilities, and community resource coordination remain fundamentally human tasks.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: AI tutoring systems handle much of content delivery and basic skills instruction by 2031. However, these teachers work with vulnerable adult populations requiring strong interpersonal support, motivation, and assessment of learning disabilities.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Content delivery, curriculum planning, and assessment can be fully automated by AI tutoring systems. However, adult learners often need motivational support, cultural sensitivity, and interpersonal connection that keeps human teachers relevant, especially for vulnerable populations learning English.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Teaching is fundamentally interpersonal and cognitive work involving instruction, mentoring, and classroom management. There is no physical labor component for robots to automate.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Teaching adults in classroom settings is entirely interpersonal and knowledge-based. No physical tasks amenable to robotic automation.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Teaching involves in-person human interaction, emotional connection, and adaptive pedagogy. While some instruction can be digitized, the physical classroom presence and personal mentoring relationship is the core value. Minimal physical task content for robots.
adoption_friction_rationale: Education sector has strong institutional inertia and social preference for human teachers, especially for vulnerable adult learners. Fragmented across community colleges, nonprofits, and government programs. Regulatory requirements for teacher certification add friction.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Enormous unmet need for adult education and ESL instruction globally. If AI tools make each teacher more effective, programs can serve far more learners at lower cost, unlocking significant latent demand among underserved populations.

title: Advertising sales agents
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Work is predominantly digital: locating clients, making presentations, preparing sales literature, media kits, and processing correspondence. AI assists with prospect research, proposal generation, and ad performance analytics by 2028. However, relationship building and client negotiation remain human-driven.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Client prospecting, proposal preparation, media kit creation, and contract processing are highly digital and automatable. AI agents can match advertisers to inventory and generate personalized pitches; remaining human roles focus on high-value relationship selling.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Programmatic advertising and AI-driven media buying have already eroded this role. By 2036, AI agents handle client prospecting, campaign proposal generation, pricing optimization, and routine account management. Only high-value relationship-based enterprise sales retain a small human workforce.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Advertising sales agents sell ad space through client meetings and presentations. This is interpersonal sales work with no physical labor component.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Sales work involving client meetings, presentations, and relationship building. Entirely knowledge and interpersonal work with no physical labor component.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Entirely relationship-based sales work involving client meetings, presentations, and negotiations. No meaningful physical tasks for robotic automation.
adoption_friction_rationale: Mix of large media companies and small agencies. Relationship-driven sales has moderate social barriers to AI replacement. Digital advertising already heavily automated, reducing friction for further AI adoption in analytics and targeting.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Programmatic advertising has already reduced the need for human sales agents. AI further automates ad buying and targeting. Demand for advertising grows, but the intermediary sales role shrinks as platforms self-serve.

title: Advertising, promotions, and marketing managers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Core duties—market research analysis, campaign planning, budget management, and creative direction—are heavily digital. AI copilots by 2028 accelerate content creation, audience targeting, and performance analytics. Strategic decision-making, team leadership, and client relationships still require human judgment.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: AI agents autonomously handle campaign analytics, market research synthesis, content generation, and media buying optimization. Managers shift to strategic vision, brand stewardship, and client relationships, but teams are significantly smaller.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI handles campaign creation, market research analysis, media planning, A/B testing, and content generation autonomously. Human managers remain for brand strategy in ambiguous competitive contexts, high-stakes creative direction where human authorship matters, and executive-level client relationships.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Marketing managers plan and oversee promotional campaigns. This is entirely strategic and managerial knowledge work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Strategic planning, creative direction, and team management. Purely knowledge work with no physical automation potential.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Strategic management and creative direction work that is entirely cognitive. No physical labor component for robots to address.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large corporations adopt AI marketing tools readily, but strategic and creative judgment is valued. Moderate employer fragmentation. AI tools for analytics and content generation are already widely adopted, lowering friction for further integration.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Every business wants more and better marketing. Lower costs from AI tools enable more campaigns, more personalization, and more channels. Historical pattern: digital marketing expanded the total marketing workforce despite automation of individual tasks.

title: Aerospace engineering and operations technologists and technicians
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Core work involves physically building, installing, calibrating, and maintaining test equipment and aircraft systems. While they record data and use computer systems, the hands-on laboratory and manufacturing floor work dominates. AI helps with data recording and simulation but cannot replace physical tasks.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Core duties involve physical installation, calibration, and testing of aircraft systems and equipment. While data recording and simulation tasks benefit from AI, hands-on hardware work in safety-critical aerospace environments limits digital exposure.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: While AI automates data recording, simulation analysis, and test procedure documentation, the core work involves physical installation, calibration of equipment, hands-on testing of aircraft systems, and maintaining test facilities. The physical and safety-critical nature limits digital exposure.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Aerospace technicians install, test, and maintain equipment in structured aerospace facilities. They perform hands-on physical tasks in controlled environments, with some automation potential for testing and calibration.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Involves hands-on installation, calibration, and testing of aerospace equipment in controlled but variable environments. Some routine testing and calibration tasks are increasingly automated, but the variety of systems and precision requirements still need human technicians for many tasks.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Significant hands-on work installing, testing, and maintaining aerospace equipment. By 2036, robots handle much of the routine installation and calibration, but the high-precision, safety-critical, and variable nature of aerospace work still requires human oversight and judgment for novel test configurations.
adoption_friction_rationale: Heavy regulatory oversight from FAA and defense agencies. Large employers (Boeing, Lockheed Martin, NASA) have resources to adopt but face strict certification requirements. Safety-critical work demands rigorous validation of any AI/robotic systems.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Demand is tied to the number of aircraft and spacecraft being built and tested, which grows slowly. AI may speed testing but doesn't dramatically change the volume of physical testing required. Roughly neutral.

title: Aerospace engineers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Design work using CAD/CAE software, simulation, and analysis is heavily digital. AI copilots assist with design optimization, code generation for simulations, and technical documentation by 2028. However, physical testing, safety-critical judgment, and regulatory compliance require deep human expertise.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: AI generates and optimizes designs, runs simulations, and produces engineering analyses autonomously by 2031. Engineers shift to validating AI-generated designs, handling novel problems, and managing safety-critical decisions, but productivity per engineer increases dramatically.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI handles detailed design optimization, simulation, structural analysis, and documentation by 2036. Human engineers remain essential for novel system architecture decisions, cross-domain integration challenges, safety certification judgment, and managing the physical testing and manufacturing interface.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Aerospace engineers design aircraft and spacecraft using engineering software and analysis. This is knowledge work with no physical labor for robots to automate.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Design, analysis, and testing oversight work that is primarily computational and knowledge-based. Physical prototyping and testing is done by technicians.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Primarily design, analysis, and computational work. Physical prototyping and testing increasingly automated but the core engineering role is cognitive. Minor physical component in inspections.
adoption_friction_rationale: Dominated by large defense contractors and aerospace companies with resources to adopt AI. However, FAA and DoD certification requirements for safety-critical systems create significant regulatory friction. ITAR restrictions add complexity.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Some expansion as AI-assisted design enables more complex projects and faster iteration cycles. Growing space economy and drone markets create new demand. But aerospace programs are capital-constrained, not engineer-constrained.

title: Agricultural and food science technicians
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Core duties involve hands-on lab and field work: collecting samples, operating equipment, examining specimens, and maintaining sterile environments. Report preparation and data compilation benefit from AI, but the physical specimen handling and equipment operation dominate the role.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Most work involves physical laboratory procedures, field sample collection, and equipment operation. AI assists with data analysis and reporting, but the hands-on experimental and field work remains human-driven.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: This role centers on physical laboratory work including collecting samples, conducting field tests, and operating lab equipment. AI automates data analysis and reporting components, but the hands-on specimen collection, equipment operation, and field work remain human tasks.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: These technicians work in labs and fields collecting samples and running tests. The lab component is semi-structured but involves varied procedures; field work adds environmental variability. Limited robotic exposure by 2028.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Laboratory and field work involving sample collection, testing, and equipment operation. Routine lab analysis is increasingly automated, but fieldwork and novel experimental setups still require human adaptability.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Lab and field work involving sample collection, testing, and equipment operation. By 2036, much routine laboratory analysis and field sampling is automated. Humans remain for novel experimental setups and interpreting unexpected results.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large agribusiness and food companies are primary employers with resources and motivation to automate. Lab work is increasingly automated. Some regulatory oversight from USDA/FDA but manageable. Labour shortages in agriculture lower friction.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Demand tied to agricultural output and food safety testing, which grows slowly with population. AI may improve efficiency but doesn't dramatically expand the volume of lab work needed.

title: Agricultural and food scientists
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: A blend of field research, laboratory work, and knowledge work including data analysis, report writing, and compliance documentation. AI meaningfully assists literature review, data analysis, and report generation by 2028, but field research, physical experiments, and regulatory oversight require human expertise.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Research design, data analysis, and literature synthesis are significantly aided by AI agents. However, laboratory experiments, fieldwork, and the creative aspects of developing new food products or farming methods require human judgment and physical presence.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI handles literature review, experimental design optimization, data analysis, and modeling of agricultural systems. Human scientists remain for novel hypothesis generation, fieldwork oversight, cross-disciplinary insight, and interpreting results in context of complex ecological systems.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Agricultural and food scientists primarily conduct research and analysis. Their work is predominantly knowledge-based with some lab work, but not physical labor that robots would automate.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Primarily research, analysis, and oversight work. Some fieldwork but the role is fundamentally about scientific inquiry and knowledge application rather than physical labor.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Primarily research and analytical work with some fieldwork and laboratory components. The physical aspects (field sampling, lab experiments) are partially automatable, but the core scientific judgment and research design are cognitive.
adoption_friction_rationale: Employed by large agribusiness, universities, and government agencies. Research work benefits from AI but requires human judgment for experimental design. Academic institutional inertia and peer review processes create moderate friction.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Some latent demand for better crop varieties, sustainable farming methods, and food safety research. AI accelerates research but also opens new research directions in precision agriculture and alternative proteins.

title: Agricultural engineers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Design work using computer software, climate modeling, and system optimization is substantially digital. AI assists with design tools, simulation, and technical documentation. However, physical site visits, equipment testing, and direct collaboration with farmers and contractors remain essential.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Design and analysis work is heavily digital—AI generates equipment designs and optimizes systems. However, field testing, site-specific problem solving, and integration with physical agricultural operations moderate the exposure compared to pure software roles.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Design calculations, system modeling, and documentation are automated. However, agricultural engineering involves significant fieldwork, site assessment, understanding local soil and water conditions firsthand, and working with farmers on practical implementation—retaining substantial human involvement.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Agricultural engineers design equipment and systems. Their work is primarily engineering design and analysis - knowledge work that is not exposed to physical robotic automation.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Design and engineering work that is primarily knowledge-based. May visit farms and facilities but the role centers on designing systems rather than physical labor.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Primarily design and engineering work that is cognitive. Some site visits and field testing, but the core role is problem-solving and system design rather than physical labor.
adoption_friction_rationale: Strong economic incentive from agricultural labour shortages. Large equipment manufacturers and agribusiness drive adoption. Regulatory requirements are moderate. Precision agriculture and automated equipment are already well-established trends.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Growing demand for precision agriculture and sustainable farming technology. AI enables new agricultural engineering applications, but the sector is relatively small and capital-constrained.

title: Agricultural workers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Almost entirely physical labor: planting, harvesting, irrigating, operating farm machinery, feeding livestock, and cleaning animal enclosures. Minimal digital component beyond basic equipment operation. AI has negligible impact on day-to-day physical farm tasks by 2028.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Farm labor—planting, harvesting, tending livestock, operating equipment in variable outdoor conditions—is overwhelmingly physical. AI has minimal direct impact on manual agricultural tasks at the 2031 horizon.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Agricultural work is overwhelmingly physical—planting, harvesting, tending livestock, operating equipment in variable outdoor conditions. Digital AI exposure is minimal, limited to some automated monitoring and record-keeping tasks.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Agricultural workers perform physical labor in fields including planting, tending, and harvesting crops. Large-scale operations are piloting robotic harvesting for certain crops, but variable outdoor conditions and crop diversity limit exposure.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: By 2031, robotic harvesting covers an expanded range of crops on large-scale operations, and automated planting/spraying is widespread. However, many crops still require human dexterity for harvest, and small/medium farms with variable terrain need human workers for exceptions and diverse tasks.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: By 2036, commercial agriculture is heavily automated with robotic harvesting, planting, and tending for most crops. Remaining human roles are for genuinely novel situations, delicate specialty crops, and supervisory functions. The vast majority of routine field labor is robot-performed.
adoption_friction_rationale: Severe labour shortages create enormous economic pull for automation. Large agricultural operations dominate production. Existing adoption of automated harvesting and planting equipment. Seasonal workforce challenges accelerate adoption despite some regulatory friction around pesticide application.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Physical farm labor demand is tied to acreage and crop volume, which is relatively fixed. Automation and robotics will gradually reduce headcount for routine tasks like harvesting, though some manual work resists automation.

title: Air traffic controllers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Work involves real-time monitoring of radar/computer systems and radio communication with pilots—a mix of digital tools and high-stakes human judgment. AI aids with traffic flow optimization and weather integration, but safety-critical real-time decision-making and direct communication with pilots remain firmly human due to regulatory and safety constraints.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: AI systems increasingly assist with traffic sequencing and conflict detection, but the safety-critical, real-time nature of air traffic control and strict regulatory requirements keep humans firmly in the loop for authorization and emergency decisions.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI systems can manage routine traffic separation, sequencing, and flow management. However, regulatory mandates for human oversight, handling of emergency and non-standard situations, and the safety-critical nature of the role ensure humans remain in the loop, even as the cognitive workload shifts dramatically.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Air traffic control is primarily a cognitive and communication task performed at computer workstations. There is no physical labor component for robots to automate.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Highly cognitive work involving real-time decision-making in safety-critical environments. While the work environment is physical (control towers), the actual task is purely mental coordination and communication. Automation assists but human judgment remains essential.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Primarily a cognitive/digital monitoring and decision-making role. While physically located in towers, the work is screen-based coordination. Already heavily computerized; physical embodiment irrelevant.
adoption_friction_rationale: Extremely safety-critical role with FAA oversight, strong union (NATCA), and zero tolerance for error. Public trust and regulatory barriers are immense. Infrastructure modernization (NextGen) is already decades behind schedule, demonstrating institutional inertia.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Demand is fixed by the number of flights, which grows slowly. AI and automation can handle more flights per controller, directly reducing headcount needs. Safety regulations may slow adoption but the trajectory is clear.

title: Aircraft and avionics equipment mechanics and technicians
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Predominantly hands-on physical work: repairing aircraft components, testing electronic equipment, installing instruments using hand and power tools. Record-keeping and reading technical manuals benefit from AI, but the core physical repair and inspection work under strict FAA regulations is unaffected.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Core work is hands-on inspection, repair, and maintenance of aircraft systems. AI aids diagnostics and parts ordering, but physical mechanical work on safety-critical aircraft components remains firmly human.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: The core work is physical—inspecting, repairing, and maintaining aircraft systems by hand in hangars and on tarmacs. AI assists with diagnostics and maintenance scheduling, but the hands-on mechanical and electrical repair work in safety-critical aviation contexts remains human-performed.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Aircraft mechanics perform highly regulated maintenance in hangar environments. While somewhat structured, the precision requirements and safety-critical nature mean human oversight remains essential by 2028.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Skilled hands-on work in variable configurations—each aircraft has unique wear patterns and issues. Diagnostics increasingly automated, but physical repair work in tight spaces with diverse components requires human dexterity and judgment. Safety-critical nature slows automation adoption.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Hands-on maintenance and repair in complex, variable environments. By 2036, robots assist with routine inspections and standardized repairs, but aircraft maintenance involves highly variable configurations, tight spaces, and safety-critical judgment that still requires significant human involvement.
adoption_friction_rationale: FAA certification requirements are stringent (A&P license). Airlines and MRO facilities are large employers but safety regulations demand human sign-off. Liability framework heavily regulated. Some labour shortages provide adoption pull.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Demand tied to fleet size, which grows modestly. AI diagnostics may speed repairs but planes still need physical maintenance. Predictive maintenance could reduce emergency repairs while increasing scheduled maintenance efficiency.

title: Airline and commercial pilots
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Core work is physically operating aircraft, conducting pre-flight inspections, and managing real-time flight decisions. While cockpit instruments are computerized and AI assists with flight planning and navigation, the physical presence, safety responsibility, and real-time judgment in the cockpit cannot be automated by 2028.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: While autopilot and AI systems handle much routine flight, pilots remain essential for safety-critical decision-making, regulatory compliance, and emergency response. Digital tasks like flight planning benefit from AI, but the physical cockpit role persists.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI autopilot and autonomous flight systems handle routine operations, but regulatory requirements, passenger trust, and the need for human judgment in emergencies keep pilots in cockpits. The role shifts toward monitoring and exception handling, with significant portions of the traditional skill set automated.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Commercial aviation already has extensive autopilot systems, but regulatory requirements mandate human pilots in the cockpit. Full autonomous commercial flight is not deployed or permitted by 2028.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Autopilot handles much of routine flight, but pilots remain essential for safety oversight, emergency response, and complex operations. Regulatory and public trust barriers remain high. Autonomous cargo flights may begin but passenger flights still require human pilots.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Autonomous flight systems handle most routine operations by 2036. Regulatory and safety requirements still mandate human pilots, but their role is increasingly supervisory. Humans essential for genuinely novel emergencies and edge cases.
adoption_friction_rationale: Extremely heavy FAA regulation, massive liability exposure, and strong public resistance to pilotless commercial aircraft. Powerful unions (ALPA). While autopilot handles much flight, full automation faces decade-plus regulatory and social barriers.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Demand tied to flight volume, which grows modestly. Automation handles more of the flying task but regulatory and safety requirements keep two pilots in cockpits. Long-term trajectory toward reduced crew sizes.

title: Animal care and service workers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Almost entirely physical and interpersonal: feeding, grooming, exercising, training animals, and cleaning their living spaces. Scheduling appointments and basic record-keeping are minor digital components. AI has minimal impact on the hands-on animal care that defines this role.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Feeding, grooming, exercising, and monitoring animals are hands-on physical tasks. Record-keeping benefits minimally from AI, but the core caregiving duties have negligible digital AI exposure.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: This is almost entirely hands-on physical work—feeding, grooming, exercising, and caring for animals. Digital AI has negligible exposure beyond basic scheduling and record-keeping tools.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Animal care involves handling live animals in variable settings, requiring responsiveness to unpredictable animal behavior. The judgment and dexterity needed for animal handling are beyond 2028 robotic capabilities.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Working with live animals requires constant adaptation to unpredictable behavior. Animals need trust-based relationships with handlers. Environments vary widely from kennels to veterinary offices to outdoor settings. Robots cannot yet manage the variability and emotional sensitivity required.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Working with live animals in variable environments requires adaptability to unpredictable animal behavior. By 2036, robots handle routine feeding and cleaning in structured facilities, but grooming, training, and handling diverse animals still needs significant human involvement due to animal variability and emotional bonding.
adoption_friction_rationale: Highly fragmented employer base of small veterinary clinics, kennels, and pet care businesses. Physical animal handling requires dexterity and judgment. Strong owner preference for human caregivers. Low capital availability among small operators.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Pet ownership and spending on pet care continues to grow. AI has limited impact on physical animal care. Some expansion as lower-cost veterinary diagnostics enable more preventive care and pet services become more accessible.

title: Announcers and DJs
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: A mix of live performance (presenting, interviewing, emceeing events) and digital content work (researching topics, selecting content, operating studio equipment). AI-generated voices and content curation tools are emerging by 2028, affecting pre-recorded and routine broadcast segments, but live personality-driven performance remains human.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: AI can generate playlists, produce scripted announcements, and even create synthetic voices for routine broadcasting. Live event hosting and personality-driven content retain human value, but many routine announcing roles are displaced.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI can generate natural-sounding voice content, curate playlists algorithmically, and produce automated radio programming. Human announcers remain primarily for live events, personality-driven shows where human authenticity is the value proposition, and local community connection.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Announcers present information via broadcast media. Communication work with no physical labor.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: On-air broadcasting is primarily verbal and creative. While AI-generated voices exist, live announcing requires real-time improvisation and human personality. The physical component (sitting at a microphone) is minimal.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Entirely voice/personality/communication work. No physical labor component. AI voice synthesis is a digital AI issue, not physical/embodied.
adoption_friction_rationale: AI voice synthesis is advancing rapidly. Large media companies can adopt quickly, but audience preference for human personalities and local knowledge provides moderate friction. Union protections (AFTRA) in major markets. Small market stations have limited capital.
demand_elasticity_rationale: AI can generate synthetic voices for routine broadcasting, reducing demand for basic announcing. But podcasting and streaming have expanded opportunities for personality-driven content. Net roughly neutral.

title: Anthropologists and archeologists
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Fieldwork (excavation, observation, interviews) is physical, but substantial knowledge work includes data analysis, report writing, and research planning. AI assists with literature review, data pattern analysis, and report drafting by 2028. The blend of field and desk work places this at moderate exposure.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Research synthesis, data analysis, and report writing benefit substantially from AI agents. However, fieldwork, excavation, cultural interpretation, and ethnographic research requiring deep contextual human understanding limit full automation.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI transforms the analytical components—artifact classification, pattern recognition in data, literature synthesis, and report writing. However, fieldwork, ethnographic research requiring cultural immersion, and interpretive scholarship involving nuanced cultural understanding retain significant human roles.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Archeologists perform some fieldwork involving excavation, but the primary role is research and analysis. Field excavation in unpredictable sites limits robotic exposure.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Primarily research and analysis work. Archaeological fieldwork involves physical digging but in highly variable, novel environments where each site is unique. The intellectual interpretation is the core of the work.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Fieldwork involves working in highly unstructured, novel environments (excavation sites, remote communities). The physical components of archeological digs occur in genuinely unpredictable terrain. Primarily cognitive research and analysis work.
adoption_friction_rationale: Primarily academic and government employment with strong institutional inertia. Fieldwork requires physical presence and cultural judgment. Small employer base with limited technology budgets. Research methodology has strong traditions resistant to AI substitution.
demand_elasticity_rationale: AI tools (satellite imaging, pattern recognition) enable more archaeological discoveries and cultural analysis. Some latent demand for cultural consulting and heritage preservation work that becomes more feasible with AI assistance.

title: Arbitrators, mediators, and conciliators
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Core work is interpersonal: facilitating dialogue, managing conflict, and guiding negotiations between parties. However, legal research, document review, and settlement agreement preparation are digital tasks AI can assist with. The essential human skills of empathy, persuasion, and real-time negotiation limit overall exposure.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: AI handles case research, document analysis, and precedent review efficiently. However, the core function—facilitating human negotiation, reading interpersonal dynamics, and rendering judgment in disputes—requires deep human skills.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI can analyze case precedents, draft settlement proposals, and handle routine dispute documentation. However, the core value is interpersonal—reading emotional dynamics, building trust between parties, and exercising human judgment in fairness determinations that parties will accept as legitimate.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Mediators facilitate dispute resolution through communication. This is entirely interpersonal and cognitive work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Entirely interpersonal and cognitive work involving dispute resolution, negotiation, and legal reasoning. No physical component.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Entirely interpersonal and cognitive work involving negotiation, judgment, and conflict resolution. No physical component for robotic automation.
adoption_friction_rationale: Dispute resolution requires deep human judgment, empathy, and trust from all parties. Legal framework requires human decision-makers. Strong social barriers to accepting AI-mediated outcomes in personal and commercial disputes. Fragmented practice structure.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Some latent demand for dispute resolution—many disputes go unresolved due to cost. AI-assisted mediation could make resolution more accessible, expanding the market for alternative dispute resolution services.

title: Architects
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Design work using CAD software, preparing specifications, and contract documents is heavily digital. AI tools by 2028 assist with generative design, code compliance checking, and documentation. However, client meetings, site visits, creative vision, and construction oversight require significant human involvement.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: AI generates design options, produces construction documents, performs code compliance checks, and creates renderings autonomously. Architects focus on client relationships, creative vision, and complex site-specific judgment, but team sizes shrink notably.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI generates designs, optimizes building performance, ensures code compliance, and produces construction documents. Human architects remain for creative vision where human authorship is valued, client relationship management, complex site-specific judgment, and navigating the intersection of aesthetics, community impact, and regulation.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Architects design buildings using CAD software and creative judgment. This is entirely knowledge-based design work with no physical labor component.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Design work that is primarily computational and creative. Site visits occur but the role is fundamentally about design, planning, and client communication.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Primarily creative design and planning work that is cognitive. Site visits involve observation rather than physical labor. CAD and modeling tools are digital, not robotic.
adoption_friction_rationale: Mix of large firms and small practices. AI design tools are already being adopted, but licensing requirements (NCARB), liability for structural safety, and client relationships create moderate friction. Building codes and zoning require human interpretation.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Significant latent demand for architectural services. Most buildings are designed without architects due to cost. AI-assisted design tools could make architectural services accessible to smaller projects, renovations, and developing markets.

title: Architectural and engineering managers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Management duties include project planning, budgeting, staff coordination, and technical oversight—substantially digital. AI assists with project tracking, report generation, and resource planning. However, leadership, hiring decisions, cross-functional collaboration, and technical judgment remain human-driven.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Project coordination, scheduling, budgeting, and reporting are highly automatable. Managers retain value in strategic decision-making, client relationships, and team leadership, but AI agents handle most routine management information processing.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Project coordination, resource allocation, scheduling, and technical review are largely automated. Human managers remain for strategic decision-making, cross-functional leadership, client relationships, and navigating ambiguous situations where organizational and interpersonal judgment is required.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Engineering managers oversee technical teams and projects. This is managerial and strategic work with no physical labor component.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Management and oversight role that is entirely knowledge-based. Involves planning, coordinating, and directing technical projects.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Management and coordination role that is entirely cognitive. Planning, directing teams, and making strategic decisions. No physical labor component.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large firms have resources to adopt AI tools, but management roles require human judgment and leadership. Professional licensing and liability create moderate barriers. Role is more about coordination and decision-making than automatable tasks.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Management roles scale with the number of projects and teams, not individual productivity. AI may enable managers to oversee more projects, slightly reducing headcount, but growing infrastructure needs offset this.

title: Archivists, curators, and museum workers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: A blend of physical work (restoring objects, managing collections, designing exhibits) and digital tasks (cataloging, creating digital records, research). AI helps with cataloging and digital preservation by 2028, but physical conservation, exhibit curation, and public engagement require human expertise and presence.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Cataloging, research, and digital collection management are significantly aided by AI. However, physical conservation, exhibition design, and contextual interpretation of cultural artifacts require human expertise and presence.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates cataloging, digitization, collection analysis, and exhibit content generation. Human roles persist in physical conservation work, curatorial judgment about cultural significance, community engagement, and the interpersonal aspects of museum education and public programming.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Museum workers handle, preserve, and display artifacts. While some handling is in controlled settings, the delicate and varied nature of artifacts limits robotic involvement by 2028.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Conservators perform delicate physical work on unique, irreplaceable artifacts requiring extreme care and judgment. Museum technicians handle installation in variable spaces. The uniqueness of each object and environment limits automation potential significantly.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Conservation work involves delicate handling of unique, irreplaceable artifacts requiring fine motor skills and aesthetic judgment. Museum installation has some automatable components, but the variability and preciousness of objects limits robotic handling. Curatorial work is primarily cognitive.
adoption_friction_rationale: Cultural institutions have limited budgets and strong institutional inertia. Physical conservation work requires specialized manual skills. Curatorial judgment involves subjective cultural expertise. Fragmented across many small museums and institutions.
demand_elasticity_rationale: AI enables better digitization, cataloging, and preservation of collections. Growing demand for cultural tourism and digital museum experiences could expand roles. Some latent demand for conservation work on deteriorating collections.

title: Art directors
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Work is predominantly digital: developing visual styles, reviewing designs, coordinating creative teams, and presenting concepts to clients. AI image generation and design tools substantially assist production work by 2028. However, creative vision, team management, and client relationship skills remain essential human contributions.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: AI generates visual concepts, layouts, and design variations at scale by 2031. Art directors shift to creative vision, brand coherence, and client communication, but the production workforce under them shrinks dramatically.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI generates visual concepts, layouts, and design variations at scale. Human art directors retain value in establishing creative vision where human authorship matters, managing client relationships, and making aesthetic judgments in ambiguous brand and cultural contexts that require taste and cultural awareness.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Art directors manage visual aspects of creative projects. This is creative knowledge work with no physical labor component.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Creative management and visual direction work. Entirely knowledge and aesthetic judgment based with no physical automation potential.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Creative direction and visual design management is entirely cognitive work. Decision-making about visual aesthetics, managing creative teams. No physical labor.
adoption_friction_rationale: Creative direction involves subjective aesthetic judgment valued by clients. Large agencies and media companies can adopt AI tools, but human creative vision is central to the role. Mix of large and small employers. AI design tools are already augmenting the role.
demand_elasticity_rationale: AI tools accelerate production but every brand, product, and campaign needs creative direction. The explosion of digital content and channels creates more need for art direction. Latent demand from smaller businesses wanting professional creative work.

title: Assemblers and fabricators
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Core work is physical assembly using hand and power tools: positioning parts, connecting components, conducting quality checks, and maintaining equipment. Reading schematics has a minor digital component, but the overwhelmingly manual nature of assembly work means AI has minimal direct impact by 2028.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Assembly work is predominantly physical—fitting parts, soldering, wiring, and operating tools on production lines. AI has minimal impact on these manual dexterity tasks at the 2031 horizon.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: This is hands-on manufacturing work—assembling parts, using tools, and operating on production lines. Digital AI exposure is minimal, limited to instruction displays and quality tracking systems. The work is physical, not digital.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Assemblers work in structured factory environments performing repetitive assembly tasks. Humanoid robots and robotic arms are being commercially deployed for these tasks in automotive and electronics manufacturing by 2028.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: By 2031, robotic assembly systems handle the large majority of repetitive assembly tasks across manufacturing. Human workers focus on complex assemblies, quality exceptions, and tasks requiring unusual dexterity. Standardized assembly lines are heavily automated.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Repetitive assembly work in structured manufacturing environments is highly automatable by 2036. Robots handle the vast majority of assembly tasks. Remaining human roles are supervisory and for genuinely novel or very low-volume custom work.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large manufacturing employers (automotive, electronics) with strong economic incentive and existing automation culture. Acute labour shortages in manufacturing. Robots are already widely deployed in assembly. Clear ROI and minimal regulatory barriers beyond workplace safety.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Manufacturing assembly is increasingly automated with robotics. Demand is tied to production volume, which is relatively fixed domestically. AI-guided robots directly replace assembly workers in routine tasks.

title: Athletes and sports competitors
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Core value is entirely physical: practicing, training, exercising, and competing in sporting events. While AI assists with performance analytics and video review, the fundamental work product—athletic performance—is entirely non-digital and cannot be automated.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Athletic performance is entirely physical and embodied. AI assists with training analytics and game strategy, but competing in sports is inherently a human physical activity with no digital substitution.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Athletic competition is inherently physical and embodied. AI may assist with training analytics and strategy, but the core product—human physical performance in competition—has essentially zero digital AI exposure.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Athletes compete in physical sports. While physically demanding, this is human performance and competition that robots cannot replace.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Athletic performance is inherently human—audiences value human competition. While training technology advances, the actual performance is entirely about human physical capability and cannot be replaced by robots.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Athletic competition is inherently about human physical performance. The entire value proposition is humans competing physically. Robots cannot substitute for human athletes in sports.
adoption_friction_rationale: The entire value proposition is human physical achievement and competition. Audiences watch for human drama, skill, and narrative. League governance, cultural tradition, and the fundamental nature of sport make AI/robot substitution essentially impossible.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Entertainment demand grows with population and media. More leagues, more sports content, more global audiences. AI has minimal direct impact on athletic performance demand. Esports creates adjacent demand.

title: Athletic trainers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Predominantly physical and interpersonal: applying bandages and braces, providing first aid, developing rehabilitation programs, and working directly with athletes. Administrative duties like record-keeping and treatment planning benefit from AI, but hands-on patient care dominates.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Core duties involve hands-on injury assessment, rehabilitation exercises, and taping/bracing. AI aids with treatment planning and injury risk analysis, but physical patient care and real-time clinical judgment during sporting events remain human.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates injury risk assessment, rehabilitation protocol design, and performance analytics. However, the core work involves hands-on physical assessment, manual therapy, taping and bracing, and the interpersonal relationship with athletes that is central to effective sports medicine.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Athletic trainers provide injury prevention and rehabilitation through physical assessment and treatment. The varied athletic contexts and individualized physical care limit robotic exposure by 2028.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Hands-on physical assessment and treatment of athletes in highly variable situations. Each injury and athlete is different, requiring skilled touch, trust, and real-time judgment. The interpersonal and diagnostic aspects resist automation.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Hands-on physical assessment, rehabilitation exercises, and injury treatment involving direct human contact. The therapeutic relationship and adaptive physical manipulation based on patient response requires human presence, though diagnostic equipment is increasingly automated.
adoption_friction_rationale: Healthcare-adjacent role requiring hands-on physical assessment and treatment. State licensing requirements and liability concerns. Employed by schools, sports teams, and clinics with varying resources. Strong preference for human touch in injury assessment and rehabilitation.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Growing health consciousness and sports participation expand demand. AI diagnostics help trainers serve more athletes and identify injuries earlier, but the hands-on nature of the work limits pure headcount reduction.

title: Atmospheric scientists, including meteorologists
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Heavily digital work: analyzing atmospheric data, running computational weather models, preparing forecasts and reports, and using specialized software. AI significantly enhances weather prediction, data analysis, and forecast generation by 2028. Some fieldwork for instrument deployment remains physical.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Weather modeling, data analysis, and forecast generation are heavily digital tasks where AI agents excel. Remaining human roles focus on interpreting novel weather patterns, communicating forecasts, and research into climate phenomena.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Weather modeling, forecast generation, data analysis, and climate research are heavily digital and highly automatable by AI. Human roles remain in communicating forecasts to the public, interpreting novel weather patterns, and research into genuinely new atmospheric phenomena.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Meteorologists analyze weather data and create forecasts. This is entirely knowledge-based analytical work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Purely analytical and computational work involving weather modeling and forecasting. No physical labor component.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Entirely analytical and computational work involving data analysis, modeling, and forecasting. No physical component for robotic automation.
adoption_friction_rationale: AI/ML is already transforming weather prediction. Government agencies (NOAA, NWS) and media companies are primary employers. Regulatory requirements for public safety forecasting create some friction. Broadcasting role faces moderate social barriers.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Climate change increases demand for weather prediction and climate modeling. AI dramatically improves forecasting capabilities, enabling new applications in agriculture, insurance, and disaster preparedness.

title: Audiologists
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Core work is clinical and interpersonal: examining patients, conducting hearing tests, fitting hearing devices, and counseling patients on treatment. While diagnostic equipment is computerized and AI may assist with test interpretation, the direct patient care and physical examination components dominate.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Audiologists perform physical hearing tests, fit devices, and provide in-person patient counseling. AI assists with diagnostic interpretation and hearing aid programming, but the clinical, hands-on patient care limits digital exposure.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates hearing test interpretation, hearing aid programming, and treatment planning from digital data. However, audiologists perform physical examinations, fit devices requiring manual dexterity, and provide patient counseling and education that retain significant human involvement.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Audiologists diagnose hearing disorders and fit devices. While their work involves some physical testing equipment use, it is primarily diagnostic and clinical with minimal physical labor exposure to robotics.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Clinical work requiring patient interaction, physical examination of ears, and fitting of hearing devices. Each patient presents unique anatomy and needs. Trust and communication are essential components.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Clinical work involving patient interaction, physical examination of ears, fitting hearing devices. Requires human trust and communication. Some diagnostic testing is automatable, but the patient relationship and adaptive clinical judgment remain human-centered.
adoption_friction_rationale: State licensing, healthcare regulation, and insurance billing requirements create significant friction. Fragmented practice with many small clinics. Patients expect human interaction for hearing assessment and device fitting. Moderate liability concerns.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Aging population increases hearing loss prevalence. AI-powered hearing aids may reduce some diagnostic visits, but growing awareness and accessibility of hearing care expands the patient pool.

title: Automotive body and glass repairers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Predominantly hands-on physical work: removing dents, replacing panels, refinishing surfaces, and installing windshields. Damage estimation and cost reporting have digital components that AI can assist with, but the core repair work is entirely manual.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: This is hands-on physical repair work—straightening frames, replacing glass, painting vehicles. AI has negligible impact on these manual skilled trade tasks.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: This is almost entirely physical skilled trade work—removing dents, replacing glass, painting, and welding automotive body panels. Digital AI exposure is negligible beyond estimate generation and parts ordering.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Auto body repair involves assessing and fixing unique damage on different vehicles. The variability of each repair job and need for skilled manual work makes robotic replacement impractical by 2028.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Each vehicle presents unique damage patterns requiring assessment and custom repair approaches. Some standardized repairs (windshield replacement) are becoming more automated, but body work requires significant human judgment and dexterity for variable damage.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: By 2036, many standardized body repairs and glass replacements are robot-performed in structured shop environments. However, damage assessment and repair of complex, unique damage patterns still requires human judgment. Robots handle most routine panel and glass work.
adoption_friction_rationale: Highly fragmented industry of small independent shops with limited capital. Physical repair work in varied conditions requires dexterity. Insurance and liability frameworks assume human technicians. Some labour shortages but infrastructure not ready for robotic repair.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Demand tied to accident rates, which may decline with autonomous driving and safety tech. Physical repair work resists automation but the volume of work may decrease over time.

title: Automotive service technicians and mechanics
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Core duties are physical: inspecting, maintaining, and repairing vehicles using diagnostic equipment and hand tools. While computerized diagnostics are integral, the hands-on repair, parts replacement, and testing work dominates. AI assists with diagnostics and service manual lookup but cannot perform physical repairs.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Core work is physical diagnosis and repair of vehicle systems. AI-enhanced diagnostics help identify issues faster, but the mechanical repair work itself remains manual and requires physical skill.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: The core work is hands-on mechanical diagnosis and repair. AI enhances diagnostic capabilities through OBD systems, but the physical repair, parts replacement, and hands-on troubleshooting remain fundamentally human tasks requiring manual skill.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Auto mechanics diagnose and repair varied vehicle issues requiring skilled dexterity and problem-solving. Each repair is different, and the variable positioning and access requirements limit robotic deployment by 2028.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Diagnostics increasingly automated, but physical repair work varies enormously by vehicle, problem, and environment. Working in tight engine compartments with diverse fasteners and components requires human dexterity. Shops vary widely in layout and equipment.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Vehicle repair involves significant diagnostic work and physical manipulation in variable configurations. By 2036, robots handle many standardized maintenance tasks (oil changes, tire rotations, brake replacements), but diagnosing complex problems and working on varied vehicle models still requires significant human involvement.
adoption_friction_rationale: Fragmented between dealerships (larger) and independent shops (smaller). Diagnostic AI is already used, but physical repair requires manual dexterity in varied conditions. ASE certification and liability create moderate barriers. Labour shortages provide some pull.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Electric vehicles require less maintenance than ICE vehicles, reducing long-term demand. AI diagnostics speed up troubleshooting but the physical repair work still needs humans. Net slight decline in headcount.

title: Bakers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Almost entirely physical work: measuring ingredients, mixing dough, kneading, shaping, and baking products. Inventory management is a minor digital component. AI has negligible impact on the manual food preparation that defines this role.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Baking involves physical preparation—mixing, shaping, decorating, and operating ovens. AI has minimal relevance to these hands-on food production tasks.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Baking is hands-on physical production work—mixing, shaping, baking, and decorating food products. Digital AI has minimal exposure beyond recipe management and inventory systems.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Commercial baking involves repetitive production of standardized products in semi-structured environments. Industrial bakeries use significant automation; smaller operations less so. Moderate robotic exposure by 2028.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Commercial/industrial baking is increasingly automated with robotic mixing, shaping, and packaging. Large bakeries and chain operations use extensive automation. Artisanal and custom baking still requires human skill, but the majority of volume production is automatable by 2031.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Commercial baking in production environments is highly automated by 2036. Robots handle mixing, shaping, baking, and packaging for standard products. Artisanal and custom baking retains some human craft, but the vast majority of commercial baking is robot-operated.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large commercial bakeries and food manufacturers are already highly automated. Retail/artisanal bakeries are more fragmented but represent a smaller market share. Food safety regulations are manageable. Labour shortages in food production create adoption pull.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Artisanal baking demand grows with food culture trends, but industrial baking is already highly automated. AI has limited impact on physical baking. Demand is tied to population and food consumption patterns.

title: Barbers, hairstylists, and cosmetologists
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Core work is entirely physical and interpersonal: cutting, styling, and coloring hair, skin care, and direct client interaction. Appointment scheduling is a minor digital component. AI cannot perform physical grooming services.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Hair cutting, styling, coloring, and skin treatments are entirely hands-on personal services. AI might assist with appointment scheduling or style visualization, but core service delivery is physical.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Hair cutting, styling, and cosmetic services are entirely hands-on, interpersonal services. The value proposition includes human connection and personal attention. Digital AI exposure is limited to booking systems and trend reference.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Hairstyling and barbering require skilled dexterity with varied hair types and customer preferences. The fine motor control and creative adaptation needed are beyond 2028 robotic capabilities.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Highly personal service requiring trust, communication, creative judgment, and skilled dexterity on unique human heads. Each client's hair, preferences, and head shape differ. The social and aesthetic aspects are core to the service. Very resistant to robotic automation.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Haircutting and styling involves intimate personal contact where the human relationship IS the product for many clients. High variability in hair types, styles, and client preferences. By 2036, basic cuts might be robot-assisted, but the personal service, aesthetic judgment, and client relationship keep this predominantly human.
adoption_friction_rationale: Extremely fragmented industry of independent practitioners and small salons. State licensing requirements. Strong social preference for human touch, personal relationships, and aesthetic judgment. Physical manipulation of hair requires exceptional dexterity. Low capital availability.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Personal grooming is inherently physical and in-person. Growing consumer spending on personal care and appearance. Some latent demand as services become more accessible, though AI has minimal direct impact on the hands-on work.

title: Bartenders
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Core duties are physical and interpersonal: mixing drinks, serving customers, managing bar inventory, and ensuring responsible alcohol service. POS system use is a minor digital component. AI has minimal impact on the in-person service nature of this work.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Mixing drinks, serving customers, and managing a bar are physical and interpersonal tasks. AI has negligible impact on the core bartending role.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Bartending is a physical and interpersonal service role—mixing drinks, managing a bar, and providing social interaction. Digital AI has minimal relevance beyond POS systems and inventory management.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Bartending combines drink preparation with significant social interaction in variable settings. While robotic bartenders exist as novelties, the social and creative aspects of the role limit meaningful exposure by 2028.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Robotic bartending systems exist for standardized drinks in high-volume venues. However, craft cocktail preparation, customer interaction, and the social nature of bartending in most establishments still require humans. The hospitality and improvisation aspects resist full automation.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: By 2036, robotic bartending systems handle standard drink preparation efficiently. However, the social/entertainment aspect of bartending, customer interaction, and craft cocktail culture retain human value. High-volume venues largely automated; craft and hospitality-focused venues retain humans.
adoption_friction_rationale: Mix of large chain restaurants/hotels and independent bars. Some automated cocktail systems exist but social/entertainment value of human bartenders is significant. Labour shortages provide moderate pull. Alcohol service regulations require human judgment for ID checks and overservice.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Hospitality demand grows modestly with population and tourism. The social and experiential nature of bartending resists automation. Demand is somewhat fixed by the number of bars and restaurants.

title: Bill and account collectors
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Work is almost entirely screen-based: using databases to find debtors, making phone calls, sending correspondence, negotiating repayment plans, and recording account information. AI chatbots and automated outreach systems can handle routine collection tasks by 2028, with active displacement of entry-level positions.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Account tracking, payment reminder generation, debtor communication scripting, and collections workflow management are heavily digital and highly automatable. AI agents can handle most outreach autonomously; only complex negotiation cases require humans.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Account identification, contact scheduling, payment processing, and routine collection communications are fully automatable. AI agents handle the vast majority of debt collection workflows. Only complex negotiations with high-value accounts or legally sensitive situations retain human involvement.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Bill collectors contact debtors by phone and manage accounts. This is communication and administrative work with no physical labor.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Office-based work involving phone calls, correspondence, and negotiation. Entirely knowledge and communication work with no physical component.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Entirely communication-based work involving phone calls, negotiations, and record-keeping. No physical component for robotic automation.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large financial institutions and collection agencies are primary employers with resources to adopt AI. Much work is already automated (auto-dialers, payment systems). FDCPA regulations require some compliance attention but don't prohibit automation. Clear ROI.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Highly routine communication work that AI can largely automate. Demand is tied to the volume of delinquent accounts, which is relatively fixed. AI chatbots and automated systems directly replace human collectors for most interactions.

title: Biochemists and biophysicists
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: A significant blend of physical lab work (conducting experiments, operating equipment) and digital knowledge work (data analysis, modeling, report writing, literature review). AI meaningfully assists with computational biology, protein structure prediction, and manuscript preparation by 2028, but wet-lab experimental work remains human.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: AI accelerates literature review, data analysis, molecular modeling, and experiment design. However, wet-lab work, novel hypothesis generation, and interpreting unexpected results in biological systems require human scientists.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI transforms data analysis, literature synthesis, molecular modeling, experimental design, and paper writing. However, wet lab work, novel hypothesis generation from cross-disciplinary intuition, and interpreting unexpected experimental results in complex biological systems retain meaningful human roles.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Biochemists work primarily in labs conducting experiments. Lab automation handles some routine tasks, but the research-oriented nature of their work is primarily cognitive.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Lab work involves some physical manipulation of equipment and samples, with automated lab systems handling routine procedures. However, novel experimental design and non-standard protocols still require human researchers. The core intellectual work is not physical.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Laboratory research involves physical manipulation of equipment and samples, but the core work is cognitive research and analysis. By 2036, lab automation handles much routine experimentation, but novel research setups and experimental design remain human-driven.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large pharmaceutical companies and research universities are primary employers. AI is already transforming drug discovery and protein folding. Lab work still requires physical presence. Academic institutional inertia and peer review create moderate friction.
demand_elasticity_rationale: AI dramatically accelerates drug discovery, protein folding analysis, and molecular research. This opens new research directions and makes previously impossible research feasible, expanding the total volume of biochemistry work.

title: Bioengineers and biomedical engineers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Core duties include designing medical devices using CAD, developing software for medical systems, and writing technical reports—substantially digital.
