AI assists with design optimization, simulation, and documentation. Physical prototyping, clinical testing, and regulatory navigation require human expertise.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Design simulation, data analysis, and regulatory documentation are heavily aided by AI. However, hands-on device prototyping, clinical testing, and navigating complex medical-regulatory environments require human expertise.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Design optimization, simulation, regulatory documentation, and data analysis are automated. Human engineers remain for novel device conceptualization, clinical interface work, navigating complex regulatory pathways requiring judgment, and the physical prototyping and testing phases.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Biomedical engineers design medical equipment and devices. This is engineering design knowledge work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Primarily design and engineering work that is knowledge-based. Some prototype testing involves physical work, but the role centers on design, analysis, and problem-solving.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Primarily design, analysis, and research work that is cognitive. Some prototype testing and lab work, but the core engineering role involves minimal physical labor that robots would address.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large medical device companies and hospitals are primary employers with resources to adopt. FDA regulatory requirements for medical devices create friction for AI-designed products. But the field itself is technology-forward and already integrating AI tools.
demand_elasticity_rationale: AI enables new medical device designs, personalized prosthetics, and diagnostic tools. Growing healthcare spending and aging populations create demand. Significant latent demand for medical technology in developing countries.

title: Biological technicians
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Primarily hands-on laboratory work: setting up equipment, collecting samples, conducting experiments, and maintaining sterile environments. Data recording and report preparation have digital components that AI assists with, but the physical laboratory operations dominate day-to-day work.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Laboratory procedures—preparing samples, operating equipment, conducting experiments—are primarily physical. AI helps with data recording and analysis, but bench work remains human-driven.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: The role splits between lab bench work (physical sample preparation, running experiments, maintaining equipment) and data tasks. AI automates the data analysis and reporting side, but hands-on laboratory procedures remain human-performed.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Biological technicians work in labs performing experiments and maintaining equipment. Lab environments are structured and some sample handling is automatable, but varied procedures limit full robotic exposure.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Laboratory work with increasing automation of routine procedures like sample preparation, testing, and data collection. However, novel experimental setups and troubleshooting still require human technicians. Automated lab systems handle much of the standardized work.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Lab work involving sample preparation, equipment operation, and routine testing. By 2036, much laboratory processing is automated. Humans remain for novel experimental procedures and equipment troubleshooting in variable research contexts.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large pharmaceutical, biotech, and research institutions are primary employers. Lab automation is well-established and advancing. Some regulatory requirements for GLP/GMP compliance. Routine lab work is highly amenable to robotic automation.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Lab work volume tied to research funding and pharmaceutical development. AI may automate some data analysis but physical lab work persists. Research expansion roughly offsets efficiency gains.

title: Boilermakers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Almost entirely physical skilled trade work: reading blueprints, welding, installing boilers, and performing structural repairs using hand and power tools. The work requires physical presence in industrial settings with minimal digital component beyond blueprint reading.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Installing, maintaining, and repairing boilers and pressure vessels is physically demanding skilled trade work. AI has minimal impact on these hands-on construction and maintenance tasks.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Boilermaking involves physically assembling, installing, and repairing boilers, tanks, and vats in industrial settings. This is heavy manual skilled trade work with negligible digital AI exposure.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Boilermakers fabricate, install, and maintain boilers in industrial settings. While some factory fabrication is automated, field installation and repair in varied environments requires skilled manual work beyond 2028 robotics.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Heavy industrial work in variable environments—power plants, refineries, ships. Each installation is different, requiring skilled welding and metalwork in confined spaces. The variability of work sites and need for skilled judgment limits automation, though some routine welding tasks are automated.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Heavy industrial work in variable environments (power plants, refineries). By 2036, robots handle much welding and assembly in accessible locations, but boilermaker work often involves confined spaces, variable site conditions, and safety-critical judgment. Significant but not complete automation.
adoption_friction_rationale: Specialized construction trade with strong union presence (IBB). Work in confined spaces and hazardous conditions makes robotics challenging. Fragmented contractor base. ASME codes and safety regulations require certified human welders. Labour shortages provide some pull.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Demand tied to industrial infrastructure construction and maintenance, which is relatively stable. Physical work resists automation but new construction may use alternative technologies reducing boilermaker-specific demand.

title: Bookkeeping, accounting, and auditing clerks
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Almost entirely screen-based work: entering financial data, using bookkeeping software, producing reports, and reconciling records. AI can automate most routine data entry, classification, and report generation by 2028. Active headcount reduction is underway as organizations consolidate these roles.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Recording transactions, reconciling accounts, and producing financial reports are routine digital tasks that AI agents automate almost entirely by 2031. Only exception handling and complex reconciliations may require human review.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Basic bookkeeping—recording transactions, reconciling accounts, processing payroll, maintaining ledgers—is entirely digital routine work that AI systems handle end-to-end by 2036. This occupation has effectively ceased to exist in its traditional form.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Bookkeeping clerks maintain financial records and process transactions. This is entirely desk-based clerical work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Entirely desk-based data entry and record-keeping work. No physical component. Already heavily digitized.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Entirely digital/office work involving financial record-keeping. No physical component for robotic automation.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large organizations already use accounting software extensively. AI-powered bookkeeping tools are widely available. Employers range from large to small, but the work is highly standardized and digital. Regulatory requirements (tax compliance) actually drive automation adoption.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Highly routine data entry and record-keeping that AI and automation directly replace. Software like QuickBooks already reduced demand significantly. Remaining demand shrinks further as AI handles more complex reconciliation and categorization.

title: Broadcast, sound, and video technicians
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: A mix of physical equipment setup and operation with digital editing and monitoring. While AI assists with automated mixing, editing, and quality control for recorded content, live broadcast operation and physical equipment management remain hands-on. The role bridges physical and digital work.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: AI automates much of video editing, sound mixing, and broadcast switching. However, live production, physical equipment setup, and troubleshooting hardware in real-time performance settings retain significant human involvement.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates video editing, audio mixing, color correction, and routine broadcast operations. However, live event production, physical equipment setup and maintenance, and creative technical decisions in complex production environments retain human roles.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Broadcast technicians set up and operate audio/video equipment. While some tasks involve physical setup, the technical judgment and variable venues limit robotic exposure.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Technical work setting up and operating audio/video equipment in variable venues and studios. Each setup is different, requiring troubleshooting and adaptation. Some studio operations are increasingly automated, but live event work requires human adaptability.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Equipment setup, operation, and maintenance involves physical work in variable environments (studios, live events). By 2036, some routine setup is automated, but live production environments are highly variable and require adaptive problem-solving with physical equipment.
adoption_friction_rationale: Mix of large media companies and small production houses. Technical work is increasingly software-based and amenable to AI. Union presence in major markets (IATSE, IBEW). Equipment operation still requires physical presence for live events.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Explosion of content creation (streaming, podcasting, live events) increases demand for production technicians. AI tools help but the technical setup and management of broadcast equipment remains hands-on.

title: Budget analysts
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Almost entirely digital: analyzing financial data in spreadsheets, preparing budget reports, reviewing spending patterns, and writing recommendations. AI excels at financial modeling, variance analysis, and report drafting by 2028. Routine budget analysis is highly automatable, with experienced analysts focusing on strategic advisory.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Budget preparation, variance analysis, forecasting, and report generation are highly digital tasks that AI agents handle autonomously. Human budget analysts shift to strategic recommendations and stakeholder communication, but routine analysis is automated.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Budget preparation, variance analysis, financial forecasting, and compliance reporting are structured digital tasks fully automatable by AI. The remaining human role is in strategic budget prioritization discussions with leadership and navigating politically sensitive allocation decisions.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Budget analysts review financial data and prepare budget reports. This is entirely desk-based analytical work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Purely analytical office work involving financial planning and budget review. No physical component.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Entirely analytical and computational work. No physical component whatsoever.
adoption_friction_rationale: Primarily employed by large organizations and government agencies. Work is highly quantitative and amenable to AI tools. Government institutional inertia provides some friction, but budget pressure creates incentive to adopt. Moderate regulatory requirements.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Budget analysis for a fixed number of organizations and government agencies is relatively inelastic. AI can automate much of the data gathering and projection work, directly reducing the number of analysts needed per organization.

title: Bus drivers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Core work is entirely physical: operating a large vehicle, managing passenger safety, navigating routes, and performing pre-trip inspections. While GPS and scheduling systems are digital, the fundamental task of safely driving a bus with passengers requires physical presence that AI cannot replace by 2028.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Driving buses on fixed or variable routes, managing passengers, and ensuring safety are physical tasks. While autonomous vehicle technology advances, widespread deployment for public transit remains limited at the 2031 horizon.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Bus driving is primarily a physical operation role. While autonomous vehicle technology may transform this occupation, that represents physical AI/robotics rather than digital AI exposure. Digital AI exposure is limited to route optimization and scheduling systems.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Bus driving requires navigating fixed routes but in complex urban traffic with passenger interactions. Autonomous buses are in limited pilots in controlled settings, but widespread deployment is not yet reached by 2028.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Autonomous vehicle technology covers many fixed routes by 2031, especially dedicated bus lanes and highway segments. However, complex urban environments, passenger assistance, and safety oversight still require human drivers for many routes. School bus drivers face additional trust and regulatory barriers.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: By 2036, autonomous vehicles handle most fixed-route bus operations. Remaining human drivers are for genuinely challenging routes, extreme weather, and passenger safety/assistance needs. Urban and suburban fixed routes are largely autonomous.
adoption_friction_rationale: Strong union presence (ATU) and public safety regulations from DOT/FMCSA. Public transit agencies are government entities with institutional inertia. School bus regulations are especially stringent given child safety. Autonomous bus pilots exist but regulatory path is slow. Labour shortages provide moderate pull.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Demand tied to fixed transit routes and ridership. Autonomous vehicle technology directly threatens this role long-term. In the medium term, driver shortages may offset some displacement, but the trajectory is toward fewer human drivers.

title: Butchers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Almost entirely physical work: receiving meat, cutting, deboning, grinding, weighing, and packaging products. Customer interaction and inventory are minor components. AI has negligible impact on the manual meat processing skills that define this trade.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Cutting, trimming, and preparing meat are manual physical tasks requiring skilled knife work. AI has no meaningful impact on this hands-on production role.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Butchering is hands-on physical work involving cutting, trimming, and preparing meat products. Digital AI exposure is negligible, limited to inventory and ordering systems.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Butchering involves repetitive cutting tasks in structured processing environments. Large meat processing plants are deploying robotic cutting systems, though the variability of animal anatomy limits full automation.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Industrial meat processing is heavily automated with robotic cutting, deboning, and packaging systems. Custom retail butchering still requires human skill for variable cuts and customer interaction, but the majority of meat processing volume is increasingly automated.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: By 2036, most commercial meat cutting and processing is robotic, with advanced vision systems and dexterous manipulation handling varied animal anatomy. Custom butchering for specialty markets retains some human craft, but volume operations are heavily automated.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large meatpacking plants (Tyson, JBS) already use significant automation. Retail butcher shops are more fragmented. USDA food safety regulations are manageable. Labour shortages in meatpacking are severe, creating strong adoption pull. Physical dexterity for varied cuts creates moderate technical barriers.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Meat processing is increasingly automated in industrial settings. Demand tied to meat consumption, which is stable or declining in developed countries. Artisanal butchery has a niche but overall headcount trends down.

title: Calibration technologists and technicians
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Primarily hands-on work: inspecting, adjusting, and testing precision measurement devices against standards. While documentation and data comparison have digital aspects that AI assists with, the physical calibration of instruments and equipment requires manual skill and precision.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Physical calibration of instruments and equipment is hands-on work. AI assists with documentation and scheduling, but the core task of adjusting and verifying precision equipment requires human manual skill.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: The core work involves physically inspecting, testing, and adjusting precision instruments and equipment. AI assists with calibration data analysis and documentation, but the hands-on measurement and adjustment work remains human-performed.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Calibration technicians test and adjust precision instruments in structured lab/factory environments. The controlled settings and repetitive testing procedures offer moderate automation potential by 2028.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Routine calibration of standardized equipment is increasingly automated, but technicians still needed for diverse equipment types, field calibration, and troubleshooting. The variety of instruments and environments provides some protection from full automation.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Routine calibration of instruments and equipment is highly automatable in structured environments. By 2036, robots handle most standard calibration procedures. Humans remain for novel equipment, troubleshooting, and field calibration in variable environments.
adoption_friction_rationale: Employed by manufacturers, labs, and government agencies. Work requires precision but is increasingly automatable. Regulatory requirements for calibration standards (NIST traceability) create some friction. Moderate employer fragmentation.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Demand tied to the volume of precision instruments and equipment requiring calibration, which grows modestly with manufacturing and healthcare. AI may speed calibration processes but physical work persists.

title: Cardiovascular technologists and technicians
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Core work involves hands-on patient care: conducting cardiac tests, assisting in procedures, operating imaging equipment, and monitoring patients. While test results are digitally processed and AI assists with image analysis, the physical patient interaction and equipment operation dominate.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Operating cardiac monitoring equipment involves physical patient interaction and device manipulation. AI significantly aids image interpretation and report generation, but hands-on patient procedures and equipment operation remain human tasks.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates image interpretation, diagnostic analysis, and reporting. However, operating imaging equipment, positioning patients, and performing invasive procedures like cardiac catheterization require physical presence and manual skill that retains human involvement.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Cardiovascular techs operate diagnostic equipment and assist with cardiac procedures. The work involves medical equipment operation with patient interaction, but limited physical labor for robots to automate.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Patient-facing medical work requiring trust and physical positioning of patients and equipment. Each patient's anatomy varies. Imaging automation assists but human operators needed for patient interaction, positioning, and clinical judgment.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Patient-facing diagnostic work involving equipment operation and patient positioning. By 2036, much imaging is automated, but patient interaction, positioning of varied body types, and adaptive testing still require human involvement. Regulatory requirements also mandate human presence.
adoption_friction_rationale: Healthcare regulation, licensing, and liability create significant friction. Hospital employers are large but healthcare institutional inertia is strong. Patient interaction and clinical judgment requirements. AI-assisted diagnostics are emerging but regulatory approval is slow.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Demand tied to patient volume and cardiovascular disease prevalence. AI improves diagnostic accuracy but doesn't change the number of tests needed. Aging population increases demand while AI efficiency offsets.

title: Career and technical education teachers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Teaching vocational skills (auto repair, cosmetology, culinary arts) involves significant hands-on demonstration and student supervision. Lesson planning, curriculum development, and grading benefit from AI by 2028, but the physical instruction and mentoring in trades remains fundamentally human.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: AI handles content delivery, lesson planning, and assessment grading. However, CTE teachers provide hands-on skills training, mentoring, and workplace readiness coaching that require human presence and expertise.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Theoretical content delivery and curriculum planning are automated. However, CTE teaching inherently involves hands-on skills instruction—demonstrating trades, supervising workshop practice, and mentoring students in applied settings—which preserves significant human roles.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Teaching is fundamentally interpersonal and cognitive work involving instruction, mentoring, and classroom management. There is no physical labor component for robots to automate.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Teaching is fundamentally interpersonal work. While some shop/lab teaching involves physical demonstration, the core is human instruction and mentorship. No significant physical automation potential.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Teaching involves hands-on demonstration and student mentoring in workshop environments. The educational relationship and adaptive instruction are human-centered. Physical demonstration of trades skills and supervising student practice requires human presence and judgment.
adoption_friction_rationale: Education sector institutional inertia, teacher certification requirements, and strong preference for human instruction, especially for hands-on technical training. Employed primarily by public schools and community colleges with limited technology budgets.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Growing demand for skilled trades and technical education as these fields expand. AI tools can make teachers more effective, and there's significant unmet demand for vocational training programs.

title: Carpenters
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Almost entirely physical work: constructing, installing, and repairing building frameworks using hand and power tools. Reading blueprints is a minor digital component. AI has negligible impact on the manual carpentry skills that define this trade.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Measuring, cutting, and assembling building materials on construction sites is entirely physical skilled trade work. AI has negligible impact on carpentry tasks.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Carpentry is skilled physical trade work—measuring, cutting, shaping, and installing wood and other materials on construction sites. Digital AI exposure is minimal, limited to design reference and measurement tools.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Carpenters work in highly variable job sites performing skilled manual work with diverse materials. Every project differs, and the unstructured nature of construction sites makes robotic deployment impractical by 2028.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Residential and custom carpentry involves highly variable environments—each building, renovation, and design is different. While some prefabrication and CNC work is automated, on-site carpentry requires constant adaptation to existing structures and conditions. Commercial construction has more standardized tasks.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Residential and commercial carpentry involves highly variable work environments, custom measurements, and adaptation to existing structures. By 2036, robots handle many standardized framing and installation tasks, but custom work, renovation, and site-specific adaptation still require significant human skill and judgment.
adoption_friction_rationale: Highly fragmented between large commercial contractors and many independent operators. Physical work in varied, unstructured environments. Union protections in some markets. Building codes require human accountability. Labour shortages provide some pull but jobsite robotics infrastructure is lacking.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Physical construction demand tied to building activity. Carpentry resists automation due to the custom, on-site nature of the work. Housing demand is significant but constrained by factors beyond labor cost.

title: Cartographers and photogrammetrists
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Almost entirely digital work: using GIS software, remote sensing data, and computer tools to create and update maps. AI significantly accelerates geospatial data analysis, automated feature extraction, and map generation by 2028. Most output is delivered digitally with minimal fieldwork required.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Map production, spatial data processing, aerial image analysis, and GIS operations are heavily digital tasks that AI agents can largely automate. Human cartographers focus on novel analysis, quality validation, and complex spatial interpretation.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Map production, geospatial data processing, satellite imagery analysis, and terrain modeling are highly digital tasks that AI handles autonomously. Human roles persist in novel cartographic interpretation, quality assurance for critical applications, and specialized fieldwork.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Cartographers create maps using geographic data and software. This is knowledge-based technical work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Primarily digital/computational work using GIS software and satellite imagery. Some fieldwork for ground-truthing but the role is fundamentally desk-based analysis and map creation.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Primarily digital/analytical work involving GIS software, remote sensing data, and map creation. Minimal physical component—some field surveying but mostly screen-based work.
adoption_friction_rationale: GIS and remote sensing are already heavily computerized. Government agencies and tech companies (Google, Esri) are primary employers with resources to adopt AI. Satellite imagery analysis is increasingly automated. Moderate regulatory requirements for official maps.
demand_elasticity_rationale: AI and satellite imagery create massive new mapping possibilities—autonomous vehicles, precision agriculture, urban planning, and real-time environmental monitoring all need more and better mapping.

title: Cashiers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Core work is in-person customer interaction: scanning items, processing payments, and providing service. While POS systems are digital, the role requires physical presence and customer-facing engagement. Self-checkout technology displaces some positions, but AI's impact is primarily through automation of the physical checkout process rather than digital AI tools.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Self-checkout and automated payment systems reduce cashier demand, but the role is primarily physical (handling goods, assisting customers in person). Digital AI exposure is moderate—it displaces through automation of the transaction process rather than digital workflow.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: While self-checkout and automated payment systems reduce cashier roles, this is primarily a physical retail presence job. The digital AI component is limited—the displacement comes more from physical automation (self-checkout kiosks) than digital AI specifically.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Cashier work in retail involves repetitive scanning and payment processing in structured environments. Self-checkout and automated payment systems are widely deployed, and cashierless stores are expanding by 2028.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Self-checkout and automated payment systems are widespread by 2031. Many retail and fast-food locations operate with minimal cashier staff. However, some customer-facing roles remain for complex transactions, customer assistance, and stores where human interaction is valued.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Self-checkout and automated retail systems are ubiquitous by 2036. Most transaction processing is fully automated. Remaining human cashiers serve primarily social/customer-service functions in select retail environments.
adoption_friction_rationale: Self-checkout and automated payment systems are already widespread in large retail chains. Massive employer consolidation (Walmart, Amazon, Target) drives rapid adoption. Labour shortages and cost pressure accelerate automation. Minimal regulatory barriers.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Self-checkout and automated payment systems directly replace cashiers. E-commerce further reduces in-store transaction volume. Demand is purely tied to transaction volume, which doesn't increase with faster checkout.

title: Chefs and head cooks
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Predominantly physical work: food preparation, cooking, kitchen management, and quality control. Menu planning and inventory management have digital components where AI can assist, but the hands-on culinary work and kitchen leadership are entirely non-digital.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Cooking is fundamentally physical—preparing ingredients, managing kitchen operations, and creating dishes. AI assists with menu planning, inventory management, and recipe development, but hands-on culinary execution remains human.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Cooking is fundamentally physical and creative hands-on work. AI can assist with menu planning, recipe optimization, and inventory management, but the core value—culinary creativity, kitchen leadership, and physical food preparation—remains human.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Chefs create dishes requiring creativity, taste judgment, and varied techniques. Their role emphasizes culinary creativity and management beyond repetitive preparation, limiting robotic exposure.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Executive chefs focus on menu creation, kitchen management, and quality control—largely creative and managerial. While robotic kitchen systems handle some routine cooking in chains, head chefs in restaurants provide creative direction and handle complex preparations that require taste, judgment, and improvisation.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Head chefs are primarily creative and managerial. Menu design, recipe development, quality oversight, and kitchen management are cognitive tasks. By 2036, robots handle much routine food preparation, but creative culinary work, taste judgment, and kitchen leadership remain human-centered.
adoption_friction_rationale: Mix of large restaurant chains (lower friction) and independent restaurants (higher friction). Creative culinary work has social value. Food safety regulations manageable. Labour shortages in food service create pull, but kitchen robotics still face physical dexterity challenges in varied environments.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Growing dining-out culture and food delivery expand demand for culinary creativity. AI has limited impact on creative cooking. Cloud kitchens and delivery platforms create new venues for chef-led food businesses.

title: Chemical engineers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Substantial digital work in process design, simulation, data analysis, and technical documentation using specialized software. AI assists with process optimization, safety analysis, and report generation by 2028. However, plant visits, equipment oversight, and safety-critical judgment require physical presence and human expertise.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Process simulation, data analysis, and documentation are significantly aided by AI. However, plant operations, hands-on process troubleshooting, and safety-critical decision-making in physical chemical environments moderate overall exposure.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Process simulation, reaction modeling, and documentation are automated. However, chemical engineering involves significant plant-floor presence, physical process oversight, and hands-on troubleshooting in industrial environments that retain human roles alongside the digital transformation.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Chemical engineers design chemical processes and equipment. This is engineering knowledge work with no physical labor component.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Design and process engineering work that is primarily knowledge-based and computational. Plant visits occur but the role is about design and optimization, not physical labor.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Primarily design, analysis, and process optimization work that is cognitive. Site visits and plant inspections have minor physical components, but the core role is engineering problem-solving.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large chemical, pharmaceutical, and energy companies are primary employers with resources to adopt. Process automation is already well-established. EPA and OSHA regulations create some friction for AI-controlled processes. Safety-critical nature of chemical processes requires human oversight.
demand_elasticity_rationale: AI accelerates process optimization and materials discovery. Growing demand for sustainable energy, new materials, and pharmaceutical manufacturing. Some latent demand for chemical engineering in emerging economies.

title: Chemical technicians
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Primarily hands-on laboratory work: monitoring chemical processes, testing product quality, operating instruments, and maintaining equipment. Data recording and analysis have digital components, but the physical laboratory operations and quality control testing dominate the role.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Laboratory procedures—mixing chemicals, operating equipment, collecting samples—are primarily physical. AI assists with data recording and analysis, but bench work remains hands-on.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: The role centers on physical laboratory and plant work—conducting tests, preparing chemical solutions, and operating equipment. AI automates data analysis and reporting, but hands-on lab procedures and quality testing remain human-performed.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Chemical technicians work in labs performing tests and monitoring processes. Lab environments are structured, and some routine testing is automatable, but varied chemical procedures limit full exposure.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Laboratory work with increasing automation of routine testing and analysis. Automated systems handle standardized procedures, but technicians still needed for sample preparation, equipment maintenance, and non-routine testing.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Laboratory and plant work involving routine testing, sample preparation, and equipment operation. By 2036, much routine chemical analysis and process monitoring is automated. Humans remain for novel procedures and troubleshooting.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large chemical and pharmaceutical companies are primary employers. Lab automation is advancing rapidly. Regulatory requirements (EPA, OSHA, GLP) create moderate friction. Routine analytical work is highly amenable to automation. Some physical lab work remains.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Lab work volume tied to industrial and pharmaceutical production. AI may improve analytical efficiency but physical testing and quality control persist. Demand grows modestly with industry.

title: Chemists and materials scientists
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: A blend of physical lab work (carrying out experiments, operating instruments) and digital knowledge work (data analysis, computational modeling, report writing). AI assists with molecular modeling, literature review, and data analysis by 2028, but hands-on experimental work remains essential.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: AI accelerates molecular modeling, literature review, data analysis, and experiment design. However, wet-lab experimentation, synthesizing novel compounds, and interpreting unexpected physical results require human scientists.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI excels at molecular modeling, literature analysis, experimental design optimization, and data interpretation. Human scientists remain for wet lab work, novel hypothesis generation, interpreting surprising results, and cross-disciplinary research requiring intuitive leaps.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Chemists conduct research primarily in laboratories. While lab automation handles some routine analysis, the research nature of the work is primarily cognitive.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Research work with some physical lab components. Automated lab systems handle routine synthesis and testing, but novel research requires human creativity and adaptation. The core work is intellectual.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Research work with significant lab components. By 2036, routine lab procedures are automated, but novel experimental design and research requiring creative physical manipulation of materials remains human-driven. Core work is cognitive analysis.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large companies and research institutions are primary employers. AI is already accelerating materials discovery and chemical analysis. Academic institutional inertia in university settings. Lab work still requires physical presence for novel experiments.
demand_elasticity_rationale: AI dramatically accelerates materials discovery and chemical research. New materials for batteries, semiconductors, and sustainable products create expanding research frontiers. Historical pattern: computational chemistry expanded the field.

title: Childcare workers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Almost entirely physical and interpersonal: supervising children, organizing activities, preparing meals, and fostering early development. The work requires constant physical presence and human care that AI cannot replace. Record-keeping is a negligible digital component.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Caring for children—feeding, supervising play, ensuring safety, and providing emotional support—is entirely physical and interpersonal. AI has negligible impact on direct childcare duties.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Childcare is fundamentally physical and interpersonal—supervising, nurturing, feeding, and engaging children. Human presence and emotional connection are the core product. Digital AI has negligible exposure beyond administrative record-keeping.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Childcare workers care for children requiring constant attention, empathy, and adaptive responses. The safety-critical nature and need for human nurturing make robotic replacement inappropriate and infeasible.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Caring for young children requires constant human attention, emotional sensitivity, and improvisation. Each child's needs differ moment to moment. Parents require deep trust in caregivers. Among the most resistant occupations to physical automation.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Childcare is fundamentally about human emotional presence, safety, and nurturing relationships. Children require human warmth, adaptability, and emotional intelligence. By 2036, robots may assist with monitoring and routine tasks, but the core caregiving role demands human presence and intimacy.
adoption_friction_rationale: Extreme social resistance to non-human childcare. Heavy state licensing and safety regulations. Parents strongly prefer human caregivers. Highly fragmented employer base of small daycare centers and home providers. Low wages limit capital for technology investment. Liability concerns are paramount.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Enormous unmet demand for affordable childcare. If AI tools help childcare workers manage larger groups more effectively or reduce administrative burden, more families could access care. Physical care of children cannot be automated.

title: Chiropractors
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Core work is physical patient care: spinal manipulation, musculoskeletal assessment, and hands-on treatment. Patient records, imaging review, and treatment planning have digital components where AI assists, but the essential hands-on therapeutic work and patient interaction dominate.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Spinal adjustments and musculoskeletal treatments are hands-on physical procedures. AI assists with diagnostic imaging interpretation and treatment planning, but the core manual therapy remains human.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Chiropractic care is primarily hands-on physical therapy involving spinal manipulation and manual adjustments. AI assists with diagnostic imaging interpretation and treatment planning, but the physical treatment delivery and patient relationship remain entirely human.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Chiropractors perform manual spinal adjustments requiring precise physical manipulation and patient-specific judgment. The intimate, varied physical techniques are beyond 2028 robotic capabilities.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Hands-on therapeutic work requiring skilled touch, patient communication, and real-time judgment based on each patient's unique physiology. Trust between practitioner and patient is essential. Very resistant to robotic automation.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Hands-on physical manipulation therapy where human touch and adaptive physical response to patient feedback IS the treatment. By 2036, some diagnostic imaging is automated, but the core spinal manipulation and patient relationship remains human-centered.
adoption_friction_rationale: State licensing and healthcare regulation. Highly fragmented independent practices with limited capital. Hands-on physical manipulation is central to the role. Strong patient preference for human practitioners. Malpractice liability concerns. Scope-of-practice debates add regulatory complexity.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Hands-on physical treatment resists automation. Growing interest in alternative and preventive healthcare. Some latent demand as chiropractic becomes more mainstream and accessible.

title: Civil engineering technologists and technicians
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: A mix of field work (site inspections, surveying, materials testing) and digital tasks (drafting using CAD, analyzing data, preparing reports). AI assists with design drafting and data analysis by 2028, but physical site work and hands-on testing remain significant portions of the role.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Drafting, CAD work, and calculations are increasingly automated by AI. However, site inspections, material testing, and physical survey work keep a significant portion of duties grounded in the physical world.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Drafting, calculation, and plan review components are automated by AI. However, field surveying, construction site inspection, materials testing, and physical oversight of infrastructure projects retain significant human roles.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Civil engineering technicians assist with plans and field measurements. Some field work involves physical tasks, but the role is primarily technical support work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Mix of office-based design work and field testing/inspection. Field work involves variable sites and conditions. Some testing is automated but site inspection and field measurement in diverse environments requires human adaptability.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Field testing, site inspection, and laboratory work with physical components. By 2036, some routine testing and surveying is automated, but variable field conditions and site-specific judgment require human involvement. Mix of office analysis and fieldwork.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large engineering firms and government agencies are primary employers. CAD and GIS work is already heavily computerized. Field inspection work requires physical presence. Moderate regulatory requirements for infrastructure projects. Government institutional inertia provides some friction.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Demand tied to infrastructure projects, which are growing with government investment. AI assists with calculations and modeling but physical site work and testing persist. Growth in infrastructure roughly offsets efficiency gains.

title: Civil engineers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Substantial digital work: using CAD and simulation software for design, analyzing data, preparing project specifications, and writing reports. AI assists with design optimization and documentation by 2028. However, site visits, construction supervision, and safety-critical regulatory judgment require human presence and expertise.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: AI generates structural designs, performs analysis, and produces documentation. Engineers shift to site-specific judgment, stakeholder management, and overseeing safety-critical infrastructure decisions, but design productivity increases dramatically.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Structural analysis, design optimization, code compliance checking, and documentation are automated. Human civil engineers remain for complex site-specific judgment, managing stakeholder relationships, navigating permitting processes, and overseeing physical construction.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Civil engineers design infrastructure projects using engineering analysis and software. This is knowledge work with no physical labor component.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Primarily design, analysis, and project management work. Site visits occur but the role is fundamentally about engineering design and oversight.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Primarily design, analysis, and project management work. Site visits involve observation and assessment rather than physical labor. Core work is cognitive engineering problem-solving.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large firms and government agencies have resources to adopt AI tools. Professional licensing (PE) and liability for public safety create significant friction. AI is already used for design optimization but regulatory approval of AI-designed infrastructure is slow. Government project bureaucracy adds inertia.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Massive infrastructure deficit creates latent demand. AI-assisted design enables more projects to be completed. Aging infrastructure, climate adaptation, and urbanization all drive growing demand for civil engineering.

title: Claims adjusters, appraisers, examiners, and investigators
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Predominantly digital work: reviewing claims documentation, analyzing policy coverage, calculating settlements, and preparing reports. AI significantly accelerates claims processing, fraud detection, and damage estimation by 2028. Physical site inspections for complex claims provide some insulation.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Document review, damage assessment from photos, policy analysis, and claims processing are heavily digital tasks AI agents handle autonomously. Complex fraud investigations and disputed claims still need human judgment, but routine claims work is largely automated.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Claims processing, damage assessment from photos and documents, coverage determination, and settlement calculation are structured digital tasks AI handles end-to-end. Only complex fraud investigations, disputed claims requiring negotiation, and catastrophic loss situations retain human adjusters.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Claims adjusters review insurance claims and investigate losses. This is primarily analytical and investigative desk work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Mostly office-based analytical work. Some field inspection of damage sites, but the core work is reviewing claims and making determinations. Physical inspection increasingly supplemented by drones and photographic evidence.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Primarily analytical work with some field inspection. By 2036, drone and robotic inspection assists with physical site assessment, but the investigative judgment and human interaction for claims assessment remain cognitive. Limited physical component.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large insurance companies are primary employers with strong technology adoption culture and clear ROI. Much claims processing is already automated. State insurance regulations create some friction. Physical inspection component for some claims limits full automation.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Insurance claims processing is highly automatable with AI image analysis and data processing. Many straightforward claims can be settled without human adjusters. Complex claims persist but represent a smaller share.

title: Clinical laboratory technologists and technicians
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Core work is hands-on laboratory testing: preparing specimens, operating complex analytical equipment, and performing quality control. While lab information systems and AI-assisted diagnostics are part of the digital infrastructure, the physical specimen handling and equipment operation dominate daily work.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Operating lab equipment, preparing specimens, and conducting tests are physical tasks. AI significantly aids result interpretation and quality control analysis, but hands-on specimen processing remains human-driven.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates result interpretation, quality control analysis, and reporting. However, specimen processing, equipment maintenance, troubleshooting instrument malfunctions, and handling non-standard samples require physical laboratory presence.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Lab techs process samples and run tests in structured laboratory environments with standardized procedures. Lab automation and robotic sample handling systems are commercially deployed in large reference laboratories by 2028.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Clinical lab work is increasingly automated with robotic sample handling, automated analyzers, and AI-assisted diagnostics. High-volume standardized tests are largely automated. Technologists focus on complex tests, quality control, and troubleshooting automated systems.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: By 2036, clinical laboratory analysis is highly automated with robotic sample handling, analysis, and reporting. Most routine blood work, urinalysis, and microbiological testing is fully automated. Humans remain for complex or unusual samples and quality oversight.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large hospital systems and reference labs are primary employers. Lab automation is well-established and advancing. CLIA regulations and state licensing create moderate friction. Routine analytical work is highly amenable to robotic automation. Some manual sample handling remains.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Demand tied to patient volume and testing orders. AI improves diagnostic accuracy and speed but doesn't change the number of samples needing processing. Aging population increases testing demand while automation improves throughput.

title: Coaches and scouts
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Primarily physical and interpersonal: conducting practices, teaching techniques, providing motivation, and attending games. Scouting involves video analysis and statistical evaluation where AI helps by 2028, but the core coaching relationship and in-person instruction remain fundamentally human.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Coaching requires physical presence, interpersonal motivation, and real-time tactical decisions during competition. AI enhances performance analytics and scouting reports, but the human relationship and in-person leadership are central.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: While AI transforms performance analytics, game strategy, and talent evaluation from video, coaching is fundamentally interpersonal—motivating athletes, building team culture, and making real-time physical-context decisions. Scouting retains the need for in-person evaluation of intangibles.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Coaches and scouts train athletes and evaluate talent. Their work is interpersonal leadership and observation with no physical labor for robots to automate.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Coaching involves interpersonal leadership, motivation, strategy, and real-time decision-making during competitions. While analytics and video technology assist, the human connection and leadership aspects are core. Minimal physical automation potential.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Coaching is about human motivation, strategic thinking, and interpersonal leadership. Physical demonstration is a minor component. The core value is human relationship, inspiration, and tactical judgment. Scouting involves observation and evaluation.
adoption_friction_rationale: Sports coaching involves deep human relationship, motivation, and mentorship. Strong cultural attachment to human coaches. Fragmented across youth sports, schools, and professional organizations. AI analytics tools are used for scouting but cannot replace interpersonal coaching dynamics.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Growing sports participation at all levels and expanding professional sports globally. AI analytics enhance coaching but don't replace the motivational and interpersonal aspects. Youth sports and fitness coaching have significant unmet demand.

title: Community health workers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Core work is interpersonal and community-based: conducting outreach, providing health education, connecting people with services, and advocating for underserved populations. Record-keeping and resource coordination have digital components, but the face-to-face community engagement dominates.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Connecting community members with health resources, providing education, and offering emotional support are deeply interpersonal duties. AI assists with resource databases and health information, but in-person community engagement is the core function.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates health education content creation, resource referral matching, and data tracking. However, the core value is interpersonal—building trust with underserved communities, providing culturally sensitive outreach, and connecting people to services through personal relationships.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Community health workers provide outreach and education in communities. Their work is interpersonal and educational with no physical labor for robots to automate.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Interpersonal outreach and health education work in community settings. Entirely about human connection, trust-building, and communication. No physical automation potential.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Work centers on community relationships, health education, and connecting people with services. Requires cultural competency, empathy, and trust-building. Minimal physical tasks; mostly interpersonal and cognitive.
adoption_friction_rationale: Role is fundamentally about human connection, cultural competency, and trust-building in underserved communities. Fragmented across nonprofits, clinics, and government programs. Low-resource employers with limited technology budgets. Strong social barriers to AI substitution in community outreach.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Enormous unmet need for community health outreach, particularly in underserved populations. AI tools can help workers cover more ground and identify at-risk individuals. The personal connection and trust-building aspects cannot be automated.

title: Compensation and benefits managers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Predominantly digital knowledge work: analyzing salary data, designing compensation structures, managing benefits programs, and ensuring regulatory compliance using HRIS systems. AI assists with market benchmarking, plan modeling, and compliance monitoring by 2028. Staff supervision and strategic decision-making remain human.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Compensation analysis, benefits benchmarking, compliance tracking, and report generation are heavily digital and automatable. Managers retain strategic decision-making and employee relations roles, but analytical workload shrinks dramatically.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Compensation benchmarking, benefits administration, compliance tracking, and market analysis are fully automated digital tasks. Human managers remain for strategic compensation philosophy decisions, executive negotiation, and navigating complex organizational politics around pay equity.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Compensation managers oversee pay and benefits programs. This is entirely administrative and strategic knowledge work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Office-based management work involving policy development and administration. Purely knowledge work.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Entirely office-based management and analytical work. No physical component for robotic automation.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large corporations are primary employers with resources to adopt HR tech. Work is increasingly data-driven and amenable to AI. Moderate regulatory complexity (ERISA, ACA, tax law) but this drives rather than hinders automation. Some judgment required for strategy.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Each organization needs limited compensation management regardless of AI speed. AI can automate benchmarking, analysis, and plan administration. The number of managers scales with organizations, not with task volume.

title: Compensation, benefits, and job analysis specialists
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Almost entirely screen-based: analyzing wage data, evaluating job descriptions, administering benefits programs, and preparing reports. AI significantly assists with salary benchmarking, job classification, and benefits analysis by 2028. Routine analytical tasks face meaningful automation pressure.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Job analysis, salary surveys, benefits administration, and classification work are routine digital tasks AI agents handle autonomously. Remaining human roles focus on complex policy interpretation and employee counseling.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Job analysis, salary surveys, benefits comparison, classification systems, and compliance documentation are structured digital tasks AI handles autonomously. Only novel organizational design questions and sensitive employee communications retain human involvement.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: These specialists analyze compensation data and job descriptions. Entirely desk-based analytical work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Analytical office work involving job analysis and compensation planning. No physical component.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Entirely analytical and administrative work. No physical component.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large employers and HR consulting firms dominate. Work is highly data-driven and amenable to AI tools. HRIS systems already automate much of the work. Regulatory compliance requirements (FLSA, ACA) actually drive adoption of automated systems.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Much of the analytical work (salary surveys, job classification, benefits administration) is highly automatable. Demand tied to the number of organizations, which is fixed. AI directly reduces the number of specialists needed per organization.

title: Compliance officers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Predominantly digital knowledge work: reviewing regulations, conducting audits, analyzing organizational practices, and preparing compliance reports. AI excels at monitoring regulatory changes, scanning documents for compliance issues, and generating reports by 2028. However, judgment in ambiguous situations and organizational advisory remain human.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Regulatory monitoring, document review, audit preparation, and compliance reporting are heavily digital. AI agents track regulations and flag issues autonomously. Human compliance officers focus on judgment calls, investigations, and organizational culture.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Regulatory monitoring, policy documentation, audit trail analysis, and compliance reporting are automated. Human officers remain for interpreting ambiguous regulations, managing relationships with regulators, handling whistleblower investigations, and exercising judgment in novel compliance gray areas.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Compliance officers ensure regulatory adherence through review and assessment. This is knowledge-based regulatory work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Regulatory review and oversight work that is entirely knowledge-based. Some facility inspections but the core is analytical.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Primarily analytical and investigative work reviewing records and procedures. Some facility inspections have minor physical components, but the core role is regulatory knowledge and judgment.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large corporations and financial institutions are primary employers. AI is already used for regulatory monitoring and compliance checking. Complex regulatory landscape (SEC, FINRA, HIPAA) creates both friction and incentive for automation. Human judgment still needed for interpretation.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Regulatory complexity continues to grow across industries. AI helps with monitoring but also creates new compliance domains (AI ethics, data privacy). Every company needs compliance regardless of size, and smaller firms have unmet compliance needs.

title: Computer and information research scientists
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Almost entirely digital: designing algorithms, conducting computing research, writing papers, and developing new technologies. AI accelerates experimentation, code writing, and literature review by 2028. However, novel research direction-setting and theoretical breakthroughs still require deep human expertise, providing some insulation at the senior level.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: AI agents assist with literature review, code generation, and experiment execution. However, novel research directions, theoretical breakthroughs, and creative problem formulation remain human. Productivity per researcher increases enormously.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates literature review, code implementation, experimental execution, and paper drafting. Human researchers remain for identifying genuinely novel research directions, cross-disciplinary insight, and theoretical breakthroughs. The occupation is restructured but the frontier research role persists.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Computer scientists conduct research in computing. Entirely knowledge-based technical work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Purely knowledge work involving research, algorithm development, and computational analysis. No physical component.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Purely cognitive research and computational work. No physical component whatsoever.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large tech companies and research institutions are primary employers with the most advanced AI capabilities. The field itself drives AI development. Some academic institutional inertia. Cutting-edge research still requires human creativity and insight.
demand_elasticity_rationale: AI research itself is a rapidly expanding field. Every breakthrough opens new research questions and applications. The demand for advancing computing capabilities is virtually unlimited as AI transforms every industry.

title: Computer and information systems managers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Predominantly digital: planning IT strategy, managing technology teams, overseeing system implementations, and coordinating budgets. AI assists with project tracking, capacity planning, and vendor evaluation by 2028. Leadership, cross-functional coordination, and strategic technology decisions remain human-driven.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Project planning, system monitoring, vendor management documentation, and reporting are heavily aided by AI. Managers shift to strategic technology decisions, stakeholder management, and organizational change leadership.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: IT planning, system monitoring, vendor evaluation, and technical documentation are automated. Human managers remain for organizational IT strategy, managing cross-functional stakeholder relationships, cybersecurity crisis response, and aligning technology with business objectives in ambiguous contexts.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: IT managers oversee technology operations and strategy. Managerial knowledge work with no physical component.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: IT management and strategic planning. Purely knowledge and management work.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Management and strategic planning role that is entirely cognitive. No physical labor component.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large corporations are primary employers with strong technology culture. Management role requires human judgment and leadership. AI tools for IT management are already widely adopted. Moderate friction from organizational change management and decision-making complexity.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Every organization needs IT management, and digital transformation keeps expanding IT's scope. AI creates new management challenges (AI governance, data strategy) even as it automates some operational tasks.

title: Computer hardware engineers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Significant digital work in circuit design, simulation, and testing using EDA tools, plus technical documentation. AI assists with design optimization and verification by 2028. Physical prototyping, lab testing, and manufacturing oversight provide meaningful non-digital components.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Circuit design, simulation, and testing documentation benefit from AI automation. However, physical prototyping, lab testing, and novel hardware architecture decisions require human expertise and hands-on work.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Circuit design, simulation, testing analysis, and documentation are automated. Human engineers remain for novel architecture decisions, physical prototyping, lab testing, and cross-domain integration challenges at the hardware-software interface.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Hardware engineers design computer components, with some prototype testing. The work is primarily design-focused knowledge work with minimal physical lab component.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Design work that is primarily knowledge-based. Some prototype testing and lab work, but the core role is design and analysis.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Primarily design work that is cognitive, with some physical prototyping and testing. By 2036, much hardware testing is automated, but novel prototype evaluation still has a human physical component. Core role is design and analysis.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large tech companies (Intel, AMD, Apple) are primary employers with resources and motivation to use AI in chip design. AI is already used for circuit design optimization. Physical prototyping and testing still require human oversight. Moderate regulatory requirements.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Exploding demand for AI chips, custom silicon, edge computing devices, and IoT hardware. AI design tools enable faster iteration but the demand for new hardware architectures and specialized processors is growing rapidly.

title: Computer network architects
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Predominantly digital: designing network topologies, evaluating hardware/software, analyzing data traffic, and planning implementations. AI assists with network optimization, security analysis, and capacity planning by 2028. However, strategic architecture decisions and cross-organizational coordination remain human-driven.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Network design, capacity planning, protocol configuration, and documentation are highly digital tasks AI agents handle effectively. Human architects focus on novel architectures, security strategy, and complex integration decisions.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Network design, capacity planning, security architecture, and documentation are highly automatable digital tasks. Human architects remain for novel enterprise-scale integration challenges, strategic technology decisions, and vendor relationship management.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Network architects design computer networks. Entirely knowledge-based technical work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Network design and planning work that is entirely knowledge-based and digital.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Entirely design and planning work for network systems. No physical labor component.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large tech companies, telecom firms, and enterprises are primary employers. Network design and optimization is highly amenable to AI. Existing technology culture facilitates adoption. Security concerns create some regulatory friction but also drive AI adoption for threat detection.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Growing cloud, edge computing, and IoT infrastructure needs. AI helps optimize network design but the proliferation of connected devices and services creates ever-expanding network complexity.

title: Computer programmers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Almost entirely screen-based: writing, testing, debugging, and maintaining code. AI coding agents by 2028 can autonomously handle routine coding tasks, translating specifications into working code. Active headcount reduction in pure coding roles as AI handles 50-70% of routine programming. Senior architecture and complex problem-solving remain human.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: By 2031, AI agents write, test, and debug well-specified code autonomously. Junior programming roles are largely automated. Remaining human programmers handle complex system integration, legacy codebases, and novel algorithmic challenges.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Pure code implementation from specifications is exactly the task AI excels at by 2036. The traditional programmer role—translating designs into code—has been fully automated. Remaining software roles are at the architecture, product, and strategy level, which are distinct occupations.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Programmers write and test code. Entirely desk-based knowledge work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Entirely digital work involving writing and testing code. No physical component.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Purely digital/cognitive work. No physical component whatsoever.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large tech companies and enterprises are primary employers with strong incentive to adopt AI coding tools. AI code generation is already widely used (Copilot, etc.). Clear ROI and existing tech culture. Minimal regulatory barriers. Market competition drives rapid adoption.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Massive latent demand for custom software. When programming becomes faster and cheaper, every small business, every process, and every device gets custom software. Historical pattern: every productivity gain in programming led to more software being built.

title: Computer support specialists
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Predominantly digital: troubleshooting software/hardware issues, maintaining networks, training users, and managing IT tickets. AI chatbots and diagnostic tools handle routine support queries by 2028. Some physical hardware maintenance provides insulation, but Tier 1 support faces significant automation.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Troubleshooting, ticket resolution, system configuration, and documentation are heavily digital tasks AI agents handle autonomously. Complex escalations and physical hardware issues still need humans, but routine IT support is largely automated.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Troubleshooting, ticket resolution, system configuration, and technical documentation are automated by AI agents. Human specialists remain for complex physical hardware issues, sensitive user situations, and novel problems that fall outside automated resolution patterns.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Some IT support involves physical hardware setup and troubleshooting, but the majority of support is remote/desk-based. Physical component is limited.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Mostly remote/desk-based troubleshooting. Some physical hardware setup and repair, but increasingly handled remotely. The physical component is minor.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Mix of remote and on-site support. On-site hardware troubleshooting has physical components. By 2036, remote diagnostics handle most issues, and physical hardware work is increasingly standardized. Some hands-on work in variable office environments remains.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large employers with IT help desk operations have clear ROI for AI chatbots and automated support. AI-powered support tools already widely deployed. Moderate employer fragmentation in MSP segment. Technical nature of work suits AI well. Labour shortages provide pull.
demand_elasticity_rationale: AI chatbots and automated diagnostics handle increasing portions of tier-1 support. The volume of support tickets grows with technology adoption but AI resolves more issues without human intervention.

title: Computer systems analysts
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Almost entirely digital: studying organizational systems, designing IT solutions, preparing specifications, and coordinating implementations. AI assists with requirements analysis, system modeling, and documentation by 2028. Routine systems analysis is highly automatable, with experienced analysts focusing on complex organizational change.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Requirements gathering documentation, system evaluation, workflow analysis, and implementation planning are highly digital and automatable. Human analysts focus on complex organizational needs assessment and stakeholder management.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Requirements gathering, system evaluation, workflow analysis, and implementation planning are structured analytical tasks AI handles end-to-end. The remaining human role is in navigating complex organizational politics, stakeholder management, and genuinely novel system integration challenges.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Systems analysts study computer systems and design solutions. Entirely knowledge-based analytical work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Analytical work designing and improving IT systems. Purely knowledge work.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Entirely analytical and consulting work. No physical component.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large corporations and consulting firms are primary employers with strong technology adoption culture. Work involves analysis and recommendation that AI tools can augment. Existing enterprise AI tool adoption facilitates integration. Moderate complexity of organizational change.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Every organization needs systems analysis for digital transformation. AI accelerates analysis but also creates new complexity to analyze. Growing demand for integrating AI systems into existing infrastructure.

title: Concierges
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: A mix of interpersonal service (greeting guests, handling personal requests) and digital tasks (making reservations, researching information, coordinating services). AI chatbots handle routine information requests by 2028, but the personalized, in-person service experience remains human-driven.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Information lookup, reservation making, and recommendation generation are tasks AI handles well. However, in-person hospitality, reading guest needs, and handling complex or unusual requests retain human value, especially in luxury settings.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI handles recommendation generation, booking, information lookup, and routine guest requests. However, the premium concierge role exists precisely for personal human connection, reading subtle social cues, and providing the warmth and discretion that luxury hospitality demands.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Concierges provide information and services to guests through interpersonal interaction. This is service-oriented communication work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Customer-facing service role requiring interpersonal skills, local knowledge, and problem-solving. Some tasks (information lookup, reservations) are digitized, but the personal service and human interaction aspects are central. Minimal physical labor.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Primarily interpersonal service providing recommendations and assistance. The human touch and personal relationship is central to the role. Minimal physical tasks; mostly communication and knowledge-based.
adoption_friction_rationale: Hotels and large venues employ concierges, with some chains already deploying AI concierge services. Strong guest preference for human interaction in luxury segment. Mix of large hotel chains (lower friction) and independent properties (higher friction). Service quality expectations vary by segment.
demand_elasticity_rationale: AI chatbots handle basic concierge queries, reducing demand for routine assistance. But high-end hospitality still values human concierges. Net roughly neutral as automation offsets some growth in travel and hospitality.

title: Conservation scientists and foresters
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Significant fieldwork: inspecting forests, monitoring land quality, and overseeing conservation activities. Data analysis, mapping, and report writing are digital components where AI assists by 2028. The blend of outdoor field work and office-based analysis places this at moderate exposure.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Fieldwork—assessing forests, managing land, and monitoring ecosystems—is physical. AI assists with data analysis, GIS mapping, and report generation, but outdoor site work and stakeholder engagement require human presence.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates land survey analysis, forest inventory modeling, environmental impact assessments, and management plan documentation.
