However, significant fieldwork—assessing terrain, evaluating ecosystems in person, and managing land use—requires physical presence and environmental judgment.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Conservation scientists conduct research and develop plans for land management. Their work is primarily knowledge-based with some fieldwork, but not physical labor exposed to robotic automation.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Research and management work primarily involving analysis and planning. Some fieldwork in natural environments, but the role is about scientific assessment and policy rather than physical labor.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Fieldwork in natural environments involves physical data collection and site assessment. By 2036, drones and sensors automate much monitoring, but working in unstructured natural environments for conservation assessment still requires human judgment and physical presence in novel terrain.
adoption_friction_rationale: Government agencies (USFS, BLM) and nonprofits are primary employers with limited budgets and institutional inertia. Fieldwork in remote locations requires physical presence. GIS and remote sensing tools are already adopted. Environmental policy requires human judgment and stakeholder engagement.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Climate change and biodiversity loss increase demand for conservation science. AI tools (satellite monitoring, species identification) enable more comprehensive environmental management. Growing public and regulatory interest in conservation.

title: Construction and building inspectors
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Core work requires physical site visits to inspect structures, verify code compliance, and assess building conditions. While report writing and code reference have digital components AI assists with, the essential on-site inspection and professional judgment require physical presence.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Physical site visits to inspect structures, verify code compliance, and assess safety are the core duties. AI helps with documentation, code lookup, and report generation, but on-site inspection remains hands-on.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates code compliance checking from plans and documentation. However, physical site inspection—examining structural integrity, verifying installations, identifying safety hazards in person—remains fundamentally human and is the core of the role.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Building inspectors visit diverse construction sites to evaluate compliance. Their work requires professional judgment in variable environments; drone-based inspection assists but doesn't replace the physical inspection role by 2028.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Field inspection work in variable construction environments. Each site and building is unique. While drones and sensors assist, physical access to inspect structural elements, electrical systems, and plumbing in diverse configurations still requires human presence and judgment.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Site inspections involve navigating variable construction environments and making safety/compliance judgments. By 2036, drones and robotic sensors assist with data collection, but the interpretive judgment in highly variable building conditions still requires human expertise. Physical access to varied sites remains challenging for robots.
adoption_friction_rationale: Government-employed inspectors face institutional inertia and union protections. Building code interpretation requires human judgment. Liability for missed violations is significant. Some AI-assisted inspection tools emerging but physical presence in varied conditions is essential. Regulatory framework assumes human inspectors.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Demand tied to the fixed number of construction projects and buildings requiring inspection. AI-assisted inspection tools (drones, image recognition) may increase inspector throughput, reducing headcount needed for the same inspection volume.

title: Construction equipment operators
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Almost entirely physical: operating heavy machinery like bulldozers, cranes, and excavators on construction sites. Equipment maintenance and GPS-guided operation are minor digital components. AI has negligible impact on the hands-on equipment operation that defines this role.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Operating excavators, cranes, and bulldozers on construction sites is entirely physical skilled work. AI-assisted equipment exists but full autonomy in varied construction environments is not achieved by 2031.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Operating heavy machinery on construction sites is entirely physical work. While GPS guidance and autonomous equipment represent physical automation, digital AI exposure per se is minimal, limited to equipment monitoring systems.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Heavy equipment operation on construction sites involves semi-structured tasks. Autonomous bulldozers and excavators are in pilot programs for grading and excavation, but complex site conditions limit widespread deployment by 2028.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Large-scale earthmoving and grading increasingly automated with GPS-guided autonomous equipment on structured sites. Excavation and routine operations on large commercial projects use autonomous or semi-autonomous machines. Complex operations in tight spaces or variable terrain still need human operators.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: By 2036, autonomous construction equipment handles most grading, excavation, and material moving on well-mapped sites. Human operators remain for genuinely novel terrain, urban environments with complex obstacles, and oversight of autonomous operations.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large construction companies and mining operations have resources to adopt autonomous equipment. GPS-guided and autonomous heavy equipment already exists (Caterpillar, Komatsu). Labour shortages in construction create strong pull. Union presence provides some friction. OSHA safety requirements are manageable.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Physical operation of heavy equipment on construction sites resists full automation due to variable terrain and conditions. Demand tied to construction activity. Semi-autonomous equipment may eventually reduce operators but adoption is slow.

title: Construction laborers and helpers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Entirely physical labor: cleaning work areas, loading materials, operating hand tools, and assisting skilled tradespeople. This is one of the most purely physical occupations with virtually no digital component that AI could affect by 2028.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Manual labor—carrying materials, digging, cleaning sites, and assisting tradespeople—is entirely physical with no meaningful digital component. AI has essentially zero impact on these tasks.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Construction labor is physically demanding manual work—carrying materials, digging, mixing concrete, and assisting skilled trades on job sites. Digital AI has essentially no exposure to this work.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Construction laborers perform diverse physical tasks across highly variable and unstructured job sites. While some material handling could theoretically be automated, the chaotic nature of construction limits robotic deployment by 2028.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Repetitive tasks on structured construction sites (material handling, site cleanup, concrete work) increasingly automated. However, the variety of tasks, changing environments, and need to work alongside human tradespeople in variable conditions means humans still needed for many tasks.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: General construction labor involves varied physical tasks in changing environments. By 2036, robots handle much material moving, concrete work, and repetitive tasks. But the high variability of construction sites and need for adaptive physical work means significant human involvement remains for site-specific challenges.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large commercial contractors can adopt automation, but work is in highly varied physical environments. Severe labour shortages create strong pull. Union presence in some markets. OSHA regulations manageable. Residential and small contractor segment is more fragmented.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Physical labor on construction sites is hard to automate due to unstructured environments. Demand tied to construction activity. Persistent labor shortages suggest demand currently exceeds supply.

title: Construction managers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: A mix of digital project management (budgeting, scheduling, contract administration, reporting) and physical site oversight. AI assists with cost estimation, schedule optimization, and document management by 2028. However, on-site supervision, contractor coordination, and safety management require significant physical presence.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Scheduling, budgeting, and documentation are aided by AI. However, on-site supervision, subcontractor coordination, safety management, and real-time problem solving on physical job sites require substantial human presence and judgment.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates scheduling, cost estimation, document management, and compliance tracking. However, construction management requires substantial on-site presence, managing subcontractor relationships, resolving physical construction problems, and navigating complex interpersonal dynamics with crews and clients.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Construction managers primarily plan, coordinate, and oversee projects. Their work is managerial and cognitive, with site visits but no physical labor component that robots would automate.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Management and coordination role. While overseeing increasingly automated job sites, the role itself is about planning, scheduling, problem-solving, and human coordination. Minimal physical labor.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Primarily management, planning, and coordination work. Site visits involve observation rather than physical labor. Core role is project management, budgeting, and team leadership—cognitive tasks.
adoption_friction_rationale: Mix of large contractors and small firms. Management role requires human judgment, coordination, and stakeholder management. AI project management tools are emerging. Licensing requirements in some states. Liability concerns for project outcomes create moderate friction.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Management of physical construction projects requires on-site presence and human judgment. AI tools help with scheduling and logistics but the number of managers scales with projects, not productivity.

title: Cooks
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Almost entirely physical work: preparing ingredients, cooking food, plating dishes, and maintaining kitchen cleanliness. POS system interaction is a negligible digital component. AI has minimal impact on the manual culinary tasks that define this role.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Preparing food, operating kitchen equipment, and maintaining cleanliness are entirely physical tasks. AI has negligible direct impact on cooking duties.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Cooking is hands-on physical work—preparing food, operating kitchen equipment, and managing a fast-paced physical environment. Digital AI exposure is negligible beyond recipe and inventory systems.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Cooks prepare food in commercial kitchens, a semi-structured environment. Fast-food chains are piloting robotic food prep for limited menu items by 2028, but full-service cooking with varied recipes remains largely manual.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Chain restaurant and institutional cooking increasingly automated with robotic kitchen systems handling standardized recipes. Fast-food preparation is highly automatable. However, varied menu items, special orders, and non-chain restaurants still require human cooks for adaptation and quality.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: By 2036, robotic cooking systems handle most restaurant and institutional food preparation for standard menu items. Human cooks remain for creative dishes, quality oversight, and adaptation to ingredient variability. High-volume, standardized cooking environments are largely automated.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large fast-food chains (McDonald's, Chipotle) can adopt kitchen automation at scale. Severe labour shortages provide strong pull. Independent restaurants are more fragmented. Food safety regulations manageable. Robotic cooking systems exist but kitchen environment variability creates moderate technical barriers.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Food service demand tied to population and dining habits. Physical cooking resists automation except in fast food. Delivery platforms expand demand modestly. AI has minimal direct impact on cooking labor.

title: Correctional officers and bailiffs
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Predominantly physical and interpersonal: supervising inmates, maintaining order, conducting searches, and responding to emergencies. Report writing and record-keeping have digital components, but the core security and supervision work requires constant physical presence.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Supervising inmates, maintaining order, and ensuring facility security are physical and interpersonal duties. AI assists with surveillance monitoring and record-keeping but cannot replace human presence in correctional environments.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Correctional work is fundamentally physical presence and interpersonal authority—maintaining order, supervising inmates, conducting searches, and responding to incidents. AI assists with monitoring and documentation but the core role requires human physical presence.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Correctional officers supervise inmates in secure but unpredictable environments requiring human judgment and physical intervention. The security and interpersonal aspects limit robotic deployment by 2028.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Security and supervision of inmates requires constant human judgment, de-escalation skills, and physical presence in unpredictable environments. Surveillance technology assists but the interpersonal and safety aspects require human officers. Trust and authority dynamics are inherently human.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Security work requiring human judgment, authority, and physical presence for inmate management. By 2036, surveillance is heavily automated, but the human authority, de-escalation skills, and physical intervention capability remain necessary. Regulatory and ethical requirements mandate human presence.
adoption_friction_rationale: Government employment with strong union protections (AFSCME, FOP). Public safety and constitutional requirements for humane treatment demand human presence. Liability for use of force and inmate safety. Deep institutional inertia in corrections. Some AI surveillance tools being adopted but officers cannot be replaced.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Demand tied to incarceration rates, which are policy-driven and have been trending down in some jurisdictions. Technology (surveillance cameras, electronic monitoring) can reduce the number of officers needed per facility.

title: Cost estimators
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Predominantly digital work: analyzing data, calculating material/labor/time costs, using estimation software, and preparing detailed reports. AI significantly enhances cost modeling, historical data analysis, and proposal generation by 2028. Some site visits for complex projects provide partial insulation.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Analyzing blueprints, calculating material/labor costs, and preparing bid documents are heavily digital tasks AI agents can automate. Human estimators handle complex project-specific variables and client negotiations, but routine estimation is largely automated.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Cost estimation from plans, specifications, and historical data is a structured digital analytical task that AI handles end-to-end. AI processes drawings, calculates material quantities, applies pricing databases, and generates detailed estimates. Only novel or highly complex projects retain human estimator involvement.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Cost estimators analyze data to estimate project costs. Desk-based analytical work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Analytical work involving project cost analysis and estimation. Primarily desk-based knowledge work. Some site visits but the core work is analytical.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Entirely analytical work involving calculations, project assessment, and financial modeling. No physical component.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large construction and manufacturing companies are primary employers. Work is highly quantitative and amenable to AI modeling. Historical data-driven estimation suits machine learning. Moderate employer fragmentation. Some professional judgment still required for complex projects.
demand_elasticity_rationale: AI can automate much of the data gathering and calculation in cost estimation. The number of projects requiring estimates is relatively fixed. Historical pattern: spreadsheets and databases reduced estimator headcount.

title: Court reporters and simultaneous captioners
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Almost entirely digital output: creating verbatim transcriptions using specialized equipment. AI speech-to-text technology by 2028 can produce highly accurate real-time transcriptions, directly threatening this role. Active displacement is occurring as automated transcription replaces routine proceedings.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Real-time transcription and captioning are tasks where AI speech-to-text systems reach near-human accuracy by 2031. Court reporters remain for high-stakes legal proceedings requiring certified accuracy, but demand shrinks dramatically.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Real-time speech-to-text transcription is a task AI performs with superhuman accuracy by 2036. The traditional court reporter role of verbatim transcription has been fully automated, though some jurisdictions may retain human oversight for legal proceedings.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Court reporters transcribe legal proceedings. Desk-based specialized transcription work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Transcription work that is increasingly digital. While physically present in courtrooms, the work is capturing spoken words, not physical labor.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Entirely transcription and recording work. No physical component relevant to robotics.
adoption_friction_rationale: AI transcription technology is advancing rapidly and already competitive with human accuracy. Large court systems and deposition firms have resources to adopt. Some state certification requirements and union presence create moderate friction. But economic pressure is strong.
demand_elasticity_rationale: AI speech-to-text technology directly replaces much of the transcription function. Real-time captioning is increasingly automated. Legal requirements for certified human reporters are the main barrier to faster displacement.

title: Craft and fine artists
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Core work is physical creation: painting, sculpting, ceramics, glassblowing, and other hands-on artistic techniques. While AI generates digital art, the physical craft process and unique artistic vision of fine artists remain distinctly human. Marketing and portfolio work have digital components.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Creating physical artworks—sculpture, painting, ceramics—is hands-on creative work. AI generates digital art but cannot replicate the physical craftsmanship and unique human expression valued in fine arts markets.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Fine art and craft involve physical creation—sculpting, painting, ceramics, glassblowing. While AI generates digital art, the value of handmade physical artwork and human artistic authorship preserves this role. Digital tools are supplementary rather than displacing.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Fine artists create artwork using physical materials and techniques. The creative, expressive nature of art-making is beyond robotic capability, though some tools may assist.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Artisanal creation involving unique creative vision and skilled handwork with novel materials and techniques. Each piece is unique. The creative and improvisational aspects are core. Audiences value human-made art. Very resistant to physical automation.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Artistic creation is fundamentally about human creative expression and aesthetic judgment with unique materials. The physical craft IS the art. By 2036, robotic tools may assist, but the creative vision and manual artistry remain inherently human.
adoption_friction_rationale: Highly individualized creative work where human authorship is central to value. Extremely fragmented self-employed base. Art market values human creativity and provenance. AI art controversy has heightened resistance. No meaningful employer structure to drive adoption.
demand_elasticity_rationale: AI-generated art creates controversy but also expands demand for human-verified authentic art. Growing art market and demand for unique, handcrafted work. Art therapy, custom commissions, and art education have latent demand.

title: Credit counselors
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: A blend of interpersonal counseling (advising clients on debt management, budgeting) and digital tasks (analyzing financial data, preparing repayment plans, processing applications). AI assists with financial analysis and plan generation by 2028, but the empathetic client relationship and personalized guidance remain human.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Financial analysis, debt management planning, and resource referrals are digital tasks AI handles well. However, counseling clients through financial distress requires empathy, motivational interviewing, and interpersonal trust that retain human value.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Financial analysis, debt management plan creation, budgeting, and credit report review are automated. However, credit counseling has a significant interpersonal component—motivating behavioral change, providing emotional support during financial stress, and building client trust—that retains some human roles.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Credit counselors advise people on financial matters. Interpersonal advisory work with no physical component.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Advisory and counseling work that is entirely interpersonal and knowledge-based. No physical component.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Entirely interpersonal counseling and financial advisory work. No physical component.
adoption_friction_rationale: Mix of nonprofit agencies and financial institutions. Role involves empathetic human interaction with financially distressed clients. State licensing in some jurisdictions. Moderate employer fragmentation. Some financial guidance can be automated but emotional support component resists substitution.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Significant unmet demand for financial counseling among consumers with debt problems. AI tools can help counselors serve more clients and provide better analysis, but the counseling relationship requires human trust and empathy.

title: Customer service representatives
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Predominantly screen-based: handling phone/chat/email inquiries, processing orders, resolving complaints, and updating account records. AI chatbots and virtual agents handle 50-70% of routine customer interactions by 2028. Active headcount reduction in basic customer service roles is underway.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Routine inquiries, account lookups, complaint processing, and information provision are overwhelmingly digital and automated by AI agents by 2031. Only complex escalations and emotionally sensitive situations require human representatives.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Routine customer inquiries, complaint handling, order processing, and account management are fully automated by AI agents by 2036. The traditional customer service representative role has ceased to exist, replaced by AI with human escalation only for the most complex or sensitive situations.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Customer service reps handle inquiries by phone and computer. Desk-based communication work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Office/call-center work involving communication and problem-solving. While increasingly handled by AI chatbots, the remaining human roles are entirely interpersonal, not physical.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Primarily communication-based work via phone, chat, or in-person. Physical component is negligible. Digital AI handles most automation, not physical robots.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large corporations are primary employers with massive economic incentive to automate. AI chatbots and virtual agents already widely deployed. Clear ROI. Minimal regulatory barriers. Some customer preference for humans in complex situations but basic inquiries are rapidly being automated.
demand_elasticity_rationale: AI chatbots and virtual assistants handle increasing volumes of routine customer inquiries. Companies aggressively adopt AI to reduce call center costs. Complex and emotional interactions persist but represent a shrinking share of total volume.

title: Dancers and choreographers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Core work is physical: performing, rehearsing, and creating dance routines through bodily movement. While choreographers may use video tools and AI-assisted composition software, the essential physical performance and creative embodiment cannot be digitized by 2028.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Dance performance is entirely physical and embodied. AI may assist choreographers with movement visualization or music selection, but creating and performing dance remains a human art form.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Dance is fundamentally embodied physical performance art. While AI can assist with music selection and movement visualization, the core product is human physical expression. Choreography retains more digital exposure through AI-assisted creation tools, but the art form is inherently physical.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Dancers perform artistic physical movement for entertainment. While physically demanding, this is creative performance art that robots cannot meaningfully replicate.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Performance art that is fundamentally about human physical expression and creativity. Audiences value human performers. While motion-capture exists, live dance is inherently human.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Dance is fundamentally human physical artistic expression. The entire value is human bodily movement and creative expression. Robots cannot substitute for human dancers in artistic performance.
adoption_friction_rationale: Performing arts are fundamentally about human physical expression and artistry. Audiences value human performance. Extremely fragmented employment across companies, studios, and freelance work. Union protections (AGMA). No meaningful economic incentive to automate human dance performance.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Live performance demand grows with entertainment spending. AI cannot replicate live dance performance. Growing interest in dance fitness, cultural events, and content creation expands opportunities.

title: Data scientists
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Almost entirely digital: collecting, analyzing, and modeling data using programming languages and statistical tools. AI significantly accelerates data cleaning, exploratory analysis, model building, and visualization by 2028. Routine data science tasks face strong automation, with experienced practitioners focusing on complex problem framing.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Data cleaning, feature engineering, model training, and report generation are heavily automated by AI agents. Senior data scientists focus on problem framing, novel methodology, and translating insights to business strategy, but junior analytical roles are largely displaced.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Data cleaning, exploratory analysis, model building, feature engineering, and routine insight generation are fully automated. Human data scientists remain for framing novel business questions, interpreting results in complex organizational contexts, and communicating findings to stakeholders.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Data scientists analyze data using statistical methods and programming. Entirely desk-based knowledge work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Purely digital analytical work involving data analysis, modeling, and programming. No physical component.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Purely computational and analytical work. No physical component whatsoever.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large tech companies and enterprises are primary employers with the most advanced AI tools. AutoML and AI-assisted analytics are already widely used. Strong technology culture facilitates adoption. Clear ROI. The field is inherently technology-forward with minimal regulatory barriers.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Every organization wants to be data-driven. AI tools make data science more productive, enabling analysis of more datasets and more complex questions. The volume of data and potential applications grows faster than efficiency gains reduce headcount.

title: Database administrators and architects
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Almost entirely screen-based: designing database systems, managing data storage, ensuring security, optimizing performance, and troubleshooting issues. AI assists with query optimization, capacity planning, and automated monitoring by 2028. Routine database administration faces significant automation pressure.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Database monitoring, query optimization, backup management, and routine administration are highly automatable by AI agents. Human DBAs focus on complex architecture decisions, security strategy, and migration planning.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Database management, query optimization, backup procedures, security configuration, and schema design are structured digital tasks AI handles autonomously. Human roles persist only for novel architecture decisions in complex enterprise environments and strategic data governance.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Database administrators manage and maintain data systems. Entirely desk-based technical work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Digital work managing and maintaining database systems. No physical component beyond occasional hardware interaction.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Entirely digital/technical work managing database systems. No physical component.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large enterprises are primary employers with strong incentive to automate database management. Cloud-managed databases and AI-powered administration tools already widely adopted. Clear ROI and existing technology culture. Minimal regulatory barriers beyond data privacy compliance.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Cloud databases and AI-managed infrastructure automate much routine database administration. The number of databases grows but automated management tools reduce the humans needed per database.

title: Delivery truck drivers and driver/sales workers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Core work is physical: driving delivery vehicles, loading/unloading packages, navigating routes, and interacting with customers. GPS and routing software are digital tools, but the fundamental task of physically driving and delivering packages requires human presence. Autonomous delivery vehicles remain limited by 2028.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Driving delivery vehicles, loading/unloading packages, and interacting with customers are physical tasks. Autonomous delivery vehicles remain limited in scope by 2031; most last-mile delivery still requires human drivers.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Driving and package delivery are physical tasks. While route optimization is digitally automated, the core work of operating vehicles and physically delivering packages has minimal digital AI exposure. Autonomous delivery represents physical automation, not digital AI exposure.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Delivery driving involves navigating varied urban/suburban routes and physically handling packages at diverse delivery points. Autonomous last-mile delivery is in early pilots but the physical delivery component in unstructured environments limits exposure.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Autonomous delivery vehicles operational on many urban and highway routes by 2031. Last-mile delivery robots handling some residential deliveries. However, complex delivery scenarios (inside buildings, rural areas, customer interaction) still require human drivers. Driver-sales roles have an interpersonal component that resists automation.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: By 2036, autonomous delivery vehicles handle most mapped-route deliveries. Last-mile delivery robots are widespread. Human drivers remain for unmapped areas, customer interaction for sales, and genuinely novel delivery scenarios. The vast majority of routine delivery is automated.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large logistics companies (UPS, FedEx, Amazon) have resources for autonomous vehicles. Last-mile delivery faces more complexity than highway driving. DOT regulations will need updating. Labour shortages provide pull. Mix of large fleets (lower friction) and small operators (higher friction).
demand_elasticity_rationale: Autonomous delivery vehicles and drones threaten this role long-term. E-commerce growth increases delivery demand but automation will eventually reduce driver headcount. Last-mile delivery may resist automation longer.

title: Dental and ophthalmic laboratory technicians and medical appliance technicians
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Primarily hands-on manufacturing work: creating dentures, eyeglasses, prosthetics using specialized tools and materials. CAD/CAM technology and 3D printing are increasingly used, with AI assisting design, but manual craftsmanship and fitting remain essential.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Fabricating dental prosthetics, eyeglass lenses, and medical devices involves precision manual work. AI aids with CAD/CAM design, but hands-on fabrication, finishing, and quality inspection remain human tasks.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates design from digital impressions and specifications, but the physical fabrication of dental prosthetics, eyewear, and medical devices—grinding, polishing, molding, and fitting—remains hands-on skilled work.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Lab technicians fabricate dental appliances and medical devices in structured workshop environments. CAD/CAM and automated milling are increasingly deployed for dental prosthetics by 2028.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Dental and ophthalmic lab work increasingly automated with CAD/CAM systems, 3D printing, and robotic milling for standardized prosthetics and lenses. Custom and complex cases still need human technicians, but the majority of standard production is highly automated.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: By 2036, manufacturing of dental prosthetics, lenses, and medical appliances is highly automated with precision robotics and 3D printing. Custom fitting and adjustment work retains some human involvement, but production is largely robotic.
adoption_friction_rationale: Mix of large dental labs and small independent operations. CAD/CAM and 3D printing already transforming the field. FDA regulations for medical devices create moderate friction. Physical precision work increasingly automated. Some labour shortages provide pull.
demand_elasticity_rationale: 3D printing and digital manufacturing automate much of the fabrication work. CAD/CAM systems already reduce the labor per unit. Demand for dental/optical devices grows with population but production headcount shrinks.

title: Dental assistants
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Core work is clinical and hands-on: preparing patients, handing instruments to dentists, taking X-rays, and sterilizing equipment. Record-keeping and appointment scheduling have digital components, but the chairside clinical work dominates the role.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Chairside assistance during dental procedures, sterilizing instruments, and preparing patients are hands-on clinical tasks. AI helps with scheduling and records, but physical patient care is the core function.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Dental assisting is primarily physical chairside work—preparing instruments, assisting during procedures, taking X-rays, and sterilizing equipment. AI automates scheduling and records management, but the hands-on clinical support role remains human.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Dental assistants support dentists with instruments and patient care in variable clinical situations. The role requires quick responsiveness and varied manual tasks that are beyond 2028 robotic capabilities.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Patient-facing work requiring trust, communication, and assisting dentists in variable clinical situations. Each patient's mouth is different. Chairside assistance requires real-time adaptation. Some sterilization and prep tasks automatable but direct patient care resists automation.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Patient-facing clinical support involving handing instruments, suctioning, and patient comfort during procedures. By 2036, robotic assistance handles some routine tasks, but the patient interaction, adaptive support during variable procedures, and human comfort provision require continued human presence.
adoption_friction_rationale: State licensing requirements and dental board regulations. Mix of large dental chains and independent practices. Chairside assistance requires physical presence and dexterity. Patient comfort expectations favor human interaction. Moderate liability concerns in healthcare setting.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Demand tied to dental patient volume. AI may improve scheduling and imaging analysis, but the hands-on chairside assistance role persists. Growing dental care access may offset any efficiency gains.

title: Dental hygienists
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Predominantly physical patient care: cleaning teeth, examining patients for oral diseases, applying preventive treatments, and educating patients. Digital charting and X-ray systems are tools used, but the core hands-on clinical work cannot be automated by AI.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Cleaning teeth, taking X-rays, and providing oral health education are hands-on clinical duties. AI assists with patient records and diagnostic imaging interpretation, but the physical clinical work limits digital exposure.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Dental hygiene involves hands-on clinical procedures—cleaning teeth, applying sealants, taking X-rays, and examining patients' mouths. AI assists with patient education and record-keeping, but the physical clinical work remains human-performed.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Dental hygienists perform cleaning and examination procedures requiring skilled dexterity in a patient's mouth. The intimate patient contact and variable oral conditions limit robotic deployment by 2028.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Hands-on clinical work in patients' mouths requiring skilled dexterity, patient communication, and real-time adaptation. Each patient's oral anatomy differs. Trust and comfort are essential. While some cleaning tools become more automated, the core work requires human touch and judgment.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Hands-on cleaning and examination inside patients' mouths requires dexterity and patient interaction. By 2036, robotic cleaning tools may assist, but the intimate oral care, patient communication, and adaptive clinical judgment in variable oral conditions keep significant human involvement.
adoption_friction_rationale: State licensing and scope-of-practice regulations. Most employed by small dental practices with limited capital. Physical oral manipulation requires exceptional dexterity. Patient preference for human touch. Professional associations protect scope. Liability concerns in healthcare.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Demand tied to patient volume and preventive care visits. The hands-on cleaning and assessment work resists automation. Aging population and growing preventive care focus support stable demand.

title: Dentists
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Core work is clinical: examining patients, diagnosing conditions, performing procedures, and providing treatment. Digital imaging and AI-assisted diagnostics help with treatment planning, but the hands-on surgical and procedural work, patient communication, and clinical judgment dominate.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Dental procedures—fillings, extractions, examinations—are hands-on clinical work. AI aids with diagnostic imaging, treatment planning, and records, but the physical practice of dentistry and patient interaction remain firmly human.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates diagnostic imaging interpretation, treatment planning, and administrative tasks. However, dental procedures are inherently physical—drilling, filling, extracting, and performing oral surgery require manual dexterity and in-person patient care. The patient relationship also retains human value.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Dentists perform precise manual procedures in patients' mouths requiring fine dexterity and clinical judgment. The variable patient anatomy and need for real-time clinical decisions limit robotic replacement by 2028.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Complex clinical procedures in highly variable oral environments. Each patient presents unique anatomy and pathology. Robotic dental systems emerging for some standardized procedures, but the diagnostic judgment, patient communication, and procedural adaptation still require human dentists.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Complex oral procedures requiring fine dexterity, patient relationship, and clinical judgment. By 2036, robotic systems assist with standardized procedures, but complex restorative work, diagnosis of novel conditions, and patient management remain human-centered. Regulatory requirements also mandate human oversight.
adoption_friction_rationale: Heavy state licensing and regulation. Majority in small independent or group practices. Physical manipulation inside the oral cavity requires extreme precision and patient trust. Malpractice liability framework assumes human practitioners. Strong professional association resistance. Patient preference for human dentists.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Significant unmet dental care need globally. AI diagnostics and robotic assistance could enable dentists to see more patients. Lower-cost dental care unlocks demand from underserved populations.

title: Desktop publishers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Almost entirely screen-based: using design software to create page layouts for print and digital media. AI tools by 2028 can automate template-based layout, typography selection, and image placement. This role faces active displacement as AI handles most production-level desktop publishing tasks.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Layout design, formatting, and document production are entirely digital tasks that AI handles with high quality by 2031. Remaining human roles focus on creative direction and complex brand-specific formatting requirements.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Layout design, formatting, and document preparation from provided content are entirely digital tasks that AI handles end-to-end. This occupation has effectively ceased to exist in its traditional form, absorbed by AI-powered publishing tools.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Desktop publishers format text and graphics for publication. Desk-based design work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Entirely digital design and layout work. No physical component.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Entirely digital design and layout work. No physical component.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large media and publishing companies are primary employers. AI layout and design tools already widely available. Work is entirely digital and amenable to automation. Clear ROI. Minimal regulatory barriers. Field is already shrinking due to automation and template-based tools.
demand_elasticity_rationale: AI design tools and templates largely automate page layout and desktop publishing. The role has already shrunk significantly as software improved. Remaining work is absorbed by graphic designers and content creators.

title: Diagnostic medical sonographers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Core work is hands-on: operating ultrasound equipment on patients, positioning transducers, and acquiring diagnostic images. While AI assists with image interpretation by 2028, the physical patient interaction, equipment manipulation, and real-time image acquisition require skilled human operators.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Operating ultrasound equipment requires physical patient interaction and transducer manipulation. AI significantly aids image interpretation and reporting, but the hands-on scanning process and patient communication remain human tasks.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates image interpretation and reporting. However, performing ultrasound examinations requires physical transducer manipulation, real-time adjustment based on patient anatomy, and patient interaction—skills that retain the human role despite automated analysis.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Sonographers operate ultrasound equipment requiring skilled probe manipulation adapted to each patient. While AI aids image interpretation, the physical scanning technique requires adaptive human touch.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Patient-facing imaging work requiring physical manipulation of transducers on patients. Each scan requires real-time adaptation to patient anatomy and pathology. AI assists interpretation but the physical scanning and patient positioning still need human operators who can communicate with patients.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Operating ultrasound equipment requires physical manipulation of the probe on patients with varied body types. By 2036, automated scanning assists, but adaptive probe positioning and real-time diagnostic interpretation during scanning still requires human skill and patient interaction.
adoption_friction_rationale: Hospital systems are large employers with resources. AI-assisted ultrasound interpretation is advancing. State licensing and healthcare regulations create moderate friction. Physical scanning requires operator skill and patient interaction. FDA approval needed for AI diagnostic tools.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Demand tied to patient volume and imaging orders. AI assists with image interpretation but a human operator must physically perform the scan. Aging population increases imaging demand while AI improves throughput.

title: Diesel service technicians and mechanics
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Core work is hands-on: inspecting, repairing, and overhauling diesel engines using diagnostic equipment and hand tools. Computerized diagnostics aid troubleshooting, but the physical repair, parts replacement, and mechanical work dominate. AI assists with technical manual lookup but cannot perform repairs.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Diagnosing and repairing diesel engines and heavy equipment is hands-on mechanical work. AI aids with diagnostic codes and parts identification, but physical repair remains entirely human.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Diesel repair is hands-on mechanical work—diagnosing engine problems, replacing parts, and performing maintenance on heavy vehicles. AI assists with diagnostics, but the physical repair work in garages and on roadsides remains human.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Diesel mechanics maintain and repair large engines and vehicles with varied issues. The diagnostic complexity and variable physical access requirements limit robotic deployment by 2028.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Heavy equipment and truck repair in variable conditions. Each vehicle and problem is different. Working on large diesel engines requires significant physical effort and skilled diagnosis. While some diagnostic tools are automated, the physical repair work in diverse configurations resists automation.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Heavy vehicle repair involves physical work in variable conditions. By 2036, robots handle many standardized maintenance procedures, but diagnosing complex problems on diverse diesel equipment and working in field conditions still requires significant human involvement.
adoption_friction_rationale: Mix of large fleet maintenance operations and independent shops. Physical repair in varied conditions requires dexterity. ASE certification and EPA emissions regulations. Labour shortages in diesel mechanics provide some pull. Heavy equipment infrastructure not ready for robotic repair.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Diesel equipment requires ongoing physical maintenance. Transition to electric vehicles is slower for heavy-duty applications. Demand tied to the fleet of diesel vehicles, which remains large in the medium term.

title: Dietitians and nutritionists
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: A mix of interpersonal counseling (meeting patients, conducting assessments) and digital knowledge work (meal planning, nutritional analysis, report writing). AI assists with dietary analysis, meal plan generation, and research by 2028, but personalized patient counseling and clinical assessment remain human-driven.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Meal planning, nutritional analysis, and dietary recommendations are tasks AI handles well. However, patient counseling, motivational interviewing, and adapting plans to complex medical conditions require human judgment and interpersonal skills.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI generates personalized meal plans, analyzes nutritional data, and produces dietary recommendations from health data. However, patient counseling, motivational interviewing for behavioral change, and working with complex medical cases requiring interpersonal sensitivity retain human dietitians.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Dietitians develop nutrition programs and counsel patients. Their work is knowledge-based and interpersonal with no physical labor component.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Advisory and counseling work about nutrition and diet. Entirely knowledge and interpersonal work with no physical component.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Primarily counseling and analytical work involving meal planning and health education. No meaningful physical component for robotic automation.
adoption_friction_rationale: State licensing and healthcare regulation. Mix of hospital employment (larger) and private practice (fragmented). Patient counseling involves empathy and behavioral change support. Insurance billing requirements. AI nutrition tools exist but clinical practice has regulatory requirements.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Enormous unmet demand for personalized nutrition counseling. Most people would benefit from dietary guidance but can't afford it. AI tools enable dietitians to create more personalized plans and serve more clients at lower cost.

title: Drafters
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Almost entirely screen-based: converting designs into technical drawings using CAD software. AI-assisted design tools by 2028 can automate much of routine drafting, including generating standard components and checking compliance. Active headcount pressure in production drafting roles.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Technical drawing, CAD operations, and specification documentation are heavily digital tasks AI agents automate by 2031. AI generates construction drawings from design parameters; human drafters handle complex revisions and quality review.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Technical drawing, CAD work, and producing construction documents from engineer specifications are structured digital tasks AI handles autonomously by 2036. The traditional drafter role is largely automated, with remaining work folded into engineering positions.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Drafters create technical drawings using CAD software. Desk-based technical work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Entirely digital design work using CAD software. No physical component.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Entirely CAD and digital design work. No physical component.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large engineering and architecture firms are primary employers. CAD work is already heavily computerized and AI-assisted design is advancing rapidly. Clear ROI for automation. Minimal regulatory barriers for the drafting function itself. Generative design tools already in market.
demand_elasticity_rationale: CAD software and AI-assisted design tools increasingly automate drafting tasks. AI can generate initial drafts from specifications. The role has already contracted as software improved; further AI gains continue this trend.

title: Drywall installers, ceiling tile installers, and tapers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Entirely physical work: hanging wallboard, installing ceiling tiles, applying tape and joint compound, and sanding surfaces. This is one of the most purely manual trades with no meaningful digital component that AI could affect by 2028.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Installing drywall, applying tape and compound, and finishing surfaces are entirely physical construction tasks with no meaningful digital component.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: This is entirely physical skilled trade work—hanging drywall, taping joints, applying compound, and installing ceiling tiles. Digital AI has essentially no exposure to this occupation.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Drywall installation involves physical labor in variable building interiors. Construction robotics for drywall finishing are in very early development; the varied environments make deployment impractical by 2028.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Some large commercial drywall installation is becoming automated for uniform walls and ceilings. However, residential work, custom installations, corners, and finishing/taping require human skill and adaptation to each building's unique characteristics.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: By 2036, robotic systems handle much standardized drywall installation in new construction with uniform layouts. However, renovation work, complex ceiling configurations, and finishing/taping in variable conditions still require human skill. Significant automation of routine installation.
adoption_friction_rationale: Highly fragmented between commercial contractors and independent tradespeople. Physical work in varied building interiors. Union presence in some markets. Limited capital among small operators. Construction site conditions challenge robotics. Labour shortages provide moderate pull but infrastructure not ready.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Physical installation work on construction sites resists automation. Demand tied to construction activity. Labor shortages suggest current demand exceeds supply. AI has minimal direct impact on this manual trade.

title: Economists
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Almost entirely digital: conducting statistical analysis, building economic models, writing research reports, and evaluating policy impacts. AI significantly accelerates data analysis, forecasting, and report drafting by 2028. Routine economic analysis faces strong automation, with senior economists focusing on novel research and policy judgment.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Data analysis, econometric modeling, literature synthesis, and report writing are heavily digital and aided by AI agents. Economists retain value in novel theoretical frameworks, policy interpretation, and strategic advisory, but research productivity increases dramatically.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Data analysis, econometric modeling, forecasting, literature review, and report writing are automated. Human economists remain for novel theoretical frameworks, interpreting results in complex policy contexts, advising decision-makers on ambiguous trade-offs, and public communication of economic concepts.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Economists study economic data and develop forecasts. Entirely analytical knowledge work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Purely analytical and research work. No physical component.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Entirely analytical and research work. No physical component whatsoever.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large institutions (government, banks, consulting firms) are primary employers with resources to adopt AI. Economic modeling and data analysis are highly amenable to AI. Academic institutional inertia for university economists. Some judgment and communication skills still valued.
demand_elasticity_rationale: AI tools enable more sophisticated economic modeling and analysis. Growing demand for economic analysis in policy, business strategy, and technology assessment. Every organization could benefit from economic analysis if it were cheaper.

title: Editors
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Almost entirely screen-based: reviewing text, correcting errors, verifying facts, and managing content workflows. AI writing and editing tools by 2028 handle much of routine copyediting and proofreading. Active headcount reduction in editorial departments as AI assists with content review and revision.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Reviewing, revising, and planning content are entirely digital tasks. AI agents produce polished drafts, perform copyediting, and check facts autonomously by 2031. Senior editors retain creative vision and editorial judgment roles, but team sizes shrink dramatically.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Copy editing, fact-checking, formatting, and routine content editing are fully automated. Human editors remain for high-level editorial vision, managing creative relationships with authors, and making judgment calls about tone and audience in prestigious or sensitive publications.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Editors review and revise written content. Desk-based knowledge work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Knowledge work involving reviewing and improving written content. Entirely digital/desk-based.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Entirely cognitive work involving reading, writing, and editorial judgment. No physical component.
adoption_friction_rationale: Mix of large media companies and freelance/small publisher base. AI editing and proofreading tools already widely used. Content quality judgment still valued. Moderate employer fragmentation. Clear ROI for large publishers. Creative editorial judgment creates moderate social friction.
demand_elasticity_rationale: AI generates vastly more content requiring human editorial judgment. While AI automates basic proofreading, the explosion of AI-generated content creates new demand for human editors to ensure quality, accuracy, and voice.

title: Electrical and electronic engineering technologists and technicians
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: A blend of physical work (building prototypes, testing equipment, calibrating instruments) and digital tasks (using CAD, analyzing test data, maintaining records). AI assists with data analysis and design documentation, but hands-on equipment testing and prototyping remain central.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Building, testing, and repairing electrical components involves significant hands-on work. AI assists with circuit simulation and documentation, but physical assembly, testing, and troubleshooting of hardware remain human tasks.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates circuit analysis, testing data interpretation, and documentation. However, the core work involves physical hands-on tasks—building prototypes, testing circuits, calibrating equipment, and troubleshooting hardware in labs and manufacturing floors.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: EE technicians build, test, and repair electronic equipment in labs and factories. The physical component involves hands-on work in somewhat structured environments, but varied equipment limits automation.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Hands-on testing and repair of electrical/electronic systems in variable configurations. Each system and problem differs. While automated testing equipment handles routine checks, troubleshooting and repair in diverse environments requires human technicians.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Hands-on testing, building prototypes, and troubleshooting electronic equipment. By 2036, routine testing is automated, but working with novel prototypes and diagnosing complex faults in variable equipment still requires human dexterity and judgment.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large manufacturers and utilities are primary employers with resources to adopt. Testing and diagnostic work increasingly automated. Moderate regulatory requirements. Physical lab and field work requires some manual presence. Existing technology culture facilitates adoption.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Demand tied to manufacturing and R&D activity. Physical testing and prototype work persists. The volume of electronic products grows but automation improves throughput per technician.

title: Electrical and electronics engineers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Predominantly digital: designing circuits and systems using EDA software, running simulations, analyzing test data, and writing specifications. AI copilots significantly assist with design optimization and documentation by 2028. Physical prototyping and testing provide some non-digital balance.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Circuit design, simulation, analysis, and documentation are heavily digital tasks where AI generates designs and optimizes parameters. Engineers focus on novel architectures, safety-critical validation, and physical prototyping oversight.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Circuit design, simulation, analysis, and documentation are automated. Human engineers remain for novel system architecture, physical prototyping and testing, cross-domain integration challenges, and managing the interface between digital design and physical manufacturing.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Electrical engineers design electrical systems. Primarily knowledge-based engineering work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Design and engineering work that is primarily knowledge-based and computational.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Primarily design and analysis work that is cognitive. Minor hands-on prototyping component. Core role is engineering problem-solving.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large tech companies and manufacturers are primary employers. AI-assisted circuit design and simulation already widespread. Professional licensing in some roles. Moderate regulatory requirements. Existing technology culture facilitates adoption. Physical prototyping still requires presence.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Exploding demand for electronics in EVs, IoT, renewable energy, and AI hardware. AI design tools enable faster iteration but the applications for electrical engineering keep expanding into new domains.

title: Electrical and electronics installers and repairers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Primarily hands-on work: installing, maintaining, and repairing electrical equipment in transportation and industrial settings. Using diagnostic instruments and reading technical manuals have digital components, but the physical installation and repair work dominates.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Installing and repairing electrical equipment is hands-on physical work. AI aids diagnostics, but the manual installation, wiring, and repair tasks remain firmly human.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: This is hands-on physical work—installing, maintaining, and repairing electrical equipment. AI assists with diagnostics and troubleshooting guides, but the physical installation and repair work remains human-performed.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Electrical/electronics repair involves troubleshooting and fixing varied equipment in different settings. The diagnostic complexity and variable environments limit robotic replacement by 2028.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Installation and repair of electrical equipment in commercial/industrial settings. Some standardized installations are becoming more automated, but the variety of equipment, settings, and fault conditions requires human adaptability. More structured than residential work.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Installation and repair work in variable environments. By 2036, robots handle standardized installations, but troubleshooting complex electrical systems in diverse settings (industrial, commercial) still requires human diagnostic skill and adaptive physical work.
adoption_friction_rationale: Mix of large utilities and manufacturers (lower friction) and smaller contractors. Physical installation and repair in varied environments. Licensing and safety regulations (NEC, OSHA). Some labour shortages provide pull. Equipment diversity challenges standardized robotic solutions.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Physical installation and repair work resists automation. Demand tied to the installed base of electrical equipment, which grows steadily. AI diagnostics help but hands-on work persists.

title: Electrical power-line installers and repairers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Almost entirely physical outdoor work: climbing utility poles, stringing cables, repairing power lines, and erecting transmission towers. This is dangerous physical labor with virtually no digital component that AI could meaningfully affect by 2028.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Climbing poles, stringing lines, and repairing electrical infrastructure in outdoor environments is dangerous physical work with essentially no digital AI substitution.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Line work is physically demanding outdoor labor—climbing poles, stringing wire, and repairing power lines often in dangerous weather conditions. Digital AI has essentially no exposure to this occupation beyond outage mapping systems.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Power-line workers perform dangerous work at heights on utility poles and towers in variable outdoor environments. The hazardous, unpredictable conditions are well beyond current robotic capabilities.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Outdoor work on utility lines in highly variable environments—poles, trenches, weather conditions. Each installation and repair scenario is different. Working at heights and in adverse conditions requires human judgment and dexterity. Drones assist inspection but physical line work remains human.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Working on power lines involves climbing poles, working at heights, and navigating outdoor environments in all conditions. By 2036, drones and climbing robots assist significantly, but the variability of outdoor conditions, emergency repair scenarios, and working on energized systems still requires substantial human involvement.
adoption_friction_rationale: Utility companies are large employers but work involves climbing poles and towers in varied outdoor conditions. Strong union presence (IBEW). Safety regulations are stringent. Physical environment is extremely challenging for robotics. Labour shortages provide some pull but infrastructure not adaptable.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Physical utility line work in varied outdoor environments strongly resists automation. Demand tied to grid expansion and maintenance needs. Growing electrification and renewable energy infrastructure increase demand.

title: Electricians
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Predominantly hands-on skilled trade work: installing wiring, outlets, circuit breakers, and maintaining electrical systems. Blueprint reading and code compliance have digital aspects, but the physical electrical work in buildings and factories dominates. AI assists with code lookup but cannot perform installations.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Wiring buildings, installing fixtures, and troubleshooting electrical systems are hands-on skilled trades. AI assists with code lookup and project planning, but physical electrical work remains human.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Electrical work is hands-on skilled trade work—running wire, installing fixtures, troubleshooting circuits in buildings and construction sites. AI assists with code lookup and load calculations, but the core physical work remains entirely human.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Electricians perform skilled wiring and installation in variable residential and commercial buildings. Fine dexterity in unpredictable environments with different building layouts makes robotic replacement infeasible by 2028.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Residential and commercial electrical work in highly variable environments. Each building has unique wiring configurations and challenges. Troubleshooting requires creative problem-solving. While some standardized commercial installations see automation, the variety of work resists full automation.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Residential and commercial electrical work involves highly variable environments—every building is different. By 2036, robots handle standardized new-construction wiring, but renovation work, troubleshooting in existing buildings, and adapting to unique configurations require significant human judgment and dexterity.
adoption_friction_rationale: Highly fragmented between commercial (larger contractors) and residential (many independents). NEC code compliance requires human judgment in varied conditions. State licensing requirements. Strong union presence (IBEW). Labour shortages provide pull but physical work environment resists robotics.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Growing demand from electrification, EV charging infrastructure, solar installations, and smart building technology. Physical wiring work in variable environments resists automation. Persistent labor shortages indicate unmet demand.

title: Electro-mechanical and mechatronics technologists and technicians
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Core work involves operating, testing, and maintaining automated and robotic equipment—a blend of physical hands-on work and digital monitoring. AI assists with diagnostics and programming, but physical equipment maintenance and troubleshooting remain central.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Operating, testing, and maintaining electro-mechanical equipment involves hands-on work with physical systems. AI aids with diagnostics and documentation, but manual technical work predominates.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates testing data analysis and documentation. However, the role centers on physical work—assembling, testing, and maintaining electromechanical devices and automated manufacturing systems, requiring hands-on skills.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Electro-mechanical technicians test and maintain automated equipment in structured industrial environments. Their work involves hands-on calibration and repair in controlled settings with moderate automation potential.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Testing and maintenance of electromechanical equipment. Routine testing and calibration increasingly automated. However, troubleshooting and repair of diverse systems in various settings still requires human technicians. A mix of automated and human work.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Testing and maintaining electro-mechanical equipment. By 2036, routine maintenance and testing procedures are automated, but troubleshooting complex integrated systems in variable industrial environments retains human involvement for novel fault diagnosis.
adoption_friction_rationale: Manufacturing and industrial employers have resources to adopt. Work bridges electrical and mechanical systems with some automation already. Moderate regulatory requirements. Existing technology culture in manufacturing. Physical repair and assembly work requires manual presence.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Demand tied to manufacturing and automation equipment maintenance. As factories add more robots and automated systems, there's growing need for technicians to maintain them, roughly offsetting efficiency gains.

title: Elementary, middle, and high school principals
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: A mix of interpersonal leadership (managing staff, student discipline, parent relations) and digital administrative work (budgeting, scheduling, reporting, curriculum oversight). AI assists with data analysis and administrative tasks by 2028, but the human leadership, community engagement, and judgment calls remain essential.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Administrative tasks—scheduling, budgeting, compliance reporting, data analysis—are heavily automated by AI. Principals retain essential roles in school culture, community relations, staff leadership, and complex disciplinary decisions.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates administrative tasks like scheduling, budgeting, data analysis, compliance reporting, and communication drafting. However, school leadership is fundamentally interpersonal—building school culture, managing staff, engaging parents, handling disciplinary situations, and community relations.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Education administrators perform management, planning, and coordination. Their work is entirely administrative and cognitive with no physical labor component.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: School leadership and management work that is entirely administrative, interpersonal, and knowledge-based. No physical component.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Management and leadership role involving strategic planning, staff management, and community relations. Entirely cognitive and interpersonal. No physical labor component.
adoption_friction_rationale: Government-employed educational administrators with deep institutional inertia. Role requires human leadership, community engagement, and crisis management. Union relationships and school board politics require human navigation. Strong social expectation of human school leadership.
demand_elasticity_rationale: School leadership positions scale with the number of schools, which is relatively fixed. AI may help principals with administrative tasks but doesn't change the fundamental need for one leader per school.

title: Elevator and escalator installers and repairers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Almost entirely physical skilled trade work: installing elevator components, troubleshooting mechanical systems, and performing maintenance in confined spaces. Blueprint reading and diagnostic tools are minor digital components. AI has negligible impact on this hands-on trade.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Installing and maintaining elevators and escalators is skilled physical work in building shafts and mechanical rooms. AI has minimal impact on these hands-on tasks.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Installing and repairing elevators is physically demanding, highly specialized mechanical work. AI assists with diagnostics and maintenance scheduling, but the hands-on installation, repair, and safety testing remain human-performed.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Elevator installation and repair involves complex mechanical work in confined, variable building shafts. The highly specialized manual tasks in unpredictable environments are beyond robotic capabilities by 2028.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Specialized installation and repair in confined, variable environments. Each building and elevator system presents unique challenges. Safety-critical work requiring skilled mechanical and electrical expertise. The variability of installations and safety requirements limit automation.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Specialized work in confined, vertical spaces with safety-critical requirements. By 2036, standardized installations benefit from robotic assistance, but the variability of building shafts, retrofitting older buildings, and safety-critical troubleshooting still require significant human skill.
adoption_friction_rationale: Specialized trade with strong union (IUEC) and strict safety regulations. Work in confined, vertical spaces is challenging for robotics. State licensing requirements. Moderate employer consolidation (major elevator companies) but installation conditions vary greatly. Safety liability is high.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Demand tied to the number of elevators in buildings, which grows with construction. Physical installation and maintenance work resists automation. Specialized skills and safety requirements maintain stable demand.

title: Emergency management directors
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: A blend of digital planning (developing emergency plans, analyzing risk data, coordinating logistics) and physical/interpersonal response work (leading disaster response, coordinating with officials, conducting community outreach). AI assists with risk modeling and communication planning by 2028.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: AI assists with risk modeling, communication coordination, and resource planning. However, real-time crisis leadership, inter-agency coordination, and high-stakes judgment during emergencies require human decision-making and presence.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates risk modeling, resource allocation planning, communication systems, and situation monitoring. However, emergency management requires real-time human judgment in crisis situations, inter-agency coordination, public communication under pressure, and community relationship building.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Emergency management directors plan and coordinate disaster response. This is managerial and planning work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Planning, coordination, and leadership during emergencies. Entirely managerial and knowledge-based work.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Entirely planning, coordination, and management work. No physical labor component.
adoption_friction_rationale: Government employment with institutional inertia. Role requires human judgment in crisis situations, public communication, and inter-agency coordination. Political accountability requirements. Moderate adoption of AI for planning and monitoring but decision-making must remain human.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Climate change increases frequency and severity of natural disasters, expanding demand for emergency management. AI tools enhance preparedness and response but the coordination and decision-making role requires human leadership.

title: EMTs and paramedics
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Core work is physical emergency response: assessing injuries, providing medical care, transporting patients, and operating emergency vehicles. Electronic patient records and dispatch systems are digital tools, but the hands-on emergency medical care dominates. AI cannot replace physical life-saving interventions.
