digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Providing emergency medical care, transporting patients, and performing life-saving procedures in the field are entirely physical and interpersonal. AI aids with diagnostics and protocol guidance, but hands-on emergency care remains human.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Emergency medical response is fundamentally physical—transporting patients, performing life-saving procedures, and making rapid assessments in the field. AI assists with protocol guidance and hospital communication, but the hands-on emergency care in uncontrolled environments remains human.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: EMTs and paramedics respond to emergencies in highly unpredictable environments requiring rapid physical intervention. The chaotic, uncontrolled settings are among the most challenging for robotic deployment.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Emergency medical response in highly unpredictable, novel environments. Each emergency is unique—accident scenes, homes, public spaces. Requires rapid human judgment, physical improvisation, and patient trust. Among the most resistant occupations to physical automation.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Emergency medical response in highly unstructured, unpredictable environments. Every scene is different—accident sites, homes, public spaces. By 2036, robotic medical equipment assists, but the chaotic, variable nature of emergency scenes and need for rapid human judgment and intimate patient contact keep this predominantly human.
adoption_friction_rationale: Emergency medical care requires split-second human judgment in unpredictable environments. State licensing and medical protocol requirements. Liability for patient outcomes. Strong public trust requirement. Physical patient handling in varied emergency scenes. Labour shortages provide some pull but barriers are formidable.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Demand tied to emergency call volume, which is relatively stable per capita. AI may assist with triage and diagnostics but the physical emergency response cannot be automated. Aging population may increase demand slightly.

title: Entertainment and recreation managers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: A mix of digital management (scheduling, budgeting, marketing, reporting) and interpersonal/physical oversight (facility management, staff supervision, community engagement). AI assists with scheduling optimization and marketing content by 2028, but on-site management and personal leadership remain essential.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Scheduling, budgeting, marketing, and reporting benefit from AI automation. However, managing staff, creating guest experiences, and handling on-site operations require physical presence and interpersonal leadership.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates scheduling, financial management, marketing, and administrative tasks. However, managing entertainment venues and programs requires physical presence, staff leadership, event oversight, and creating experiences that depend on human interpersonal skills.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Recreation managers oversee facilities and programs. Managerial work with no physical labor.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Management and business oversight work. Purely administrative and interpersonal.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Management and planning role that is entirely cognitive and interpersonal. No physical labor component.
adoption_friction_rationale: Mix of large entertainment companies and small venues. Management role requires human judgment and customer relations. Moderate employer fragmentation. AI tools for operations already used in large venues. Creative programming and community engagement resist automation.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Growing spending on entertainment and experiences. AI tools help manage operations but the demand for diverse entertainment venues and programming continues to expand with disposable income.

title: Environmental engineering technologists and technicians
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: A blend of physical fieldwork (operating pollution control equipment, collecting samples, site inspections) and digital tasks (maintaining records, analyzing data, preparing reports). AI assists with data analysis and reporting, but hands-on equipment operation and field testing remain significant.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Field sampling, equipment operation, and site inspections are physical tasks. AI aids with data analysis, report generation, and regulatory compliance checking, creating a moderate blend of digital and physical duties.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates data analysis, environmental modeling, and report writing. However, field sampling, site inspections, equipment operation, and environmental monitoring in the field require physical presence and hands-on work.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Environmental engineering techs collect samples and test in labs and field. Mixed lab/field work with some physical component, but primarily technical support.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Field testing and monitoring work in variable environments. Each site has unique conditions. While automated monitoring equipment handles routine data collection, field sampling and site assessment in diverse environments requires human adaptability.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Field sampling, monitoring, and testing in varied environmental sites. By 2036, automated monitoring handles much routine data collection, but site-specific environmental assessment in novel locations still requires human judgment and physical presence.
adoption_friction_rationale: Government agencies and large environmental firms are primary employers. Field sampling and monitoring work has some physical requirements. EPA regulations create compliance framework. Lab analysis increasingly automated. Moderate institutional inertia in government settings.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Climate change and stricter environmental regulations increase demand for environmental monitoring and remediation. AI tools enable more comprehensive environmental assessment but the physical fieldwork persists.

title: Environmental engineers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Substantial digital work: designing pollution control systems using engineering software, analyzing environmental data, writing impact reports, and modeling solutions. AI assists with simulation, data analysis, and documentation by 2028. Site investigations and regulatory coordination add non-digital components.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Modeling, analysis, report writing, and regulatory documentation are digital tasks increasingly handled by AI. Field assessment, stakeholder engagement, and novel remediation design require human expertise.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Environmental modeling, regulatory compliance analysis, remediation design, and impact assessment documentation are automated. Human engineers remain for site-specific judgment, stakeholder engagement, novel contamination scenarios, and navigating complex regulatory negotiations.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Environmental engineers design solutions for environmental problems. Knowledge-based engineering work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Design and engineering work that is primarily knowledge-based. Some field visits but the role centers on analysis and design.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Primarily design and analytical engineering work. Some site visits but core role is cognitive problem-solving and regulatory compliance analysis.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large engineering firms and government agencies (EPA, state agencies). Environmental regulations create both friction (regulatory complexity) and pull (compliance needs). Professional licensing required. AI tools for modeling and analysis are emerging. Government institutional inertia.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Climate change, pollution remediation, and sustainability mandates create growing demand. AI-assisted modeling enables tackling more complex environmental problems. Significant latent demand for environmental engineering in developing nations.

title: Environmental science and protection technicians
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: A blend of field monitoring (collecting samples, conducting inspections, operating monitoring equipment) and digital tasks (analyzing data, preparing reports, maintaining records). AI assists with data analysis, but physical fieldwork and sample collection remain central.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Field sampling, laboratory testing, and site inspections are predominantly physical. AI helps with data analysis and compliance documentation, but fieldwork remains the core duty.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: The role involves substantial fieldwork—collecting samples, conducting inspections, monitoring pollution. AI automates lab data analysis and reporting, but physical sample collection, site assessment, and field monitoring remain human tasks.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Environmental techs collect field samples and perform lab tests. Some physical fieldwork and lab work, but variable outdoor conditions limit robotic exposure.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Field sampling and monitoring in variable natural environments. Each site is unique. Automated sensors handle routine monitoring, but field collection, site assessment, and equipment deployment in diverse conditions requires human adaptability.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Field work collecting samples and monitoring conditions in varied natural and industrial environments. By 2036, automated monitoring handles routine sampling, but novel site assessment and working in unstructured environments still requires human presence.
adoption_friction_rationale: Government agencies and environmental firms. Field sampling and monitoring requires physical presence. EPA and state regulations create compliance framework. Lab work increasingly automated. Moderate institutional inertia. Some remote sensing and AI monitoring tools already in use.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Growing environmental monitoring requirements driven by climate change and regulations. AI tools enable more comprehensive data collection and analysis. Physical sampling and fieldwork persist.

title: Environmental scientists and specialists
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: A mix of fieldwork (collecting environmental samples, conducting site investigations) and digital knowledge work (analyzing data, writing reports, developing remediation plans). AI meaningfully assists with data analysis, modeling, and report generation by 2028, balanced by essential fieldwork.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Data analysis, modeling, literature review, and report production are digital tasks AI handles well. Fieldwork, regulatory negotiation, and complex site-specific environmental judgment retain strong human involvement.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates data analysis, environmental modeling, literature review, and report generation. Human scientists remain for fieldwork, novel research questions, interpreting complex ecosystem interactions, and communicating findings to policymakers and communities.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Environmental scientists conduct research and analysis. Primarily knowledge-based work with some fieldwork.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Research and analysis work with some fieldwork. The role is primarily about scientific assessment and policy recommendation rather than physical labor.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Primarily analytical and research work with some fieldwork. The physical field components (sampling, site assessment) are partially automatable with drones and sensors, but the core scientific analysis and regulatory judgment are cognitive.
adoption_friction_rationale: Government agencies, consulting firms, and nonprofits. Field work and stakeholder engagement require human presence. Regulatory framework (NEPA, EPA) requires human judgment for environmental assessments. Moderate institutional inertia. AI tools for analysis are emerging.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Climate change and sustainability drive expanding demand for environmental science. AI enables analysis of larger datasets and more complex environmental systems. Every industry needs environmental assessment.

title: Epidemiologists
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Predominantly digital: analyzing disease data, conducting statistical studies, writing research reports, and developing public health policies. AI significantly accelerates data analysis, pattern detection, and literature review by 2028. Community education and fieldwork investigations provide some non-digital balance.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Statistical analysis, disease surveillance data processing, literature synthesis, and report generation are heavily digital tasks AI agents automate. Human epidemiologists focus on novel outbreak investigation, study design, and public health policy interpretation.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Disease surveillance, statistical analysis, outbreak modeling, and report writing are highly automatable digital tasks. Human epidemiologists remain for novel pathogen investigation, study design in ambiguous situations, and communicating complex health risks to policymakers and the public.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Epidemiologists study disease patterns using data analysis. Their work is entirely knowledge-based with no physical labor component.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Purely analytical research work involving disease pattern analysis. No physical component.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Entirely analytical and research work involving data analysis and disease investigation. No physical component for robotic automation.
adoption_friction_rationale: Government agencies (CDC, state health departments) and research institutions. AI/ML is already transforming disease surveillance and modeling. Institutional inertia in government slows adoption. Data analysis work is highly amenable to AI. Some human judgment needed for policy recommendations.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Post-pandemic awareness dramatically increased demand for disease surveillance. AI tools enable real-time tracking and more sophisticated modeling. Growing public health infrastructure investment worldwide expands roles.

title: Exercise physiologists
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Core work is hands-on and interpersonal: administering fitness assessments, developing exercise programs, and working directly with patients. Some digital analysis of test results and program documentation exists, but the physical patient interaction and exercise supervision dominate.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Administering fitness tests, designing exercise programs, and working directly with patients are hands-on clinical duties. AI assists with data tracking and program optimization, but physical patient interaction is central.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates exercise program design and physiological data analysis. However, the core work involves hands-on patient assessment, supervising exercise sessions, and providing motivational coaching—physical and interpersonal tasks that remain human.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Exercise physiologists design fitness programs based on clinical assessment. Their work is primarily knowledge-based with patient instruction, not physical labor exposed to robotic automation.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Hands-on patient assessment and exercise program supervision. Each patient has unique physical conditions and needs. Requires trust, communication, and real-time adaptation to patient responses. The interpersonal and clinical judgment aspects resist automation.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Hands-on patient assessment and exercise program implementation. Requires physical demonstration, patient motivation, and adaptive response to individual patient conditions. By 2036, monitoring equipment is automated, but the personal guidance and physical interaction remain human-centered.
adoption_friction_rationale: Mix of hospital/clinical settings and private practice. Healthcare regulations and licensing requirements. Physical assessment and exercise supervision require human presence. Patient relationship is important. Moderate employer fragmentation. Some wearable technology already augmenting the role.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Growing health and fitness consciousness creates latent demand. Most people could benefit from personalized exercise prescription but can't access it. AI tools help physiologists create personalized programs and monitor more clients.

title: Farmers, ranchers, and other agricultural managers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Predominantly physical: overseeing crop production, managing livestock, operating equipment, and maintaining facilities. Financial planning and market analysis have digital components where AI assists, but the hands-on agricultural management and outdoor work dominate.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Farm management involves significant physical oversight of land, livestock, and equipment. AI aids with crop planning, market analysis, and precision agriculture data, but hands-on management of agricultural operations limits digital exposure.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates crop planning, market analysis, financial management, and precision agriculture data. However, farming and ranching are fundamentally physical—managing land, equipment, livestock, and workers in variable outdoor conditions with constant hands-on decision-making.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Farm managers primarily make business and operational decisions. While they may perform some physical tasks, their role is predominantly managerial and not directly exposed to robotic physical automation.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Management role overseeing increasingly automated farm operations. While farm equipment is increasingly autonomous, farmers still make critical decisions about planting, livestock management, and operations in variable conditions. The management and judgment aspects are more important than physical labor.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Management role with significant physical oversight component. By 2036, most farming operations are automated, but managers must still make judgment calls about variable conditions, animal welfare, and novel situations. Physical presence for inspection and decision-making in variable environments.
adoption_friction_rationale: Mix of large agribusiness operations (lower friction) and small family farms (higher friction). Severe labour shortages create strong pull for automation. Precision agriculture technology already widely adopted. Management decisions require local knowledge and judgment. USDA regulations manageable.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Farm consolidation and precision agriculture technology enable fewer managers to oversee larger operations. AI-powered autonomous equipment reduces the management intensity per acre. Total farm management positions decline gradually.

title: Fashion designers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Significant digital work: sketching designs using CAD, selecting fabrics and patterns, and creating production specifications. AI image generation tools assist with concept development and trend analysis by 2028. However, physical fabric selection, fitting, and creative artistic vision remain distinctly human.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: AI generates design variations, creates technical drawings, and handles trend analysis. However, creative vision, fabric selection, fitting garments on bodies, and understanding cultural aesthetics retain strong human components.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI generates design concepts, creates patterns, produces technical specifications, and handles trend analysis. Human designers retain value for creative vision where human authorship is the brand, understanding cultural and social dynamics, client relationships, and physical fabric and fit expertise.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Fashion designers create clothing designs. Creative knowledge work with some physical prototype making, but primarily design-focused.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Creative design work that is primarily conceptual and digital. While garment production is physical, design itself is knowledge and creativity based.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Primarily creative design work that is cognitive. Prototype creation and fitting have physical components, but the core value is aesthetic vision and trend interpretation.
adoption_friction_rationale: Mix of large fashion houses and many independent designers. AI design tools are emerging but creative vision is highly valued. Industry culture values human creativity and brand identity. Moderate employer fragmentation. Fast fashion segment more amenable to AI-driven design.
demand_elasticity_rationale: AI tools accelerate design iteration, but every brand and retailer wants unique fashion. Fast fashion, direct-to-consumer brands, and sustainable fashion create new design opportunities. Latent demand from smaller brands wanting custom design.

title: Film and video editors and camera operators
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Camera operation is physical, requiring on-location presence and artistic judgment. Video editing is heavily digital and AI-assisted by 2028 with automated editing, color correction, and effects. The blend of physical camera work and digital post-production places this at high-moderate exposure.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: AI automates rough cuts, color grading, sound mixing, and effects compositing. Camera operation remains physical, but editing workflows are heavily digitized. Senior editors retain creative storytelling roles, but production teams shrink.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates routine editing, color correction, and assembly cuts. Camera operation requires physical presence and creative framing judgment. Human editors and operators remain for creative storytelling decisions, live event coverage, and premium productions where human artistic vision is valued.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Camera operators handle physical equipment on varied sets, but editing is desk-based. The physical camera work occurs in variable environments limiting robotic exposure.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Camera operation involves physical equipment handling in variable environments, but editing is entirely digital. Automated cameras handle some standardized shots, but creative cinematography requires human artistic vision. Editing is purely digital knowledge work.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Editing is entirely digital. Camera operation involves physical manipulation of equipment in variable environments. By 2036, some automated camera systems exist, but creative cinematography requires human artistic judgment about movement, framing, and timing.
adoption_friction_rationale: Mix of large studios and many freelancers. AI editing tools advancing rapidly. Camera operation for controlled settings amenable to automation but live/documentary work requires human judgment. Union protections (IATSE, editors guild). Creative judgment valued by industry.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Explosive growth in video content for streaming, social media, corporate, and advertising. AI assists with editing tasks but the volume of content needing production grows faster. Every business now needs video content.

title: Financial analysts
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Almost entirely screen-based: analyzing financial data, building valuation models, writing research reports, and making investment recommendations. AI significantly accelerates data analysis, modeling, and report generation by 2028. Routine financial analysis faces strong automation pressure.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Financial modeling, data analysis, report generation, and market research are heavily digital tasks AI agents handle autonomously. Human analysts focus on client relationships, novel strategic insights, and complex deal evaluation.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Financial modeling, market analysis, report generation, and investment screening are structured digital tasks AI handles autonomously. Human analysts remain for novel strategic insights, relationship-based advisory work, and interpreting market dynamics in unprecedented situations.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Financial analysts evaluate investments using data analysis. Entirely desk-based knowledge work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Purely analytical desk-based work involving financial modeling and analysis. No physical component.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Entirely analytical and computational work. No physical component.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large financial institutions are primary employers with strong technology adoption culture and clear ROI. Quantitative analysis is highly amenable to AI. Bloomberg, FactSet already integrate AI. CFA credential creates some professional friction but employers drive adoption.
demand_elasticity_rationale: AI automates much quantitative financial analysis. But the number of investment decisions and financial assessments is somewhat fixed by the number of companies and transactions. Some expansion in fintech advisory offsets automation.

title: Financial clerks
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Almost entirely screen-based: updating financial records, processing transactions, verifying data, and preparing reports. AI automation handles most routine data entry, reconciliation, and processing tasks by 2028. Active headcount reduction in financial clerk positions as organizations automate.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Processing financial transactions, maintaining records, and handling routine financial paperwork are digital tasks AI automates almost entirely. Only exception handling and complex reconciliations require human intervention.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Processing financial transactions, maintaining records, billing, and payment handling are routine digital tasks fully automated by 2036. This occupation has effectively ceased to exist in its traditional form.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Financial clerks process financial transactions and maintain records. Desk-based clerical work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Office-based clerical work involving financial record processing. No physical component.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Office-based administrative work. No meaningful physical component for robotic automation.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large financial institutions and corporations are primary employers. Work is highly standardized and data-driven. Extensive automation already in place. Clear ROI. Minimal regulatory barriers for clerical functions. Labour market is already contracting due to automation.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Highly routine transaction processing and record-keeping that AI and software directly automate. Online banking, automated billing, and digital payments reduce the need for human clerks. Demand tied to transaction volume but automation handles more.

title: Financial examiners
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Predominantly digital: reviewing financial records, evaluating compliance, assessing risk levels, and writing examination reports. AI assists with automated compliance checking, risk scoring, and report generation by 2028. Complex regulatory judgment and on-site examinations provide some insulation.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Reviewing financial records, analyzing compliance, and assessing risk are heavily digital tasks AI agents handle efficiently. Human examiners focus on complex investigations, regulatory judgment calls, and enforcement decisions.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Reviewing financial records, assessing compliance, and producing examination reports are structured analytical tasks AI handles. Human examiners remain for complex fraud investigations, interpreting ambiguous regulatory situations, and exercising enforcement judgment.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Financial examiners review financial institutions for compliance. Desk-based regulatory work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Regulatory review and analysis work. Entirely knowledge-based with occasional site visits.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Entirely analytical and investigative work reviewing financial records. No physical component.
adoption_friction_rationale: Government agencies (FDIC, OCC, state regulators) are primary employers with institutional inertia. Regulatory examination requires human judgment and discretion. AI tools for financial analysis are available but regulatory culture is conservative. Moderate adoption in compliance monitoring.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Demand tied to the number of financial institutions, which is relatively fixed. AI-powered monitoring can flag issues automatically, reducing the number of examiners needed. Regulatory requirements maintain a floor on staffing.

title: Financial managers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Predominantly digital knowledge work: creating financial reports, directing investments, analyzing market trends, and developing strategic plans. AI copilots significantly assist with financial modeling and reporting by 2028. Strategic decision-making, stakeholder management, and organizational leadership remain human-driven.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Financial reporting, forecasting, and analysis are heavily automated. Managers retain strategic planning, stakeholder communication, risk governance, and organizational leadership roles, but analytical teams shrink significantly.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Financial reporting, budgeting, forecasting, and compliance management are automated. Human financial managers remain for strategic financial planning in ambiguous business contexts, stakeholder relationships, capital allocation decisions, and organizational leadership.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Financial managers oversee financial operations. Managerial knowledge work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Management of financial operations. Purely knowledge and leadership work.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Management and strategic financial planning. Entirely cognitive work.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large corporations and financial institutions are primary employers. Strategic financial management requires human judgment. AI tools for analysis and forecasting already widely used. Professional expectations and fiduciary duty create moderate friction. Regulatory requirements (SOX, SEC) are manageable.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Every organization needs financial management, but AI automates much of the analytical heavy lifting. The number of financial manager positions scales with organizations, not with task volume. Growth in fintech creates some new roles.

title: Fire inspectors
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Core work requires physical inspections: examining buildings for fire hazards, investigating fire scenes, and enforcing fire codes. Report writing and code compliance research have digital components, but the essential on-site inspection and investigation work requires physical presence.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Physical building inspections, arson investigation at fire scenes, and code enforcement require on-site presence. AI assists with report writing and code compliance checking, but fieldwork dominates.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates code compliance analysis and report generation. However, fire inspection requires physical building walkthroughs, on-site evaluation of fire hazards, and investigation of fire scenes—hands-on work that retains significant human involvement.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Fire inspectors examine buildings for compliance, involving site visits to varied structures. The diverse environments and judgment required limit robotic exposure, though drone inspection assists in some cases.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Field inspection and investigation in variable buildings and fire scenes. Each scene is unique. While some monitoring technology assists, physical inspection of diverse structures and investigation of fire causes requires human judgment and adaptability.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Site inspections in variable environments (burned buildings, construction sites). By 2036, drones and sensors assist with data collection, but investigating fire scenes in structurally compromised buildings requires human judgment in truly unstructured environments.
adoption_friction_rationale: Government employment with institutional inertia. Fire investigation requires physical scene examination and human judgment. Building inspection involves code interpretation in varied conditions. Liability for missed hazards. AI tools for analysis emerging but physical presence essential.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Demand tied to the fixed number of buildings and fires requiring inspection/investigation. AI-assisted inspection tools and sensors may increase throughput per inspector. The volume of inspections is set by regulation.

title: Firefighters
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Almost entirely physical: responding to emergencies, putting out fires, rescuing people, operating equipment, and maintaining physical fitness. Report writing is a minor digital component. AI has minimal impact on the physically demanding emergency response that defines this role.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Fighting fires, performing rescues, and providing emergency medical care are entirely physical, high-risk duties. AI aids with dispatch optimization and hazard identification, but frontline firefighting is firmly human.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Firefighting is fundamentally physical emergency response—entering burning buildings, operating equipment, rescuing people, and providing medical aid. Digital AI has minimal exposure, limited to dispatch optimization and incident documentation.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Firefighters operate in extremely unpredictable, hazardous environments requiring improvisation and physical strength. The chaotic nature of fire and rescue operations makes robotic replacement infeasible by 2028.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Emergency response in highly unpredictable, dangerous, novel environments. Each fire and rescue scenario is unique. Requires constant physical improvisation, teamwork, and split-second human judgment. Robotic assistance for specific tasks (hazmat, reconnaissance drones) but human firefighters essential.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Emergency response in highly unstructured, dangerous, and unpredictable environments. Every fire scene is novel. By 2036, robotic firefighting assists in some structured scenarios, but search and rescue in burning buildings, wildland fire, and complex emergency scenes remain predominantly human due to extreme environmental unpredictability.
adoption_friction_rationale: Government employment with extremely strong unions (IAFF). Life-safety role with high public trust requirements. Physical rescue in unpredictable, dangerous environments. Enormous liability and public accountability. Deep cultural identity and institutional traditions. Some drone/robot assistance but human firefighters are irreplaceable.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Emergency response demand tied to fire and disaster frequency, which is relatively stable to increasing (wildfires). The physical, on-scene nature of firefighting resists automation. Climate change may increase wildfire demand.

title: Fishing and hunting workers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Entirely physical outdoor work: operating boats, catching fish, maintaining nets and equipment, and navigating waterways. This is one of the most physically demanding and non-digital occupations with no meaningful AI exposure by 2028.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Catching fish, operating boats, and maintaining nets and equipment are physical outdoor tasks. AI has minimal impact on these manual labor duties.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Fishing and hunting are entirely physical outdoor occupations involving operating boats, deploying nets and traps, and processing catch. Digital AI has negligible exposure beyond navigation and weather tools.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Commercial fishing involves physical work in highly unpredictable marine environments. The variable conditions, live animal handling, and hazardous settings make robotic replacement infeasible by 2028.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Work on water in highly variable natural conditions. Each fishing trip involves different weather, seas, and catch conditions. Commercial fishing operations see some automation of processing, but actual fishing in open water with variable conditions requires human judgment and physical adaptability.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Fishing involves highly variable natural environments—weather, sea conditions, fish behavior. By 2036, commercial fishing vessels benefit from significant automation for net handling and processing, but the unpredictable ocean environment and real-time adaptation to conditions require human judgment.
adoption_friction_rationale: Highly fragmented industry of small vessel operators. Work at sea in unpredictable conditions. Maritime regulations (Coast Guard). Limited capital among small operations. Some large commercial fishing operations adopting technology. Environmental and quota regulations add complexity.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Fish stocks are limited, and sustainable fishing quotas constrain demand. Technology and larger boats enable fewer fishers to catch the same volume. Aquaculture growth shifts some demand away from wild fishing.

title: Fitness trainers and instructors
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Core work is physical and interpersonal: leading exercise classes, demonstrating techniques, motivating clients, and monitoring form. AI fitness apps provide some competition for basic programming, but the in-person instruction, motivation, and physical correction remain fundamentally human.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Leading exercise sessions, demonstrating movements, and motivating clients are physical and interpersonal duties. AI generates workout plans and tracks metrics, but in-person coaching and physical demonstration remain central.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI generates workout programs and tracks fitness data. However, personal training is fundamentally interpersonal—motivating clients, correcting form in person, and providing accountability through human relationships. The social and physical nature of group fitness also retains human instructors.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Fitness trainers provide instruction, motivation, and exercise guidance. Their work is primarily interpersonal coaching with no physical labor component that robots would automate.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Interpersonal work motivating and guiding exercise. Requires personal connection, real-time form assessment, and adaptation to individual clients. While fitness apps and AI coaching exist, in-person training is about human motivation and physical guidance.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Personal training involves human motivation, relationship, physical demonstration, and adaptive coaching. The personal connection and motivational presence IS the product for many clients. By 2036, robotic exercise equipment exists, but the human trainer's role as motivator and form corrector remains valued.
adoption_friction_rationale: Extremely fragmented industry of independent trainers, small gyms, and large fitness chains. Strong client preference for human motivation and personal attention. AI fitness apps exist but in-person training valued. Low barrier to entry means many small operators. Some certification requirements.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Enormous unmet demand for personalized fitness guidance. Most people would benefit from a trainer but can't afford one. AI tools enable trainers to serve more clients with personalized programs while maintaining the motivational human element.

title: Flight attendants
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Almost entirely physical and interpersonal: ensuring passenger safety, serving food and beverages, managing cabin emergencies, and providing customer service in flight. The work requires physical presence aboard aircraft with minimal digital component.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Ensuring passenger safety, serving food and beverages, and managing cabin operations are physical and interpersonal duties performed in aircraft. AI has minimal impact on these in-person service roles.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Flight attendant work is physical and interpersonal—ensuring passenger safety, serving food and beverages, managing cabin situations, and providing customer service in a physical aircraft. Digital AI has minimal direct exposure.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Flight attendants perform safety demonstrations, serve passengers, and handle emergencies in a confined but highly variable human-interaction environment. Robotic replacement is not feasible by 2028.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Safety-critical role requiring passenger interaction, emergency response, and service in the confined, variable environment of aircraft cabins. Trust and human presence are essential for passenger safety and comfort. Regulatory requirements mandate human crew.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: In-cabin service involves passenger interaction, safety management, and working in confined variable environments. By 2036, routine beverage/food service may be partially automated, but passenger safety, emergency response, and customer service in the variable cabin environment require human presence. Regulatory requirements also mandate humans.
adoption_friction_rationale: FAA safety regulations require human cabin crew for emergency procedures. Strong union protections (AFA). Airlines are large employers but regulatory requirements for emergency response mandate human presence. Passenger service expectations favor human interaction. Liability for safety compliance.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Demand directly tied to the number of flights and passengers, which grows modestly. Airlines may reduce crew sizes with technology. Safety requirements provide a floor but long-term trajectory favors efficiency.

title: Flooring installers and tile and stone setters
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Entirely physical work: removing old flooring, measuring and cutting materials, laying tile, carpet, or hardwood, and finishing surfaces. This is purely manual skilled trade work with no meaningful digital component that AI could affect.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Measuring, cutting, and installing flooring, tile, and stone are entirely physical construction tasks with no meaningful digital component.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Installing flooring, tile, and stone is entirely hands-on physical skilled trade work requiring precise cutting, laying, and finishing. Digital AI has essentially no exposure to this occupation.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Flooring and tile installation involves skilled manual work in varied interior environments. Tile-laying robots are in very early prototyping; the variable conditions of each job make deployment limited by 2028.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Skilled installation work in variable residential and commercial spaces. Each floor, wall, and layout is different. Requires precise dexterity and adaptation to existing structures. Some large commercial flooring projects see limited automation, but custom tile work remains human.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Flooring and tile work involves variable substrates, custom patterns, and adaptation to room geometry. By 2036, robots handle standardized large-area flooring installation, but custom tile work, complex patterns, and renovation in irregular spaces still require significant human skill.
adoption_friction_rationale: Highly fragmented trade with many small contractors and independent operators. Physical precision work in varied building conditions. Union presence in some markets. Limited capital for small operators. Each installation is unique, challenging robotic standardization. Labour shortages provide some pull.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Physical installation work in variable environments resists automation. Demand tied to construction and renovation activity. Custom tile work is particularly resistant to automation.

title: Floral designers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Predominantly physical and creative: arranging flowers, selecting materials, and interacting with customers. Online ordering and inventory management are minor digital components. AI has limited impact on the hands-on artistic arrangement and customer service that define this role.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Selecting flowers, creating arrangements, and setting up displays are hands-on creative tasks. AI might assist with design inspiration or inventory management, but physical floral work remains human.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Floral design is hands-on creative physical work—selecting, cutting, and arranging flowers. While AI can suggest designs, the physical creation and the artisanal nature of the work remain human. Digital exposure is limited to ordering and design reference.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Floral designers create arrangements requiring artistic judgment and fine motor handling of delicate materials. The creative and dexterous nature of the work limits robotic replacement by 2028.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Creative arrangement of natural materials that vary in shape, size, and condition. Each arrangement is custom. While simple bouquet assembly could be partially automated, creative floral design requires artistic judgment and handling of fragile, variable natural materials.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Creative arrangement of natural materials with high variability. Each flower is unique. By 2036, basic bouquet assembly may be automated, but creative custom design requiring aesthetic judgment with variable natural materials remains human-centered.
adoption_friction_rationale: Extremely fragmented industry of small independent florists. Physical arrangement work requires artistic judgment and dexterity. Some large event companies and grocery chains have more resources. Limited capital among small operators. Consumer preference for artisanal arrangements. Moderate technical barriers.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Demand tied to events, gifting, and decoration—modestly growing market. AI has limited impact on physical flower arranging. Online ordering expands access but automated arrangements are limited.

title: Food and beverage serving and related workers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Almost entirely physical and interpersonal: taking orders, serving food, clearing tables, and providing customer service. POS system use is a minor digital tool. AI has minimal impact on the in-person food service that defines this role.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Serving food, clearing tables, and interacting with customers in restaurants are entirely physical and interpersonal tasks. AI ordering systems exist, but human servers remain for the service experience.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Serving food and beverages is physical interpersonal work—taking orders, carrying plates, and interacting with customers. Digital AI exposure is limited to ordering systems and POS technology.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Food servers interact with customers in variable restaurant environments, carrying food and navigating crowded dining areas. While robotic delivery is piloted in some restaurants, the social and dexterous aspects limit exposure.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Robotic serving systems operational in some chain restaurants and high-volume venues. Automated drink dispensing and food runners in standardized environments. However, full-service restaurant work requiring customer interaction, carrying multiple plates through crowded spaces, and personalized service still needs humans.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: By 2036, robotic serving systems are common in many restaurant and institutional settings. Automated ordering, food delivery robots, and self-service are widespread. Human servers persist in fine dining and hospitality-focused venues where personal service is the product.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large restaurant chains can adopt serving robots and ordering kiosks at scale. Severe labour shortages provide strong pull. Hospitality preference for human service in fine dining but fast-casual is automating. Mix of large chains (lower friction) and independent restaurants (higher friction).
demand_elasticity_rationale: Hospitality demand grows with population and dining trends. The physical and interpersonal nature of serving resists full automation. Some automation (ordering kiosks) reduces headcount but table service persists.

title: Food preparation workers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Entirely physical work: slicing meat, cutting vegetables, preparing ingredients, and maintaining kitchen cleanliness. This is among the most purely manual food service roles with no meaningful digital component.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Washing, cutting, measuring, and preparing food ingredients are manual physical tasks with no meaningful digital AI component.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Food preparation is entirely hands-on physical work—washing, cutting, measuring, and preparing ingredients. Digital AI has negligible exposure to this occupation.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Food prep workers perform repetitive tasks like chopping, portioning, and packaging in commercial kitchens. Fast-food and institutional settings are piloting robotic food prep for standardized tasks by 2028.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Routine food prep tasks (chopping, mixing, portioning) increasingly automated in chain restaurants and institutional kitchens. Robotic prep systems handle standardized ingredients. Human workers focus on quality control and non-standard preparations. High-volume operations are substantially automated.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Routine food preparation—chopping, portioning, basic cooking—is highly automated by 2036. Robotic food prep systems handle standardized tasks in institutional and fast-food settings. Humans remain for creative preparation and quality oversight.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large food service chains and food manufacturing drive adoption. Severe labour shortages create strong pull. Work is repetitive and standardizable in commercial settings. Food safety regulations manageable. Some prep robotics already deployed (chopping, portioning). Independent restaurants more fragmented.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Routine food prep tasks are increasingly automated in fast food and institutional settings. Demand tied to food service volume, which grows modestly. Automation directly replaces repetitive chopping, portioning, and assembly tasks.

title: Food processing equipment workers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Predominantly physical: operating food processing machinery, loading equipment, monitoring production lines, and maintaining sanitary conditions. Machine controls may have digital interfaces, but the core work is operating and monitoring physical equipment.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Operating food processing machinery, monitoring production lines, and handling materials are physical production tasks. AI assists with quality monitoring but does not replace manual equipment operation.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Operating food processing machinery is physical production work. AI assists with quality monitoring and process control, but operating, cleaning, and maintaining processing equipment remains hands-on.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Food processing occurs in structured factory environments with repetitive tasks like sorting, packaging, and machine operation. Robotic automation is actively being deployed in large food processing facilities by 2028.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Factory-based food processing is highly automated with robotic systems handling sorting, cutting, packaging, and quality inspection. Standardized processing lines operate with minimal human intervention. Humans supervise and handle exceptions. Tobacco processing similarly automated.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Food processing in factory environments is highly automated by 2036 with robotic handling, sorting, and processing equipment. Standardized production lines run with minimal human intervention. Humans remain primarily for oversight and maintenance.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large food processing companies (Tyson, Cargill, Nestlé) are primary employers with strong incentive and resources. Severe labour shortages in food processing. USDA/FDA regulations manageable. Assembly-line work is highly amenable to robotics. Significant automation already deployed.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Factory food processing is heavily automated. AI and robotics continue to automate quality control, sorting, and packaging. Demand tied to food production volume but each worker handles more through automation.

title: Food service managers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: A blend of physical on-site management (overseeing kitchen operations, ensuring food quality, managing staff) and digital tasks (scheduling, budgeting, inventory management, ordering). AI assists with scheduling and inventory optimization by 2028, but the hands-on restaurant management dominates.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Inventory management, scheduling, and financial reporting benefit from AI. However, on-site staff supervision, customer interaction, food quality oversight, and managing the physical restaurant environment require human presence.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates inventory management, scheduling, cost analysis, and menu optimization. However, food service management requires physical presence—overseeing kitchen operations, managing staff in person, handling customer issues, and ensuring quality through direct observation.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Food service managers oversee operations, staff, and finances. Their role is primarily managerial and not exposed to physical robotic automation.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Management role overseeing increasingly automated kitchen and service operations. The role itself is about planning, staffing, quality control, and customer relations rather than physical labor.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Management role involving planning, staff supervision, and quality control. Physical inspection of food and facilities is a component, but the core role is cognitive management and decision-making. By 2036, automated monitoring assists, but managerial judgment remains human.
adoption_friction_rationale: Mix of large restaurant chains (lower friction) and independent restaurants (higher friction). Management requires human judgment, staff supervision, and customer relations. AI tools for scheduling, inventory, and analytics already used. Health inspection compliance requires human accountability.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Management roles scale with the number of food service establishments. AI helps with scheduling and inventory but on-site management persists. Restaurant industry grows modestly with population.

title: Forensic science technicians
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: A blend of physical crime scene work (collecting evidence, documenting scenes) and laboratory analysis (testing evidence, analyzing DNA, preparing reports). AI assists with database searches and pattern matching by 2028, but physical evidence collection and expert testimony remain human-dependent.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Crime scene evidence collection is physical work. However, laboratory analysis, database searches, and report writing are digital tasks aided by AI. The blend of field and lab work creates moderate overall exposure.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates evidence analysis (DNA matching, fingerprint comparison, digital forensics) and report generation. However, physical evidence collection at crime scenes, maintaining chain of custody, and testifying in court retain significant human roles.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Forensic technicians collect evidence at crime scenes and analyze it in labs. Crime scenes are unstructured, but lab analysis is more controlled. Mixed physical/analytical role with limited robotic exposure.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Crime scene work in highly variable environments—each scene is unique. Lab analysis is increasingly automated, but scene investigation, evidence collection, and documentation in diverse locations requires human judgment and careful physical work.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Crime scene investigation involves working in highly variable, unstructured environments. By 2036, lab analysis is heavily automated, but crime scene evidence collection in novel, unpredictable settings still requires human judgment and careful physical work.
adoption_friction_rationale: Government crime labs are primary employers with institutional inertia. DNA analysis and digital forensics increasingly automated. Chain of custody and court testimony requirements demand human accountability. Physical evidence collection at crime scenes requires human presence and judgment.
demand_elasticity_rationale: AI enhances forensic analysis capabilities (DNA matching, digital forensics, pattern recognition). Growing complexity of crime (cybercrime, digital evidence) creates new forensic specialties. Backlog of unprocessed evidence suggests unmet demand.

title: Forest and conservation workers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Almost entirely physical outdoor work: planting trees, fighting fires, maintaining trails, and using forestry equipment. Data recording is a minor digital component. AI has negligible impact on the manual conservation labor that defines this role.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Planting trees, fighting wildfires, maintaining trails, and monitoring forest health are physical outdoor tasks. AI has minimal impact on this hands-on conservation work.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Forest conservation work is physical outdoor labor—planting trees, fighting fires, maintaining trails, and managing forest land. Digital AI has negligible exposure to this occupation.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Forest workers perform physical labor in highly unstructured outdoor environments. The unpredictable terrain and varied tasks make robotic deployment extremely challenging by 2028.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Outdoor work in highly variable natural environments. Tasks include planting, trail maintenance, and fire management in forests with diverse terrain. Some planting operations automated on cleared land, but most forest work requires human adaptability to unpredictable natural conditions.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Outdoor work in unstructured natural environments—every forest site is different. By 2036, automated equipment handles some routine operations, but the variable terrain, weather conditions, and ecological judgment required in conservation work keep significant human involvement.
adoption_friction_rationale: Government agencies and logging companies. Physical outdoor work in varied terrain. Limited technology infrastructure in remote forest locations. Moderate employer fragmentation. Environmental regulations require human judgment. Some mechanization already in logging but conservation work requires fieldcraft.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Physical outdoor work resists automation. Demand tied to forestry and conservation programs, which grow modestly with environmental awareness. Climate change increases need for forest management.

title: Fundraisers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Predominantly digital: researching donors, writing grant proposals, designing promotional materials, managing donor databases, and coordinating campaigns. AI significantly assists with prospect research, proposal drafting, and campaign analytics by 2028. In-person relationship building provides some insulation.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Donor research, campaign analytics, communication drafting, and database management are digital tasks AI handles well. Human fundraisers focus on major donor relationships, event hosting, and strategic campaign direction, but routine outreach is automated.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates prospect research, campaign analytics, grant writing, donor communications, and event planning logistics. However, major gift fundraising depends on building deep personal relationships with donors, and the interpersonal persuasion and trust-building aspects retain human fundraisers.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Fundraisers organize campaigns and solicit donations. Interpersonal and strategic work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Interpersonal and strategic work involving donor relations and campaign planning. Entirely knowledge and relationship based.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Entirely interpersonal and strategic work. No physical component for robotic automation.
adoption_friction_rationale: Mix of large nonprofits and hospitals (lower friction) and small nonprofits (higher friction). Relationship-driven work with strong donor preference for human connection. AI tools for prospect research and analytics already used. Moderate employer fragmentation. Major gift fundraising is deeply personal.
demand_elasticity_rationale: AI tools enable more personalized outreach and donor identification, but the relationship-building core of fundraising requires human connection. Nonprofit sector growth and growing charitable giving create expanding demand.

title: Funeral service workers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Core work is interpersonal and physical: comforting families, coordinating ceremonies, preparing remains, and managing logistics. Administrative tasks like scheduling and documentation have digital components, but the deeply personal and hands-on nature of funeral service dominates.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Preparing bodies, coordinating ceremonies, and supporting grieving families are physical and deeply interpersonal duties. AI assists with administrative tasks and scheduling, but the core service is human-centered.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Funeral service is a deeply interpersonal and physical occupation—preparing remains, coordinating ceremonies, and supporting grieving families. AI assists with administrative tasks and documentation, but the human compassion and physical service delivery are the core product.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Funeral workers prepare bodies and manage services. The sensitive nature of the work and varied procedures limit robotic involvement, though some preparation tasks are semi-structured.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Sensitive service work requiring extreme interpersonal care and trust. Physical tasks include preparation and ceremony management, but the human sensitivity and trust required makes this highly resistant to automation. Each service is unique and emotionally charged.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Funeral services involve intimate human care, emotional sensitivity, and handling of deceased with dignity. By 2036, some preparation procedures may be partially automated, but the deeply personal and emotional nature of the work, along with the physical care requiring human sensitivity, keeps this predominantly human.
adoption_friction_rationale: Extremely high social/emotional barriers to automation. Families expect human empathy and care during bereavement. State licensing requirements. Fragmented industry of independent funeral homes. Strong cultural and religious traditions around death care. Limited economic incentive for automation.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Demand tied to death rate, which is relatively fixed and predictable. Growing preference for simpler services and direct cremation reduces service intensity per death. Limited scope for AI to expand demand.

title: Gambling services workers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Predominantly in-person service: dealing cards, operating gaming equipment, interacting with patrons, and monitoring gaming tables. Surveillance and cash management systems are digital tools, but the physical casino floor presence and customer interaction dominate.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Operating gaming tables, managing slot machines, and interacting with patrons are primarily physical and interpersonal. AI aids with surveillance and analytics, but floor operations remain human-staffed.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Casino and gambling work involves physical presence—dealing cards, operating gaming equipment, and providing customer service on the casino floor. AI automates surveillance and some customer analytics, but the physical and interpersonal aspects of the role remain.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Gambling workers operate games and manage equipment in casino settings. While casinos are structured, the interpersonal nature of table games and varied customer interactions limit robotic exposure.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Casino floor work involving equipment operation and customer interaction. Some gaming operations (slot machine monitoring) increasingly automated. Table game dealers require dexterity and customer engagement. The entertainment and hospitality aspects resist full automation.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Casino and gaming operations involve equipment operation and customer interaction in structured environments. By 2036, many gaming floor operations are automated (slot machines, automated table games), but the customer service and entertainment aspects retain human presence.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large casino companies (MGM, Caesars) are primary employers with resources and incentive to adopt technology. Gaming commissions regulate operations. Some positions (dealers) have social/entertainment value. Electronic gaming already dominant. Sports betting increasingly automated.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Casino and gaming demand grows modestly with entertainment spending. Some roles (dealers) resist automation due to customer interaction, while others (cage operations) face automation pressure. Net roughly neutral.

title: General maintenance and repair workers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Almost entirely physical: fixing machines, repairing plumbing, painting, maintaining electrical systems, and performing general building upkeep. Work order management is a minor digital component. AI has negligible impact on the hands-on repair work.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Fixing plumbing, electrical, HVAC, and other building systems is hands-on physical work. AI assists with scheduling and diagnostics, but manual repair remains entirely human.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: General maintenance is entirely hands-on physical work—fixing plumbing, electrical issues, painting, and performing building repairs. Digital AI has minimal exposure beyond work order management systems.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: General maintenance workers handle diverse, unpredictable repair tasks across buildings and facilities. The extreme variety of tasks and environments makes this one of the hardest roles for robots to automate.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Variable work across many building systems—plumbing, electrical, HVAC, painting. Each repair is different. Some routine maintenance tasks (cleaning, basic checks) automated, but the variety of problems and environments encountered by general maintenance workers requires human adaptability.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Wide variety of repair tasks in variable building environments. By 2036, robots handle many routine maintenance tasks (changing filters, basic plumbing, painting), but the extreme variability of maintenance requests across diverse buildings and systems requires human adaptability for novel problems.
adoption_friction_rationale: Extremely varied work across many different building systems and conditions. Large property management companies and institutions are major employers but work environments are highly variable. OSHA and building regulations. Labour shortages provide pull but task diversity challenges robotics.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Physical repair and maintenance of buildings resists automation. Demand tied to the building stock, which grows slowly. AI diagnostics may improve efficiency but the hands-on work persists across varied tasks.

title: General office clerks
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Almost entirely screen-based: answering phones, typing documents, filing records, managing correspondence, and data entry. AI automation handles most routine clerical tasks by 2028, including document processing, scheduling, and correspondence. Active displacement occurring in basic office clerk positions.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Filing, data entry, correspondence, scheduling, and record-keeping are routine digital tasks that AI agents automate almost entirely by 2031. Only tasks requiring physical office presence or complex judgment remain.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Filing, data entry, mail processing, scheduling, and routine administrative tasks are entirely digital routine work that AI handles end-to-end by 2036. This occupation has effectively ceased to exist in its traditional form.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Office clerks perform general administrative tasks. Desk-based clerical work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Office-based administrative work that is entirely knowledge-based. Filing, data entry, and correspondence. No physical component beyond basic office activities.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Entirely office-based administrative work. No physical component for robotic automation.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large employers across all sectors. Work is highly standardized and administrative. Extensive automation already in place with office software and RPA. Clear ROI. Minimal regulatory barriers. Role has been declining for decades due to technology adoption.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Routine clerical tasks (filing, data entry, scheduling, copying) are directly automated by AI and office software. The generalist nature of the role means AI can handle most individual tasks. Significant headcount reduction is ongoing.

title: Genetic counselors
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: A blend of interpersonal counseling (supporting families, explaining genetic risks, guiding decisions) and digital analysis (reviewing genetic test results, researching conditions). AI assists with test interpretation and risk assessment by 2028, but the empathetic patient counseling and complex decision support remain human.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: AI assists with genetic data interpretation and risk calculation. However, counseling patients about genetic conditions, emotional support during difficult diagnoses, and helping families make complex decisions require deep human empathy and communication.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates genetic data interpretation, risk calculation, and report generation. However, genetic counseling is fundamentally interpersonal—helping patients understand complex genetic information, supporting emotional responses to results, and guiding reproductive and health decisions.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Genetic counselors provide consultation and education to patients about genetic conditions. This is entirely knowledge and interpersonal work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Patient-facing counseling work that is entirely interpersonal and knowledge-based. No physical component.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Entirely cognitive and interpersonal counseling work. No physical component.
adoption_friction_rationale: Healthcare regulation and state licensing. Mostly employed by hospital systems and specialty clinics. Role involves complex emotional counseling alongside scientific interpretation. Patient preference for human counselor in sensitive genetic decisions. Growing field with established professional standards.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Enormous unmet demand for genetic counseling as genomic testing becomes cheaper and more common. Most people could benefit from genetic risk assessment but access is limited. AI tools help counselors interpret more complex genetic data and serve more patients.

title: Geographers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Predominantly digital: using GIS tools, analyzing spatial data, writing research reports, and creating maps and visualizations. AI significantly assists with geospatial data analysis and pattern detection by 2028. Some fieldwork provides non-digital balance, but the role is heavily screen-based.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: GIS analysis, spatial data processing, map production, and research synthesis are heavily digital tasks AI agents handle well. Fieldwork and complex place-based analysis retain human value, but analytical productivity increases dramatically.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Geographic data analysis, mapping, spatial modeling, and research synthesis are highly digital tasks AI handles autonomously. Human geographers remain for fieldwork, novel research questions about human-environment interactions, and policy advising in complex socio-spatial contexts.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Geographers study Earth's features and human-geographic relationships. Knowledge-based research work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Research and analysis work. Primarily desk-based knowledge work using GIS and data analysis.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Primarily research and analytical work. Minimal physical fieldwork; mostly computational and GIS-based.
adoption_friction_rationale: Government agencies and tech companies are primary employers. GIS analysis is highly amenable to AI. Remote sensing and spatial analysis already heavily computerized. Academic institutional inertia for university-based geographers. Moderate employer consolidation. Limited regulatory barriers.
demand_elasticity_rationale: AI and geospatial analytics expand applications of geographic analysis. Climate change, urban planning, and logistics optimization all need geographic expertise. Growing demand for spatial analysis across industries.

title: Geological and hydrologic technicians
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: A blend of fieldwork (collecting samples, operating monitoring equipment, conducting surveys) and digital tasks (analyzing data, preparing reports, using GIS tools). AI assists with data analysis and mapping, but physical field operations and sample collection remain central.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Field sampling and laboratory testing are physical, but data analysis, mapping, and reporting are digital tasks aided by AI. The mixed nature of duties creates moderate exposure.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates data analysis and modeling. However, the role involves significant fieldwork—collecting rock and water samples, operating monitoring equipment, and conducting site surveys—that requires physical presence.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Geological techs collect field samples and perform lab analysis. Some physical fieldwork in variable conditions, but primarily technical support.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Field work collecting samples and operating equipment in variable geological environments. Each site has unique conditions. While automated sensors and drilling equipment handle some routine operations, field work in diverse terrain requires human adaptability.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Field sampling and testing in variable geological environments. By 2036, automated sampling equipment handles routine collection, but working in novel geological settings and interpreting site conditions still requires human judgment and physical presence.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large oil and gas companies and geological survey agencies are primary employers with resources to adopt. Field sampling requires physical presence. Lab analysis increasingly automated. Moderate regulatory requirements. Industry has existing technology adoption culture.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Petroleum industry faces long-term decline. AI automates much data analysis in geological surveys. Some shift toward renewable energy and environmental monitoring, but net demand for petroleum-specific roles declines.

title: Geoscientists
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: A mix of field research (collecting rock samples, conducting surveys) and digital knowledge work (analyzing geological data, modeling, writing reports). AI assists with data interpretation and simulation by 2028, balanced by essential fieldwork and physical sample analysis.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Data analysis, modeling, literature review, and report writing are digital tasks increasingly automated. Fieldwork, site-specific geological interpretation, and stakeholder consultation retain human value.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates data analysis, geological modeling, seismic interpretation, and report writing. Human geoscientists remain for fieldwork, novel geological interpretation, cross-disciplinary research, and advising on complex environmental and resource extraction decisions.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Geoscientists study Earth's physical aspects. Knowledge-based research with some fieldwork, but primarily analytical.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Research work with some fieldwork. The role is primarily about scientific analysis and interpretation rather than physical labor.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Primarily research and analytical work with some fieldwork. Physical field components are partially automatable, but the core scientific analysis is cognitive.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large energy companies, mining firms, and government agencies are primary employers. AI/ML for geological modeling advancing rapidly. Field work requires physical presence. Professional licensing in some states. Moderate institutional inertia in government settings. Clear ROI for resource exploration.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Petroleum geoscience demand declines while environmental and mineral geoscience grows. AI enables more sophisticated modeling but the field is transitioning. Net roughly neutral as new applications offset declining oil/gas work.

title: Glaziers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Entirely physical skilled trade work: cutting glass, installing windows, removing old glass, and working at heights. Blueprint reading is a minor reference task. AI has no meaningful impact on this manual construction trade.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Cutting, fitting, and installing glass in buildings is entirely physical skilled trade work with no meaningful digital component.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Glazing is entirely physical skilled trade work—cutting, fitting, and installing glass in buildings and vehicles. Digital AI has essentially no exposure to this occupation.
