physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Glaziers install glass in varied building environments requiring precise fitting and handling of fragile materials. The variable work sites and need for careful dexterity limit robotic deployment by 2028.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Installation of glass in variable buildings and structures. Each installation is different. Working with fragile materials at heights and in diverse configurations requires human dexterity and judgment. Some large commercial installations see limited automation for standard windows.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Glass installation involves working with heavy, fragile materials in variable building environments. By 2036, robots assist with large commercial installations, but residential work, renovation, and custom configurations still require human dexterity and judgment.
adoption_friction_rationale: Fragmented construction trade with many small contractors. Physical installation of glass in varied building conditions. Union presence in commercial sector (IUPAT). Limited capital among small operators. Each installation is unique. Labour shortages provide some pull but jobsite conditions challenge robotics.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Physical glass installation resists automation. Demand tied to construction activity. Growing demand for energy-efficient windows and smart glass provides modest growth. AI has minimal direct impact.

title: Graphic designers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Almost entirely screen-based: creating visual concepts using design software, developing layouts for ads, brochures, and digital media. AI image generation and design tools by 2028 handle much of template and production design work. Active restructuring in production-level graphic design roles.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: AI generates logos, layouts, illustrations, and brand materials at high quality by 2031. Senior designers retain creative direction and brand strategy roles, but production design work is largely automated, dramatically reducing team sizes.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI generates logos, layouts, illustrations, and complete design systems from briefs. By 2036, routine graphic design is fully automated. Human designers persist in creative director roles where human artistic vision and brand authorship are premium, and in highly novel or culturally sensitive design contexts.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Graphic designers create visual content using design software. Desk-based creative work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Entirely digital creative work. No physical component.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Entirely digital creative work. No physical component for robotic automation.
adoption_friction_rationale: Mix of large agencies and many freelancers. AI design tools (Midjourney, DALL-E, Canva AI) already widely adopted. Clear ROI for corporate clients. Digital workflow facilitates AI integration. Some creative judgment still valued but routine design work rapidly automating. Large employer segment adopts quickly.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Massive latent demand for professional design. Every small business, every social media account, every product wants good design. AI tools make designers more productive and enable serving clients who couldn't previously afford design services.

title: Grounds maintenance workers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Entirely physical outdoor work: mowing lawns, pruning shrubs, planting flowers, removing snow, and maintaining landscapes. This is among the most purely physical occupations with no digital component that AI could affect.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Mowing lawns, trimming hedges, planting flowers, and maintaining outdoor spaces are entirely physical tasks. AI has essentially zero impact on grounds maintenance labor.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Grounds maintenance is entirely physical outdoor work—mowing, trimming, planting, and maintaining landscapes. Digital AI has essentially no exposure to this occupation.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Grounds maintenance includes mowing, trimming, and landscaping in semi-structured outdoor environments. Robotic mowers are commercially available and some tasks are automatable, but varied landscaping work limits full exposure.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Commercial lawn mowing and landscape maintenance increasingly automated with robotic mowers and autonomous equipment for large, uniform areas. However, complex landscaping, garden maintenance, and work on varied residential properties still requires human workers. Large commercial grounds substantially automated.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: By 2036, robotic mowing, trimming, and basic landscaping of uniform areas is widespread. Autonomous grounds maintenance equipment handles most routine tasks. Human workers remain for complex landscape design implementation and genuinely novel environments.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large property management companies and municipalities are major employers. Robotic mowing and autonomous equipment already commercial. Severe labour shortages provide strong pull. Minimal regulatory barriers. Landscaping work in structured environments is amenable to automation. Some fragmented residential segment.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Physical outdoor maintenance work resists automation in varied environments. Robotic mowers handle some lawn care but landscaping and grounds work requires human judgment. Demand tied to property stock.

title: Hand laborers and material movers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Entirely physical work: moving freight, loading trucks, stacking materials, and cleaning vehicles by hand. This is one of the most purely manual occupations with no meaningful digital component.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Moving materials by hand, loading trucks, and stocking shelves are entirely physical labor tasks. AI has essentially zero impact on these manual duties.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: This is entirely physical manual labor—loading, unloading, and moving materials by hand or with basic equipment. Digital AI has no meaningful exposure to this occupation.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Material movers in warehouses and factories perform repetitive lifting and transport tasks in structured environments. Humanoid robots and AMRs are being commercially deployed for these tasks in large facilities by 2028.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Warehouse and logistics material handling heavily automated with robotic systems. Palletizing, sorting, and transport within facilities largely robotic. Human workers handle exceptions, irregularly shaped items, and tasks in non-standardized environments. High-volume facilities operate with minimal human labor.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: By 2036, material handling in warehouses, factories, and loading docks is overwhelmingly automated. Robotic lifting, sorting, and moving equipment handles the vast majority of tasks. Human involvement is marginal—supervisory and for genuinely unusual items or situations.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large warehouse and logistics companies (Amazon, UPS) are primary employers with massive investment in automation. Acute labour shortages. Clear ROI. Robotic material handling already widely deployed. Minimal regulatory barriers. Repetitive physical work in controlled environments.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Warehouse automation and robotics directly replace material handling tasks. AI-optimized logistics reduces unnecessary movement. Amazon and others invest heavily in automated fulfillment. Physical work persists but headcount declines.

title: Hazardous materials removal workers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Almost entirely physical: identifying and disposing of hazardous substances, using protective equipment, and following strict safety protocols. Documentation and compliance records are minor digital components. The dangerous hands-on work cannot be automated by AI.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Identifying, removing, and disposing of hazardous materials like asbestos and lead is dangerous physical work requiring protective equipment and manual procedures. AI has negligible impact.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Hazmat removal is physical, dangerous work—identifying, containing, and removing hazardous materials using protective equipment. Digital AI has negligible exposure beyond safety documentation.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Hazmat workers remove dangerous materials from varied sites. While robots could assist in hazardous environments, the unpredictable conditions and varied sites limit deployment by 2028.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Removal work in variable and dangerous environments. Each hazmat site is unique. Robotic systems handle some hazmat cleanup (especially radiation), but many situations require human judgment and dexterity in complex, confined spaces. Safety regulations evolving to allow more robotic intervention.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Hazmat work involves variable and dangerous environments. By 2036, robotic systems handle many routine hazmat removal tasks (asbestos, lead paint in accessible areas), but complex contamination scenarios in unstructured environments still require human judgment. The danger actually accelerates robot adoption.
adoption_friction_rationale: Safety-critical work with EPA and OSHA regulations. Large environmental remediation firms and government contracts. Hazardous conditions actually favor robotic deployment. Labour shortages and worker safety concerns provide pull. Regulatory frameworks would need updating but economic incentive is clear.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Demand tied to environmental remediation projects and regulations. Physical hazmat work in dangerous environments resists automation. Volume determined by contamination sites and regulatory requirements.

title: Health and safety engineers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Substantial digital work: analyzing safety data, designing safety systems, writing reports, and evaluating compliance with regulations. AI assists with risk modeling, incident analysis, and compliance monitoring by 2028. Physical site inspections and investigations provide non-digital balance.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Risk analysis, compliance documentation, and safety system design are digital tasks AI handles well. However, physical site inspections, accident investigations, and implementing safety measures in real environments require human presence.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates risk analysis, regulatory compliance checking, incident data analysis, and safety documentation. However, on-site inspections, workplace assessments, and working with management to implement safety changes require physical presence and interpersonal skills.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Health and safety engineers design safety systems and procedures. Knowledge-based engineering work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Engineering design and analysis work focused on workplace safety. Primarily knowledge-based with some facility inspections.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Primarily analytical and design work focused on workplace safety systems. Site inspections have minor physical components, but core role is cognitive engineering and regulatory compliance.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large corporations and government agencies (OSHA) are primary employers. Analysis and compliance work amenable to AI. Professional licensing and liability concerns. Physical site inspection requires human presence. Moderate institutional inertia. Regulatory complexity both drives and hinders automation.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Growing regulatory complexity and workplace safety requirements. AI enables more comprehensive safety analysis and monitoring. New technologies (AI systems, autonomous vehicles) create new safety engineering domains.

title: Health education specialists
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: A mix of interpersonal community work (conducting workshops, training, outreach) and digital tasks (developing educational materials, analyzing health data, writing reports). AI assists with content creation and data analysis by 2028, but face-to-face community engagement remains essential.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: AI generates health education content, analyzes community health data, and personalizes outreach materials. However, community engagement, workshop facilitation, and culturally sensitive health communication require human presence and interpersonal skills.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates content creation, program design, data analysis, and health communication materials. However, community outreach, group facilitation, cultural adaptation of health messages, and building relationships with underserved populations retain significant human roles.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Health education specialists develop programs and materials to promote health. This is knowledge and communication work with no physical labor.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Educational and outreach work that is entirely interpersonal and knowledge-based. No physical component.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Entirely educational and interpersonal work. No physical component for robotic automation.
adoption_friction_rationale: Government agencies, nonprofits, and healthcare systems. Community health education requires human connection and cultural competency. Moderate employer fragmentation. Some digital health education tools already in use. Institutional inertia in public health. Behavioral change work requires human empathy.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Enormous unmet demand for health education, particularly in underserved communities. AI tools help educators create personalized programs and reach more people. Preventive health education reduces downstream healthcare costs.

title: Health information technologists and medical registrars
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Almost entirely screen-based: managing electronic health records, analyzing clinical data, ensuring coding accuracy, and advising on healthcare IT systems. AI significantly automates data coding, quality checking, and system management by 2028. Active headcount pressure in routine health information roles.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Coding medical records, managing health databases, ensuring data quality, and processing registrations are routine digital tasks AI agents automate almost entirely. Only complex coding disputes and system implementation require human oversight.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Medical coding, record classification, data management, and health information system administration are structured digital tasks AI handles autonomously. The remaining human role is in complex case coding disputes and system governance decisions.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Health IT workers manage electronic health records and medical data systems. Their work is purely knowledge-based and computer-oriented with no physical labor for robots to automate.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Office-based health data management work. Entirely digital and knowledge-based.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Entirely digital/data management work. No physical component.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large hospital systems and health organizations are primary employers. Work is data-driven and highly amenable to AI and automation. HIPAA regulations create compliance requirements but don't prevent automation. EHR systems already heavily computerized. Clear ROI for AI integration.
demand_elasticity_rationale: AI automates much health data coding, classification, and registry management. The volume of health records grows but automated processing reduces headcount per record. Electronic health records continue to automate workflows.

title: Heating, air conditioning, and refrigeration mechanics and installers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Predominantly hands-on: installing, maintaining, and repairing HVAC systems using hand tools and testing equipment. Computerized diagnostics assist with troubleshooting, but the physical installation and repair work in buildings dominates. AI has minimal direct impact.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Installing and repairing HVAC systems is hands-on skilled trade work. AI aids with diagnostics and system design, but physical installation and repair remain entirely human tasks.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: HVAC work is hands-on physical skilled trade work—installing, repairing, and maintaining heating and cooling systems. AI assists with diagnostics, but the physical installation and repair work remains entirely human.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: HVAC technicians install and repair systems in varied buildings with different configurations. The unpredictable access conditions and diagnostic requirements make robotic replacement impractical by 2028.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Installation and repair in variable buildings and environments. Each system and building presents unique challenges. Working in tight spaces (attics, crawlspaces) with diverse equipment configurations requires human dexterity and problem-solving. Some standardized commercial installations see limited automation.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: HVAC work involves variable building environments and diverse equipment configurations. By 2036, robots handle standardized new-construction installations, but diagnosing problems in existing systems and working in varied building spaces (attics, crawlspaces, rooftops) requires human judgment and adaptability.
adoption_friction_rationale: Highly fragmented between large HVAC companies and many independent operators. Physical work in varied building conditions. EPA Section 608 certification for refrigerants. Acute labour shortages provide pull but physical installation and repair in confined spaces challenges robotics. State licensing requirements.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Growing demand from climate change (more AC), heat pump adoption, and building electrification. Physical installation and repair work resists automation. Persistent labor shortages indicate unmet demand.

title: Heavy and tractor-trailer truck drivers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Core work is physical: operating heavy vehicles, managing cargo, performing pre-trip inspections, and navigating routes. GPS and electronic logging are digital tools, but the fundamental task of driving large vehicles safely requires physical presence. Autonomous trucking remains limited by 2028.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Long-haul driving remains primarily human at the 2031 horizon despite autonomous trucking advances. Route planning and logistics benefit from AI, but operating trucks in varied conditions, loading/unloading, and regulatory compliance keep drivers essential.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Truck driving is a physical operation role. While autonomous vehicle technology may transform this occupation, that represents physical automation rather than digital AI exposure. Digital AI exposure is limited to route planning and logging systems.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Long-haul trucking on interstate corridors is in advanced autonomous commercial pilots by 2028. However, most routes still require human drivers for last-mile, urban segments, and non-highway portions.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Autonomous trucks operational on most interstate routes by 2031. Highway driving largely automated. However, complex urban delivery, loading/unloading, and last-mile navigation still require human drivers for many scenarios. Human role shifting toward complex route segments and customer interaction.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: By 2036, autonomous long-haul trucking on mapped highways is the norm. Human drivers remain primarily for unmapped last-mile delivery, extreme weather, and genuinely novel route conditions. The vast majority of interstate freight moves autonomously.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large fleet operators (J.B. Hunt, Werner, Schneider) have resources for autonomous trucks. Severe driver shortage creates massive economic pull. Highway driving is most amenable to autonomy. DOT/FMCSA regulations will need updating but industry lobbying is strong. Teamsters union provides some friction.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Autonomous trucking technology threatens long-haul driving. Freight demand grows but autonomous trucks will handle increasing portions of highway miles. Last-mile and local delivery may persist longer for human drivers.

title: Heavy vehicle and mobile equipment service technicians
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Predominantly hands-on: inspecting, maintaining, and repairing heavy construction and farming equipment. Computerized diagnostic tools assist with troubleshooting, but the physical repair and maintenance work dominates. AI cannot perform manual mechanical repairs.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Repairing and maintaining heavy equipment—bulldozers, cranes, farm machinery—is physical skilled work. AI assists with diagnostics, but hands-on mechanical repair remains human.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Repairing and maintaining heavy vehicles and construction equipment is hands-on physical mechanical work. AI assists with diagnostics, but the physical repair work in shops and on job sites remains human.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Heavy equipment mechanics work on diverse large machines with varied repair needs. The unstructured environments and diagnostic judgment required are beyond 2028 robotic capabilities.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Repair and maintenance of large, diverse equipment in variable settings—construction sites, mines, farms. Each machine and problem is different. Working on heavy equipment requires significant physical effort and skilled diagnosis in variable environments.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Maintaining heavy equipment involves physical work on large, variable machines in diverse environments. By 2036, diagnostic automation and robotic maintenance assist with routine service, but field repairs on diverse equipment in variable conditions require significant human involvement.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large fleet operators and equipment dealers are major employers. Physical repair of heavy equipment in varied conditions requires dexterity and judgment. ASE and manufacturer certifications. Labour shortages provide pull. Equipment diversity challenges standardized robotic repair solutions.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Physical equipment maintenance resists automation. Demand tied to the fleet of heavy vehicles and equipment. Transition to electric equipment may eventually change maintenance needs but the timeline is long.

title: High school teachers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Core work is interpersonal: classroom instruction, student engagement, maintaining discipline, and parent communication. Lesson planning, grading, and curriculum development benefit from AI tools by 2028, but the face-to-face teaching relationship and classroom management remain fundamentally human.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: AI tutoring systems handle content delivery, grading, and personalized learning paths. Teachers shift to mentoring, social-emotional development, classroom management, and facilitating higher-order discussions—roles that remain deeply human.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates content delivery, lesson planning, assessment creation and grading, and personalized learning pathways. However, mentoring adolescents, classroom management, social-emotional development, and the human relationship at the core of effective teaching preserve substantial human roles.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Teaching is fundamentally interpersonal and cognitive work involving instruction, mentoring, and classroom management. There is no physical labor component for robots to automate.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Teaching is fundamentally interpersonal work. Classroom instruction, mentoring, and student engagement require human presence and judgment. No significant physical automation potential.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Teaching is fundamentally about human relationships, mentoring, and adaptive instruction. Physical classroom presence, managing student behavior, and providing emotional support are central. Minimal physical task content for robots; the human connection is the value.
adoption_friction_rationale: Government employment with strong unions and deep institutional inertia. State certification requirements. Strong social preference for human teachers, especially for adolescents. Classroom management requires human presence and judgment. Moderate technology adoption in curriculum but teaching role resists replacement.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Class sizes could be reduced if AI makes teachers more productive, improving education quality. Growing population in some areas and persistent teacher shortages indicate unmet demand. AI tutoring supplements but doesn't replace teachers.

title: Historians
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Predominantly digital knowledge work: researching archives, analyzing historical documents, writing reports and publications, and presenting findings. AI significantly assists with document analysis, literature review, and drafting by 2028. Some physical archival research remains, but the work is heavily text-based.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Archival research, source analysis, literature synthesis, and writing are heavily digital tasks AI assists with substantially. Historians retain value in interpretive frameworks, original arguments, and contextualizing complex historical narratives.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates archival research, source analysis, literature synthesis, and narrative drafting. Human historians remain for genuinely novel interpretive frameworks, evaluating contested historical narratives requiring cultural sensitivity, and scholarly work where human authorship and perspective are valued.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Historians research and analyze historical events. Entirely knowledge-based research work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Research and analysis work that is entirely knowledge-based. No physical component.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Entirely research and analytical work. No physical component.
adoption_friction_rationale: Primarily academic and museum employment with strong institutional inertia. Research involves interpretive judgment and archival work. AI tools for text analysis emerging but humanistic interpretation is central. Fragmented employment across universities and cultural institutions. Limited technology budgets.
demand_elasticity_rationale: AI tools enable analysis of vastly larger historical archives and datasets. Growing demand for historical context in policy debates, cultural preservation, and public education. Digital humanities expand the field's applications.

title: Home health and personal care aides
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Almost entirely physical and interpersonal: assisting with daily activities like bathing, dressing, meal preparation, and monitoring patient conditions. Documentation is a minor digital component. AI cannot replace the hands-on personal care that defines this role.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Assisting patients with bathing, dressing, meals, and daily activities is entirely physical and interpersonal caregiving. AI has minimal impact on these hands-on personal care duties.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Home health care is entirely physical and interpersonal—bathing, dressing, feeding, and providing companionship to elderly and disabled individuals in their homes. Digital AI has minimal exposure beyond scheduling and care documentation.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Home health aides provide personal care in diverse residential settings with highly variable patient needs. The unstructured home environments and intimate care requirements are beyond 2028 robotic capabilities.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Routine physical support tasks (lifting, transfers, mobility assistance) see some robotic assistance. However, working in diverse home environments with unique patient needs and the trust required for intimate personal care limits automation. Robotic assistive devices supplement but don't replace human aides.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: By 2036, home-care robots handle routine physical tasks—mobility assistance, medication management, household chores. However, the emotional support, human dignity in intimate personal care (bathing, toileting), and adaptive response to varied home environments keep significant human involvement. Robot assistance reduces but doesn't eliminate the human role.
adoption_friction_rationale: Severe labour shortages create enormous pull for automation. But highly fragmented employer base of small agencies and individual households. Physical caregiving in home environments challenges robotics. State regulations vary. Patients prefer human caregivers. Low wages limit technology investment but demographic crisis accelerates change.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Massive unmet demand driven by aging population. Most elderly who need home care can't afford it. AI monitoring tools can extend the reach of each aide. The physical, compassionate nature of the work resists automation.

title: Human resources managers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Predominantly digital knowledge work: overseeing recruitment, managing HRIS systems, developing policies, and analyzing workforce data. AI assists with resume screening, benefits analysis, and compliance monitoring by 2028. Strategic leadership, employee relations, and organizational development remain human-driven.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Recruitment screening, benefits administration, compliance tracking, and workforce analytics are heavily automated. HR managers retain strategic workforce planning, employee relations, organizational culture, and complex conflict resolution roles.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates HR analytics, policy drafting, compliance monitoring, compensation analysis, and recruitment screening. Human HR managers remain for sensitive employee relations, organizational culture leadership, executive coaching, and navigating complex interpersonal workplace dynamics.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: HR managers oversee personnel policies and recruiting. Managerial knowledge work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Management and strategic planning work that is entirely knowledge and interpersonal based. No physical component.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Entirely management and interpersonal work. No physical component.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large corporations are primary employers with HR technology already well-adopted. Strategic HR management requires human judgment. AI tools for analytics, recruitment, and benefits widely used. Moderate regulatory complexity (employment law) but manageable. Some friction from sensitivity of personnel decisions.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Each organization needs HR management, scaling with organization count not individual productivity. AI automates recruitment screening and benefits administration, but strategic HR leadership persists. Roughly neutral.

title: Human resources specialists
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Predominantly screen-based: screening resumes, scheduling interviews, processing benefits, maintaining employee records, and drafting communications. AI significantly automates resume screening, onboarding paperwork, and benefits administration by 2028. In-person interviewing and employee relations provide some insulation.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Resume screening, onboarding documentation, benefits processing, and policy administration are routine digital tasks AI agents handle autonomously. Human specialists focus on complex employee relations, investigations, and strategic talent initiatives.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Recruiting, screening, onboarding documentation, benefits administration, and compliance tasks are automated by AI. Human specialists remain for sensitive employee conversations, complex workplace investigations, and situations requiring interpersonal judgment and empathy.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: HR specialists handle recruiting and employee relations. Administrative and interpersonal work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Administrative and interpersonal work involving recruitment, employee relations, and compliance. No physical component.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Entirely administrative and interpersonal work. No physical component.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large corporations are primary employers with extensive HR tech adoption. Recruiting, onboarding, and benefits administration already heavily automated. AI tools for resume screening and scheduling widespread. Clear ROI. Employment law compliance actually drives automation. Moderate social friction for sensitive interactions.
demand_elasticity_rationale: AI automates resume screening, initial candidate assessment, and benefits enrollment. The transactional portions of HR work shrink. Strategic HR work persists but requires fewer specialists per organization.

title: Hydrologists
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: A mix of fieldwork (measuring water properties, collecting samples) and heavily digital analysis (modeling water systems, analyzing data, writing reports). AI assists with hydrological modeling and data analysis by 2028, but field research and site-specific judgment remain important.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Water resource modeling, data analysis, and report writing are digital tasks AI handles well. Fieldwork, site-specific assessment, and stakeholder consultation on water management retain human value.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Water resource modeling, data analysis, environmental impact calculations, and report writing are automated. Human hydrologists remain for fieldwork, novel watershed challenges, stakeholder engagement in water policy, and interpreting complex environmental systems.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Hydrologists study water distribution and flow. Knowledge-based scientific work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Scientific research and analysis work. Primarily desk-based with some fieldwork, but the role centers on data analysis and modeling.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Research and analytical work with some fieldwork in natural water systems. By 2036, automated monitoring handles routine data collection, but the core work is cognitive analysis and modeling.
adoption_friction_rationale: Government agencies and environmental firms are primary employers. Modeling and data analysis amenable to AI. Field work requires physical presence for monitoring. Moderate institutional inertia in government. Environmental regulations require human judgment for assessments. Limited regulatory barriers for AI tools.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Climate change increases demand for water resource analysis and flood prediction. AI enables more sophisticated hydrological modeling. Growing water scarcity concerns drive investment in water management science.

title: Industrial designers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Predominantly digital: using CAD/CAM software, creating 3D renderings, developing product specifications, and preparing presentations. AI generative design tools significantly assist concept development by 2028. Physical prototyping and user research provide some non-digital balance, but the work is heavily screen-based.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: AI generates product design concepts, 3D models, and renderings rapidly. Designers shift to user research, creative vision, physical prototyping, and brand-specific design judgment, but design production teams shrink significantly.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI generates design concepts, 3D models, and specifications from requirements. Human designers retain value for novel product innovation, understanding ergonomic and cultural nuances through physical prototyping, and creative vision where human authorship differentiates products.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Industrial designers develop product concepts and designs. Creative knowledge work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Creative design work with some physical prototyping. The core work is conceptual design using digital tools. 3D printing and automated prototyping reduce physical work, but design ideation remains human.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Primarily creative design work with some physical prototyping. By 2036, 3D printing and robotic prototyping assist, but the creative vision and ergonomic judgment are cognitive. Some hands-on material testing remains.
adoption_friction_rationale: Mix of large manufacturers and design consultancies. AI-assisted design and generative design tools advancing rapidly. Creative vision still valued but routine design tasks automating. Moderate employer fragmentation. Existing digital workflow facilitates AI integration. Some professional judgment still required.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Every product could benefit from better design. AI tools accelerate the design process and enable rapid prototyping. Growing consumer expectations for well-designed products and the maker economy expand demand.

title: Industrial engineering technologists and technicians
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: A blend of physical production floor work (studying workflows, conducting time studies, inspecting processes) and digital tasks (analyzing data, preparing reports, using statistical software). AI assists with data analysis and process optimization by 2028.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Data collection on production floors is physical, but process analysis, time studies, and documentation are digital tasks AI aids with. The blend of hands-on manufacturing observation and digital analysis creates moderate exposure.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates time studies, process analysis, workflow optimization, and documentation. However, physical plant observation, equipment testing, and hands-on implementation of efficiency improvements on manufacturing floors retain human roles.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Industrial engineering techs assist with factory layout and process improvement, involving some physical work in manufacturing environments. The structured factory setting offers moderate physical exposure.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Technical work in manufacturing environments involving process testing and optimization. Some routine testing automated, but troubleshooting and process improvement in diverse industrial settings requires human analysis and physical presence.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Work involves testing equipment, monitoring production, and hands-on process optimization in factory environments. By 2036, much monitoring and testing is automated, but troubleshooting production issues in variable manufacturing contexts still requires human judgment.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large manufacturing companies are primary employers with strong automation culture. Process optimization work is highly amenable to AI. Existing technology infrastructure in manufacturing facilitates adoption. Clear ROI. Moderate regulatory requirements. Labour shortages in manufacturing provide pull.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Demand tied to manufacturing activity. AI improves process optimization but physical plant work persists. Automation creates new systems that need technician support, roughly offsetting efficiency gains.

title: Industrial engineers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Predominantly digital: designing production systems, analyzing workflows using simulation software, conducting statistical studies, and writing efficiency reports. AI copilots significantly assist with process optimization and data analysis by 2028. Factory floor observation provides some physical component.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Process optimization, workflow analysis, simulation modeling, and efficiency reporting are heavily digital tasks AI agents handle autonomously. Engineers shift to implementing changes on physical production floors and managing complex organizational transitions.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Process optimization, supply chain modeling, quality analysis, and system design are automated. Human engineers remain for on-site facility assessment, managing implementation with workers, and novel manufacturing challenges requiring cross-domain physical and organizational insight.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Industrial engineers design efficient production systems. Knowledge-based engineering work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Design and optimization of industrial processes. Primarily analytical work with some facility observation. The role is about system design rather than physical labor.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Primarily analytical and design work focused on optimizing systems and processes. Site observation and analysis but minimal physical labor. Core work is cognitive.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large manufacturers and logistics companies are primary employers with strong incentive to adopt AI for process optimization. The field itself focuses on efficiency, making AI adoption natural. AI tools for simulation and optimization already widely used. Moderate regulatory requirements.
demand_elasticity_rationale: AI creates massive new optimization opportunities across manufacturing, logistics, and services. Every process could be optimized. Historical pattern: automation increased demand for industrial engineers to design and manage automated systems.

title: Industrial machinery mechanics, machinery maintenance workers, and millwrights
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Predominantly hands-on: repairing factory equipment, dismantling machinery, replacing parts, and performing preventive maintenance. Computerized maintenance systems and diagnostics are tools used, but the physical mechanical work in industrial settings dominates.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Repairing and maintaining industrial machinery is hands-on mechanical work. AI-enhanced predictive maintenance helps scheduling, but physical repair and installation remain human tasks.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Maintaining and repairing industrial machinery is hands-on physical work in factories and plants. AI assists with predictive maintenance analytics and diagnostics, but the physical repair and installation work remains human.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Industrial machinery mechanics work in factory settings (more structured) maintaining complex equipment. While the environment is more controlled than field work, the diagnostic variety limits full automation by 2028.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Maintenance and repair of industrial machinery in factory settings. Some predictive maintenance and routine servicing automated, but troubleshooting breakdowns of diverse equipment requires human skill and judgment. Each machine and failure mode is different.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Maintaining and repairing diverse industrial machinery in variable factory environments. By 2036, predictive maintenance and robotic repair handle routine issues, but diagnosing novel equipment failures and working on varied machinery configurations requires significant human expertise.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large manufacturing facilities are primary employers. Physical repair of diverse machinery in industrial settings. Acute labour shortages provide strong pull. Predictive maintenance AI already deployed. But physical repair in varied conditions challenges robotics. OSHA safety requirements manageable.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Physical machinery maintenance resists automation. As factories add more complex automated equipment, maintenance needs grow. Demand tied to installed machinery base, which expands with automation.

title: Industrial production managers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: A blend of digital management (production planning, scheduling, budgeting, quality reporting) and physical floor oversight (inspecting production lines, supervising workers, ensuring safety). AI assists with production optimization and reporting by 2028, but on-site management remains essential.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Production scheduling, quality data analysis, and reporting benefit from AI. However, managing factory floor operations, supervising workers, and making real-time production decisions require physical presence and human leadership.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates production scheduling, quality metrics analysis, inventory management, and compliance reporting. However, managing factory floor operations requires physical presence, staff leadership, real-time problem-solving, and supplier relationship management.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Production managers oversee manufacturing operations. Managerial work with no direct physical labor.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Management of manufacturing operations. Overseeing increasingly automated production, but the role is about planning, coordination, and decision-making rather than physical work.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Management role focused on planning and overseeing production. Physical floor presence for oversight but the core role is decision-making and coordination. No significant physical labor.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large manufacturing companies are primary employers with strong technology adoption culture. Management role requires human judgment and coordination. AI tools for production planning and quality control already widely used. Industry 4.0 initiatives facilitate adoption. Moderate regulatory requirements.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Management positions scale with the number of production facilities. AI optimizes production but someone must oversee operations. Smart factories may slightly reduce managers needed per facility.

title: Information clerks
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Predominantly screen-based: maintaining records, collecting data, processing forms, and providing information to customers via phone/email. AI chatbots and automation handle most routine information requests and data processing by 2028. Active displacement in basic information clerk roles.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Answering inquiries, maintaining records, processing forms, and providing information are routine digital tasks AI chatbots and agents handle autonomously. Only in-person reception duties and complex problem resolution retain human value.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Answering inquiries, providing information, processing requests, and maintaining records are routine digital tasks AI handles completely by 2036. This occupation has effectively ceased to exist in its traditional form, replaced by AI chatbots and virtual assistants.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Information clerks provide information to the public. Desk-based or counter-based communication work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Customer-facing information roles (reception, hotel front desk). Kiosks and digital interfaces handle many routine information requests. Remaining human roles focus on complex queries and hospitality. Minimal physical labor.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Primarily communication and customer service work. Minimal physical component—mostly seated desk work providing information. Digital AI handles more automation than physical robots.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large employers (hospitals, hotels, government) with clear ROI for AI-powered information systems. Kiosks and AI chatbots already widely deployed. Work is highly standardized. Minimal regulatory barriers. Labour shortages provide pull. Role already declining due to digital self-service.
demand_elasticity_rationale: AI chatbots and kiosks directly replace routine information-providing functions. Self-service digital tools handle most informational queries. Demand for human clerks shrinks as automated systems handle more interactions.

title: Information security analysts
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Almost entirely digital: monitoring networks, analyzing security threats, implementing protective measures, and writing incident reports. AI significantly enhances threat detection and automated response by 2028. However, novel threat analysis, strategic security architecture, and incident response coordination require experienced human judgment.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: AI agents handle threat detection, vulnerability scanning, log analysis, and incident response automation. Human analysts focus on novel attack investigation, security architecture decisions, and organizational risk strategy.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Threat monitoring, vulnerability assessment, security audit documentation, and incident response procedures are automated. Human analysts remain for novel attack vector analysis, security architecture for unprecedented threats, and organizational security strategy in complex environments.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Security analysts protect computer systems from threats. Entirely desk-based technical work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Entirely digital work involving cybersecurity analysis and protection. No physical component.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Entirely digital/analytical work. No physical component.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large enterprises are primary employers with strong incentive and resources. AI-powered security tools already essential and widely deployed. Existing technology culture. Clear ROI given rising cyber threats. Moderate regulatory requirements (PCI DSS, HIPAA) actually drive AI adoption. Talent shortages provide pull.
demand_elasticity_rationale: AI increases both cyber threats and defense capabilities, creating an arms race that demands more security professionals. Every organization faces growing cyber risks. The attack surface expands with digital transformation. Massive skill shortage persists.

title: Instructional coordinators
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Predominantly digital: developing curricula, analyzing educational data, evaluating teaching methods, and writing reports. AI assists with content development, data analysis, and assessment design by 2028. Teacher training and school-based collaboration provide interpersonal balance.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Curriculum development, standards alignment, assessment design, and training material creation are digital tasks AI handles well. Coordinators retain value in teacher coaching, institutional change management, and adapting programs to local contexts.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Curriculum development, training material creation, assessment design, and educational data analysis are highly automatable. Human coordinators remain for teacher mentoring relationships, navigating school district politics, and adapting curricula to nuanced community needs.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Education administrators perform management, planning, and coordination. Their work is entirely administrative and cognitive with no physical labor component.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Educational planning and curriculum development work. Entirely knowledge-based.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Entirely planning and educational design work. No physical component.
adoption_friction_rationale: Education sector with strong institutional inertia. Government and school district employment. Curriculum development requires pedagogical judgment. Moderate bureaucratic friction. Some AI-powered adaptive learning tools emerging but educational culture resists rapid technology change. State standards compliance requires human judgment.
demand_elasticity_rationale: AI in education creates demand for curriculum designers who understand how to integrate AI tools. Growing need for personalized learning pathways and educational technology coordination.

title: Insulation workers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Entirely physical work: installing, replacing, and removing insulation materials in buildings and mechanical systems. Blueprint reading is a minor reference task. AI has no meaningful impact on this manual construction trade.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Installing insulation in walls, floors, and ceilings is entirely physical construction work with no meaningful digital component.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Installing insulation in buildings and mechanical systems is entirely physical skilled trade work. Digital AI has essentially no exposure to this occupation.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Insulation workers install materials in varied building cavities and structures. The unpredictable access spaces and different building configurations limit robotic deployment by 2028.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Installation of insulation in buildings. Some large commercial projects with uniform spaces see automated insulation installation. However, residential and variable commercial work in tight spaces (attics, walls, pipes) requires human dexterity and adaptation. Each installation site is different.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Insulation installation in new construction is increasingly automated by 2036, especially spray-applied products. However, retrofit work in existing buildings with variable configurations and confined spaces retains human involvement. Standardized new construction is heavily automated.
adoption_friction_rationale: Fragmented construction trade with many small contractors. Physical installation in varied building conditions including confined spaces. Union presence in commercial sector. Limited capital among small operators. Labour shortages provide pull but work conditions challenge robotics. Building code compliance requires human inspection.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Physical installation work resists automation. Demand tied to construction and energy retrofit activity. Growing energy efficiency mandates may increase insulation demand.

title: Insurance sales agents
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Predominantly digital: researching policies, generating quotes, processing applications, managing client databases, and preparing presentations. AI significantly assists with policy comparison, lead generation, and administrative processing by 2028. Client relationship building provides some interpersonal insulation.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Quote generation, policy comparison, application processing, and client communication are digital tasks AI handles efficiently. Agents retain value for complex policy advisory, relationship management, and high-value client acquisition.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Policy comparison, risk assessment, quote generation, and routine policy servicing are fully automated. Human agents persist for complex commercial insurance requiring relationship-based consultative selling and for clients who prefer human guidance on major coverage decisions.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Insurance agents sell policies through client meetings. Interpersonal sales work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Sales and advisory work that is entirely interpersonal and knowledge-based. No physical component.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Entirely sales and relationship work. No physical component.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large insurance companies can deploy AI for routine policy sales. Online insurance platforms already handle simple policies. But complex commercial and life insurance involves relationship-building. State licensing requirements. Mix of captive agents (lower friction) and independent agents (higher friction).
demand_elasticity_rationale: Online comparison tools and direct digital purchasing reduce need for sales intermediaries. AI-powered recommendation engines replace much of the advisory function. Complex commercial insurance persists but personal lines shift to self-service.

title: Insurance underwriters
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Almost entirely screen-based: analyzing insurance applications, evaluating risk using data models, determining premiums, and reviewing policy terms. AI excels at automated risk scoring and application processing by 2028. Active headcount reduction in routine underwriting as AI handles standard risk assessments.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Risk evaluation, policy pricing, application review, and documentation are routine digital tasks AI agents automate with high accuracy. Human underwriters handle only complex, novel, or high-value cases requiring judgment beyond standard risk models.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Risk evaluation, policy pricing, application review, and compliance checking are structured digital analytical tasks AI handles autonomously. Human underwriters remain only for novel or highly complex risk scenarios and strategic portfolio decisions.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Underwriters evaluate insurance applications. Desk-based analytical work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Risk assessment and policy pricing work. Entirely analytical and knowledge-based.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Entirely analytical and decision-making work. No physical component.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large insurance companies are primary employers with strong technology adoption culture and clear ROI. Underwriting is highly data-driven and amenable to AI. Automated underwriting systems already widely deployed. State regulatory requirements manageable. Risk assessment is a natural AI application.
demand_elasticity_rationale: AI risk assessment models directly automate underwriting decisions. Algorithmic underwriting handles standard policies without human review. Complex or novel risks still need human judgment but represent a shrinking share.

title: Interior designers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Significant digital work: creating designs using CAD software, selecting materials digitally, and preparing presentations. AI generative design tools assist with space planning and visualization by 2028. Physical site visits, client meetings, and hands-on material selection provide non-digital balance.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: AI generates design concepts, space layouts, and material selections. However, client relationships, understanding lived experiences in spaces, hands-on material selection, and site visits retain strong human components.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI generates design concepts, space plans, material selections, and renderings from client briefs. Human designers retain value for understanding clients' emotional needs, physical space assessment, managing contractor relationships, and creative vision in premium markets.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Interior designers plan interior spaces. Creative knowledge work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Creative design work that is primarily conceptual and uses digital tools. Site visits occur but the role is about aesthetic design and client communication.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Primarily creative design and client consultation work. Some physical site measurement and installation oversight, but the core value is aesthetic vision and client relationship.
adoption_friction_rationale: Mix of large firms and many independent practitioners. AI design and visualization tools advancing rapidly. Client relationships and aesthetic judgment valued. State licensing in some jurisdictions. Moderate employer fragmentation. Some routine design work automating but custom work retains human value.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Significant latent demand—most people want professional interior design but can't afford it. AI visualization tools and virtual staging make design services more accessible. Every home renovation, office, and commercial space could benefit.

title: Interpreters and translators
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Translation work is almost entirely digital and highly automatable by AI by 2028. Machine translation handles most routine document translation. Live interpretation faces pressure from real-time AI translation tools. Active displacement in routine translation, with specialized and high-stakes interpretation retaining human value.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Machine translation reaches near-professional quality for most language pairs by 2031. AI handles routine document translation and basic interpretation autonomously. Human translators remain for literary, legal, and culturally nuanced work.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Routine translation and interpretation are performed at near-human quality by AI. The occupation has been fundamentally restructured—human interpreters remain only for high-stakes diplomatic, legal, and medical contexts where cultural nuance and accountability require human presence.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Interpreters translate between languages. Cognitive and communication work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Language work that is entirely cognitive. While AI translation improves, the remaining human roles focus on nuance and cultural context. No physical component.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Entirely language and communication work. No physical component for robotic automation.
adoption_friction_rationale: Mix of large language service providers and many freelancers. AI translation (Google, DeepL) already competitive for many language pairs. Conference interpretation has higher social barriers. Government and legal settings require certification. Creative and cultural nuance still valued for literature and high-stakes contexts.
demand_elasticity_rationale: AI translation quality improves rapidly. Routine document translation and basic interpretation are increasingly automated. Specialized and nuanced translation persists but AI handles growing volumes without human involvement.

title: Ironworkers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Entirely physical and dangerous work: installing structural steel, reinforcing iron, welding, and working at heights. Blueprint reading is a minor reference task. AI has no meaningful impact on this demanding construction trade.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Erecting steel frameworks, welding beams, and connecting structural components at height are entirely physical, dangerous construction tasks with no digital AI substitution.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Ironwork is physically demanding construction work—erecting steel structures, reinforcing concrete, and welding at heights. Digital AI has essentially no exposure to this occupation.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Ironworkers erect steel structures at heights in dynamic, hazardous construction environments. The highly unstructured and dangerous conditions are far beyond current robotic capabilities by 2028.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Assembly and installation of structural steel in construction. Some standardized steel erection tasks on large commercial projects becoming more automated with robotic welding and placement. However, working at heights in variable configurations requires human judgment and coordination. Each structure is unique.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Ironwork involves heavy physical labor at heights in variable construction environments. By 2036, robotic systems assist with lifting and placement of structural steel, but the variable site conditions, heights, and need for real-time structural judgment keep significant human involvement.
adoption_friction_rationale: Specialized construction trade working at heights in dangerous conditions. Strong union presence (Iron Workers). Physical work in varied outdoor conditions at elevation. Strict OSHA safety requirements. Labour shortages provide some pull but work environment is extremely challenging for robotics. State licensing.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Physical structural work at height in variable conditions resists automation. Demand tied to construction activity, particularly large commercial and infrastructure projects. AI has minimal direct impact.

title: Janitors and building cleaners
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Entirely physical work: sweeping, mopping, vacuuming, cleaning restrooms, emptying trash, and maintaining building cleanliness. This is one of the most purely physical occupations with no digital component that AI could affect.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Mopping floors, cleaning restrooms, emptying trash, and maintaining building cleanliness are entirely physical tasks. AI has essentially zero impact on janitorial work.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Janitorial work is entirely physical—cleaning floors, restrooms, and facilities using mops, vacuums, and cleaning supplies. This is the prototypical zero digital AI exposure occupation.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Janitorial work in large commercial buildings involves repetitive cleaning tasks in semi-structured environments. Robotic floor cleaners are widely deployed, and humanoid robots are being piloted for broader cleaning tasks in large facilities.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Commercial cleaning of standardized spaces (offices, malls, airports) heavily automated with robotic floor cleaners and automated systems. However, detailed cleaning, restroom maintenance, and work in variable spaces still requires human workers. Large commercial facilities substantially automated.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: By 2036, commercial cleaning robots are deployed at scale for routine cleaning of floors, surfaces, and bathrooms. Standardized building environments are largely robot-cleaned. Human cleaners remain for complex cleaning situations and oversight.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large property management companies and institutions are major employers. Robotic cleaning equipment already widely deployed. Severe labour shortages provide strong pull. Minimal regulatory barriers. Clear ROI. Some facility variability but controlled indoor environments suit robotics. Fragmented residential segment is higher friction.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Robotic floor cleaners and automated cleaning systems handle some routine cleaning. Demand tied to building stock but AI/robotics gradually automates repetitive tasks. Detailed and varied cleaning still needs humans.

title: Jewelers and precious stone and metal workers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Predominantly hands-on craft work: designing, constructing, and repairing jewelry using specialized tools and materials. CAD is increasingly used for design, but the manual craftsmanship—cutting, soldering, setting stones—dominates. AI assists with design concepts but cannot perform physical jewelry work.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Crafting jewelry, setting stones, and repairing pieces are manual precision tasks. AI assists with CAD design, but hands-on metalworking and gemstone work remain human skills.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Jewelry making is primarily hands-on artisanal work—cutting gems, setting stones, soldering metal, and finishing pieces. AI assists with design visualization and CAD, but the physical craftsmanship remains human and is often the primary value proposition.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Jewelers perform fine manual work with precious materials in workshop settings. The extreme precision and varied designs require skilled human dexterity beyond 2028 robotic capabilities.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Highly skilled artisanal work with precious materials. Each piece requires unique design and precision handwork. Custom jewelry creation and repair involves creative dexterity with variable materials. While some mass production uses automation, craft jewelry work resists automation.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Fine craft work requiring artistic vision and extreme precision with unique, valuable materials. By 2036, some routine settings and casting are automated, but custom design, repair of unique pieces, and artistic judgment keep this predominantly human. The craft tradition and artisan value proposition persist.
adoption_friction_rationale: Extremely fragmented industry of small independent shops and artisans. Physical precision work requiring artistic judgment. Consumer value placed on handcrafted artisanship. Limited capital among small operators. CAD/CAM tools adopted for some production but custom work resists automation. Moderate regulatory requirements.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Artisanal craft work that blends art and technical skill. CAD and 3D printing change production methods but custom jewelry demand persists. Market is relatively niche and stable.

title: Judges and hearing officers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: A blend of courtroom presence (presiding over proceedings, hearing testimony, managing courtroom) and digital knowledge work (researching case law, reviewing evidence, writing opinions). AI assists with legal research and document review by 2028, but judicial discretion, courtroom management, and constitutional authority remain firmly human.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: AI assists with legal research, case precedent analysis, and document review. However, judicial decision-making, courtroom management, sentencing, and interpreting law in complex human situations require human authority and judgment.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates legal research, case law analysis, and drafting of routine orders. However, judicial decision-making in contested cases requires human authority, legitimacy, and accountability. Legal and constitutional mandates ensure human judges remain, though their analytical workload decreases substantially.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Judges preside over legal proceedings. Entirely cognitive and judicial work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Legal decision-making work that is entirely cognitive and interpersonal. No physical component.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Entirely cognitive and deliberative work. No physical component.
adoption_friction_rationale: Constitutional requirements for human judicial decision-making. Enormous public trust and accountability requirements. Legal framework assumes human judges. Deep institutional inertia in the judiciary. Political appointment/election process. Liability and appeals framework built around human judgment. Most friction-resistant occupation.
demand_elasticity_rationale: The number of judges scales with caseload and court structure, set by statute. AI may speed case preparation but doesn't change the fundamental requirement for human judicial decision-making. Court reform could alter demand in either direction.

title: Kindergarten and elementary school teachers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Core work is interpersonal: teaching young children, managing classrooms, providing individualized attention, and communicating with parents. AI assists with lesson planning, assessment creation, and progress tracking by 2028, but the nurturing, in-person teaching of young children remains fundamentally human.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: AI handles some content delivery and assessment, but young children require extensive in-person care, social-emotional guidance, and developmental support. The interpersonal and caregiving aspects of elementary teaching strongly limit digital exposure.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates lesson content, assessment, and administrative tasks. However, elementary teaching is heavily interpersonal—nurturing young children, managing classroom behavior, supporting social-emotional development, and partnering with parents. The younger the students, the more irreplaceable the human teacher.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Teaching is fundamentally interpersonal and cognitive work involving instruction, mentoring, and classroom management. There is no physical labor component for robots to automate.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Teaching young children requires human presence, emotional sensitivity, and constant improvisation. Each child needs individual attention and care. Among the most interpersonal occupations. No physical automation potential.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Teaching young children is fundamentally about human warmth, emotional presence, and nurturing relationships. Physical activities (arts, play, demonstrations) require human engagement. The emotional and developmental needs of young children demand human presence.
adoption_friction_rationale: Government employment with strong unions and deep institutional inertia. Young children require human nurturing, social-emotional development, and supervision. State certification requirements. Parents strongly prefer human teachers. Classroom management of young children is irreplaceable by AI. Liability concerns for child safety.
demand_elasticity_rationale: AI tutoring tools can supplement teaching but young children need human attention, socialization, and care. Smaller class sizes improve outcomes—latent demand for more teachers per student. Teacher shortages indicate current unmet demand.

title: Labor relations specialists
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Predominantly knowledge work: negotiating contracts, researching labor law, mediating disputes, and preparing documentation. AI assists with contract analysis, precedent research, and drafting by 2028. In-person negotiation, relationship management, and advocacy remain human-driven.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Contract analysis, compliance tracking, and grievance documentation are digital tasks AI handles well. However, negotiation, mediation, and managing sensitive labor-management relationships require human interpersonal skills and political judgment.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates contract analysis, grievance documentation, labor law research, and compensation benchmarking. However, union negotiations, mediating workplace disputes, and managing sensitive employee relations require interpersonal skills and human judgment.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Labor relations specialists handle workplace disputes and negotiations. Interpersonal and analytical work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Negotiation and mediation work that is entirely interpersonal and knowledge-based.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Entirely interpersonal negotiation and analytical work. No physical component.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large corporations and government agencies are primary employers. Work involves negotiation, conflict resolution, and legal knowledge. Human judgment essential for union relations and dispute resolution. Moderate regulatory complexity (NLRA). Some analytical work amenable to AI but interpersonal component resists automation.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Demand tied to the number of unionized workplaces and labor disputes, both relatively fixed. AI can assist with analysis but the negotiation and relationship aspects persist. Declining union membership reduces overall demand.

title: Landscape architects
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Significant digital work: creating landscape plans using CAD, preparing site analyses, estimating costs, and writing specifications. AI assists with design generation and environmental analysis by 2028. Physical site visits, client meetings, and construction oversight provide meaningful non-digital components.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: AI generates site designs, produces construction documents, and performs environmental analysis. Architects retain client relationships, creative vision, site visits, and complex regulatory navigation, but design production accelerates dramatically.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates design generation, site analysis, environmental modeling, and construction documentation. Human landscape architects remain for creative vision, community engagement, physical site assessment, and navigating complex stakeholder dynamics in public space design.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Landscape architects design outdoor spaces. Creative design knowledge work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Design work primarily using digital tools and creative vision. Site visits occur but the role is about design and planning.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Primarily creative design and planning work. Site visits involve observation rather than physical labor. Core work is cognitive design and project management.
adoption_friction_rationale: Mix of large firms and small practices. AI design tools advancing. Professional licensing required. Environmental regulations and community engagement require human judgment. Moderate employer fragmentation. Site-specific design requires physical assessment. Some routine design work amenable to AI.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Growing demand for sustainable landscape design, urban green spaces, and climate-adaptive landscaping. AI visualization tools make services more accessible. Most commercial and residential projects could benefit from professional landscape design.

title: Lawyers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Predominantly digital knowledge work: legal research, document drafting, contract review, and case analysis. AI significantly accelerates research, document review, and drafting by 2028. However, courtroom advocacy, client counseling, strategic judgment, and complex negotiations remain firmly human-driven.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: AI handles legal research, document drafting, contract review, and case analysis autonomously. Lawyers shift to courtroom advocacy, complex negotiation, client counseling, and strategic judgment. Junior associate work is heavily displaced, but regulatory and trust requirements maintain senior roles.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI handles legal research, document review, contract drafting, compliance analysis, and routine legal work autonomously. Human lawyers remain for courtroom advocacy, client counseling in sensitive matters, novel legal strategy, and situations where human judgment and accountability are legally mandated.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Lawyers provide legal representation and advice. Entirely knowledge-based professional work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Legal analysis, argumentation, and client representation. Entirely knowledge and interpersonal work.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Entirely cognitive and analytical work—legal research, argumentation, and client counseling. No physical component.
adoption_friction_rationale: Mix of large law firms (lower friction for AI tools) and many small practices (higher friction). Professional licensing (bar admission) and malpractice liability. AI legal research tools already widely used. Court appearances require human advocacy. Legal ethics rules restrict non-human practice. Client trust barriers.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Vast unmet legal need among individuals and small businesses. AI makes legal research and document preparation faster and cheaper, potentially making legal services accessible to millions who currently go without. Historical pattern: technology expanded legal services.

title: Librarians and library media specialists
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: A substantial digital role: managing digital catalogs, conducting research, evaluating information sources, and developing programs. AI assists with cataloging, research support, and content curation by 2028. In-person community engagement, programming, and reader advisory provide interpersonal balance.
