digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Cataloging, reference queries, and collection management are heavily automated by AI. Librarians retain community programming, information literacy instruction, and serving as trusted community resource navigators.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates cataloging, reference services, collection analysis, and information retrieval. Human librarians remain for community programming, digital literacy education, serving as trusted information guides for complex research, and the community gathering space function of libraries.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Librarians manage collections, assist patrons, and organize information. Their work is primarily knowledge-based and interpersonal with minimal physical labor.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Information management and community service work. While automated book handling systems exist, the role is primarily about knowledge curation, community programs, and patron assistance. Minimal physical component.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Primarily knowledge management and patron assistance. Physical book handling is minor compared to research guidance, programming, and community engagement. By 2036, automated book sorting and shelving exist, but the core librarian role is cognitive and interpersonal.
adoption_friction_rationale: Government and academic institutional inertia. Role is evolving from information retrieval to community engagement and digital literacy. Strong professional association culture. Budget-constrained institutions. AI search tools already transforming information access but community role valued. State certification in some settings.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Libraries evolve into community information and technology hubs. AI helps librarians curate and provide access to information more effectively. Growing need for information literacy education and digital access in an AI-driven world.

title: Library technicians and assistants
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: A blend of physical tasks (shelving materials, maintaining collections) and digital work (cataloging, managing databases, processing checkouts). AI assists with cataloging and patron queries by 2028. The mix of physical and digital tasks places this at moderate exposure.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Shelving, cataloging, circulation management, and basic reference are increasingly automated. Human assistants handle physical materials management and patron interaction, but much routine work is AI-handled.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Cataloging, shelving records, circulation management, and routine reference tasks are automated. The remaining human role is primarily in physical materials handling and in-person patron assistance, significantly reducing the traditional scope of the occupation.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Library assistants shelve books and manage physical materials in organized environments. While book-sorting automation exists, the varied shelving locations and patron assistance aspects limit robotic exposure.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Book handling, shelving, and circulation management. Automated shelving and retrieval systems operational in some large libraries. Self-checkout widespread. However, many libraries still require human staff for physical collection management, especially in older facilities.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Shelving, organizing, and handling physical materials. By 2036, automated systems handle most book sorting, shelving, and circulation. Human role shifts to patron interaction and handling special materials. Routine physical tasks are largely automated.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large library systems have resources to adopt automation. Self-checkout systems widely deployed. Digital cataloging amenable to AI. But community service role valued. Government institutional inertia. Moderate employer consolidation. Some routine tasks already automated. Budget constraints may paradoxically drive automation.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Routine library tasks (cataloging, circulation, shelving) are increasingly automated. Self-checkout and digital catalogs reduce the need for human assistance. Some community engagement role persists but routine work shrinks.

title: Licensed practical and licensed vocational nurses
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Predominantly hands-on patient care: changing bandages, inserting catheters, measuring vitals, and administering medication. Electronic health records and care documentation have digital components, but the physical bedside nursing care dominates the role.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Taking vital signs, administering medications, wound care, and direct patient care are hands-on clinical tasks. AI assists with documentation and care coordination, but bedside nursing remains physical and interpersonal.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates care planning, medication management documentation, and patient monitoring analysis. However, LPN work is fundamentally hands-on clinical care—administering medications, wound care, taking vital signs, and providing direct patient comfort.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: LPNs provide direct patient care including wound dressing, monitoring vitals, and assisting patients. The varied patient conditions and need for clinical judgment limit robotic replacement by 2028.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Patient care requiring trust, communication, and physical assistance in variable clinical settings. Each patient has unique needs. Bedside care, medication administration, and wound care require human judgment and dexterity. Robotic assistance supplements but doesn't replace LPNs.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Patient care involving vital signs, medication administration, wound care, and patient comfort. By 2036, robotic systems assist with routine monitoring and medication delivery, but the intimate patient care, variable clinical situations, and human comfort provision require continued significant human involvement.
adoption_friction_rationale: State licensing and healthcare regulations. Mix of hospital systems (larger) and nursing homes/home health (fragmented). Physical patient care requires human touch and judgment. Severe labour shortages provide pull but regulatory, liability, and social barriers are high. Patient preference for human nurses is strong.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Aging population and healthcare expansion increase patient care demand. LPNs provide essential hands-on care that resists automation. Shortage of nursing staff indicates significant unmet demand.

title: Loan officers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Almost entirely screen-based: evaluating loan applications, analyzing financial data, calculating risk, and processing documentation. AI significantly automates credit assessment, document verification, and routine loan processing by 2028. Active headcount pressure in standard loan processing roles.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Application processing, credit analysis, risk assessment, and documentation are digital tasks AI agents handle autonomously. Human loan officers focus on complex cases, client relationships, and regulatory compliance decisions.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Credit analysis, underwriting decisions, document processing, and compliance checking are structured digital tasks AI handles autonomously. Human loan officers persist only for complex commercial lending relationships and high-value clients who prefer personal guidance.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Loan officers evaluate and approve loan applications. Desk-based financial work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Financial analysis and client advisory work. Entirely knowledge-based with some client interaction.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Entirely analytical and client-relationship work. No physical component.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large banks and mortgage companies are primary employers. AI-driven loan origination and underwriting systems already deployed. Clear ROI. Regulatory requirements (TILA, RESPA, ECOA) manageable and actually drive automation for compliance. Consumer lending increasingly automated. Complex commercial loans retain human element.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Algorithmic lending and automated underwriting reduce the need for human loan officers. Online mortgage and loan applications bypass traditional loan officer roles. Complex commercial lending persists but standard loans are increasingly automated.

title: Lodging managers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: A blend of interpersonal management (guest relations, staff supervision, handling complaints) and digital tasks (revenue management, booking systems, financial reporting). AI assists with pricing optimization and operations analytics by 2028, but on-site hospitality management remains human-driven.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Revenue management, booking optimization, and administrative reporting are automated by AI. However, guest relations, staff management, property maintenance oversight, and handling on-site issues require human presence.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates revenue management, booking systems, guest communications, staffing schedules, and financial reporting. However, hotel management requires physical presence, staff leadership, handling guest complaints in person, and maintaining the human touch in hospitality.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Hotel managers oversee lodging operations. Managerial work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Hotel management involving coordination and customer service. While hotel operations increasingly automated (check-in kiosks, robotic room service), the management role focuses on staff supervision, guest relations, and operational decisions.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Management role focused on operations, staff, and guest relations. Physical facility inspection is minor. Core work is cognitive management and hospitality leadership.
adoption_friction_rationale: Mix of large hotel chains (lower friction) and independent properties (higher friction). Management role requires human judgment and guest relations. AI tools for revenue management and operations already used. Hospitality culture values human service. Labour shortages provide moderate pull.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Management positions scale with the number of properties. AI helps with pricing and operations but on-site management persists. Growing travel and hospitality demand is offset by technology-enabled efficiency.

title: Logging workers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Entirely physical outdoor work: felling trees, operating chainsaws and heavy logging equipment, and grading timber. This is among the most physically demanding occupations with no meaningful digital component.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Felling trees, operating logging equipment, and transporting timber are physical outdoor tasks. AI has minimal impact on this hands-on forestry work.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Logging is physically demanding outdoor work—felling trees, operating heavy equipment in forests, and transporting timber. Digital AI has essentially no exposure to this occupation.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Logging involves operating heavy machinery and physical labor in variable forest environments. While mechanized logging is common, the unpredictable terrain limits further robotic automation by 2028.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Mechanized logging uses increasingly automated equipment. Some harvesting operations use autonomous or semi-autonomous machines on managed timber lands. However, variable terrain, diverse tree species, and environmental conditions require human operators for many situations.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: By 2036, automated harvesting equipment handles most commercial logging operations. However, the extreme variability of forest environments, terrain, and tree conditions means human operators remain for complex situations. Significant but not complete automation.
adoption_friction_rationale: Mix of large timber companies and small independent operators. Physical work in remote, varied terrain. Mechanization already advanced but full automation in forest conditions is challenging. Labour shortages and safety concerns provide pull. Environmental regulations add complexity. Infrastructure in forests is limited.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Mechanical harvesting equipment reduces the labor intensity of logging. Demand tied to timber markets, which are relatively stable. Environmental restrictions may reduce total logging volume in some areas.

title: Logisticians
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Predominantly digital: analyzing supply chain data, coordinating logistics using software systems, negotiating with suppliers, and optimizing distribution. AI significantly enhances supply chain optimization, demand forecasting, and route planning by 2028. Some warehouse visits and supplier meetings provide physical balance.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Supply chain optimization, inventory management, route planning, and logistics analysis are heavily digital tasks AI agents handle autonomously. Human logisticians focus on strategic supplier relationships, crisis management, and complex multi-party coordination.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Supply chain optimization, inventory modeling, routing, demand forecasting, and logistics planning are highly automatable digital analytical tasks. Human logisticians remain for crisis response, managing complex supplier relationships, and novel supply chain disruptions.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Logisticians analyze and coordinate supply chains. Knowledge-based analytical work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Supply chain planning and optimization work. Primarily analytical and knowledge-based. While overseeing automated logistics systems, the role is about planning and coordination.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Entirely analytical and planning work optimizing supply chains. No physical component.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large corporations and logistics companies are primary employers with strong technology adoption culture. Supply chain optimization is a natural AI application. AI tools already widely deployed. Clear ROI. Moderate regulatory requirements for some industries. Military and defense logistics already AI-augmented.
demand_elasticity_rationale: AI optimization of supply chains creates both efficiency and new complexity to manage. Growing global trade and e-commerce expand logistics needs. Every supply chain could be better optimized.

title: Machinists and tool and die makers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Primarily hands-on work: operating CNC machines and manual lathes, measuring precision parts, and using hand tools. CNC programming has a digital component, but the physical machine operation, setup, and quality inspection dominate. AI assists with CNC code generation but not the physical work.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Operating lathes, mills, and grinders to produce precision parts is hands-on skilled work. AI-driven CNC programming aids efficiency, but setting up machines, inspecting parts, and troubleshooting require manual expertise.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: While AI assists with CNC programming and design optimization, the core work is physical—operating machine tools, measuring precision parts, and performing hands-on fabrication. The craft skill and manual precision of machining retain strong human roles.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Machinists operate precision machine tools in structured shop environments. CNC automation handles much of the machining, and robotic loading/unloading is increasing. But skilled setup and custom work remains manual.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: CNC machines handle most routine machining with high precision. Automated tool changers and robotic loading widespread. Human machinists focus on complex setups, custom work, and quality control. Tool and die making for unique molds requires more human skill, but standard machining is heavily automated.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: By 2036, CNC machines and robotic manufacturing handle most precision machining. Humans remain for truly custom tooling, novel setups, and quality control of complex parts. The standardized, production-run work is heavily automated.
adoption_friction_rationale: Manufacturing employers with CNC automation already well-established. AI-assisted machining and tool path optimization advancing. Labour shortages provide pull. Skilled work still requires human judgment for complex parts. Moderate regulatory requirements. Apprenticeship traditions create some institutional inertia.
demand_elasticity_rationale: CNC automation and AI-guided machining improve productivity but custom and precision work still needs skilled machinists. Demand tied to manufacturing activity. Reshoring of manufacturing may increase demand.

title: Management analysts
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Almost entirely digital knowledge work: analyzing organizational data, developing recommendations, preparing reports and presentations, and conducting research. AI copilots significantly accelerate analysis, benchmarking, and report drafting by 2028. Routine consulting deliverables face strong automation pressure.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Data analysis, process mapping, benchmarking, report production, and recommendations are heavily digital tasks AI agents handle autonomously. Human consultants focus on client relationships, organizational politics, and implementing complex change.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Data analysis, benchmarking, process documentation, and recommendation reports are structured digital tasks AI handles autonomously. The traditional management consulting deliverable is automated. Human consultants remain for navigating complex organizational politics, executive relationship management, and implementation leadership.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Management consultants analyze business operations. Entirely knowledge-based consulting work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Consulting and advisory work that is entirely knowledge-based. No physical component.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Entirely cognitive consulting and analytical work. No physical component.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large consulting firms and corporations are primary employers with resources to adopt AI. Analytical work amenable to AI tools. McKinsey, BCG already deploying AI for analysis. But client relationships and strategic judgment valued. Moderate employer fragmentation with many independent consultants.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Every organization could benefit from management consulting. AI tools make analysis faster and more accessible, potentially bringing consulting to smaller organizations that couldn't afford it before.

title: Manicurists and pedicurists
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Entirely physical and interpersonal: cleaning, shaping, and beautifying nails through hands-on manual work. Appointment scheduling is a negligible digital component. AI has no impact on the physical nail care services.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Nail care, manicures, and pedicures are entirely hands-on personal services. AI has negligible impact on these physical grooming tasks.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Nail care is entirely hands-on physical service work with strong interpersonal components. Digital AI has essentially no exposure to this occupation.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Nail technicians perform fine motor work on clients' hands and feet. The precision required on varied client anatomy and the personal service nature limit robotic deployment by 2028.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Intimate personal service requiring dexterity, customer interaction, and trust. Each client's nails and preferences differ. The social and personal nature of the service, combined with detailed work on human hands and feet, strongly resists automation.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Intimate personal care where human touch and relationship are central to the service experience. By 2036, some nail-application automation exists, but the personal pampering, artistic nail design, and customer relationship keep this predominantly human-delivered.
adoption_friction_rationale: Extremely fragmented industry of small salons and independent operators. Physical manipulation of nails and hands requires fine motor skills. Strong client preference for human touch and personal service. Limited capital among small operators. State licensing requirements. Cultural expectations of personal service.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Personal care service that is inherently physical and in-person. Growing consumer spending on self-care and beauty services. Demand expanding with broader cultural acceptance and more accessible pricing.

title: Marine engineers and naval architects
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Substantial digital work: designing vessels using CAD, running simulations, analyzing performance data, and writing technical specifications. AI assists with design optimization and documentation by 2028. Physical sea trials, shipyard visits, and equipment inspections provide non-digital balance.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Ship design, structural analysis, and engineering documentation are digital tasks AI aids substantially. However, vessel inspections, sea trials, and marine-specific engineering judgment in physical environments limit full automation.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Ship design, structural analysis, and systems engineering are automated. Human engineers remain for novel vessel concepts, physical testing and sea trials, shipyard oversight, and navigating complex maritime regulatory environments.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Marine engineers design ships and marine equipment. Knowledge-based engineering work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Design and engineering work that is primarily knowledge-based and computational.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Primarily design and engineering work that is cognitive. Some shipyard inspections but core role is analysis and design.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large shipbuilding companies and naval operations are primary employers. Design work amenable to AI tools. Coast Guard and classification society regulations. Safety-critical maritime systems require human oversight. Moderate employer consolidation. Defense contracts have specific requirements.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Niche field with demand tied to shipbuilding activity. AI assists with design but the volume of new vessels is relatively fixed. Some growth from offshore renewable energy and autonomous vessel design.

title: Market research analysts
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Almost entirely digital: designing surveys, analyzing consumer data, building statistical models, and preparing market reports. AI significantly automates data collection, trend analysis, and report generation by 2028. Routine market research faces strong automation pressure.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Survey design, data collection, statistical analysis, trend identification, and report generation are heavily digital tasks AI agents handle autonomously. Human analysts focus on strategic interpretation, client presentation, and novel research design.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Survey design, data collection, statistical analysis, trend identification, and report generation are fully automatable digital tasks. Human analysts remain for interpreting market dynamics in genuinely novel situations and communicating insights to executive stakeholders.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Market researchers analyze consumer data and trends. Desk-based analytical work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Analytical work involving data collection and analysis. Entirely knowledge-based.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Entirely analytical work. No physical component.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large corporations and research firms are primary employers with clear ROI for AI analytics. Data analysis and survey processing highly amenable to AI. AI tools for sentiment analysis and predictive modeling already deployed. Some qualitative research requires human judgment. Minimal regulatory barriers.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Every business decision could benefit from market research. AI tools make analysis faster and cheaper, enabling more decisions to be research-informed. Historical pattern: data analytics tools expanded the research industry.

title: Marriage and family therapists
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Core work is deeply interpersonal: conducting therapy sessions, assessing clients' emotional states, and facilitating family and couples' communication. Progress notes and treatment planning have digital components, but the therapeutic relationship and clinical judgment are fundamentally human.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Therapeutic relationships require deep empathy, real-time emotional attunement, and trust built through human presence. AI assists with intake assessments and session notes, but the core therapeutic process is inherently human.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: While AI can provide psychoeducation and basic therapeutic tools, the core of therapy is deeply interpersonal—building therapeutic alliance, navigating complex family dynamics, reading nonverbal cues, and providing human empathy. The human relationship is the therapeutic mechanism.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Therapists provide counseling to individuals and families. Interpersonal therapeutic work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Therapeutic counseling work that is entirely interpersonal. No physical component.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Entirely interpersonal counseling work. No physical component.
adoption_friction_rationale: Extreme social resistance to non-human therapy. State licensing and healthcare regulation. Deeply personal therapeutic relationship is central to treatment. Malpractice liability. Highly fragmented independent practice structure. Professional ethics codes require human practitioners. Insurance billing requires licensed human providers.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Enormous unmet demand for relationship and family therapy. Most families could benefit but can't access or afford services. AI tools can help therapists serve more clients, but the therapeutic relationship requires human empathy and connection.

title: Masonry workers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Entirely physical skilled trade work: laying bricks, blocks, and stone; mixing mortar; and building walls and structures. Blueprint reading is a minor reference task. AI has no meaningful impact on this manual construction trade.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Laying bricks, blocks, and stone is entirely physical skilled trade work requiring manual dexterity and construction site presence. AI has zero impact on masonry tasks.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Masonry is entirely physical skilled trade work—laying brick, block, and stone in construction. Digital AI has essentially no exposure to this occupation.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Masonry involves skilled manual work in variable outdoor and construction environments. Bricklaying robots exist in early forms but are limited to simple walls; most masonry work remains too variable for robots by 2028.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Some large commercial bricklaying projects use robotic bricklaying systems for uniform walls. However, residential work, custom patterns, stone masonry, and repair/restoration require human skill and adaptation. The variety of materials and configurations limits full automation.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Masonry involves working with heavy materials in variable construction environments. By 2036, robotic bricklaying handles standardized wall construction, but complex patterns, restoration work, and variable site conditions still require human craftmanship.
adoption_friction_rationale: Highly fragmented trade with many small contractors and independent operators. Physical work in varied outdoor conditions requiring craftsmanship. Union presence in commercial sector. Limited capital among small operators. Each project is unique. Labour shortages provide pull but robotic masonry in field conditions is nascent.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Physical masonry work in variable conditions resists automation. Demand tied to construction activity. Specialized craft skills maintain demand. Some robotic bricklaying emerges but adoption is limited.

title: Massage therapists
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Almost entirely physical and interpersonal: applying pressure to manipulate soft tissues and joints. Client communication and scheduling are minor digital components. AI cannot perform hands-on bodywork.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Providing therapeutic massage is entirely hands-on physical work. AI has negligible impact on manual bodywork techniques and direct patient care.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Massage therapy is entirely hands-on physical work—manipulating soft tissue through touch. The human touch and interpersonal connection are the core product. Digital AI has negligible exposure.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Massage therapists perform skilled manual bodywork requiring sensitivity to tissue and patient feedback. While massage chairs and basic robots exist, therapeutic massage requires adaptive human touch beyond 2028 robotics.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Highly personal hands-on therapy requiring skilled touch, real-time assessment of muscle tension and patient response, and trust. Each client's body is different. The therapeutic relationship and tactile sensitivity are core. Very resistant to robotic automation.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Human touch IS the therapy. The physical intimacy, therapeutic relationship, and adaptive response to the individual body are central to massage. By 2036, massage chairs and robotic devices improve, but the human touch and emotional presence remain the core value proposition.
adoption_friction_rationale: State licensing requirements. Extremely fragmented industry of independent practitioners and small practices. Physical touch is the fundamental service. Strong client preference for human touch and therapeutic relationship. Limited capital among solo practitioners. Liability concerns for physical manipulation.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Inherently physical, hands-on work that fully resists automation. Growing wellness and preventive health spending. Significant latent demand as more people seek stress relief and physical therapy.

title: Material moving machine operators
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Almost entirely physical: operating forklifts, cranes, and other material-moving equipment in warehouses and construction sites. Inventory tracking systems are minor digital tools. The core physical machine operation cannot be replaced by AI by 2028.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Operating forklifts, conveyors, and cranes to move materials is physical work. Warehouse automation advances, but human operators remain essential for varied environments and complex material handling at the 2031 horizon.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Operating forklifts, cranes, and other material-moving equipment is physical work. While some automation exists, the digital AI exposure per se is minimal, limited to inventory tracking systems.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Operating forklifts and material-moving equipment in warehouses and factories involves structured, repetitive routes. Autonomous mobile robots and automated guided vehicles are commercially deployed in large facilities by 2028.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Warehouse and facility material moving heavily automated with autonomous forklifts, AGVs, and robotic palletizers. Large distribution centers and factories use automated material handling systems extensively. Human operators focus on non-standard loads and complex environments.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: By 2036, autonomous forklifts, cranes, and material-moving equipment are standard in warehouses and distribution centers. The vast majority of material moving is automated. Human operators remain for unusual loads and genuinely novel situations.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large warehouse, mining, and logistics companies are primary employers. Autonomous forklifts and material handling robots already deployed. Severe labour shortages create strong pull. Clear ROI. Minimal regulatory barriers beyond OSHA workplace safety. Controlled industrial environments suit automation.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Autonomous forklifts and material handling robots increasingly automate warehouse and distribution operations. AI-optimized logistics reduces inefficiency. Demand for human operators declines as automation spreads.

title: Material recording clerks
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Predominantly digital: tracking shipments in databases, managing inventory records, preparing shipping documents, and scheduling deliveries using software systems. AI automates much of routine inventory tracking and order processing by 2028. Physical warehouse verification provides some balance.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Tracking shipments, recording inventory, and processing receiving documents are routine digital tasks AI agents automate almost entirely. Only physical warehouse verification and exception handling retain human involvement.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Inventory tracking, shipping documentation, receiving logs, and stock records are structured digital tasks AI handles autonomously. Combined with automated scanning and IoT sensors, the traditional clerical recording function is largely eliminated.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Material recording involves inventory tracking in warehouses, combining physical counting with data entry. Robotic inventory systems (drones, AMRs with scanners) are being piloted in large warehouses, but much work remains clerical.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Inventory tracking and warehouse administration increasingly automated with RFID, automated scanning, and warehouse management systems. Physical inventory counts supplemented by drones and automated systems. However, receiving, inspecting, and handling exceptions still requires human workers.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Inventory tracking, receiving, and shipping documentation. By 2036, automated inventory systems with robotic counting and tracking handle most material recording. RFID, computer vision, and automated warehousing minimize human involvement.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large warehouse and logistics companies are primary employers. Work is highly standardized and data-driven. RFID, barcode, and inventory management systems already heavily automated. Clear ROI. Minimal regulatory barriers. Labour shortages in warehousing provide pull.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Inventory management, shipping records, and material tracking are heavily automated by barcode/RFID systems and AI-powered warehouse management. Routine record-keeping is directly displaced by technology.

title: Materials engineers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Significant digital work: using simulation software for materials modeling, analyzing test data, and writing technical reports. AI assists with computational materials science and property prediction by 2028. Physical laboratory testing and manufacturing process oversight provide non-digital balance.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Materials simulation, property analysis, and documentation are digital tasks AI handles well. However, laboratory testing, physical material characterization, and developing novel materials for specific applications require human expertise.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Materials modeling, property prediction, failure analysis, and documentation are automated. Human engineers remain for physical testing, novel material development requiring lab work, and applying materials science judgment in complex cross-disciplinary engineering contexts.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Materials engineers develop and test materials. Knowledge-based engineering work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Research and design work that is primarily knowledge-based. Lab work is secondary to analysis and design.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Primarily research and analytical work. Some lab testing with physical components, but core role is cognitive materials science and engineering design.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large manufacturers, aerospace, and tech companies are primary employers. AI for materials discovery and testing advancing rapidly. Professional engineering requirements. Moderate regulatory requirements depending on industry. Physical testing and lab work requires presence. Existing technology culture facilitates adoption.
demand_elasticity_rationale: AI dramatically accelerates materials discovery for batteries, electronics, aerospace, and sustainable products. Every industry needs better materials. The computational materials science revolution opens vast new research directions.

title: Mathematicians and statisticians
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Almost entirely digital: analyzing data, developing mathematical models, applying statistical methods, and writing research papers. AI significantly accelerates data analysis, model building, and computation by 2028. Routine statistical analysis faces strong automation, with theoretical mathematics retaining more human value.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Statistical analysis, model building, data processing, and report generation are heavily automated by AI agents. Human mathematicians focus on novel theoretical problems, research direction, and complex model interpretation.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Statistical analysis, modeling, computation, and routine mathematical research are automated. Human mathematicians remain for genuinely novel theoretical work, framing problems in unprecedented ways, and communicating complex quantitative concepts to non-technical decision-makers.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Mathematicians and statisticians analyze data and develop models. Entirely computational knowledge work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Purely analytical work involving mathematical modeling and statistical analysis. No physical component.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Purely computational and analytical work. No physical component whatsoever.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large tech companies, government agencies, and research institutions. Work is highly quantitative and amenable to AI. AI/ML tools already integrated into statistical practice. Academic institutional inertia for university positions. Clear ROI in industry applications. Minimal regulatory barriers.
demand_elasticity_rationale: AI and big data create massive demand for mathematical and statistical expertise. Every industry needs people who understand algorithms, probability, and data. AI itself requires mathematical foundations.

title: Mechanical engineering technologists and technicians
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: A blend of physical work (testing equipment, building prototypes, operating machinery) and digital tasks (making sketches, recording data, preparing reports using CAD). AI assists with data analysis and drafting by 2028, but hands-on testing and prototype work remain significant.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Building prototypes, testing mechanical devices, and operating lab equipment are physical tasks. AI aids with CAD work and data analysis, but hands-on fabrication and testing remain human-driven.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates data analysis, drafting, and documentation. However, the core work involves physical testing, prototype building, equipment operation, and hands-on troubleshooting in labs and manufacturing environments.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Mechanical engineering techs build prototypes and test equipment in labs and shops. The hands-on work in semi-structured environments has moderate physical exposure, but varied tasks limit automation.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Hands-on testing and fabrication of mechanical systems. Some routine testing automated, but prototyping, troubleshooting, and testing in variable configurations requires human technicians.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Building, testing, and maintaining mechanical devices. By 2036, routine testing and assembly is automated, but working with novel prototypes and diagnosing complex mechanical issues in variable equipment requires human involvement.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large manufacturers are primary employers with resources to adopt. Testing and quality control work increasingly automated. Moderate regulatory requirements. Physical lab and shop work requires manual presence. Existing manufacturing technology culture facilitates adoption.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Demand tied to manufacturing and R&D activity. Physical prototyping and testing persists. CAD tools improve productivity but new product development maintains demand. Roughly neutral.

title: Mechanical engineers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Predominantly digital: designing mechanical systems using CAD, running simulations, analyzing test data, and writing specifications. AI copilots significantly assist with design optimization, thermal analysis, and documentation by 2028. Physical prototyping and testing provide some balance. Calibration anchor occupation.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: AI generates mechanical designs, runs simulations, and produces engineering analyses autonomously. Engineers shift to validating designs, physical prototyping, testing, and handling novel engineering challenges. Productivity per engineer increases dramatically.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Design optimization, simulation, analysis, and documentation are automated. Human engineers remain for novel system conceptualization, physical prototyping and testing, manufacturing oversight, and cross-disciplinary integration challenges.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Mechanical engineers design mechanical systems. Knowledge-based engineering work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Design and engineering work that is primarily knowledge-based and computational.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Primarily design and analytical work. Some prototyping and testing but core role is cognitive engineering.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large manufacturers and engineering firms are primary employers. AI-assisted design, simulation, and generative design already used. Professional licensing (PE) for some roles. Moderate regulatory requirements. Physical prototyping and testing requires presence. Industry already technology-forward.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Broad field with applications across many industries. AI design tools improve productivity, but robotics, clean energy, and automation create new mechanical engineering challenges. Growing demand for sustainable product design.

title: Medical and health services managers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: A blend of digital management (budgeting, regulatory compliance, data analysis, strategic planning) and interpersonal leadership (staff management, interdepartmental coordination, patient advocacy). AI assists with operational analytics and compliance by 2028, but healthcare leadership requires human judgment.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Scheduling, budgeting, compliance tracking, and data analysis are heavily automated. Managers retain staff leadership, patient experience oversight, regulatory navigation, and strategic facility planning roles.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates scheduling, billing, compliance reporting, quality metrics, and financial management. Human managers remain for staff leadership, navigating complex healthcare politics, patient experience strategy, and crisis management in healthcare facilities.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Healthcare managers oversee facilities, staff, and operations. Their work is entirely managerial and administrative with no physical labor component exposed to robotic automation.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Healthcare management and administration. Entirely knowledge and leadership work.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Entirely management and administrative work. No physical component.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large hospital systems are primary employers. Management role requires human judgment and stakeholder coordination. AI tools for healthcare analytics and operations already adopted. Healthcare regulatory complexity (CMS, state regulations) creates moderate friction. Institutional inertia in healthcare.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Healthcare system complexity grows with technology and regulatory requirements. AI helps with administration but creates new management challenges (AI governance, data management). Aging population drives healthcare facility growth.

title: Medical assistants
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: A mix of clinical duties (taking vitals, preparing patients, assisting with examinations) and administrative tasks (scheduling, updating records, processing insurance). AI helps with scheduling and records by 2028, but the hands-on clinical support work is substantial.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Taking vitals, preparing patients, drawing blood, and assisting with procedures are hands-on clinical tasks. AI automates scheduling and records, but physical patient care duties dominate the role.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates record-keeping, scheduling, and documentation. However, medical assisting involves significant hands-on clinical tasks—taking vitals, preparing patients, assisting with procedures, drawing blood—and interpersonal patient interaction.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Medical assistants perform varied clinical and administrative tasks in healthcare settings. The mix of patient interaction, clinical procedures, and administrative work in variable situations limits robotic exposure.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Patient-facing clinical and administrative work. Each patient interaction differs. Taking vitals, assisting with examinations, and patient communication require human presence and trust. Some routine tasks automated but direct patient care resists automation.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Patient-facing clinical support—taking vitals, preparing patients, basic procedures. By 2036, automated vitals monitoring and routine sample collection assist, but patient interaction, positioning, and adaptive clinical support in varied patient encounters require human presence.
adoption_friction_rationale: Healthcare regulation and licensing. Large healthcare systems employ many but small practices are fragmented. Physical patient interaction (vitals, blood draws) requires human presence. Patient comfort expectations. EHR systems already automate some documentation. Labour shortages provide moderate pull.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Hands-on patient care tasks resist automation. Demand tied to patient volume in physician offices. AI may handle some administrative tasks but clinical assistance persists. Aging population supports demand.

title: Medical dosimetrists
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Predominantly digital: using specialized software to calculate radiation doses, design treatment plans, and analyze imaging data. AI significantly enhances automated treatment planning and dose calculation by 2028. Collaboration with physicians and patient-specific clinical judgment provide some insulation.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Radiation treatment planning, dose calculations, and treatment simulations are heavily digital tasks AI handles well. Human dosimetrists validate plans and handle complex cases, but routine treatment planning is largely automated.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Radiation dose calculation, treatment plan optimization, and plan documentation are highly digital analytical tasks AI handles with precision. Human dosimetrists remain for complex case review, quality assurance, and close collaboration with oncologists on novel treatment approaches.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Medical dosimetrists calculate radiation doses using specialized software. Their work is primarily computational and knowledge-based with no physical labor component for robots to automate.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Highly specialized calculation and planning work for radiation therapy. Primarily computational with some physical treatment planning setup. The core work is analytical.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Primarily computational planning work for radiation therapy. Minimal physical component—mostly analysis and treatment planning using software.
adoption_friction_rationale: Hospital systems are primary employers. Treatment planning is highly quantitative and amenable to AI. FDA and state radiation regulations. Professional certification requirements. AI-assisted treatment planning already in use. Patient safety demands rigorous validation. Moderate institutional inertia in healthcare.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Highly specialized role tied to radiation therapy patient volume. AI improves treatment planning but human oversight is required. Patient volume grows modestly with cancer prevalence and screening.

title: Medical equipment repairers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Predominantly hands-on: installing, testing, calibrating, and repairing medical equipment. Diagnostic software and technical documentation are digital tools, but the physical repair work with precision medical instruments dominates.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Inspecting, maintaining, and repairing medical devices is hands-on technical work. AI aids with diagnostics and documentation, but physical repair of complex medical equipment remains human.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Repairing and maintaining medical devices is hands-on technical work requiring physical diagnosis and repair skills. AI assists with troubleshooting guides and maintenance scheduling, but the physical repair work remains human.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Medical equipment repair involves diagnosing and fixing diverse electronic and mechanical medical devices. The variety of equipment and clinical settings limits robotic deployment by 2028.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Repair and maintenance of diverse medical equipment in hospital settings. Each device and problem is different. Diagnostic tools improving, but physical repair of complex medical devices in clinical environments requires human skill and judgment.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Repairing diverse medical equipment in hospital environments. By 2036, diagnostics are automated and routine maintenance is robotic, but the variety of equipment and variable repair contexts require human troubleshooting skill.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large hospital systems and medical device companies are primary employers. Physical repair of specialized equipment requires technical skill. FDA regulations for medical devices. Manufacturer training and certification. Diverse equipment types challenge standardized robotic repair. Moderate labour shortages.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Physical repair work on complex medical equipment resists automation. Growing installed base of medical devices increases maintenance demand. AI diagnostics help but hands-on repair persists.

title: Medical records specialists
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Almost entirely screen-based: processing and maintaining patient files, coding medical information, verifying records, and managing electronic health record systems. AI automates much of medical coding, data entry, and record verification by 2028. Active displacement in routine medical records roles.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Coding diagnoses, maintaining electronic health records, and processing health information are routine digital tasks AI agents automate almost entirely. Only complex coding disputes and system audits require human oversight.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Medical records management, coding, classification, and health information organization are entirely digital routine tasks that AI handles end-to-end. This occupation has effectively ceased to exist in its traditional form.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Medical records specialists organize and manage health data. This is entirely desk-based knowledge work with no physical labor component.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Data management work that is entirely digital. No physical component.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Entirely digital records management. No physical component.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large hospital systems are primary employers. Work is data-driven and highly amenable to AI. EHR systems already heavily automated. HIPAA compliance drives but doesn't prevent automation. AI coding and classification tools already deployed. Clear ROI for large healthcare systems.
demand_elasticity_rationale: AI and electronic health record systems automate coding, classification, and data management. Natural language processing extracts structured data from clinical notes. The routine aspects of medical records work are directly automated.

title: Medical scientists
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: A blend of laboratory research (conducting experiments, clinical trials) and digital knowledge work (analyzing data, writing grants and papers, reviewing literature). AI significantly assists with data analysis, literature review, and experiment design by 2028, but hands-on lab work and clinical oversight remain human.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: AI accelerates literature review, data analysis, and experiment design. However, clinical research, laboratory experimentation, patient interactions in trials, and novel hypothesis generation require human scientists.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates literature review, experimental design, data analysis, and manuscript drafting. Human scientists remain for wet lab work, clinical trial oversight, novel hypothesis generation, and interpreting complex biological results that require cross-disciplinary intuition.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Medical scientists conduct research in laboratories, which involves some physical lab work. However, their role is primarily research-focused with lab automation handling routine sample processing.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Research work with significant lab components. Automated lab systems handle routine procedures, but novel research design and experimental work requires human creativity. The core work is intellectual inquiry.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Laboratory research with physical components. By 2036, routine lab procedures are automated, but novel experimental designs and research with unique biological materials require human judgment. Core work is cognitive research.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large pharmaceutical companies and research institutions are primary employers. AI is transforming drug discovery and genomics. FDA regulatory requirements for research. Physical lab work requires presence. Academic institutional inertia for university researchers. Existing technology adoption in pharma facilitates AI integration.
demand_elasticity_rationale: AI accelerates drug discovery, clinical trial design, and biomedical research. New research directions open faster than efficiency reduces headcount. Growing healthcare spending and pandemic preparedness investment fund more research.

title: Medical transcriptionists
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Almost entirely digital: converting physician voice recordings into text documents and editing medical records. AI speech-to-text technology by 2028 handles 80%+ of transcription work with high accuracy. This is a calibration anchor for maximum digital exposure, with active displacement well underway.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: AI speech-to-text and clinical documentation systems effectively automate medical transcription by 2031. This role is functionally automated; remaining positions exist in legacy systems or for quality audit purposes only.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Medical transcription—converting voice recordings to text—is a task AI performs with superhuman accuracy. This occupation has ceased to exist in its traditional form, serving as a calibration anchor for maximum digital exposure.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Medical transcriptionists convert voice recordings to written reports. This is purely desk-based knowledge work with no physical component for robots to automate.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Audio-to-text work that is entirely digital. No physical component. Largely automated by speech recognition.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Entirely digital/audio processing work. No physical component.
adoption_friction_rationale: AI speech recognition has already largely replaced traditional medical transcription. Large healthcare systems and transcription companies drive adoption. Work is entirely amenable to AI. Clear ROI. HIPAA compliance manageable. Role has been declining rapidly due to existing automation.
demand_elasticity_rationale: AI speech recognition directly replaces medical transcription. Voice-to-text accuracy now matches or exceeds human transcriptionists. The role has already contracted significantly and the remaining work is rapidly automating.

title: Meeting, convention, and event planners
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: A blend of digital coordination (researching venues, managing budgets, coordinating logistics online) and interpersonal/physical work (site visits, on-site event management, vendor negotiations). AI assists with venue matching, logistics optimization, and communication by 2028.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Vendor research, budget tracking, logistics coordination, and communication are digital tasks AI aids substantially. However, on-site event management, vendor relationship building, and creative event design require human presence and judgment.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates vendor research, budget management, logistics coordination, marketing, and guest communication. However, event planning requires physical site visits, real-time on-site problem-solving, and managing interpersonal dynamics with clients and vendors.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Event planners coordinate meetings and events. Organizational and interpersonal work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Planning and coordination work with some physical setup oversight. The role is primarily about planning, vendor management, and logistics rather than physical labor.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Primarily planning and coordination work. Some physical venue setup oversight, but core role is organizational and interpersonal.
adoption_friction_rationale: Mix of large hotel/convention companies and many independent planners. AI tools for logistics and scheduling already used. Client relationships and creative judgment valued. Moderate employer fragmentation. Physical site management requires human presence. Some standardized events more amenable to automation.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Events and experiences economy continues to grow. AI helps with logistics and coordination but the creative and interpersonal aspects of event planning persist. Virtual events create new planning demands.

title: Metal and plastic machine workers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Predominantly physical: setting up and operating cutting, shaping, and forming machines. CNC programming has a minor digital component, but the hands-on machine operation, material loading, and quality inspection dominate this manufacturing role.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Operating metal-cutting and plastic-forming machines, loading materials, and inspecting finished parts are physical production tasks. AI-driven CNC programming helps, but manual machine operation remains human.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Operating metalworking and plasticworking machines is hands-on production work. AI assists with CNC programming and quality monitoring, but the physical machine operation, setup, and maintenance remain human tasks.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Machine operation in metal and plastics manufacturing involves repetitive tasks in controlled factory settings. Robotic loading/unloading and tending of these machines is commercially deployed by 2028.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: CNC machines and robotic systems handle most routine metal and plastic machining, stamping, and molding. Automated loading, operation, and quality inspection widespread in manufacturing. Human workers monitor equipment, handle setups, and address exceptions.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Operating metal and plastic fabrication machines in factory settings. By 2036, CNC and robotic systems handle most routine machine operation autonomously. Human involvement is primarily supervisory and for setup of novel jobs.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large manufacturers are primary employers with strong automation culture. CNC automation already pervasive. Labour shortages in manufacturing provide strong pull. Clear ROI. Minimal regulatory barriers beyond workplace safety. Controlled factory environments suit robotic operation. Industry 4.0 drives further automation.
demand_elasticity_rationale: CNC machines and robotics increasingly automate metal and plastic forming operations. AI-guided quality control reduces operator involvement. Demand tied to manufacturing volume but each worker operates more machines.

title: Microbiologists
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: A blend of physical lab work (culturing organisms, conducting experiments, operating microscopes) and digital knowledge work (analyzing data, writing research papers, reviewing literature). AI assists with data analysis and genomic sequencing interpretation by 2028, balanced by essential wet-lab work.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: AI assists with genomic analysis, literature review, and experiment design. However, wet-lab work—culturing organisms, preparing slides, conducting experiments—requires physical human presence and scientific creativity.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates genomic analysis, literature review, experimental design, and data interpretation. Human microbiologists remain for wet lab work, novel organism characterization, and research requiring cross-disciplinary biological insight.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Microbiologists conduct research in laboratories. While lab work involves some physical handling, the role is primarily research-focused knowledge work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Lab-based research with automated systems handling many routine procedures. Novel experimental work still requires human researchers. The core work is scientific analysis and interpretation.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Laboratory research with physical sample handling. By 2036, much routine microbiology lab work is automated, but novel research and experimental design with living organisms require human judgment.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large pharmaceutical companies, government labs, and research institutions. Lab automation advancing rapidly including automated microbiology systems. FDA/EPA regulatory requirements for testing. Physical lab work requires some presence. Academic institutional inertia. AI for genomics and drug discovery already deployed.
demand_elasticity_rationale: AI enables more sophisticated microbial analysis and drug development. Growing concern about antibiotic resistance and novel pathogens expands research. Food safety and environmental monitoring applications grow.

title: Middle school teachers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Core work is interpersonal classroom instruction, student engagement, and classroom management. AI assists with lesson planning, grading, and differentiated content creation by 2028, but the face-to-face teaching relationship with adolescents remains fundamentally human.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: AI tutoring handles content delivery, grading, and personalized learning. Teachers shift to adolescent mentoring, social-emotional development, classroom management, and facilitating collaborative learning—deeply human roles.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates content delivery, assessment, and lesson planning. However, middle school teaching is heavily interpersonal—managing pre-adolescent behavior, social-emotional mentoring, parent communication, and creating safe learning environments require human presence and judgment.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Teaching is fundamentally interpersonal and cognitive work involving instruction, mentoring, and classroom management. There is no physical labor component for robots to automate.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Teaching is fundamentally interpersonal. No significant physical automation potential.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Teaching adolescents requires human mentorship, behavioral management, and adaptive instruction. The educational relationship and developmental support are inherently human. Minimal physical task content for robots.
adoption_friction_rationale: Government employment with strong unions and institutional inertia. Adolescent development requires human mentorship, classroom management, and social-emotional support. State certification requirements. Strong parental and societal preference for human teachers. Moderate technology adoption in curriculum delivery.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Teacher shortages indicate unmet demand. AI tools supplement instruction but young adolescents need human mentorship and social-emotional guidance. Growing emphasis on educational quality supports smaller class sizes.

title: Military careers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Military careers span a wide range from combat roles to administrative functions. The overall profile is heavily physical (training, operations, equipment maintenance) with some digital components (communications, intelligence analysis, logistics). AI assists with planning and analysis but cannot replace physical military service.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Military service spans physical combat, training, logistics, and operations. AI aids with intelligence analysis, logistics planning, and communications, but physical duties, leadership, and decision-making under extreme conditions remain human.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Military roles span a wide range from physical combat to intelligence analysis. Digital components like intelligence analysis, logistics planning, and communications are automated, but combat operations, leadership, physical fitness requirements, and the command hierarchy mandate human involvement.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Military careers span a huge range from combat to administrative roles. Physical tasks include equipment operation and maintenance in varied conditions. Some logistics automation is advancing, but most military physical tasks remain manual.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Extremely diverse roles from combat to logistics to administration. Some military logistics and support functions see robotic systems. Autonomous vehicles and drones expand. But combat, peacekeeping, and many field operations require human judgment in unpredictable environments. Average across all military roles.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Extremely diverse roles spanning combat, logistics, maintenance, and administration. By 2036, autonomous systems handle much reconnaissance, logistics, and some combat support. However, the command judgment, rules of engagement, and diverse operational environments keep substantial human involvement across the military.
adoption_friction_rationale: Heavy government institutional inertia with strict chain of command. Enormous regulatory and legal frameworks (UCMJ, Geneva Conventions, laws of armed conflict). Public accountability for use of force. Some rapid technology adoption for support roles but combat and leadership roles face extreme friction. Security clearance requirements.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Military staffing is determined by policy and geopolitical needs, not market forces. AI and autonomous systems may reduce some roles while creating others. Net effect is policy-dependent and uncertain.

title: Mining and geological engineers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Substantial digital work: designing mines using engineering software, analyzing geological data, preparing technical reports, and running safety simulations. AI assists with mine planning optimization and data analysis by 2028. Physical site inspections and safety management provide non-digital balance.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Mine design, resource estimation, and safety analysis are digital tasks AI handles well. However, underground inspections, site-specific geological assessment, and managing physical mining operations require human presence.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates mine design, resource modeling, and safety analysis. However, mining engineering involves significant on-site work—assessing geological conditions, overseeing extraction operations, and managing safety in physically hazardous environments.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Mining engineers design mining operations. Knowledge-based engineering work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Engineering design and planning work. Primarily knowledge-based with some site visits. The role is about mine design and optimization rather than physical extraction.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Primarily engineering design and planning. Some site visits in variable mining environments, but core role is cognitive problem-solving and mine design.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large mining companies are primary employers with resources and motivation to adopt autonomous equipment. Safety concerns favor robotic deployment in hazardous conditions. MSHA regulations create compliance framework. AI for resource modeling already used. Some remote/harsh environment challenges for robotics.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Demand tied to mining activity, which fluctuates with commodity prices. AI optimizes operations but the volume of mining is resource-demand driven. Green energy transition may shift which minerals are mined.

title: Models
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Core work is physical: posing for photographs, walking runways, and fitting clothing. AI-generated models and virtual fashion shows are emerging by 2028, creating moderate digital displacement pressure. However, live modeling for fittings and in-person appearances remains human.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: AI-generated imagery increasingly substitutes for human models in digital advertising and e-commerce. However, live fashion shows, physical product fitting, and brand ambassador roles requiring human presence persist.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI-generated imagery increasingly substitutes for human models in digital media and e-commerce. However, live fashion shows, physical product fitting, and brand campaigns where human authenticity is valued preserve roles for human models. The digital displacement is significant but not total.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Models pose for visual media. This is a physical but creative/performative role that robots cannot meaningfully replace.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Physical appearance-based work. While AI-generated models exist for some digital applications, live modeling for fashion shows, commercial shoots, and fitting sessions requires human presence. The industry values authentic human presentation.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Modeling is inherently about human physical appearance and presence. The value is the human form and persona. CGI alternatives exist but are a different product.
adoption_friction_rationale: Fashion and advertising industries increasingly using AI-generated models, but strong cultural resistance in high fashion and editorial work. Fragmented employer base of agencies and brands. Human physicality valued for runway shows. Industry unions provide some protection. Legal questions around likeness rights unresolved.
demand_elasticity_rationale: AI-generated images create some displacement, but live fashion shows, product photography, and brand representation still need human models. Growing content demand and diverse representation expand opportunities.

title: Music directors and composers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: A blend of performance (conducting orchestras, leading rehearsals) and digital creative work (composing using software, arranging, producing recordings). AI music generation tools are advancing rapidly by 2028, affecting commercial composition. Live direction and artistic vision remain human.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: AI generates compositions, arrangements, and production-ready music. However, artistic vision, live performance direction, and creating emotionally resonant original works retain human value. Production music work is heavily displaced.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI composes music, arranges, and produces recordings. However, human composers retain value where artistic authorship is the brand, and music directors lead live ensembles through interpersonal leadership. The creative and performance dimensions resist full automation.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Music directors lead ensembles and composers create music. Creative artistic work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Creative and leadership work in music. Composition is knowledge-based, and conducting requires human artistic interpretation and leadership.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Entirely creative and cognitive work. No physical component for robotic automation. Music direction involves human artistic leadership.
adoption_friction_rationale: Creative work where human artistry is highly valued. Mix of large institutions (orchestras, studios) and many independent composers. AI music generation is advancing but audience and industry preference for human composers is strong. Strong copyright and creative ownership issues. Union protections in media.
demand_elasticity_rationale: AI music generation is improving but demand for original, emotionally authentic music grows with content creation. Every video, game, ad, and podcast needs music. Live performance and artistic direction remain human domains.

title: Musicians and singers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Core work is physical performance: playing instruments and singing for live audiences and in studios. AI-generated music affects commercial background music, but live performance, artistic expression, and studio artistry remain distinctly human. Some digital recording and production work exists.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Live musical performance is inherently physical and embodied. AI generates recorded music, but audiences value human performers for concerts, events, and authentic artistic expression.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Live musical performance is fundamentally embodied and interpersonal. AI generates recorded music, but the cultural value of human performance, live concerts, and artistic authenticity preserves musicians' roles. Some studio session work is displaced.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Musicians perform music requiring artistic expression. Creative performance that robots cannot meaningfully replicate.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Performance art requiring human creativity and expression. Live music is valued for its human element. No physical automation potential for live performance.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Musical performance is fundamentally human artistic expression. The value is human creativity and emotional performance. While music can be AI-generated digitally, live performance is inherently human.
adoption_friction_rationale: Live performance is fundamentally about human artistry and connection. Extremely fragmented self-employed base. Audiences value human creativity and performance. AI music generation faces strong cultural resistance and copyright questions. Union protections (AFM). Recorded music faces more AI competition than live.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Live performance demand grows with entertainment spending and cannot be automated. AI-generated music creates competition for recorded music but live shows, sessions, and unique artistry maintain human demand.

title: Natural sciences managers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Predominantly knowledge work: planning research programs, managing budgets, coordinating teams, and writing reports. AI assists with project tracking, data analysis, and proposal writing by 2028. Strategic research direction, team leadership, and cross-functional coordination remain human.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Grant management, research coordination, budgeting, and reporting are aided by AI. Managers retain strategic research direction, team leadership, stakeholder relationships, and scientific judgment roles.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates research portfolio analysis, grant management, budgeting, and reporting. Human managers remain for strategic research direction, mentoring scientists, navigating organizational politics, and making judgment calls about resource allocation for uncertain research programs.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Natural sciences managers oversee research teams. Managerial work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Management of scientific research teams. Entirely administrative and knowledge-based.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Entirely management and planning work. No physical component.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large research institutions, government agencies, and pharmaceutical companies. Management role requires human judgment and team leadership. AI tools for research management emerging. Institutional inertia in academia and government. Moderate regulatory complexity. Scientific expertise and interpersonal skills valued.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Management roles scale with the number of research teams and labs. AI helps manage projects but the number of leadership positions is tied to organizational structure, not individual productivity.

title: Network and computer systems administrators
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Almost entirely digital: installing and configuring network hardware/software, monitoring system performance, ensuring security, and troubleshooting issues. AI significantly automates routine monitoring, patch management, and incident detection by 2028. Complex architecture and incident response retain human value.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: System monitoring, configuration management, backup operations, and routine troubleshooting are highly automatable by AI agents. Human admins handle complex infrastructure decisions, security incidents, and novel system integration.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: System monitoring, configuration management, security patching, backup procedures, and troubleshooting are automated by AI operations agents. Human administrators remain only for novel infrastructure architecture and complex migration scenarios.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Network admins manage computer networks and systems. Desk-based technical work.
