physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Primarily digital system administration. Some physical server and network hardware management, but increasingly cloud-based and remote. The physical component is minor and decreasing.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Primarily digital/remote system management. Some physical hardware work in data centers, but by 2036, much physical server work is automated. Core role is cognitive systems management.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large enterprises are primary employers. Cloud automation and AI-powered network management already pervasive. Clear ROI. Existing technology culture. Automated provisioning, monitoring, and troubleshooting widely deployed. Minimal regulatory barriers. Talent shortages drive further automation.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Cloud infrastructure and AI-managed systems automate much routine network and system administration. Infrastructure-as-code reduces manual configuration. Complex environments persist but fewer admins are needed per system.

title: News analysts, reporters, and journalists
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Predominantly digital: researching stories, writing articles, conducting interviews, and publishing content. AI assists with drafting, fact-checking, and data journalism by 2028. In-person investigative reporting, source relationships, and editorial judgment provide meaningful human value. Calibration anchor area.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: AI generates routine news stories, summarizes data, and produces reports. Human journalists focus on investigative reporting, source cultivation, editorial judgment, and on-the-ground coverage—but newsroom staffing shrinks significantly.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Routine news reporting, data journalism, and content production are automated. Human journalists remain for investigative reporting requiring source cultivation, editorial judgment in ambiguous situations, on-camera presence where human credibility matters, and accountability journalism.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Journalists research and report news. Knowledge-based communication work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Journalism and reporting work that is primarily about investigation, writing, and communication. No significant physical component.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Primarily investigative and writing work. On-location reporting involves physical presence but the core value is journalism, analysis, and storytelling—cognitive work.
adoption_friction_rationale: Mix of large media companies and local outlets. AI-generated news articles already used for routine reporting. But investigative journalism, source cultivation, and on-scene reporting require human judgment. First Amendment and press freedom cultural values. Some union presence. Audience trust in human journalists.
demand_elasticity_rationale: AI generates routine news articles but investigative journalism and analysis require human judgment. Declining traditional media offset by growing digital and specialized news. Trust in human journalism provides some insulation.

title: Nuclear engineers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Significant digital work: designing reactor systems using simulation software, analyzing safety data, and writing technical reports. AI assists with modeling and safety analysis by 2028. Physical plant inspections, equipment testing, and strict regulatory compliance require human presence and expertise.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Reactor design simulation, safety analysis, and documentation are digital tasks AI handles well. However, physical plant operations, safety-critical oversight, and regulatory compliance in nuclear environments require human expertise and authority.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Reactor modeling, safety analysis, and regulatory documentation are automated. Human engineers remain for physical plant operations oversight, novel reactor design challenges, safety-critical judgment calls, and navigating highly regulated nuclear environments.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Nuclear engineers design nuclear systems. Knowledge-based engineering work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Design and engineering work for nuclear systems. Primarily knowledge-based and computational.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Primarily design and analytical engineering work. Site inspections in nuclear facilities have safety-critical physical components, but the core role is cognitive.
adoption_friction_rationale: NRC regulation is extremely stringent. Large utilities and government contractors are employers with resources. Safety-critical nuclear systems require extensive human oversight and validation. AI tools for monitoring and simulation used but regulatory approval for autonomous nuclear systems faces extreme scrutiny. Security clearance requirements.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Niche field with demand tied to nuclear energy policy. Renewed interest in nuclear power (SMRs) and nuclear security may increase demand. AI assists with design and simulation but the field remains small.

title: Nuclear medicine technologists
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Core work is hands-on clinical: preparing and administering radioactive drugs, operating imaging equipment, and working directly with patients. AI assists with image analysis by 2028, but the physical patient care and equipment operation dominate.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Preparing and administering radioactive materials, operating imaging equipment, and positioning patients are physical tasks. AI aids with image interpretation and dosimetry, but hands-on patient care remains human.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates image interpretation and dosimetry calculations. However, administering radiopharmaceuticals, positioning patients, operating imaging equipment, and ensuring radiation safety require physical presence and manual skill.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Nuclear medicine techs prepare and administer radioactive drugs and operate imaging equipment. The patient interaction and safety-critical material handling limit robotic replacement by 2028.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Patient-facing work administering radioactive materials and operating imaging equipment. Each patient requires individualized care and positioning. Safety-critical handling of radioactive materials requires human oversight. Trust and patient communication essential.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Operating imaging equipment, preparing radioactive materials, and positioning patients. By 2036, automated systems assist with routine procedures, but patient handling, variable anatomy, and safety-critical radioactive material management require human involvement.
adoption_friction_rationale: Healthcare regulation, state licensing, and NRC radiation safety requirements. Hospital systems are primary employers. Physical patient handling and radiotracer administration. FDA-regulated equipment. AI-assisted image interpretation emerging but regulatory path is slow. Patient safety demands rigorous oversight.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Demand tied to nuclear medicine procedure volume, set by patient need and physician orders. AI aids image interpretation but human technologists must handle radioactive materials and operate equipment safely.

title: Nuclear technicians
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: A blend of physical work (operating and maintaining nuclear equipment, monitoring radiation levels) and digital monitoring/data tasks. Safety-critical physical operations in nuclear environments dominate, with AI assisting on data analysis and monitoring.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Operating nuclear test and monitoring equipment, collecting samples, and ensuring radiation safety are physical tasks in controlled environments. AI assists with data analysis, but hands-on technical work predominates.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates data analysis, monitoring system interpretation, and documentation. However, physical work—operating and maintaining nuclear equipment, conducting radiation surveys, decontaminating materials—requires human presence in regulated environments.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Nuclear technicians operate and monitor nuclear equipment in controlled plant environments. The structured, regulated environment has some automation potential, but safety-critical operations still require human oversight.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Operation and monitoring of nuclear facilities. Some routine monitoring automated, but physical maintenance and inspection of nuclear systems requires human technicians with specialized training. Safety regulations mandate human oversight.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Operating and monitoring nuclear equipment in controlled but safety-critical environments. By 2036, routine monitoring and operations are automated, but the safety-critical nature and need for human judgment in unusual situations maintain significant human presence. Regulatory requirements also mandate human oversight.
adoption_friction_rationale: NRC regulation is stringent. Large utilities and government facilities. Safety-critical work with radiation exposure requires strict protocols. Some tasks amenable to robotic automation for safety reasons. Security clearance requirements. Institutional inertia in nuclear industry. Labour shortages provide moderate pull.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Demand tied to nuclear facilities operations. Safety requirements maintain staffing levels. AI helps with monitoring but physical operations and safety protocols require human presence.

title: Nurse anesthetists, nurse midwives, and nurse practitioners
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Predominantly clinical: examining patients, prescribing medications, performing procedures, and providing primary care. AI assists with diagnostic decision support and documentation by 2028, but hands-on patient care, clinical judgment, and procedures require experienced human practitioners.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Advanced clinical practice—administering anesthesia, delivering babies, diagnosing conditions—is hands-on patient care. AI assists with clinical decision support and documentation, but physical procedures and patient relationships are central.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates diagnostic support, treatment protocol recommendations, and documentation. However, these advanced practice nurses perform hands-on procedures, provide direct patient care, and manage complex clinical situations requiring physical presence and interpersonal skills.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Advanced practice nurses perform clinical examinations, procedures, and patient care. The varied patient conditions and clinical judgment required limit robotic replacement by 2028.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Advanced clinical practice requiring patient assessment, treatment decisions, and hands-on care. Each patient is unique. Trust and clinical judgment are paramount. Nurse midwives assist births in highly variable situations. Very resistant to physical automation.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Advanced practice nursing combining clinical judgment with hands-on patient care. Midwifery involves intimate birth support; anesthesia requires real-time patient monitoring and intervention. By 2036, monitoring automation assists, but the clinical judgment, patient relationship, and hands-on care in variable situations remain human-centered.
adoption_friction_rationale: Heavy healthcare regulation, state licensing, and scope-of-practice restrictions. High liability for patient outcomes. Strong patient trust requirements for procedures and prescribing. Professional association protections. Collaborative practice agreements with physicians add regulatory layers. Labour shortages provide some pull but barriers are formidable.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Major push to expand NP scope of practice to address physician shortages. Huge unmet demand for primary care and midwifery services. AI tools help with diagnosis and treatment planning while NPs provide the human care.

title: Nursing assistants and orderlies
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Almost entirely physical care: bathing patients, assisting with mobility, serving meals, and transporting patients. Documentation is a minor digital component. AI cannot replace the hands-on personal care that defines this role.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Bathing, feeding, repositioning, and transporting patients are entirely physical caregiving tasks. AI has minimal impact on these hands-on nursing duties.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Nursing assistance is fundamentally physical and interpersonal—bathing, feeding, repositioning patients, and providing basic bedside care. Digital AI has minimal exposure beyond documentation systems.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Nursing assistants provide direct physical care to patients including bathing, feeding, and mobility assistance. The intimate, varied patient interactions require human empathy and adaptability beyond 2028 robotics.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Routine physical patient care (bathing, feeding, mobility assistance) sees some robotic assistance. Robotic lift systems and mobility aids operational. However, the intimate nature of personal care, working in diverse settings, and need for human empathy and trust means human aides remain essential for many tasks.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Direct patient care—bathing, feeding, repositioning, mobility assistance. By 2036, robotic lifting equipment and basic care robots assist significantly, but intimate personal care, patient dignity, and emotional support keep substantial human involvement. Routine physical tasks are increasingly automated.
adoption_friction_rationale: Severe labour shortages in nursing facilities create enormous pull. But highly fragmented across nursing homes and healthcare facilities. Physical patient care (bathing, feeding, moving) requires human presence and empathy. State certification requirements. Patient safety and dignity concerns. Low wages limit employer technology investment.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Aging population creates massive demand for direct patient care. Physical caregiving strongly resists automation. Chronic staffing shortages indicate significant unmet demand. AI monitoring may improve care quality.

title: Occupational health and safety specialists and technicians
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: A blend of physical inspections (examining workplaces, testing equipment, collecting samples) and digital tasks (analyzing data, writing reports, developing safety programs). AI assists with compliance monitoring and data analysis by 2028, balanced by essential on-site inspection work.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Compliance documentation, data analysis, and training material creation benefit from AI. However, physical workplace inspections, incident investigations on-site, and worker safety monitoring require human presence.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates regulatory compliance analysis, incident data analysis, and safety documentation. However, workplace inspections, safety training delivery, and investigating incidents on-site require physical presence and interpersonal skills.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Safety specialists inspect workplaces and enforce regulations. Primarily analytical and inspection-based work with site visits but no physical labor.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Inspection and assessment work primarily involving observation, analysis, and compliance checking. Some automated monitoring assists, but the role is primarily analytical with physical site visits.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Site inspections and hazard assessments in variable workplaces. By 2036, automated monitoring handles routine hazard detection, but the cognitive analysis, regulatory judgment, and investigation of novel workplace situations remain human-centered.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large employers and government agencies (OSHA). Physical workplace inspection requires human presence and judgment. Regulatory compliance work amenable to AI tools. Moderate institutional inertia. Professional certification requirements. Liability for missed hazards. Some AI monitoring tools already deployed.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Demand tied to the number of workplaces and regulatory requirements. AI enables better monitoring but compliance requirements are set by regulation. New AI workplace safety concerns may expand the domain.

title: Occupational therapists
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Core work is hands-on and interpersonal: evaluating patients' abilities, developing treatment plans, and teaching daily living skills through direct interaction. Documentation and treatment planning have digital components, but the physical therapeutic work with patients dominates.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Hands-on therapeutic interventions, patient assessment through physical interaction, and adapting environments for patients with disabilities are inherently physical. AI assists with treatment planning and documentation.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI assists with treatment planning and progress documentation. However, OT is fundamentally hands-on and interpersonal—working directly with patients to improve daily living skills, adapting physical environments, and building therapeutic relationships.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Occupational therapists help patients develop or recover daily living skills through personalized physical activities. The highly individualized, adaptive nature of therapy limits robotic replacement by 2028.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Therapeutic work requiring hands-on patient assessment and treatment in variable settings—homes, hospitals, schools. Each patient has unique functional limitations. Trust, creativity in adapting activities, and interpersonal skills are core. Very resistant to automation.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Hands-on therapeutic work helping patients develop daily living skills. Requires adaptive physical interaction, patient motivation, and clinical judgment about individual needs. By 2036, assistive technology is advanced, but the therapeutic relationship and adaptive guidance remain human-centered.
adoption_friction_rationale: State licensing and healthcare regulation. Mix of hospital systems and outpatient clinics. Physical rehabilitation requires hands-on human interaction and adaptive judgment. Patient therapeutic relationship is central. Insurance billing requires licensed providers. Moderate employer fragmentation. Liability concerns.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Significant unmet demand for rehabilitation and adaptive services. Aging population and growing awareness of developmental needs expand the patient pool. AI tools help create personalized treatment plans and monitor progress.

title: Occupational therapy assistants and aides
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Predominantly physical and interpersonal: helping patients with exercises and activities, preparing treatment rooms, and assisting therapists. Record-keeping is a minor digital component. The hands-on patient care cannot be automated.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Assisting patients with therapeutic exercises, daily living activities, and rehabilitation tasks is hands-on physical work. AI has minimal impact on these direct patient care duties.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: OT assistants work directly with patients performing physical therapeutic activities. AI assists with documentation and exercise programming, but the hands-on patient interaction and physical therapy delivery remain human.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: OT assistants help patients with therapeutic activities and exercises. The personalized, adaptive physical interactions with patients are beyond 2028 robotic capabilities.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Hands-on patient support under OT supervision. Physical assistance with exercises and daily activities in variable settings. Each patient's needs differ. Some therapeutic equipment automated, but personal assistance and motivation require human presence.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Implementing therapy programs with direct patient interaction. By 2036, robotic therapy equipment assists with exercises, but guiding patients through varied activities and adapting to individual needs requires human presence and judgment.
adoption_friction_rationale: State licensing and healthcare regulation. Work under OT supervision in varied therapeutic settings. Physical patient interaction for exercises and daily living activities. Patient preference for human assistance. Moderate employer fragmentation across healthcare settings. Liability concerns.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Hands-on therapeutic assistance resists automation. Growing demand from aging population and expanded OT services. AI tools may help extend the reach of each assistant.

title: Oil and gas workers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Almost entirely physical: operating drilling equipment, maintaining pumps, working on offshore platforms, and managing extraction processes. The demanding outdoor physical work in harsh conditions has minimal digital component that AI could affect.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Operating drilling equipment, maintaining wells, and working on oil rigs are physical, hazardous tasks. AI has negligible direct impact on this hands-on extraction work.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Oil and gas extraction involves physical work on drilling rigs, pipelines, and in harsh environments. AI assists with monitoring and process optimization, but the physical operations remain human-performed.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Oil and gas workers operate drilling equipment in variable outdoor environments. While some automation exists for drilling, the harsh and variable conditions of oilfields limit robotic deployment by 2028.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Extraction operations increasingly automated with automated drilling, monitoring, and some maintenance robots. Large-scale operations use significant automation. However, variable field conditions, equipment troubleshooting, and wellsite work in diverse environments still require human workers.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Drilling and extraction in variable field environments. By 2036, automated drilling and monitoring systems handle much routine operation, but field work in diverse geological and environmental conditions requires human adaptation and judgment for novel situations.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large oil and gas companies have resources and motivation for automation. Hazardous work conditions favor robotic deployment. Labour shortages provide pull. Some offshore and remote operations already automated. OSHA and environmental regulations manageable. Mix of large operators (lower friction) and small contractors (higher friction).
demand_elasticity_rationale: Long-term energy transition reduces fossil fuel demand. Automation and remote monitoring reduce field worker headcount. AI-optimized operations extract more with fewer workers. Cyclical commodity prices add volatility.

title: Operations research analysts
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Almost entirely digital: collecting and analyzing data, developing mathematical models, using optimization software, and writing reports. AI significantly enhances modeling, simulation, and pattern detection by 2028. Routine optimization work faces strong automation pressure.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Mathematical modeling, optimization, simulation, and data analysis are heavily digital tasks AI agents handle autonomously. Human analysts focus on problem framing, interpreting results for stakeholders, and novel methodological approaches.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Mathematical modeling, optimization, simulation, and data analysis are structured digital tasks AI handles autonomously. Human analysts remain for framing novel organizational problems, interpreting results in complex stakeholder contexts, and communicating findings to decision-makers.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Operations research analysts use mathematical models to solve problems. Entirely desk-based analytical work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Purely analytical work involving mathematical optimization and modeling. No physical component.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Entirely analytical and computational work. No physical component.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large corporations and government agencies are primary employers. Work is highly quantitative and analytical, perfectly suited to AI. Operations research is inherently computational. AI/ML tools already widely integrated. Moderate institutional inertia in government settings. Clear ROI in industry.
demand_elasticity_rationale: AI creates massive new optimization opportunities. Every logistics, scheduling, and resource allocation problem can benefit from OR techniques. AI tools make OR analysis feasible for more organizations and problems.

title: Opticians
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Core work is hands-on customer service: measuring faces for eyeglasses, adjusting frames, fitting contact lenses, and helping customers select eyewear. Prescription processing is a minor digital component. The physical fitting and interpersonal service dominate.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Fitting eyeglasses, adjusting frames, and assisting customers with lens selection are hands-on tasks requiring physical interaction. AI aids with prescription processing and inventory, but face-to-face service dominates.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Dispensing optical goods involves physical fitting—adjusting frames, interpreting prescriptions, and ensuring proper lens alignment. AI assists with lens selection recommendations, but the hands-on fitting and customer interaction remain human.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Dispensing opticians fit and adjust eyeglasses for customers. The customer interaction and precise adjustment work is primarily service-oriented with minimal physical labor for robots to automate.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Patient-facing work fitting eyeglasses and contact lenses. Automated lens cutting and frame adjustment tools improve, but each patient's face and prescription is unique. The fitting, adjustment, and customer service aspects require human dexterity and interpersonal skills.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Fitting eyeglasses requires interaction with patients' faces and individual anatomy. By 2036, automated measurement and lens-fitting systems assist significantly, but the personal fitting, adjustment, and customer relationship keep human involvement.
adoption_friction_rationale: Mix of large retail optical chains (LensCrafters, Warby Parker) and independent practices. State licensing requirements for dispensing. Physical fitting and adjustment of eyewear. Customer service component. Large chains more amenable to automation. Insurance billing requirements. Moderate employer fragmentation.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Demand tied to vision correction needs in the population. Online eyewear sales provide some competition but fitting and adjustment require in-person service. Aging population supports demand.

title: Optometrists
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Predominantly clinical: performing eye examinations, using specialized equipment, prescribing corrective lenses, and counseling patients. AI assists with image analysis for disease screening by 2028, but the hands-on examination and patient care remain human-driven.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Eye examinations using specialized equipment, prescribing corrective lenses, and diagnosing conditions involve physical patient interaction. AI aids with diagnostic imaging interpretation and records, but clinical practice is hands-on.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates diagnostic image interpretation and screening test analysis. However, eye examinations require physical instrumentation, optometrists prescribe and fit corrective lenses with hands-on assessment, and the patient relationship retains human value.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Optometrists examine eyes and prescribe corrective measures. The work involves clinical examination equipment but is primarily diagnostic, with minimal physical labor component for robots to automate.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Clinical eye examinations requiring patient interaction, skilled use of diagnostic equipment, and clinical judgment. Each patient presents unique conditions. Trust and communication essential. While automated screening tools assist, comprehensive eye care requires human practitioners.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Eye examinations combining diagnostic equipment with patient interaction. By 2036, automated screening assists, but the clinical judgment, patient relationship, and hands-on examination of variable eye conditions require human expertise.
adoption_friction_rationale: State licensing and healthcare regulation. Mix of independent practices and retail chains. Clinical examination requires physical interaction and equipment operation. Patient trust in human diagnosis. Insurance billing complexity. Professional association protections. AI diagnostic tools emerging but regulatory approval slow.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Aging population increases vision care demand. AI diagnostic tools help optometrists detect disease earlier and more accurately. Some latent demand from people who don't get regular eye exams due to cost.

title: Orthotists and prosthetists
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Core work is hands-on: measuring patients, designing custom devices, fabricating artificial limbs and braces, and fitting them. CAD and 3D printing assist with design, but the physical measurement, fabrication, and patient fitting require skilled human practitioners.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Designing and fitting orthotic and prosthetic devices involves physical patient assessment, custom fabrication, and adjustment. AI aids with CAD design and biomechanical analysis, but hands-on fitting and patient care are central.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI assists with device design from digital scans. However, the core work involves physical patient assessment, custom device fabrication and fitting, adjustments requiring manual skill, and patient training—all hands-on interpersonal work.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Orthotists and prosthetists design and fit custom devices for patients. While 3D printing automates some fabrication, the patient fitting and customization require skilled manual work in variable situations.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Custom fabrication and fitting of orthotic and prosthetic devices for individual patients. Each device is customized to unique anatomy. 3D scanning and printing assist fabrication, but fitting, adjustment, and patient interaction require human skill and empathy.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Custom fitting and fabrication of orthotic/prosthetic devices for individual patients. By 2036, 3D scanning and printing automate much fabrication, but custom fitting, patient interaction, and adjustment to individual anatomy and needs require human expertise.
adoption_friction_rationale: State licensing and healthcare regulation. Highly specialized physical fitting and customization. Patient relationship for rehabilitation. Small employer base with limited capital. Insurance billing requirements. 3D printing advancing but clinical judgment and fitting require human expertise. Liability for device performance.
demand_elasticity_rationale: AI and 3D printing enable more personalized and affordable prosthetics and orthotics. Massive unmet demand globally, especially in developing countries. Technology makes custom devices accessible to more patients.

title: Painters, construction and maintenance
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Entirely physical work: preparing surfaces, applying paint and coatings, and working on ladders and scaffolding. This is purely manual construction trade work with no digital component that AI could affect.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Preparing surfaces, applying paint, and finishing walls and structures are entirely physical construction tasks with no digital component.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Painting is entirely physical manual work—preparing surfaces, mixing paint, and applying coatings to buildings and structures. Digital AI has essentially no exposure to this occupation.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Construction painters work in variable building environments with different surfaces and conditions. Unlike factory spray painting, the unstructured nature of construction sites limits robotic painting deployment by 2028.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Large commercial surfaces (warehouses, apartment buildings) increasingly painted by robotic systems. Spray-painting of uniform surfaces highly automatable. However, residential interior painting, detail work, prep work on variable surfaces, and custom finishes still require human painters.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: By 2036, robotic painting systems handle most large-area, standardized painting in commercial and new residential construction. Human painters remain for detail work, complex surfaces, decorative painting, and renovation in variable environments.
adoption_friction_rationale: Fragmented between commercial contractors and many independent painters. Physical work in varied conditions. Painting robotics exist for large flat surfaces but complex residential and detail work is challenging. Labour shortages provide moderate pull. Limited capital among small operators. Union presence in commercial sector.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Physical painting in variable environments resists automation. Demand tied to construction and building maintenance. Some robotic painting emerges for large surfaces but interior and detail work persists.

title: Painting and coating workers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Predominantly physical: operating painting machinery, preparing products for coating, and maintaining equipment. Machine controls have minor digital interfaces, but the physical manufacturing floor work dominates.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Operating paint sprayers, dipping equipment, and coating machinery in manufacturing are physical production tasks. AI has minimal impact on these manual finishing processes.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Operating painting and coating equipment in manufacturing is physical production work. Digital AI has minimal exposure beyond process control monitoring.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Industrial painting and coating in manufacturing is performed in controlled environments with repetitive motions. Robotic spray painting is already standard in automotive; by 2028 it extends further into general manufacturing.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Industrial painting and coating—automotive, furniture, appliances—heavily automated with robotic spray systems. Standardized production lines use automated coating extensively. Powder coating and e-coating fully automated. Human workers handle custom work and quality oversight.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Industrial painting and coating in factory environments is highly automated by 2036. Robotic spray systems handle most production coating. Human involvement is primarily supervisory and for custom/specialty work.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large manufacturing facilities are primary employers. Industrial painting and coating is already significantly automated (robotic spray painting). Quality control increasingly automated. OSHA and EPA regulations manageable. Controlled factory environments suit robotic coating. Labour shortages provide pull.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Industrial painting and coating is increasingly automated with robotic spraying systems. Demand tied to manufacturing volume. AI-guided quality control and robotic application reduce workers per production line.

title: Paralegals and legal assistants
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Almost entirely screen-based: conducting legal research, drafting documents, organizing case files, and managing correspondence. AI significantly automates legal research, document review, and drafting by 2028. Active restructuring in basic paralegal research roles as AI handles routine legal document work.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Legal research, document drafting, contract review, case file management, and discovery processing are heavily digital tasks AI agents handle autonomously by 2031. Human paralegals focus on complex litigation support and client interaction.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Legal research, document preparation, case organization, filing, and discovery review are structured digital tasks AI handles autonomously. The traditional paralegal role is fundamentally restructured, with remaining human work focused on client interaction and complex case coordination.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Paralegals research legal documents and assist lawyers. Desk-based legal support work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Legal research and document preparation work that is entirely knowledge-based. No physical component.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Entirely research, writing, and administrative work. No physical component.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large law firms are primary employers with resources and incentive to adopt AI. Legal research and document review already heavily AI-assisted. e-Discovery automation well-established. Moderate regulatory requirements. Some fragmentation in small firm segment. Clear ROI for document-intensive work.
demand_elasticity_rationale: AI automates much legal research, document review, and contract analysis. But expanding access to legal services (driven by AI efficiency) may create more paralegal work. Net slight reduction as routine tasks automate.

title: Personal financial advisors
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Significant digital work: analyzing financial data, developing investment strategies, and preparing financial plans. AI robo-advisors handle routine portfolio management by 2028. However, complex financial planning, client relationship management, and trust-based advisory remain human-driven.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Portfolio analysis, financial planning, tax optimization, and report generation are automated by AI. Advisors retain value in client relationships, life-stage guidance, behavioral coaching, and navigating complex financial situations.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Portfolio analysis, financial planning, tax optimization, and retirement modeling are automated. Human advisors persist because the advisory relationship involves trust, emotional guidance during market volatility, life transition counseling, and behavioral coaching that clients value from humans.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Financial advisors provide investment and financial planning advice. Interpersonal advisory work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Advisory and client management work that is entirely interpersonal and knowledge-based.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Entirely advisory and analytical work. No physical component.
adoption_friction_rationale: Mix of large firms (lower friction, robo-advisors deployed) and many independent advisors (higher friction). Fiduciary duty and SEC/FINRA regulation. Client preference for human relationship in high-net-worth segment. Robo-advisory already disrupting lower-end market. State registration requirements. Trust and liability concerns.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Robo-advisors handle basic investment allocation, but complex financial planning and the trust relationship with clients persists. Growing wealth and retirement planning needs create demand. Middle-market advisory has latent demand.

title: Pest control workers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Almost entirely physical: inspecting buildings, identifying pest infestations, applying treatments, and setting traps. Scheduling and record-keeping are minor digital components. AI has negligible impact on the hands-on pest control work.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Inspecting properties, applying pesticides, and setting traps are physical tasks requiring on-site presence. AI has negligible impact on hands-on pest control work.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Pest control involves physical on-site work—inspecting properties, applying treatments, and setting traps. Digital AI has negligible exposure to this occupation.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Pest control involves visiting diverse residential and commercial environments to identify and treat infestations. The variable settings and diagnostic assessment required limit robotic deployment by 2028.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Work in diverse residential and commercial environments. Each infestation and building is different. Some automated monitoring and treatment systems exist, but inspecting variable structures, identifying pest entry points, and applying treatments in diverse settings requires human judgment and adaptability.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Working in variable residential and commercial environments. By 2036, automated monitoring and some treatment systems exist, but the extreme variability of buildings, infestation types, and crawlspace/attic access keeps significant human involvement.
adoption_friction_rationale: Fragmented industry of many small local companies. Physical work in varied residential and commercial environments. State licensing for pesticide application. EPA regulations. Customer interaction and trust important. Labour shortages provide moderate pull. Robotic pest control in development but environment variability is challenging.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Physical pest control in varied environments resists automation. Demand tied to property stock and pest prevalence. AI-powered monitoring may improve targeting but application work needs humans.

title: Petroleum engineers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Substantial digital work: designing extraction methods using simulation software, analyzing geological data, and writing technical reports. AI assists with reservoir modeling and production optimization by 2028. Physical drilling oversight and site visits provide non-digital balance.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Reservoir simulation, production optimization, and engineering analysis are digital tasks AI handles well. However, field operations, well site decisions, and managing physical extraction processes require human presence and judgment.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Reservoir modeling, drilling optimization, production analysis, and reporting are automated. Human engineers remain for field operations oversight, novel geological challenges, managing complex multi-stakeholder projects, and on-site decision-making in hazardous environments.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Petroleum engineers design extraction methods. Knowledge-based engineering work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Engineering design and analysis work. Primarily knowledge-based and computational.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Primarily analytical and design engineering work. Some site visits but core role is cognitive.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large oil and gas companies are primary employers with resources and technology culture. AI for reservoir modeling and drilling optimization already deployed. Professional engineering licensing. Moderate regulatory requirements. Remote/offshore work conditions. Industry has strong incentive for efficiency gains.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Long-term energy transition reduces demand for petroleum engineering. AI optimizes extraction but the industry is structurally declining. Some engineers transition to geothermal and carbon capture roles.

title: Pharmacists
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: A blend of digital knowledge work (verifying prescriptions, checking drug interactions, managing inventory systems) and interpersonal patient care (counseling patients, collaborating with physicians). AI assists with interaction checking and dispensing automation by 2028, but patient counseling and clinical judgment remain human.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: AI handles drug interaction checking, prescription processing, and inventory management. Pharmacists retain patient counseling, complex medication management, clinical decision-making, and regulatory compliance roles.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates drug interaction checking, dosage calculations, insurance processing, and medication therapy management analysis. However, pharmacists provide patient counseling, administer vaccinations, and serve as accessible healthcare providers—roles combining physical presence with interpersonal care.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Pharmacists primarily provide clinical consultation and medication management (knowledge work), but also oversee physical dispensing. Robotic dispensing handles the physical component while pharmacists focus on clinical roles.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Automated dispensing systems handle majority of routine prescription filling. Robotic pharmacy systems operational in many hospitals and large retail pharmacies. Pharmacists shift to clinical consulting, patient counseling, and medication therapy management. The physical dispensing is largely automated.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: By 2036, robotic dispensing handles most routine prescription filling. Pharmacists' remaining role is clinical counseling, drug interaction assessment, and patient education—cognitive and interpersonal work. Physical dispensing is largely automated.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large pharmacy chains (CVS, Walgreens) are primary employers with resources to adopt. Robotic dispensing already deployed. State licensing and DEA regulations. Pharmacist clinical judgment for drug interactions valued. Insurance and billing complexity. Patient counseling component has social barriers. Labour shortages provide pull.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Automated dispensing systems and AI drug interaction checking reduce the need for pharmacist oversight of routine prescriptions. Clinical pharmacy roles expand but retail pharmacy faces automation pressure. Net slight decline.

title: Pharmacy technicians
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: A blend of physical tasks (counting pills, packaging medications, maintaining stock) and digital work (processing prescriptions in systems, managing inventory databases, verifying insurance). AI assists with inventory management and prescription processing by 2028, but physical medication handling remains significant.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Automated dispensing systems handle much routine medication counting and labeling. Technicians retain roles in compounding, patient interaction, insurance processing, and managing physical pharmacy operations.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates prescription processing, insurance verification, and inventory management. However, physical medication dispensing, compounding, and direct customer service at the pharmacy counter retain human roles.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Pharmacy technicians count, label, and dispense medications in structured pharmacy environments. Automated dispensing systems and robotic pharmacy fulfillment are commercially deployed in hospital and retail pharmacies by 2028.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Routine prescription filling, counting, and packaging heavily automated. Robotic pharmacy systems handle standardized dispensing. Human technicians focus on special preparations, insurance issues, and tasks automated systems cannot handle. High-volume pharmacies substantially automated.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: By 2036, robotic pharmacy systems handle most routine prescription counting, packaging, and dispensing. Human technicians remain for patient interaction, insurance resolution, and oversight. The majority of physical dispensing tasks are automated.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large pharmacy chains are primary employers. Automated dispensing systems already widespread. State certification requirements. Work is highly standardized for medication counting and filling. Patient interaction for pickup has some social element. Insurance billing increasingly automated. Labour shortages provide pull.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Automated pill counting, robotic dispensing, and digital prescription management directly reduce pharmacy technician tasks. Mail-order pharmacy further automates. Physical compounding persists but represents a small share.

title: Phlebotomists
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Almost entirely hands-on clinical work: drawing blood, labeling specimens, calming patients, and maintaining sterile equipment. Electronic record entry is a minor digital component. AI cannot perform the physical blood draw procedure.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Drawing blood, labeling specimens, and interacting with patients are entirely physical clinical tasks. AI has negligible impact on phlebotomy procedures.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Drawing blood is entirely hands-on physical clinical work requiring manual dexterity and patient interaction. AI assists with order processing and specimen tracking, but the core skill—venipuncture—remains human.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Phlebotomists draw blood requiring precise venipuncture on varied patients. Automated blood-drawing devices are in development, but patient vein variability and the need for patient comfort limit deployment by 2028.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Blood drawing requires patient interaction, vein identification in variable anatomy, and skilled needle insertion. Each patient's veins and anxiety levels differ. Trust and patient comfort essential. Automated blood-draw devices exist for some settings but patient variability limits adoption.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Blood drawing requires precise needle insertion in varied patient anatomy. By 2036, automated blood-drawing robots handle many routine venipunctures, but difficult veins, anxious patients, and varied anatomy still require human skill and patient comfort.
adoption_friction_rationale: Healthcare regulation and certification. Hospital systems are large employers. Physical blood draw requires manual skill in variable patient anatomy. Patient comfort and anxiety management requires human interaction. Automated blood draw devices emerging but not yet reliable for all patients. Liability concerns.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Physical blood drawing resists automation (though robotic phlebotomy is in development). Demand tied to lab testing volume, which grows with aging population. AI has minimal current impact on the manual skill.

title: Photographers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: A significant digital component: editing photos using software, managing digital assets, marketing services online, and delivering work digitally. AI image tools affect stock photography and routine editing by 2028. However, live shooting (weddings, events, portraits) requires physical presence and artistic vision.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: AI generates synthetic images and automates post-processing. However, event photography, portrait sessions, and creative commercial shoots requiring human presence, composition judgment, and real-world scene capture persist.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI generates stock imagery and automates post-processing. However, photography involving physical presence—events, portraits, commercial shoots, photojournalism—retains human photographers for creative vision, real-world scene composition, and the irreplaceable element of being physically present.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Photographers use cameras in varied settings to capture images. While some automated photography exists (photo booths), creative photography in variable environments requires human judgment.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Creative visual work requiring artistic vision and adaptation to variable subjects and conditions. While automated camera technology improves, professional photography is about creative interpretation, client interaction, and artistic judgment.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Creative photography requires artistic vision, composition judgment, and human interaction (for portraits). By 2036, automated cameras exist for routine documentation, but creative and portrait photography remain human-driven due to artistic judgment and interpersonal skills.
adoption_friction_rationale: Extremely fragmented industry of independent photographers and small studios. AI image generation advancing but event/portrait photography values human interaction and artistic vision. Some commercial photography amenable to AI. Limited capital among independents. Wedding and portrait market has strong human preference.
demand_elasticity_rationale: AI image generation threatens stock photography but creates more demand for authentic human photography. Every business, event, and social media presence needs photography. Latent demand from businesses that couldn't afford professional photography.

title: Physical therapist assistants and aides
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Predominantly hands-on patient care: helping patients with exercises, providing physical support, and preparing treatment areas. Documentation has a minor digital component. The physical therapeutic assistance and patient interaction cannot be automated.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Assisting patients with exercises, applying therapeutic treatments, and supporting rehabilitation are hands-on physical tasks. AI has minimal impact on direct patient care duties.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: PT assistants work directly with patients performing physical therapy exercises, providing manual therapy, and assisting with mobility. AI assists with exercise programming and documentation, but the hands-on patient care is entirely human.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: PT assistants help patients perform exercises and provide hands-on care under therapist supervision. The varied patient needs and physical interaction requirements limit robotic exposure by 2028.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Hands-on patient care guiding exercises and providing physical support. Each patient's condition and progress differs. Trust and motivation essential. Some robotic exercise equipment assists, but personal guidance and manual therapy techniques require human touch and judgment.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Hands-on therapy implementation with direct patient physical interaction. By 2036, robotic therapy equipment assists with exercises, but guiding patients through varied movements and adapting to individual physical needs requires human presence.
adoption_friction_rationale: State licensing and healthcare regulation. Physical rehabilitation exercises require hands-on guidance and patient assessment. Patient therapeutic relationship valued. Mix of hospital/clinic and outpatient settings. Insurance billing requires licensed providers. Moderate employer fragmentation. Liability concerns.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Hands-on therapeutic exercises resist automation. Aging population and growing PT demand increase needs. AI monitoring may help assistants serve more patients. Physical care cannot be delegated to AI.

title: Physical therapists
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Core work is hands-on: evaluating patients' movement, developing treatment plans through physical assessment, and guiding patients through therapeutic exercises. AI assists with treatment planning and outcome tracking by 2028, but the physical examination and manual therapy dominate.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Evaluating patients through physical examination, performing manual therapy, and guiding exercises are hands-on clinical duties. AI assists with treatment planning and outcome tracking, but physical patient interaction is central.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates treatment plan design and progress documentation. However, physical therapy is fundamentally hands-on—manual assessment, therapeutic exercise supervision, manual therapy techniques, and motivating patients through rehabilitation require human presence and touch.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Physical therapists guide patients through exercises and manual therapy requiring clinical judgment and physical interaction. The varied patient conditions and need for adaptive touch limit robotic replacement by 2028.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Clinical assessment and hands-on treatment requiring skilled touch, patient communication, and real-time adaptation to patient responses. Each patient presents unique conditions. Trust and therapeutic relationship essential. Very resistant to physical automation.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Hands-on therapeutic assessment and treatment requiring adaptive physical interaction with patients. By 2036, robotic therapy equipment is advanced, but the diagnostic touch, treatment adaptation, and patient relationship keep this predominantly human. Each patient presents unique physical challenges.
adoption_friction_rationale: State licensing and healthcare regulation. Hands-on physical treatment and patient assessment. Strong patient preference for human therapist. Malpractice liability. Mix of hospital systems and private practices. Insurance billing complexity. AI tools for exercise planning emerging but manual therapy requires human skill.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Significant unmet demand for physical therapy. Many patients are undertreated due to access and cost. AI tools help therapists create personalized programs and monitor progress remotely, extending reach to more patients.

title: Physician assistants
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Predominantly clinical: examining patients, diagnosing conditions, prescribing medications, and performing procedures. AI diagnostic support tools assist with clinical decision-making by 2028, but hands-on patient examination, procedural work, and clinical judgment remain firmly human.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Clinical examination, procedures, and patient counseling are hands-on duties. AI significantly aids with diagnostic decision support, ordering, and documentation, but direct patient care and clinical judgment remain human.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates diagnostic support, treatment protocol recommendations, and documentation. However, PAs perform physical examinations, procedures, and provide direct patient care requiring hands-on clinical skills and interpersonal patient relationships.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Physician assistants examine patients and perform clinical procedures. The varied patient encounters and clinical judgment required limit physical robotic automation by 2028.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Clinical practice involving patient examination, diagnosis, and treatment. Each patient is unique. Requires trust, communication, and hands-on clinical skills. While diagnostic tools improve, the physical examination and patient interaction remain human.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Clinical practice combining cognitive diagnosis with physical examination and procedures. By 2036, diagnostic automation assists, but the patient relationship, physical exam of varied patients, and clinical procedures in variable settings require human presence and judgment.
adoption_friction_rationale: State licensing and healthcare regulation with physician supervision requirements. Clinical examination and prescribing authority. High patient trust requirements. Malpractice liability. Employed primarily by healthcare systems. Professional scope-of-practice protections. Labour shortages provide some pull.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Massive unmet demand for primary and specialty care. PAs extend physician capacity and AI tools enhance their diagnostic capabilities. Growing scope of practice and acceptance. Healthcare access gaps indicate vast latent demand.

title: Physicians and surgeons
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Core work is clinical: examining patients, performing procedures and surgeries, and making complex diagnostic decisions. AI assists with imaging interpretation, treatment recommendations, and documentation by 2028. However, physical examinations, surgical skills, and life-or-death clinical judgment remain fundamentally human.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Physical examinations, surgeries, and patient interactions are hands-on clinical work. AI transforms diagnostics, treatment planning, and documentation, but the practice of medicine—especially surgery—requires human skill, judgment, and patient trust.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates diagnosis from imaging and lab data, treatment protocol recommendations, and medical documentation. However, physical examinations, surgical procedures, complex clinical judgment in ambiguous cases, and the patient-physician relationship where human accountability and empathy matter ensure substantial human roles.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Surgeons use robotic surgical systems (da Vinci) as tools, but these augment rather than replace the surgeon. The complex judgment and varied patient situations keep physical automation exposure minimal.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Complex clinical practice and surgery. Robotic surgical systems assist with standardized procedures, but surgeons still direct and oversee. Diagnosis requires nuanced physical examination and patient interaction. Each patient is unique. Trust is paramount.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: By 2036, robotic surgery handles most standardized procedures. Physicians' role shifts toward complex/novel cases, diagnosis of unusual conditions, and patient management. Physical examination increasingly augmented. The combination of clinical judgment, patient relationship, and procedural skill for complex cases keeps significant human involvement.
adoption_friction_rationale: Heavy state licensing, board certification, and malpractice liability. Strong patient trust requirements. FDA regulatory path for AI diagnostics is slow. Surgery requires extreme precision and judgment. AMA and specialty society protections. Deep healthcare institutional inertia. Some AI diagnostic tools emerging but full practice automation faces decade-plus friction.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Enormous global unmet demand for medical care. AI diagnostic tools augment physician capabilities rather than replace them. Physicians become more effective with AI, potentially serving more patients and catching more conditions.

title: Physicists and astronomers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Predominantly digital: running computational simulations, analyzing large datasets, building theoretical models, and writing research papers. AI significantly assists with data analysis, simulation, and literature review by 2028. Some laboratory experiment work and telescope operation provide physical balance.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Data analysis, simulation, and literature review are digital tasks AI accelerates substantially. However, designing novel experiments, theoretical breakthroughs, and operating physical instruments require human researchers.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Data analysis, simulation, literature synthesis, and computational physics are automated. Human physicists remain for genuinely novel theoretical insights, designing unprecedented experiments, and interpreting results that challenge existing frameworks. Observational astronomy data processing is fully automated.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Physicists conduct research using theoretical and experimental methods. Knowledge-based scientific work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Research work with some experimental/observational components. The core work is theoretical and analytical. Lab/observatory work involves some physical equipment but is secondary.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Primarily theoretical and computational research. Some experimental physics involves lab equipment, but the core work is cognitive. Observational astronomy is already highly automated.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large research institutions, government labs (DOE, NASA), and universities. AI/ML already transforming data analysis and simulation. Research requires creative hypothesis generation. Academic institutional inertia. Physical experimental work requires presence. Moderate employer consolidation. Limited regulatory barriers.
demand_elasticity_rationale: AI accelerates simulation and data analysis in physics. New research directions in quantum computing, fusion energy, and astrophysics. Research funding limits expansion more than productivity.

title: Plumbers, pipefitters, and steamfitters
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Predominantly hands-on skilled trade work: installing and repairing piping systems, soldering, cutting pipe, and testing for leaks. Blueprint reading and cost estimation have minor digital components. AI has minimal impact on the physical plumbing work. Calibration anchor occupation.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Installing and repairing pipes, fixtures, and plumbing systems is hands-on skilled trade work. AI has minimal impact on these physical construction tasks.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Plumbing is entirely physical skilled trade work—installing and repairing pipes, fixtures, and systems in buildings. Digital AI has essentially no exposure to this occupation.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Plumbers work in highly variable residential and commercial environments where every building presents different configurations. The unpredictable physical environment and fine manual dexterity required are beyond 2028 robotics.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Work in highly variable residential and commercial environments. Each building has unique plumbing configurations and challenges. Troubleshooting leaks, working in tight spaces, and adapting to existing infrastructure requires human dexterity and judgment.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Plumbing involves highly variable environments—every building's plumbing configuration is different. By 2036, robots handle standardized new-construction plumbing, but repair, renovation, and working in existing buildings with unknown configurations require significant human judgment and adaptability.
adoption_friction_rationale: Highly fragmented between commercial contractors and many independent operators. Physical work in varied, confined building conditions. Strong union presence (UA). State licensing requirements. Acute labour shortages provide pull but work in existing building infrastructure is extremely challenging for robotics. Code compliance requires judgment.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Physical plumbing work in variable environments resists automation. Growing demand from aging infrastructure, water systems, and new construction. Persistent labor shortages indicate unmet demand.

title: Podiatrists
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Core work is clinical and procedural: examining feet, diagnosing conditions, prescribing treatments, and performing surgery. Patient records and imaging have digital components, but the hands-on examination and surgical procedures dominate.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Examining and treating foot conditions, performing procedures, and fitting orthotics are hands-on clinical duties. AI aids with diagnostics and records, but physical patient care dominates.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI assists with diagnostic imaging interpretation and treatment planning. However, podiatric care is primarily hands-on—examining feet, performing procedures, fitting orthotics, and providing direct patient care requiring physical presence and manual skill.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Podiatrists diagnose and treat foot conditions with clinical examination and procedures. The varied patient conditions and fine clinical manual work limit robotic replacement by 2028.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Clinical foot and ankle care requiring patient examination, diagnosis, and treatment. Each patient presents unique conditions. Surgical procedures require skilled dexterity. Trust and communication essential.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Foot and ankle care combining diagnosis with physical treatment. Requires patient interaction and hands-on treatment of varied conditions. By 2036, some routine procedures may be robot-assisted, but the clinical judgment, patient relationship, and variable conditions keep this human-centered.
adoption_friction_rationale: State licensing and healthcare regulation. Mostly in small independent practices with limited capital. Physical examination and treatment of feet. Malpractice liability. Patient preference for human practitioners. Professional association protections. Insurance billing complexity. Small practice structure limits technology investment.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Demand tied to foot care needs in the population, growing modestly with aging and diabetes prevalence. AI diagnostics may help but the physical examination and treatment aspects persist.

title: Police and detectives
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: A blend of physical patrol and enforcement with digital investigative work (analyzing evidence, writing reports, searching databases). AI assists with surveillance analysis, report writing, and crime pattern detection by 2028. Physical patrol, arrests, and community interaction remain firmly human. Calibration anchor area.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Patrol, emergency response, and suspect apprehension are physical duties. AI aids detective work through data analysis, surveillance processing, and report generation, but community policing and physical law enforcement remain human.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates report writing, surveillance analysis, crime pattern analysis, and administrative tasks. However, policing is fundamentally physical and interpersonal—patrol, arrest, community interaction, interrogation, and maintaining public safety require human presence and judgment.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Police work involves unpredictable physical situations, community interaction, and investigative judgment. The highly variable and socially complex nature of policing makes robotic replacement minimal by 2028.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Law enforcement in unpredictable environments requiring split-second human judgment, de-escalation, investigation, and community interaction. Each situation is unique. Public trust and authority dynamics are inherently human. Surveillance technology assists but officers remain essential.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Law enforcement involves unpredictable human interactions, variable environments, and judgment-intensive situations. By 2036, surveillance and data analysis are automated, but the human authority, de-escalation skills, investigative judgment, and community trust required keep this predominantly human. Regulatory and ethical requirements demand human officers.
adoption_friction_rationale: Government employment with powerful unions (FOP, PBA). Constitutional requirements for law enforcement. Enormous public trust, accountability, and use-of-force liability. Deep institutional culture and traditions. Community policing requires human presence and judgment. Some AI surveillance tools adopted but officers cannot be replaced.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Public safety staffing is policy-driven and relatively stable per capita. AI aids surveillance and investigation but community policing requires human presence. Reform movements may alter staffing models in either direction.

title: Political scientists
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Almost entirely digital knowledge work: researching political systems, analyzing data, writing papers, and evaluating policy. AI significantly accelerates research, data analysis, and literature review by 2028. Routine political analysis faces strong automation, with senior researchers focusing on novel theoretical contributions.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Data analysis, policy research, literature synthesis, and report writing are heavily digital tasks AI agents handle well. Political scientists retain value in interpretive analysis, institutional knowledge, and advisory roles requiring political judgment.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Data analysis, literature review, survey analysis, and policy brief drafting are automated. Human political scientists remain for novel theoretical frameworks, interpreting complex political dynamics requiring cultural understanding, and advisory roles where human judgment about power and governance is valued.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Political scientists study political systems. Entirely knowledge-based research work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Research and analysis work that is entirely knowledge-based. No physical component.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Entirely research and analytical work. No physical component.
adoption_friction_rationale: Primarily academic employment with institutional inertia. AI tools for data analysis and polling advancing. Research requires interpretive judgment and cultural understanding. Limited policy impact without human advocacy. Moderate employer fragmentation across universities and think tanks. No significant regulatory barriers.
demand_elasticity_rationale: AI enables more sophisticated political analysis and modeling. Growing demand for policy analysis, political risk assessment, and public opinion research. Think tanks and political consulting expand.

title: Postal service workers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Predominantly physical: sorting mail, delivering letters and packages, and operating postal vehicles. Automated sorting machines handle some work, but the physical delivery routes and customer interaction dominate. AI has limited additional impact beyond existing automation.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Sorting, delivering mail, and operating postal equipment are physical tasks. Automated sorting advances, but last-mile delivery and customer-facing window services require human workers. Digital communication reduces mail volume overall.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Sorting mail has been increasingly automated, but mail carriers physically deliver to addresses, and counter clerks provide in-person customer service. Digital AI automates the sorting and routing functions, but physical delivery remains human. The overall digital exposure is moderate.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Postal workers sort and deliver mail, combining structured sorting facility work with unstructured delivery routes. Sorting automation is well advanced; delivery remains difficult for robots due to variable residential environments.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Mail sorting heavily automated with robotic systems. Delivery routes increasingly use autonomous vehicles for some segments. Counter service declining. However, residential last-mile delivery in diverse neighborhoods and buildings still requires human carriers for many routes.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: By 2036, mail sorting is fully automated and delivery is predominantly autonomous. Postal counter services are largely replaced by automated systems. Human involvement is marginal—primarily for unusual packages and remote delivery.
adoption_friction_rationale: USPS is a single large employer with motivation to automate. Mail sorting already heavily automated. Delivery requires physical presence for last-mile. Strong union protections (NALC, APWU). Government institutional inertia. Some autonomous delivery vehicle pilots. Labour shortages provide moderate pull.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Mail volume has been declining for decades as communication goes digital. AI-optimized sorting and autonomous delivery vehicles further reduce postal workforce needs. Package delivery grows but is increasingly automated.

title: Postsecondary education administrators
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Predominantly digital administrative work: managing student records, overseeing admissions processes, analyzing institutional data, and coordinating programs. AI assists with enrollment management, data analysis, and process automation by 2028. Student and faculty engagement provides interpersonal balance.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Enrollment management, financial aid processing, compliance reporting, and data analysis are digital tasks heavily automated by AI. Administrators retain strategic planning, stakeholder relations, and institutional leadership roles.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates enrollment management, financial aid processing, data analysis, compliance reporting, and scheduling. Human administrators remain for student affairs requiring personal judgment, institutional strategy, community relations, and navigating the complex politics of higher education.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Education administrators perform management, planning, and coordination. Their work is entirely administrative and cognitive with no physical labor component.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Administrative and management work in higher education. Entirely knowledge-based.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Entirely administrative and management work. No physical component.
adoption_friction_rationale: Higher education has deep institutional inertia, shared governance, and complex stakeholder relationships. Large universities have resources but bureaucratic cultures. Accreditation requirements. Some administrative functions amenable to AI but leadership, fundraising, and community roles require human presence.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Administrative positions scale with the number of institutions and students. AI may automate some administrative tasks but regulatory compliance and student services persist. Enrollment trends are mixed.

title: Postsecondary teachers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: A blend of in-person teaching (lectures, seminars, office hours) and digital knowledge work (research, writing publications, grading, developing course materials). AI significantly assists with research, grading, and content development by 2028. The teaching relationship and original research remain human-driven.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: AI tutoring systems handle content delivery, grading, and research assistance. Professors retain value in mentoring, original research, seminar facilitation, and advancing knowledge at the frontier, but course delivery is transformed.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates lecture content delivery, grading, and course material preparation. However, university teaching involves research mentorship, seminar discussion facilitation, scholarly identity where human authorship matters, and the interpersonal advising relationships that are central to graduate education.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Teaching is fundamentally interpersonal and cognitive work involving instruction, mentoring, and classroom management. There is no physical labor component for robots to automate.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Teaching and research at colleges and universities. Fundamentally interpersonal and knowledge-based. No physical automation potential.
