physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Teaching at the college level involves lecture, discussion, and mentoring. Lab courses have physical components, but the core academic role is cognitive instruction and research. Physical presence for teaching is valued but not a physical labor task.
adoption_friction_rationale: Strong academic institutional inertia and tenure protections. Research and mentorship require human judgment and creativity. Accreditation standards. Some lecture delivery amenable to AI/online but lab teaching, seminars, and advising resist automation. Academic freedom culture resists standardization.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Growing global demand for higher education. AI tools enhance teaching but cannot replace the mentorship, research guidance, and critical thinking development that professors provide. Online education expands access.

title: Power plant operators, distributors, and dispatchers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: A blend of physical equipment monitoring (operating controls, inspecting equipment) and digital system monitoring (using SCADA systems, monitoring power distribution). AI assists with predictive maintenance and load optimization, but the safety-critical physical plant operation requires human oversight.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: AI assists with grid optimization and monitoring, but operating physical plant equipment, managing safety systems, and responding to emergencies require on-site human presence and real-time judgment.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates monitoring systems, load balancing, and routine operations. However, physical plant operations, emergency response, equipment maintenance, and safety-critical oversight in regulated energy environments retain substantial human roles.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Power plant operators monitor and control equipment in structured plant environments. Control room operations are increasingly automated, and some physical plant maintenance tasks are in controlled environments.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Power plant operations increasingly automated with remote monitoring and automated control systems. Routine operations handled by automated systems. Human operators focus on anomaly response, maintenance coordination, and complex decisions. Some plants approach lights-out operation.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: By 2036, power plant operations are highly automated with remote monitoring and control. Routine operations require minimal human presence. Humans remain for emergency response, unusual conditions, and regulatory oversight.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large utilities are primary employers with resources. NERC reliability standards and NRC (nuclear) regulation. Control room automation advancing but human oversight required for safety-critical grid operations. Union presence (IBEW, UWUA). Labour shortages provide moderate pull. Infrastructure modernization is ongoing.
demand_elasticity_rationale: AI and automation increasingly manage grid operations and plant monitoring. The transition to distributed renewable energy changes the operator role. Fewer operators needed per unit of generation capacity.

title: Preschool and childcare center directors
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: A blend of interpersonal management (supervising staff, communicating with parents, ensuring child welfare) and digital administration (budgeting, enrollment management, regulatory compliance). AI assists with administrative tasks by 2028, but the in-person leadership and childcare oversight dominate.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Administrative tasks like budgeting and enrollment are aided by AI. However, managing staff caring for young children, ensuring safety, parent relationships, and regulatory compliance require significant human presence and judgment.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates administrative tasks—enrollment, billing, compliance documentation, and scheduling. However, directing a childcare center requires physical presence, staff leadership, parent relationships, and ensuring the quality of care through direct observation and interpersonal management.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Education administrators perform management, planning, and coordination. Their work is entirely administrative and cognitive with no physical labor component.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Management and educational leadership work. Entirely administrative and interpersonal.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Management role focused on program administration and staff supervision. No significant physical labor component.
adoption_friction_rationale: State licensing and child safety regulations. Fragmented industry of small centers. Parents expect human leadership for their children's care. Management requires community relationships and crisis response. Low capital availability. Strong social resistance to non-human management of childcare. Liability for child safety.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Management positions scale with the number of childcare facilities. AI may help with administration but on-site leadership persists. Growing demand for childcare offsets efficiency gains.

title: Preschool teachers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Almost entirely interpersonal and physical: teaching young children through play, supervising activities, assessing developmental progress, and communicating with parents. The nurturing, hands-on care of young children is fundamentally human with minimal digital component.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Teaching young children requires constant physical presence, emotional attunement, and hands-on care. AI has minimal application in early childhood education where human interaction and safety supervision are paramount.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Preschool teaching is fundamentally physical and interpersonal—nurturing very young children, managing behavior, facilitating play-based learning, and providing emotional security. AI has minimal applicability to the core of this deeply human, embodied role.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Teaching is fundamentally interpersonal and cognitive work involving instruction, mentoring, and classroom management. There is no physical labor component for robots to automate.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Teaching very young children requires extreme human sensitivity, improvisation, and emotional care. Each child needs individual attention. Among the most interpersonal occupations. No automation potential.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Teaching very young children requires enormous human warmth, patience, and physical engagement in play and learning activities. The emotional nurturing, safety oversight, and adaptive interaction with young children are inherently human needs.
adoption_friction_rationale: Extreme social resistance to non-human care of very young children. Heavy state licensing and safety regulations. Child development requires human nurturing, social-emotional interaction, and physical supervision. Parents strongly prefer human teachers. Liability concerns paramount. Fragmented employer base of small centers.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Enormous unmet demand for quality early childhood education. Young children need human interaction and care. AI tools can help with individualized learning plans but cannot replace the teacher-child relationship.

title: Private detectives and investigators
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: A blend of physical fieldwork (surveillance, interviewing witnesses, visiting locations) and digital research (searching databases, analyzing records, preparing reports). AI assists with background checks and data analysis by 2028, but physical surveillance and in-person investigation remain essential.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Background checks, digital surveillance, and records research are digital tasks AI handles well. However, physical surveillance, witness interviews, and undercover investigations require human presence and judgment.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates digital research, background checks, surveillance footage analysis, and report writing. However, physical surveillance, interviewing witnesses, and conducting field investigations require human presence, interpersonal skills, and situational judgment.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Private investigators conduct research, surveillance, and interviews. Their work is primarily cognitive and interpersonal with no physical labor component for robots to automate.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Investigation work in highly variable environments. Each case is unique. While surveillance technology assists, physical investigation, interviews, and undercover work require human adaptability and judgment.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Investigative work in variable environments requiring surveillance, interviews, and analysis. By 2036, surveillance technology is advanced, but the unpredictable nature of investigations and need for human judgment in novel situations keeps this human-centered.
adoption_friction_rationale: Fragmented industry of small agencies and independent operators. Surveillance and research amenable to AI tools. Physical investigation requires human presence and judgment. State licensing requirements. Some large corporate investigation firms have more resources. Legal and evidentiary requirements favor human investigators.
demand_elasticity_rationale: AI tools enhance investigation capabilities (digital forensics, background checks) but also automate some research tasks. Growing cybersecurity and corporate fraud create new investigation demand.

title: Probation officers and correctional treatment specialists
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: A blend of interpersonal work (interviewing offenders, conducting home visits, counseling) and digital tasks (writing reports, managing case files, analyzing risk assessments). AI assists with report writing and risk scoring by 2028, but the face-to-face supervision and rehabilitation work remain human.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: AI assists with risk assessment, case documentation, and compliance monitoring. However, face-to-face supervision, counseling offenders, and making judgment calls about community safety require human interpersonal skills and authority.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates risk assessment scoring, case documentation, and compliance monitoring. However, the core work is interpersonal—supervising offenders through personal meetings, counseling, crisis intervention, and building rehabilitative relationships.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Probation officers conduct assessments and supervise offenders through meetings and evaluations. This is interpersonal and administrative work with no physical labor component.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Supervision and counseling work that is entirely interpersonal. Requires trust, human judgment, and communication. No physical component.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Primarily cognitive and interpersonal work—monitoring compliance, counseling, and making judicial recommendations. Minimal physical component.
adoption_friction_rationale: Government employment with institutional inertia. Constitutional requirements for supervision and due process. Risk assessment involves human judgment about public safety. Strong union protections. Caseload management has some AI tools but direct supervision requires human presence. Liability for supervised individuals' actions.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Caseload driven by criminal justice system throughput, which is policy-dependent. AI risk assessment tools may alter supervision models. Reform movements may change demand in either direction.

title: Producers and directors
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: A mix of in-person creative leadership (directing actors, managing productions, attending shoots) and digital work (editing, budgeting, scheduling, reviewing content). AI assists with production scheduling and post-production by 2028, but creative vision and on-set leadership remain human.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: AI handles script analysis, scheduling, budgeting, and some post-production tasks. However, creative vision, on-set direction of performers, and managing the complex human dynamics of production retain strong human value.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates script analysis, scheduling, budgeting, and post-production workflows. However, directing involves real-time creative leadership on set, managing actors and crews interpersonally, and producing requires relationship-based deal-making and creative vision that retains human value.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Producers and directors oversee film and media production. Creative and managerial work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Creative management and artistic direction. Entirely knowledge-based leadership work.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Creative management and leadership roles. The physical component is overseeing production environments, but the core work is creative vision, decision-making, and team leadership.
adoption_friction_rationale: Mix of large studios (lower friction) and many independent productions (higher friction). Creative leadership and vision highly valued. Union protections (DGA, PGA). Management of complex creative teams requires human judgment. AI tools for pre-production and editing emerging but creative authority resists automation.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Explosion of content creation across streaming, social media, gaming, and corporate communications. AI tools assist production but creative vision and project leadership remain human. Every content platform needs more producers.

title: Project management specialists
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Predominantly digital: managing schedules, budgets, and resources using project management software; writing status reports; and coordinating stakeholders. AI copilots significantly assist with scheduling optimization, risk analysis, and reporting by 2028. Cross-functional leadership provides some insulation. Calibration anchor occupation.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Scheduling, tracking, reporting, risk analysis, and documentation are heavily automated by AI agents. Project managers retain stakeholder management, team leadership, complex problem resolution, and strategic decision-making roles.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Scheduling, resource allocation, progress tracking, risk analysis, and reporting are automated by AI. Human project managers remain for stakeholder management, navigating organizational politics, motivating teams through interpersonal leadership, and resolving ambiguous cross-functional conflicts.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Project managers plan and oversee projects. Managerial knowledge work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Planning, coordination, and management work. Entirely knowledge and interpersonal work.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Entirely planning, coordination, and management work. No physical component.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large corporations are primary employers with resources. AI project management tools already widely adopted. Coordination and stakeholder management require human judgment. PMP certification creates professional standards. Work is increasingly tool-augmented. Moderate employer fragmentation in consulting.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Every organization runs projects, and AI enables more ambitious projects. AI automates scheduling and tracking but the human coordination and stakeholder management aspects persist. Growing project complexity maintains demand.

title: Property appraisers and assessors
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: A blend of physical property inspections and digital analysis (researching comparable sales, analyzing market data, preparing valuation reports). AI assists with automated valuation models and report generation by 2028. Physical property inspections and professional judgment provide meaningful insulation.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Comparable sales analysis, valuation modeling, and report generation are digital tasks AI handles efficiently. Human appraisers retain physical property inspections and complex valuation judgment, but routine appraisals are largely automated.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Comparable sales analysis, valuation modeling, and report generation are automated digital tasks. Physical property inspection retains some human role, but the analytical core of appraisal—which is predominantly data-driven—is fully automated.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Property appraisers evaluate real estate values. Analytical work with site visits but no physical labor.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Property inspection and valuation work. Each property is unique. While automated valuation models assist, physical inspection of diverse properties in variable conditions still requires human judgment. The inspection component is secondary to analytical work.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Property inspection involves visiting and evaluating buildings. By 2036, drone and sensor technology assists with exterior/structural assessment, but interior evaluation and judgment about property condition still requires human presence in variable environments.
adoption_friction_rationale: Mix of government assessors and private appraisers. AI valuation models (AVMs) already widely used. State licensing requirements. Fannie Mae/Freddie Mac regulations. Physical property inspection still required for many appraisals. Liability for valuation accuracy. Fragmented independent appraiser base.
demand_elasticity_rationale: AI and automated valuation models (AVMs) increasingly provide property value estimates. Many lenders accept AI-generated appraisals for standard properties. Complex and unique properties still need human assessment but standard appraisals automate.

title: Property, real estate, and community association managers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: A blend of digital management (financial reporting, lease administration, marketing) and physical on-site work (property inspections, tenant relations, maintenance oversight). AI assists with financial analysis and communication by 2028, but property visits and tenant management remain hands-on.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Financial reporting, tenant communication, and maintenance scheduling are automated by AI. However, physical property inspections, tenant relations, vendor management, and on-site problem resolution require human presence.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates financial management, lease administration, maintenance scheduling, and compliance tracking. However, property management requires physical inspections, tenant relationship management, vendor coordination, and community leadership that retain human roles.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Property managers oversee real estate operations. Managerial work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Management work overseeing properties. Some maintenance coordination involves physical oversight, but the role is primarily administrative and interpersonal.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Primarily management and business operations work. Some property inspection, but core role is administrative and interpersonal.
adoption_friction_rationale: Mix of large management companies and small firms. Management role requires tenant/owner relationships and physical property oversight. Some AI tools for financial management and maintenance scheduling. State licensing in many jurisdictions. Moderate employer fragmentation. Human relationship component valued.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Management positions scale with the number of properties. AI helps with tenant communications and maintenance scheduling but on-site management and decision-making persist. Property stock grows modestly.

title: Psychiatric technicians and aides
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Predominantly interpersonal and physical: monitoring patient behavior, assisting with daily activities, providing therapeutic care, and maintaining safe environments. Documentation has a minor digital component, but the hands-on patient care in psychiatric settings dominates.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Monitoring patients, assisting with daily activities, and providing therapeutic support in psychiatric facilities are hands-on, interpersonal duties. AI has minimal impact on direct patient care in mental health settings.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Working with psychiatric patients involves direct physical care, behavioral observation, de-escalation of crises, and interpersonal support. AI assists with documentation, but the hands-on patient care in psychiatric facilities is fundamentally human.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Psychiatric techs provide care to patients with mental illness, including physical assistance and monitoring. The interpersonal nature and unpredictable patient interactions limit robotic replacement.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Patient care in psychiatric facilities requiring trust, de-escalation, and interpersonal skills. Each patient's needs and episodes are unpredictable. Physical assistance needed in variable situations. Human presence and judgment essential for safety and therapeutic relationships.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Direct patient care in psychiatric facilities involving monitoring, assistance, and de-escalation. By 2036, automated monitoring assists, but the human presence for patient safety, therapeutic interaction, and managing unpredictable behavioral situations requires human judgment and emotional skills.
adoption_friction_rationale: Healthcare regulation and certification. Direct patient contact with psychiatric patients requires human empathy and crisis de-escalation skills. Institutional setting (hospitals, residential facilities) with safety concerns. Patient trust essential. Moderate labour shortages. Physical intervention may be required.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Direct patient care in psychiatric settings resists automation. Growing mental health awareness and treatment access increase patient volume. Staffing shortages indicate unmet demand.

title: Psychologists
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: A blend of interpersonal clinical work (conducting therapy, administering assessments, counseling patients) and digital knowledge work (analyzing research data, writing reports, reviewing literature). AI assists with test interpretation and research by 2028, but the therapeutic relationship and clinical judgment remain human.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: AI assists with assessment scoring, research analysis, and treatment documentation. However, therapy sessions, psychological assessment, and clinical judgment about human mental health require deep interpersonal skills and human presence.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates assessment scoring, literature review, and treatment plan documentation. However, psychotherapy is deeply interpersonal—the therapeutic alliance, reading nonverbal cues, and human empathy are the mechanisms of change. Research psychologists face higher digital exposure through automated data analysis.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Psychologists study behavior and provide therapy. Cognitive and interpersonal work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Assessment and therapy work that is entirely interpersonal and knowledge-based. No physical component.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Entirely cognitive and interpersonal therapeutic/research work. No physical component for robotic automation.
adoption_friction_rationale: State licensing and healthcare regulation. Therapeutic relationship is central to treatment. Strong social resistance to AI therapy for serious conditions. Malpractice liability. Insurance billing requires licensed providers. Mix of hospital systems and many independent practices. Professional ethics codes require human practitioners.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Enormous unmet demand for psychological services. Most people who could benefit from therapy don't receive it due to cost and access. AI tools can help psychologists screen, assess, and monitor more patients while maintaining the human therapeutic relationship.

title: Public relations and fundraising managers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Predominantly digital: developing communication strategies, managing media relations, overseeing content creation, and analyzing public perception data. AI significantly assists with content drafting, media monitoring, and sentiment analysis by 2028. Strategic communication and relationship management remain human.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Media monitoring, content creation, analytics, and communications drafting are heavily automated by AI. Managers retain strategic messaging, crisis management, relationship building, and organizational reputation stewardship.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates media monitoring, press release drafting, campaign analytics, and donor research. Human managers remain for crisis communications requiring real-time judgment, building media relationships, strategic reputation management in ambiguous situations, and high-value donor cultivation.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: PR managers oversee public communications. Strategic communication work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Communication strategy and management work. Entirely knowledge-based.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Entirely communication and strategic management work. No physical component.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large corporations are primary employers. AI tools for media monitoring and content generation already used. Strategic communication and crisis management require human judgment. Moderate employer size. Relationship management with media and stakeholders valued. Minimal regulatory barriers.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Every organization needs reputation management, and the complexity of media channels grows. AI assists with monitoring and content creation but strategic communication and crisis management require human judgment.

title: Public relations specialists
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Predominantly screen-based: writing press releases, managing social media, monitoring media coverage, and creating promotional content. AI significantly accelerates content creation, media analysis, and campaign optimization by 2028. Client relationship and crisis communication remain human-driven.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Press release writing, media monitoring, content creation, and campaign analytics are digital tasks AI agents handle autonomously. Human PR specialists focus on media relationships, crisis communication, and strategic messaging.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Content creation, media monitoring, social media management, and routine communications are automated. Human specialists remain for crisis management, building personal media relationships, handling sensitive organizational communications, and strategic messaging in complex reputational situations.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: PR specialists manage public image through communications. Knowledge-based communication work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Media relations and communication work. Entirely knowledge-based.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Entirely communication and writing work. No physical component.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large corporations and PR firms are primary employers. AI tools for content creation, media monitoring, and analytics adopted. Relationship management and strategic messaging require human judgment. Moderate employer fragmentation. Digital PR workflow facilitates AI integration. Minimal regulatory barriers.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Growing number of communication channels and stakeholders to manage. AI tools help with content creation and monitoring but relationship building and strategic messaging require human skills. Every organization needs PR.

title: Public safety telecommunicators
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: A blend of interpersonal crisis communication (calming callers, gathering information under pressure) and digital dispatch coordination (using CAD systems, monitoring radio, managing resources). AI assists with call routing and resource optimization by 2028, but the human judgment in emergency triage remains essential.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: AI handles call routing, location identification, and resource allocation increasingly well. However, managing emergency callers under stress, making split-second priority decisions, and coordinating multi-agency responses retain critical human roles.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates call routing, resource allocation, and routine dispatch decisions. However, handling emergency calls from distressed callers requires human empathy, real-time judgment in ambiguous situations, and regulatory requirements for human oversight of life-safety decisions.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Dispatchers coordinate emergency responses from communication centers. Desk-based communication work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Communication and coordination work from dispatch centers. While technology-intensive, the role involves no physical labor—it's real-time decision-making and communication.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Entirely communication and coordination work at dispatch consoles. No physical component for robotic automation.
adoption_friction_rationale: Government employment with union protections. 911 dispatch requires human judgment in life-threatening situations. AI-assisted dispatch tools already deployed for routing and prioritization. Regulatory requirements for emergency services. Liability for dispatch decisions. Moderate institutional inertia. Labour shortages provide pull.
demand_elasticity_rationale: AI-assisted dispatch systems optimize routing and prioritization, reducing the number of human dispatchers needed. Computer-aided dispatch handles increasing volumes without proportional headcount increases.

title: Purchasing managers, buyers, and purchasing agents
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Predominantly digital: evaluating suppliers using databases, negotiating contracts, analyzing market data, and managing procurement systems. AI significantly enhances supplier evaluation, price analysis, and purchase order automation by 2028. Relationship negotiation provides some insulation.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Supplier research, bid analysis, contract processing, and inventory management are digital tasks AI handles autonomously. Human buyers focus on strategic supplier relationships, complex negotiations, and novel procurement decisions.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Vendor evaluation, price comparison, order processing, and supply chain analytics are automated. Human buyers remain for strategic supplier relationship management, complex contract negotiation, and procurement decisions requiring judgment in uncertain markets.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Purchasing managers negotiate and procure goods. Desk-based negotiation and analytical work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Procurement and negotiation work that is entirely knowledge-based. No physical component.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Entirely analytical and negotiation work. No physical component.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large corporations are primary employers with resources. Procurement is highly data-driven and amenable to AI. AI-powered sourcing and procurement platforms already deployed. Clear ROI. Moderate regulatory requirements for government purchasing (FAR). Supply chain optimization is a natural AI application.
demand_elasticity_rationale: AI automates supplier identification, price comparison, and routine procurement. E-procurement platforms reduce the need for purchasing intermediaries. Strategic procurement persists but transactional buying automates.

title: Quality control inspectors
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Primarily physical: examining products and materials, operating testing equipment, and conducting on-site inspections. While data recording and statistical analysis have digital components, the hands-on inspection, measurement, and testing work dominates.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Physical inspection of products—measuring dimensions, testing materials, examining finishes—requires hands-on work. AI-powered machine vision aids some visual inspection, but manual testing and judgment in varied production environments remain human.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates data analysis and statistical quality reporting. However, physical inspection—examining products by hand, operating testing equipment, and on-floor quality assessment in manufacturing—retains significant human roles.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Quality inspection in manufacturing involves repetitive visual and measurement checks in structured factory environments. Machine vision and robotic inspection systems are being commercially deployed in automotive and electronics by 2028.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Automated visual inspection and sensor-based quality control widespread in manufacturing. Machine vision systems handle most routine inspection tasks. Human inspectors focus on complex assessments, final acceptance, and non-standard products. High-volume production inspection substantially automated.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: By 2036, automated inspection systems using computer vision and sensors handle most routine quality checking in manufacturing. Human inspectors remain for novel products, complex assemblies, and final quality judgment. The vast majority of routine inspection is automated.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large manufacturers are primary employers. AI-powered visual inspection and automated testing already widely deployed. Clear ROI. Existing manufacturing technology culture. Moderate regulatory requirements (ISO, FDA for medical). Labour shortages in manufacturing provide pull. Controlled environments suit automated inspection.
demand_elasticity_rationale: AI-powered visual inspection and automated testing systems directly replace human quality inspectors on production lines. Machine vision outperforms humans in consistency and speed for many inspection tasks.

title: Radiation therapists
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: A blend of clinical patient care (positioning patients, explaining treatments, monitoring during procedures) and digital system operation (operating treatment delivery systems, reviewing treatment plans). AI assists with treatment verification, but patient positioning and care remain hands-on.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Positioning patients, operating radiation equipment, and monitoring treatment sessions are physical clinical tasks. AI aids with treatment planning and dosimetry, but direct patient care and safety monitoring remain human.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates treatment planning calculations and dosimetry. However, administering radiation treatments requires physical patient positioning, operating complex equipment, monitoring patients during treatment, and providing supportive patient care.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Radiation therapists position patients precisely for treatment using linear accelerators. Patient positioning is somewhat structured, and automated positioning systems are advancing, but patient variability limits full automation.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Patient-facing work positioning patients and operating radiation equipment. Each patient requires careful positioning and monitoring. Trust and communication essential. Robotic positioning assists but human oversight and patient interaction remain critical for safety.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Operating radiation equipment and positioning patients for treatment. By 2036, robotic patient positioning and automated treatment delivery assist significantly, but patient interaction, positioning of varied body types, and safety-critical oversight require human presence.
adoption_friction_rationale: Healthcare regulation, state licensing, and radiation safety requirements. Hospital systems are primary employers. Patient interaction and positioning requires human skill. AI-assisted treatment planning advancing. Regulatory approval for automated delivery is slow. Patient safety demands rigorous human oversight.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Demand tied to cancer patient volume receiving radiation therapy. AI improves treatment planning but human therapists must position patients and operate equipment. Patient volume grows modestly with cancer screening and aging.

title: Radiologic and MRI technologists
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Core work is hands-on: positioning patients, operating imaging equipment, and ensuring patient safety during scans. AI assists with image quality assessment and preliminary analysis by 2028, but the physical patient positioning and equipment operation cannot be automated.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Positioning patients and operating imaging equipment are physical tasks. AI significantly aids image interpretation and quality assessment, but the hands-on operation of radiologic equipment and patient interaction remain human.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates image interpretation and reporting. However, operating imaging equipment, positioning patients, adjusting techniques for individual anatomy, and ensuring patient comfort and safety require physical presence and manual skill.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Radiologic techs position patients and operate imaging equipment. Each patient requires different positioning, and the patient interaction component limits physical robotic automation by 2028.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Patient-facing imaging work requiring positioning patients and operating equipment. Each patient's anatomy and condition varies. Trust and communication needed. AI assists image interpretation but physical patient handling and positioning requires human operators.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Operating imaging equipment and positioning patients. By 2036, automated imaging systems handle much routine positioning and image acquisition. Human technologists remain for complex imaging, patient with mobility challenges, and quality oversight.
adoption_friction_rationale: Healthcare regulation, state licensing. Hospital systems are primary employers. AI-assisted image acquisition and quality control advancing. Physical patient positioning requires human interaction. FDA-regulated equipment. Patient comfort and communication important. Moderate institutional inertia in healthcare.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Demand tied to imaging order volume. AI improves image interpretation but human technologists must position patients and operate equipment. Growing imaging utilization supports demand while AI aids reading.

title: Railroad workers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Predominantly physical: operating locomotives, coupling railcars, inspecting equipment, and managing rail yard operations. Signal and dispatch systems have digital components, but the physical railroad operations dominate.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Operating trains, maintaining track, and managing railroad equipment are physical tasks. AI assists with scheduling and monitoring, but physical operations in varied outdoor conditions remain human.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Railroad work involves physical operations—maintaining track, operating trains, and managing rail yard logistics. Digital AI assists with scheduling and monitoring, but the physical work remains human.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Railroad work includes operating trains on fixed tracks (structured, automatable) and physical tasks like coupling cars and track maintenance. Train automation is advancing on freight corridors, but physical maintenance remains manual.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Rail operations increasingly automated with autonomous train systems operational on many freight routes. However, maintenance, switching, and yard operations in variable conditions still require human workers. Crew requirements declining but not eliminated.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: By 2036, autonomous train operation on fixed rail infrastructure is highly advanced. Most freight and passenger rail runs autonomously. Human workers remain for yard operations with complex switching, maintenance, and emergency response.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large railroad companies (BNSF, UP, CSX, NS) have resources. FRA regulations are extensive. Strong union presence (BLET, SMART-TD). Autonomous train technology advancing but regulatory and union barriers significant. Safety-critical nature demands extensive testing. Class I railroads are motivated by efficiency. Labour shortages provide moderate pull.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Precision train control and automation reduce crew sizes. AI-managed scheduling and maintenance improve efficiency. Freight volume grows modestly but technology reduces workers per train-mile.

title: Real estate brokers and sales agents
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Significant digital work: listing properties online, analyzing market data, preparing contracts, and marketing. AI assists with valuation, lead generation, and document preparation by 2028. However, property showings, client relationship building, and negotiation remain interpersonal and physical.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Property search, market analysis, listing preparation, and contract drafting are digital tasks AI handles well. Agents retain value in showing properties, negotiating deals, and guiding clients through complex transactions.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates property search, market analysis, document preparation, and marketing. However, real estate sales depend on interpersonal relationships, physical property showings, negotiation skills, and local market knowledge that clients value from human agents.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Real estate agents facilitate property sales through showings and negotiations. Interpersonal sales work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Sales and advisory work that is entirely interpersonal. Virtual tours exist but the core work is client relationships and negotiation.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Entirely interpersonal sales and advisory work. Property showings involve physical presence but no physical labor. Digital tools handle marketing; the core value is relationship and negotiation.
adoption_friction_rationale: Extremely fragmented industry of independent agents and small brokerages. State licensing requirements. AI tools for property valuation and marketing already used. But home buying/selling is emotionally significant with strong preference for human guidance. NAR and MLS structures create institutional inertia. Large brokerages adopting tech faster.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Online listings and AI-powered property matching reduce the traditional agent role. iBuyer platforms and self-service tools disintermediate some transactions. Complex transactions still benefit from agents but standard sales shift to technology.

title: Receptionists
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: A blend of interpersonal service (greeting visitors, managing front desk) and digital tasks (answering phones, managing schedules, processing correspondence). AI chatbots and virtual receptionists handle many phone and scheduling tasks by 2028, but physical front desk presence remains needed in many settings.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Call routing, scheduling, visitor management, and information provision are digital tasks AI handles efficiently. However, physical front-desk presence and in-person greeting remain valued in many settings, moderating full automation.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Phone answering, scheduling, visitor logging, and routine information provision are automated by AI. Physical front-desk presence retains a small human role in premium settings, but the traditional receptionist function is largely replaced by virtual assistants.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Receptionists greet visitors and manage front desk communications. Communication and administrative work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Front desk roles increasingly replaced by digital kiosks and automated check-in systems. However, many organizations still value human receptionists for visitor management, complex inquiries, and hospitality. The physical component (greeting, directing) is moderate.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: By 2036, automated reception kiosks and virtual receptionists handle routine visitor management. However, many organizations retain human receptionists for the personal touch, complex visitor needs, and physical mail/package handling. The role is split between digital and physical automation.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large employers (hospitals, hotels, corporations) with clear ROI for AI and automated systems. Virtual receptionists and kiosk systems already widely deployed. Work is highly standardized. Minimal regulatory barriers. Labour shortages provide pull. Some customer preference for human greeters in certain settings.
demand_elasticity_rationale: AI virtual receptionists, automated check-in kiosks, and digital scheduling directly replace routine reception tasks. Many offices already use automated phone systems and visitor management. The warm human greeting persists in some settings.

title: Recreation workers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Predominantly physical and interpersonal: organizing and leading activities, supervising participants, and managing recreation facilities. Administrative tasks like scheduling have digital components, but the in-person activity leadership and participant engagement dominate.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Leading recreational activities, supervising participants, and organizing events are physical and interpersonal duties. AI assists with scheduling and program planning, but in-person facilitation is the core function.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Recreation work is fundamentally physical and interpersonal—leading activities, supervising programs, and engaging participants in sports, arts, and community activities. Digital AI has minimal exposure beyond scheduling and registration systems.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Recreation workers plan and lead leisure activities. Interpersonal facilitation work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Leading recreational activities and programs for diverse groups. Requires human engagement, creativity, and adaptation to participants' needs. Each session and group is different. The interpersonal and improvisational aspects resist automation.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Organizing and leading recreational activities requires human engagement, enthusiasm, and adaptive interaction with participants. By 2036, some facility management is automated, but the interpersonal and physically active nature of leading recreation programs remains human.
adoption_friction_rationale: Government agencies and nonprofits are primary employers with limited budgets. Youth and community programming requires human interaction and supervision. Fragmented across parks departments, camps, and community centers. Moderate institutional inertia. Safety requirements for supervising participants. Limited technology infrastructure.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Growing spending on leisure and wellness activities. Physical recreation programming requires human leadership. Community recreation programs have latent demand in underserved areas.

title: Recreational therapists
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Core work is hands-on and interpersonal: planning and directing therapeutic activities, working directly with patients, and assessing treatment progress. Documentation has digital components, but the therapeutic patient interaction and activity facilitation dominate.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Planning and conducting therapeutic recreation activities with patients is hands-on, interpersonal work. AI assists with treatment documentation, but direct patient engagement through activities remains human.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Recreational therapy involves direct physical interaction with patients—leading therapeutic activities, adapting recreation for disabilities, and building therapeutic relationships. AI assists with treatment planning, but the hands-on facilitation is human.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Recreational therapists plan and lead activities for patients. While activities involve some physical demonstration, the work is primarily therapeutic facilitation with minimal robotic exposure.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Therapeutic work using recreational activities for patient rehabilitation. Each patient has unique needs. Requires trust, creativity, and adaptation. The interpersonal and therapeutic aspects are core.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Therapeutic recreation requires adaptive human interaction, emotional support, and creative activity design. By 2036, some assistive technology aids therapy, but the human relationship and adaptive guidance are central to the therapeutic value.
adoption_friction_rationale: Healthcare regulation and certification. Work with patients who have disabilities or illnesses requires human empathy and adaptive skill. Mix of hospital, rehabilitation, and community settings. Insurance billing requirements. Patient therapeutic relationship valued. Moderate employer fragmentation. Liability concerns.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Growing recognition of therapeutic recreation for rehabilitation and mental health. Significant unmet need in aging populations and disability services. AI tools help personalize programs but the therapeutic relationship is human.

title: Registered nurses
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: A blend of hands-on patient care (administering medications, monitoring conditions, providing treatments) and digital documentation (updating EHR, reviewing test results, coordinating care). AI assists with clinical decision support and documentation by 2028, but bedside nursing care remains fundamentally human. Calibration anchor.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Bedside care, medication administration, patient assessment, and clinical procedures are hands-on duties. AI automates charting, care coordination, and clinical decision support, but physical nursing care and patient relationships remain firmly human.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates care planning, medication management, documentation, and monitoring analysis. However, nursing is fundamentally hands-on—administering treatments, physical assessments, patient advocacy, and the interpersonal caring relationship. Regulatory and social expectations keep humans central to nursing.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Nurses perform diverse physical care tasks for patients with varied conditions in unpredictable clinical environments. The high variability and need for empathetic human judgment make robotic replacement minimal by 2028.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Direct patient care requiring trust, communication, clinical assessment, and hands-on nursing skills. Each patient is unique. Robotic assistance for some tasks (medication dispensing, vital sign monitoring), but bedside nursing care, patient advocacy, and clinical judgment remain human. Emotional support is core.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Nursing combines clinical judgment with hands-on patient care in variable settings. By 2036, automated monitoring, medication delivery, and routine assessments assist significantly, but complex patient care, emotional support, and clinical judgment in variable situations require human nurses.
adoption_friction_rationale: Heavy state licensing (Nurse Practice Acts), healthcare regulation, and liability. Strong patient preference for human nurses. Physical care requires human judgment and touch. Severe labour shortages provide strong pull but regulatory and social barriers are formidable. Large hospital employers have resources but nurse unions (NNU) are powerful.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Massive nursing shortage indicates enormous unmet demand. Aging population drives growing care needs. AI tools can help nurses manage more patients and catch issues earlier, but direct patient care requires human presence and compassion.

title: Rehabilitation counselors
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Predominantly interpersonal: counseling clients with disabilities, developing rehabilitation plans, and coordinating community resources. Case documentation and research have digital components, but the face-to-face counseling relationship and advocacy work dominate.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: AI assists with assessment tools, resource databases, and documentation. However, counseling individuals with disabilities, developing rehabilitation plans through personal interaction, and advocacy require deep human empathy and judgment.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates assessment scoring, resource matching, and documentation. However, rehabilitation counseling is interpersonal at its core—building rapport with individuals with disabilities, motivating behavioral change, and advocating for clients within complex service systems.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Rehabilitation counselors help people with disabilities. Interpersonal counseling work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Counseling work that is entirely interpersonal and knowledge-based. No physical component.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Primarily cognitive counseling and case management work. No physical component.
adoption_friction_rationale: State licensing and certification. Work with disabled individuals requires empathy, advocacy, and adaptive judgment. Government funding creates institutional inertia. Insurance and vocational rehabilitation requirements. Patient therapeutic relationship essential. Moderate employer fragmentation across agencies and clinics.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Significant unmet demand for rehabilitation services. Many disabled individuals lack access to counseling. AI tools help counselors assess and monitor clients. Growing disability awareness and workplace accommodation needs expand demand.

title: Respiratory therapists
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Core work is hands-on clinical care: administering breathing treatments, operating ventilators, and monitoring patients with respiratory conditions. AI assists with treatment protocol recommendations by 2028, but the physical patient care and equipment management dominate.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Operating ventilators, administering breathing treatments, and monitoring patients with cardiopulmonary disorders are hands-on clinical tasks. AI aids with treatment protocols and documentation, but bedside care is physical.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates ventilator management protocols and diagnostic data analysis. However, respiratory therapy involves hands-on clinical work—managing airways, operating respiratory equipment, and providing direct patient care in critical care settings.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Respiratory therapists manage ventilators and provide breathing treatments to patients with varied conditions. The clinical judgment and varied patient situations limit physical robotic exposure.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Patient care involving operation of respiratory equipment and patient assessment. Each patient's respiratory needs differ. Trust and communication essential. Some monitoring automated, but therapeutic interventions and patient interaction require human operators.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Operating respiratory equipment and managing patients with breathing issues. By 2036, automated ventilator management and monitoring assist, but patient assessment, airway management, and emergency intervention in variable clinical situations require human skill.
adoption_friction_rationale: State licensing and healthcare regulation. Hospital systems are primary employers. Direct patient care with ventilators and respiratory equipment requires hands-on skill. Patient assessment and emergency response. AI-assisted monitoring emerging. Labour shortages provide moderate pull. Liability for patient outcomes.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Aging population and chronic respiratory disease increase patient volume. AI assists with monitoring and treatment optimization but physical therapy delivery requires human practitioners. Pandemic awareness supports investment.

title: Retail sales workers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Predominantly in-person: greeting customers, demonstrating products, operating registers, and maintaining displays. E-commerce and AI chatbots affect the broader retail sector, but in-store sales work requires physical presence and interpersonal service.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Assisting customers, stocking shelves, and operating registers are physical and interpersonal tasks. E-commerce and AI reduce some retail positions, but in-store sales requiring product demonstration and customer service persist.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Retail sales is primarily a physical presence role—assisting customers in stores, arranging merchandise, and operating registers. E-commerce automation displaces some roles, but in-store retail remains a physical and interpersonal occupation with limited digital AI exposure.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Retail workers stock shelves and assist customers in store environments. Large chain retailers are piloting robotic shelf stocking, but customer assistance and varied store layouts limit broader replacement by 2028.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Self-service and automated checkout expanding. Some inventory management automated. However, customer assistance, product knowledge, and sales interaction remain human in many retail settings. High-end and specialty retail values human service. Lower-end retail sees more automation.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: By 2036, most retail stocking, inventory, and checkout are automated. Robotic restocking and autonomous checkout are standard. Human retail workers remain primarily for customer service, complex product consultation, and high-value sales interactions.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large retail chains are primary employers with massive incentive and resources to automate. Self-checkout, online shopping, and AI customer service already deployed. Severe labour shortages provide strong pull. Minimal regulatory barriers. Some customer preference for human assistance in specialty retail but mass retail automating rapidly.
demand_elasticity_rationale: E-commerce continues to grow, reducing in-store sales positions. Self-checkout and AI-powered recommendation engines displace sales assistance. Experiential retail maintains some roles but overall headcount declines.

title: Roofers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Entirely physical outdoor work: inspecting roofs, installing shingles, applying coatings, and working at heights. This is a calibration anchor for minimal digital exposure—pure manual construction trade with no meaningful AI impact.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Installing and repairing roofing materials at height is entirely physical construction work with no digital component. AI has zero impact on roofing tasks.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Roofing is entirely physical manual labor—installing and repairing roofs in outdoor conditions. This is the prototypical zero digital AI exposure occupation alongside janitorial work.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Roofing involves physically demanding work at heights on varied building structures. The unstructured, hazardous outdoor environment and varied roof configurations make robotic replacement infeasible by 2028.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Work at heights on variable rooftops. Each roof has unique pitch, material, and condition. Weather-exposed outdoor work. Some commercial flat-roof applications see limited automation, but the variety of residential roofing and the physical environment strongly resist robotic automation.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Roofing involves working at heights in variable weather and building conditions. By 2036, robotic roofing systems handle standardized flat and simple-pitch roofs, but complex roof geometries, repairs, and variable building conditions still require human skills and risk judgment.
adoption_friction_rationale: Fragmented construction trade with many small contractors. Physical work at heights in outdoor conditions. OSHA fall protection requirements. Limited capital among small operators. Labour shortages provide pull but rooftop robotic work is extremely challenging. Union presence in commercial sector. Liability for waterproofing failures.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Physical roofing work in variable conditions strongly resists automation. Demand tied to construction and re-roofing cycles. Climate change may increase storm damage repairs. Labor shortages indicate current unmet demand.

title: Sales engineers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Predominantly digital: preparing technical presentations, analyzing client needs, writing proposals, and demonstrating complex products. AI assists with proposal generation, product configuration, and client research by 2028. Client relationship management and technical consulting remain human-driven.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Technical presentations, proposal development, and product configuration are digital tasks AI handles well. However, client relationships, understanding complex technical needs, and on-site demonstrations retain strong human value.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates technical proposal generation, product configuration, pricing, and competitive analysis. Human sales engineers remain for complex technical consultations, building customer relationships, and translating between technical and business stakeholders in high-value enterprise sales.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Sales engineers sell complex technical products. Technical sales and consulting work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Technical sales combining engineering knowledge with client relationships. Entirely knowledge and interpersonal work.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Primarily technical sales and relationship work. No physical component for robotic automation.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large technology and manufacturing companies are primary employers. Technical expertise combined with sales relationships. AI tools for product configuration and pricing already used. Moderate employer fragmentation. Complex sales cycles require human relationship management. Clear ROI for proposal automation.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Technical sales requires deep product knowledge and relationship building. AI helps with technical documentation and proposals but the consultative selling process persists. Demand tied to technical product markets.

title: Sales managers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Predominantly digital: analyzing sales data, developing strategies, managing CRM systems, and preparing reports. AI significantly assists with forecasting, pipeline analysis, and performance tracking by 2028. Team leadership, client relationship building, and strategic decisions remain human.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Sales analytics, forecasting, territory planning, and CRM management are heavily automated. Managers retain team leadership, strategic account development, complex negotiations, and motivating sales teams.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates sales forecasting, pipeline analysis, territory optimization, and performance reporting. Human sales managers remain for team leadership, coaching sales representatives, managing key client relationships, and strategic market positioning requiring interpersonal judgment.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Sales managers oversee sales teams and strategies. Managerial work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Sales leadership and strategy work. Entirely management and interpersonal.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Entirely management and strategic work. No physical component.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large corporations are primary employers with CRM and AI sales tools already widely adopted. Management role requires human leadership and motivation. AI for forecasting and analytics already integrated. Moderate employer fragmentation in SMB segment. Human relationship management valued. Minimal regulatory barriers.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Management roles scale with sales organization size. AI optimizes sales processes and provides better analytics but human leadership of sales teams persists. E-commerce growth shifts some sales management online.

title: School and career counselors and advisors
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Core work is interpersonal: counseling students, facilitating career exploration, and supporting social-emotional development. AI assists with career matching, resource recommendations, and data tracking by 2028, but the personal counseling relationship and student advocacy remain fundamentally human.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: AI provides career assessments, college matching, and information resources. However, counseling students through personal challenges, crisis intervention, and building trusting relationships with families require human empathy and presence.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates career matching, academic planning, college application guidance, and resource referrals. However, counseling involves deep interpersonal work—supporting students through personal crises, building trust with adolescents, and navigating sensitive family dynamics.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: School counselors advise students on academic and career paths. Interpersonal advisory work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Counseling work that is entirely interpersonal and knowledge-based.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Entirely interpersonal counseling work. No physical component.
adoption_friction_rationale: Education sector with strong institutional inertia. Government employment. Students and families expect human counselors for guidance and emotional support. State certification requirements. Ethical requirements for confidentiality and human judgment. AI tools for career matching exist but counseling relationship resists automation.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Significant unmet demand for student counseling—most schools have inadequate counselor-to-student ratios. AI tools help counselors serve more students with personalized guidance. Mental health awareness increases demand.

title: Secretaries and administrative assistants
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Almost entirely screen-based: scheduling meetings, managing correspondence, preparing documents, and maintaining records. AI significantly automates scheduling, document preparation, and communication management by 2028. Active headcount reduction as AI handles routine administrative tasks.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Scheduling, correspondence, document preparation, filing, and data entry are routine digital tasks AI agents handle autonomously by 2031. Only executive assistants managing complex interpersonal logistics for senior leaders retain significant roles.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Scheduling, correspondence, document preparation, filing, and administrative coordination are entirely digital routine tasks that AI handles end-to-end. This occupation has effectively ceased to exist in its traditional form, replaced by AI executive assistants.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Administrative assistants provide office support. Desk-based clerical work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Office administrative work that is entirely desk-based. No physical component beyond basic office activities.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Entirely office-based administrative work. No physical component for robotic automation.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large employers across all sectors. Work is highly standardized and administrative. AI assistants and office automation already pervasive. Clear ROI. Minimal regulatory barriers. Role has been declining for decades. Calendar management, document preparation, and communication increasingly automated.
demand_elasticity_rationale: AI scheduling tools, email management, and document preparation directly automate core secretarial tasks. Voice assistants and digital tools reduce the need for human administrative support. The role has been contracting for decades.

title: Securities, commodities, and financial services sales agents
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Predominantly digital: analyzing financial markets, executing trades, preparing client recommendations, and managing portfolios. AI significantly assists with market analysis, trade execution, and client reporting by 2028. Client relationship building and complex advisory remain human.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Market analysis, portfolio construction, and trade execution are heavily automated. Agents retain value in client relationships, complex financial planning, and trust-based advisory, but routine sales and trading roles shrink.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Trade execution, market analysis, portfolio construction, and client reporting are automated. Human agents persist for high-net-worth relationship management, complex financial product advisory, and situations where client trust in a human advisor drives business.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Financial services sales agents sell securities and investments. Desk-based sales and analytical work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Financial sales and advisory work. Entirely knowledge and interpersonal based.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Entirely financial sales and advisory work. No physical component.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large financial institutions are primary employers. Trading already heavily automated. Wealth management and client relationships require human interaction. FINRA licensing requirements. Fiduciary duty considerations. AI tools for portfolio management and trading already deployed. Robo-advisory disrupting lower-end services.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Online trading platforms and robo-advisors reduce need for human brokers and agents. Algorithmic trading handles much of the transaction volume. Complex wealth management persists but standard financial product sales automate.

title: Security guards and gambling surveillance officers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Predominantly physical: patrolling property, monitoring entrances, responding to incidents, and enforcing rules. Surveillance camera monitoring is a digital component where AI assists, but physical security presence and response remain essential.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Patrolling premises, monitoring access points, and responding to security incidents are physical presence duties. AI-enhanced surveillance helps, but human guards remain essential for physical security and emergency response.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Security guard work is physical presence—patrolling premises, monitoring entrances, and responding to incidents. AI enhances surveillance systems, but the human deterrent and response function requires physical presence.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Security guards patrol and monitor facilities. Robotic security patrols (like Knightscope) are deployed in some structured environments like malls and campuses, but human guards are still needed for varied situations and interventions.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Patrol robots and automated surveillance systems handle routine monitoring of commercial facilities. However, human guards still needed for response, de-escalation, access control with judgment, and work in variable environments. Large facilities use robotic patrol as supplement.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: By 2036, robotic security systems and automated surveillance handle most routine security monitoring and patrol. Human guards remain for situations requiring authority, judgment, and physical intervention capability. Regulatory and insurance requirements maintain some human presence.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large security companies (Allied Universal, Securitas) are primary employers. AI surveillance and robotic patrol systems already deployed. Labour shortages provide pull. Licensing requirements vary by state. Liability concerns for security incidents. Some settings require human presence for intervention. Clear ROI for large-scale monitoring.
demand_elasticity_rationale: AI surveillance systems, drones, and automated monitoring reduce the need for human guards. Technology handles surveillance while guards respond to incidents. Demand for physical security presence persists but monitoring shifts to AI.

title: Semiconductor processing technicians
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Primarily physical cleanroom work: operating semiconductor manufacturing equipment, monitoring processes, and conducting quality tests. Process monitoring systems are computerized, but the physical equipment operation and cleanroom procedures dominate.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Operating cleanroom equipment, monitoring semiconductor fabrication processes, and conducting quality checks are physical production tasks. AI aids with process optimization, but hands-on equipment operation remains human.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Operating semiconductor fabrication equipment is hands-on cleanroom work. AI automates process monitoring and yield analysis, but physical equipment operation, maintenance, and quality inspection in fabrication facilities remain human tasks.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Semiconductor fabrication environments are highly controlled cleanrooms with repetitive wafer handling and processing steps. Much of the physical workflow is already automated, and robotic handling is commercially deployed at scale.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Semiconductor fabrication highly automated in cleanroom environments. Robotic wafer handling, automated processing equipment, and precise environmental controls dominate. Human technicians monitor, maintain, and troubleshoot but the actual processing is overwhelmingly automated.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Semiconductor fabrication is one of the most automated manufacturing environments. By 2036, cleanroom automation is near-total. Human involvement is primarily for equipment maintenance and process engineering oversight.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large semiconductor manufacturers (TSMC, Intel, Samsung) are primary employers with massive technology investment. Fab environments already highly automated and controlled. Labour shortages in semiconductor manufacturing. Clear ROI. Minimal regulatory barriers for process automation. Industry 4.0 culture.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Massive expansion of semiconductor manufacturing (CHIPS Act, AI chip demand) creates growing need for fabrication technicians. AI assists with process monitoring but cleanroom operations need human workers. Supply chain concerns drive domestic expansion.

title: Set and exhibit designers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Significant digital work: creating 3D models, rendering designs, and using CAD software. AI generative design tools assist with concept development and visualization by 2028. Physical construction oversight, material selection, and on-site installation provide non-digital balance.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: AI generates 3D renderings, design concepts, and technical drawings. However, physical construction oversight, spatial understanding from being on-site, and creative vision for experiential spaces retain human value.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI generates design concepts, 3D visualizations, and technical drawings. However, set and exhibit design involves physical construction oversight, understanding spatial dynamics in person, and creative vision in the context of live performances and physical exhibitions.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Set designers create physical spaces for productions and exhibits. While design is cognitive, construction involves physical work in variable settings, limiting robotic exposure.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Creative design work for unique sets and exhibits. Each project is custom. Physical construction may be involved but the role is primarily about creative design and direction. The uniqueness of each project resists automation.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Creative design with physical construction components. By 2036, some standardized set construction is automated, but the creative vision, custom fabrication, and site-specific installation of unique designs keep this human-centered.
adoption_friction_rationale: Mix of large entertainment companies and many independent designers. AI visualization and design tools advancing. Creative vision valued. Union protections in entertainment (IATSE). Physical construction still requires human oversight. Moderate employer fragmentation. Both film/TV and museum sectors.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Growing content production and experiential entertainment create demand. AI visualization tools help but physical design and construction of sets and exhibits requires human creativity and craftsmanship.

title: Sheet metal workers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Predominantly physical skilled trade: cutting, bending, and installing sheet metal using hand and power tools. Blueprint reading and CNC operation are minor digital components. AI has negligible impact on the hands-on fabrication and installation work.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Fabricating, installing, and repairing sheet metal products is hands-on skilled trade work. AI has minimal impact on these physical construction and manufacturing tasks.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Sheet metal work is physical skilled trade work—cutting, bending, and installing metal sheets in construction and manufacturing. Digital AI has essentially no exposure to this occupation.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Sheet metal work spans factory fabrication (more structured) and field installation (variable). Factory-based sheet metal cutting and forming is increasingly automated, but field installation remains manual by 2028.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Factory-based sheet metal fabrication (cutting, bending, forming) highly automated with CNC equipment and robotic handling. However, on-site installation in HVAC systems, ductwork in variable buildings, and custom work requires human skill. Split between automated fabrication and manual installation.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: By 2036, automated sheet metal fabrication (cutting, bending, forming) is standard in shops. Field installation in variable environments retains human involvement, but much fabrication work is robotic. Custom and on-site adaptation work remains human.
adoption_friction_rationale: Mix of large HVAC and manufacturing companies and smaller contractors. Precision fabrication increasingly automated with CNC. Field installation work is more varied and challenging. Union presence (SMART). Labour shortages provide pull. Limited capital among small operators. Building code compliance requires judgment.
