demand_elasticity_rationale: Physical metalworking in varied environments resists automation. Demand tied to construction and HVAC activity. Growing demand for HVAC systems and building renovation supports the trade.

title: Skincare specialists
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Almost entirely physical and interpersonal: performing facials, body treatments, and skin assessments through direct hands-on work. Appointment scheduling is a negligible digital component. AI cannot perform physical skin care treatments.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Performing facials, applying treatments, and providing skincare services are entirely hands-on personal care tasks. AI has negligible impact on these physical services.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Skincare treatment is hands-on physical service work—performing facials, applying treatments, and providing personal beauty care. The interpersonal pampering experience is the core product. Digital AI has minimal exposure beyond booking and product recommendation.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Skincare specialists perform facial treatments and skin analysis on varied clients. The intimate client contact and varied skin conditions require adaptive human touch beyond 2028 robotics.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Personal service requiring client trust, touch sensitivity, and adaptation to individual skin conditions. Each client's skin is unique. The spa/wellness experience is interpersonal. While some automated facial devices exist, the personal care and assessment aspects resist automation.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Personal skincare treatment where human touch and consultation are central. By 2036, some automated facial and skin analysis tools exist, but the intimate personal care, client relationship, and adaptive treatment remain human-centered.
adoption_friction_rationale: Extremely fragmented industry of independent practitioners and small spas. State licensing requirements. Physical skin treatment requires manual skill. Strong client preference for human touch and personal service. Limited capital among small operators. Some medical spa settings have more resources. Liability for skin reactions.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Growing consumer spending on skincare and wellness. Inherently physical, in-person service. AI skin analysis tools may expand client base by making consultations more accessible and personalized. Significant latent demand.

title: Small engine mechanics
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Predominantly hands-on: inspecting, servicing, and repairing small engines and motorized equipment using hand tools and diagnostic equipment. Service manual lookup has a minor digital component. AI has minimal impact on the physical repair work.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Diagnosing and repairing lawn mowers, chainsaws, and small equipment is hands-on mechanical work. AI aids with diagnostics, but physical repair remains human.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Repairing lawn mowers, chainsaws, and other small engines is hands-on mechanical work. AI assists with diagnostics, but the physical disassembly, repair, and reassembly remain human tasks.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Small engine repair involves diagnosing and fixing varied equipment in workshop settings. While more structured than field work, the variety of equipment and repairs limits robotic deployment by 2028.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Repair of diverse small engines (lawn mowers, chainsaws, boats) with each problem unique. Variable working conditions. While diagnostic tools improve, the physical repair work on many different equipment types in small shop environments requires human dexterity and problem-solving.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Repairing diverse small engines (lawn mowers, generators, boats) in variable conditions. By 2036, diagnostic automation assists, but the variety of equipment and repair scenarios requires human adaptability and judgment.
adoption_friction_rationale: Highly fragmented industry of small repair shops and independent operators. Varied equipment types challenge standardization. Limited capital for technology investment. Physical repair requires manual dexterity in varied conditions. Moderate regulatory requirements. Some labour shortages but market size doesn't justify major robotic investment.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Physical repair work resists automation. Demand tied to the installed base of small engines (mowers, generators, etc.). Transition to electric equipment may reduce long-term demand but the timeline is gradual.

title: Social and community service managers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: A blend of interpersonal management (staff supervision, community outreach, client advocacy) and digital administrative work (grant writing, budgeting, program reporting). AI assists with reporting and analysis by 2028, but community leadership and client-facing work remain human.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Grant writing, program evaluation, reporting, and budgeting are aided by AI. However, community relationships, staff supervision, crisis management, and navigating complex social service systems require human leadership and judgment.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates program evaluation, grant writing, data reporting, and resource allocation analysis. However, managing social service organizations requires staff leadership, community relationship building, advocacy, and navigating complex inter-agency dynamics.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Social service managers oversee community programs. Managerial and interpersonal work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Management and program development work. Entirely administrative and interpersonal.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Entirely management and interpersonal work. No physical component.
adoption_friction_rationale: Government agencies and nonprofits with limited budgets and institutional inertia. Managing social services requires human judgment, community relationships, and advocacy. Regulatory compliance for government-funded programs. Fragmented across many small nonprofit organizations. Stakeholder engagement requires human presence.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Growing investment in social services and community programs. AI helps with administration and program evaluation but community leadership requires human connection. Expanding social safety net programs increase demand.

title: Social and human service assistants
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: A mix of interpersonal casework (assisting clients, coordinating services, conducting intakes) and digital tasks (maintaining records, researching resources). AI assists with resource matching and documentation by 2028, but the face-to-face client support and advocacy remain human.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: AI assists with client intake, resource databases, and case documentation. However, direct client support, home visits, and connecting vulnerable populations with services require human empathy and physical presence.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates intake documentation, resource referral matching, and case tracking. However, the role involves direct client interaction—assisting vulnerable populations, accompanying clients to appointments, and providing emotional support that requires human presence and empathy.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Social service assistants help clients access services. Interpersonal support work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Client-facing social service work that is entirely interpersonal. Helping people navigate social services requires human empathy and judgment.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Primarily interpersonal case management and support work. No physical component for robotic automation.
adoption_friction_rationale: Government agencies and nonprofits with institutional inertia. Direct client interaction requires empathy and cultural competency. Fragmented employer base. Work with vulnerable populations demands human judgment and trust-building. Limited technology budgets. Moderate regulatory requirements for case management.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Significant unmet demand for social services. AI tools help assistants manage larger caseloads and connect clients with resources. The human element of advocacy and support resists automation. Growing social needs increase demand.

title: Social workers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Predominantly interpersonal: counseling individuals and families, conducting assessments, connecting clients with resources, and advocating for vulnerable populations. Case documentation and research have digital components AI assists with by 2028, but the therapeutic relationship and advocacy work remain fundamentally human.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: AI aids with case documentation, risk assessment tools, and resource matching. However, crisis intervention, home visits, therapeutic relationships, and navigating complex family dynamics require deep human judgment and interpersonal skills.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates assessment tools, documentation, resource identification, and case management tracking. However, social work is fundamentally interpersonal—building relationships with vulnerable clients, conducting home visits, crisis intervention, and advocating for clients in complex systems.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Social workers help people cope with challenges. Interpersonal therapeutic and advocacy work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Client-facing counseling and advocacy work. Entirely interpersonal and knowledge-based. No physical component.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Entirely interpersonal counseling, assessment, and advocacy work. No physical component.
adoption_friction_rationale: State licensing and ethical requirements. Work with vulnerable populations demands human empathy, advocacy, and crisis intervention. Legal requirements for child welfare investigations and court testimony. Fragmented across agencies and private practice. Deep institutional inertia in child protective services and healthcare.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Enormous unmet demand for social work services across child welfare, mental health, and community support. AI tools help with assessment and documentation but the therapeutic and advocacy roles require human empathy. Caseloads are chronically high.

title: Sociologists
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Predominantly digital knowledge work: designing research studies, analyzing survey data, building statistical models, and writing papers. AI significantly assists with data analysis, literature review, and report generation by 2028. Fieldwork interviews and community observation provide some non-digital balance.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Data analysis, survey processing, literature synthesis, and report writing are heavily digital tasks AI agents handle well. Sociologists retain value in research design, theoretical interpretation, and understanding complex social phenomena.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Data analysis, survey design, literature synthesis, and report writing are automated. Human sociologists remain for novel theoretical frameworks, ethnographic research requiring cultural immersion, and interpretive scholarship about social dynamics that requires human understanding.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Sociologists study social behavior. Knowledge-based research work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Research and analysis work. Entirely knowledge-based.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Entirely research and analytical work. No physical component.
adoption_friction_rationale: Primarily academic employment with institutional inertia. Research involves interpretive judgment and fieldwork. AI tools for data analysis emerging but qualitative research requires human insight. Limited employer base of universities and research institutes. No significant regulatory barriers but academic culture resists rapid change.
demand_elasticity_rationale: AI enables analysis of large social datasets and complex social phenomena. Growing demand for understanding social issues, inequality, and technology's impact on society. Applied sociology in policy and business expands.

title: Software developers, quality assurance analysts, and testers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Almost entirely screen-based: writing code, designing software systems, debugging, and testing applications. AI coding agents handle routine feature implementation and bug fixes autonomously by 2028. Active restructuring in junior developer roles, though architectural decisions and complex problem-solving retain strong human value.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: AI agents write, test, and deploy code for well-understood domains autonomously by 2031. Senior architects and developers handling novel system design, complex debugging, and strategic technical decisions remain, but junior coding roles are largely automated.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Code implementation, testing, debugging, and routine software development are automated. The occupation is fundamentally restructured—remaining human roles focus on product vision, system architecture, and strategic technical leadership. QA testing as traditionally defined is fully automated.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Software developers design and write code. Entirely desk-based knowledge work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Entirely digital work writing code and designing software systems. No physical component.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Purely digital/cognitive work. No physical component whatsoever.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large tech companies are primary employers with the strongest incentive and capability to adopt AI coding tools. AI code generation (Copilot, Claude) already widely used. Existing technology culture. Clear ROI. Minimal regulatory barriers. Competition drives rapid adoption of productivity tools.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Massive latent demand for custom software. Every business process, every device, and every service could benefit from better software. Historical pattern: every productivity improvement in programming led to more software being built, not fewer programmers.

title: Solar photovoltaic installers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Almost entirely physical outdoor work: installing solar panels on rooftops, wiring electrical systems, and performing maintenance. System design tools have digital components, but the hands-on installation work at heights dominates. AI has negligible impact.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Installing solar panels on rooftops—mounting hardware, wiring, and connecting systems—is physical construction work. AI has minimal impact on these hands-on installation tasks.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Solar panel installation is physical rooftop work—mounting panels, running wiring, and connecting systems. Digital AI has essentially no exposure to this occupation.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Solar panel installation involves physical labor on varied rooftops and ground-mount structures. While large utility-scale installations have some automation potential, residential and varied commercial sites limit robotic deployment by 2028.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Rooftop installation in variable environments. Each roof and installation is different. Some large-scale ground-mount solar farms see automated installation of panels in uniform arrays. But residential rooftop work at heights with variable roof conditions requires human installers.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: By 2036, robotic systems handle much standardized solar panel installation on uniform roof surfaces. However, varied roof configurations, electrical integration, and site-specific challenges retain human involvement. Standardized commercial installations are heavily automated.
adoption_friction_rationale: Mix of large solar companies (SunPower, Tesla Energy) and many small installers. Physical rooftop installation work. NEC electrical codes and building permits. Growing industry with moderate labour shortages. Regulatory requirements for grid interconnection. Large utility-scale projects more amenable to automation than residential rooftop work.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Growing demand driven by energy transition and declining solar costs. Physical rooftop installation resists automation. Government incentives and climate goals drive expansion. Some efficiency improvements in installation but demand grows faster.

title: Special education teachers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Core work is deeply interpersonal: adapting instruction for students with disabilities, developing individualized education programs, and providing behavioral support. AI assists with lesson customization and progress tracking by 2028, but the patient, individualized teaching relationship is fundamentally human.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: AI assists with IEP documentation and personalized learning content. However, working with students with disabilities requires intensive hands-on support, behavioral management, and deep interpersonal care that remains firmly human.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates IEP documentation, adaptive curriculum generation, and progress tracking. However, special education requires intensive interpersonal work—building relationships with students who have diverse disabilities, physical assistance, behavioral management, and family collaboration.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Teaching is fundamentally interpersonal and cognitive work involving instruction, mentoring, and classroom management. There is no physical labor component for robots to automate.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Teaching students with disabilities requires extreme human sensitivity, patience, and individualized attention. Each student has unique needs. Fundamentally interpersonal with no automation potential.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Teaching students with disabilities requires extraordinary human patience, emotional attunement, and adaptive physical interaction. Each student's needs are unique. The human relationship and individualized support are central to effective special education.
adoption_friction_rationale: Government employment with strong unions and institutional inertia. Students with disabilities require highly individualized human attention, empathy, and adaptive teaching. IEP legal requirements mandate human professional judgment. IDEA federal regulations. State certification requirements. Parents of special needs children strongly prefer human teachers.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Enormous unmet demand for special education services. Many students with disabilities are underserved. AI tools can help teachers create individualized education plans and adapt instruction. The human relationship is essential for these students.

title: Special effects artists and animators
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Almost entirely screen-based: creating 2D/3D models, animations, and visual effects using digital tools. AI significantly automates routine animation, texture generation, and effects work by 2028. Active restructuring in production-level VFX and animation roles, though creative direction retains human value.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: AI generates animations, visual effects, and 3D models at high quality by 2031. Senior artists retain creative direction and novel artistic vision, but production animation and effects work is heavily automated.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI generates animations, visual effects, and 3D modeling from descriptions. Routine animation production is automated. Human artists remain for creative direction in premium productions, novel artistic styles, and situations where human artistic vision is the value proposition.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Animators and special effects artists create digital visual content. Desk-based creative technical work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Entirely digital creative work using software tools. No physical component.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Entirely digital creative work. No physical component for robotic automation.
adoption_friction_rationale: Mix of large studios and many freelancers. AI art and animation tools advancing rapidly (Midjourney, Runway, Unreal). Large studios adopt quickly for efficiency. Union protections (IATSE) provide some friction. Creative vision still valued but routine animation and VFX work amenable to AI. Digital workflow facilitates integration.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Explosive demand for animation and visual effects in games, streaming, social media, and advertising. AI tools accelerate production but the creative direction and artistry remain human. Every content creator wants more visual effects.

title: Speech-language pathologists
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Core work is hands-on clinical: assessing and treating speech, language, and swallowing disorders through direct patient interaction. AI assists with assessment scoring and therapy planning by 2028, but the personalized therapeutic interventions and patient rapport remain fundamentally human.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Evaluating and treating speech, language, and swallowing disorders involves hands-on clinical work with patients. AI aids with assessment tools and therapy exercises, but direct patient interaction and clinical judgment are central.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates assessment scoring and therapy exercise generation. However, speech therapy is hands-on and interpersonal—direct patient interaction, observing and correcting speech patterns in real-time, and building therapeutic relationships, especially with children and stroke patients.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Speech-language pathologists provide therapy through communication and exercises. Their work is primarily cognitive and interpersonal with no significant physical labor component for robots to automate.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Therapeutic work requiring patient assessment, trust, and personalized treatment. Each patient has unique speech and language challenges. The interpersonal and clinical assessment aspects are core. Some digital therapy tools assist but human therapists essential.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Therapeutic work requiring close human interaction, observation of subtle physical cues, and adaptive communication exercises. By 2036, some automated speech therapy tools exist, but the human therapeutic relationship and adaptive treatment are central.
adoption_friction_rationale: State licensing and healthcare regulation. Treatment requires direct human interaction and therapeutic relationship. Physical assessment and oral-motor therapy require human skill. Insurance billing requires licensed providers. Mix of schools and healthcare settings. Patient (often children) preference for human therapist. Liability concerns.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Significant unmet demand for speech therapy services. Many children and adults who need services can't access them due to cost and availability. AI tools help with practice exercises and monitoring but the therapeutic relationship requires human guidance.

title: Stationary engineers and boiler operators
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Predominantly physical: operating and maintaining boilers, engines, and mechanical equipment. Computerized monitoring systems assist with controls, but physical equipment operation, inspection, and emergency response require hands-on presence.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Operating and maintaining boilers, generators, and mechanical systems in buildings is physical work. AI aids monitoring, but hands-on equipment operation and emergency response remain human.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Operating and maintaining boilers and mechanical systems in buildings is physical operations work. AI automates monitoring and scheduling, but hands-on equipment operation, maintenance, and emergency response in mechanical rooms remain human tasks.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Stationary engineers operate and maintain boilers and mechanical systems in buildings and plants. While monitoring is increasingly automated, the physical maintenance and repair work requires skilled judgment in variable conditions.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Operation and maintenance of building systems (boilers, HVAC, power). Routine monitoring increasingly automated. However, physical maintenance, troubleshooting, and emergency response in diverse building systems still requires human operators. Some facilities approach lights-out for routine operations.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: By 2036, building mechanical systems are heavily automated with remote monitoring and control. Routine operations are automated. Humans remain for emergency response, maintenance, and unusual conditions.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large facilities (hospitals, universities, factories) are primary employers. Building automation systems already well-established. Licensing requirements for boiler operation. Union presence in some settings. Remote monitoring and AI-assisted operations advancing. Physical equipment maintenance still requires human presence.
demand_elasticity_rationale: AI and automation improve monitoring and control of building mechanical systems. Smart building technology reduces the need for on-site operators. Demand tied to the number of large facilities with complex mechanical systems.

title: Substance abuse, behavioral disorder, and mental health counselors
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Core work is deeply interpersonal: conducting therapy sessions, building trust with clients, facilitating group sessions, and providing crisis intervention. Case documentation has digital components, but the therapeutic relationship and emotional support are fundamentally human and cannot be automated.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Counseling individuals through addiction and mental health crises requires deep empathy, trust, and human connection. AI assists with screening tools and documentation, but the therapeutic relationship is inherently human.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI provides psychoeducation tools and treatment planning support. However, counseling addicted and mentally ill individuals is deeply interpersonal—the therapeutic relationship, group facilitation, crisis intervention, and motivational interviewing require human empathy and presence.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Mental health counselors provide therapy and support. Interpersonal therapeutic work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Counseling work that is entirely interpersonal. Requires human empathy, trust, and therapeutic relationship.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Entirely interpersonal therapeutic work. No physical component for robotic automation.
adoption_friction_rationale: State licensing and healthcare regulation. Therapeutic relationship is central to addiction and mental health recovery. Strong social resistance to non-human counselors for vulnerable populations. Fragmented across agencies, clinics, and private practice. Insurance billing requires licensed providers. Confidentiality and ethical requirements.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Massive unmet demand for addiction and mental health counseling. The treatment gap is enormous. AI tools can help with screening, assessment, and between-session monitoring, but the counseling relationship requires human empathy and connection.

title: Surgical assistants and technologists
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Almost entirely hands-on: preparing operating rooms, sterilizing equipment, passing instruments during surgery, and maintaining the sterile field. Documentation is a minor digital component. The physical surgical environment work cannot be automated by AI.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Preparing operating rooms, sterilizing instruments, and assisting surgeons during procedures are hands-on clinical tasks. AI has minimal impact on these physical surgical support duties.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Surgical technology is hands-on clinical work—preparing operating rooms, sterilizing instruments, passing instruments during surgery, and maintaining the sterile field. AI assists with surgical planning, but the physical operating room role remains human.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Surgical technologists prepare operating rooms and assist during procedures in structured but high-stakes environments. While robotic surgery systems are deployed, the technologist's varied support role remains manual.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Operating room assistance involving instrument handling and sterile technique. Robotic surgical systems handle some instrument positioning. However, the variety of surgical procedures, emergency situations, and need for real-time adaptation means human technologists remain essential for most surgeries.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Assisting in surgical procedures—preparing instruments, maintaining sterile field, assisting surgeons. By 2036, robotic surgical systems handle many routine tasks, but assisting human surgeons in complex procedures and managing variable surgical situations requires human presence.
adoption_friction_rationale: Hospital systems are primary employers. Operating room requires sterile technique and human judgment. State regulation varies. Surgical robotics are physician-controlled, not replacing techs. Liability for surgical outcomes. Physical instrument handling and anticipation of surgeon needs. Moderate labour shortages provide some pull.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Demand tied to surgical volume. AI-assisted and robotic surgery changes the tech role but doesn't eliminate it. Surgical volume grows modestly with aging population and advancing surgical capabilities.

title: Survey researchers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Almost entirely digital: designing surveys, collecting data through digital platforms, analyzing statistical results, and writing reports. AI significantly automates survey design, data collection, and analysis by 2028. Routine survey research faces strong automation pressure.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Survey design, data collection, statistical analysis, and report generation are heavily digital tasks AI agents handle autonomously. Human researchers focus on novel methodology, complex interpretation, and stakeholder communication.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Survey design, data collection, statistical analysis, and report generation are structured digital tasks AI handles autonomously. Human researchers remain for novel research question formulation and interpreting results in complex social science contexts.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Survey researchers design and conduct surveys. Knowledge-based research work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Research design and analysis work. Entirely knowledge-based.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Entirely analytical and design work. No physical component.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large research firms, government agencies, and universities. Survey design and analysis highly amenable to AI. Online survey platforms already automated much data collection. Clear ROI. Moderate institutional inertia in academic settings. AI tools for questionnaire design and analysis widely available.
demand_elasticity_rationale: AI and automated survey platforms reduce the need for human researchers to design, administer, and analyze surveys. Online surveys and AI analysis handle much of the routine work. Complex research design persists.

title: Surveying and mapping technicians
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: A blend of physical fieldwork (operating surveying equipment, collecting ground measurements) and digital tasks (processing data, creating maps using GIS, preparing reports). AI assists with data processing and automated mapping by 2028, balanced by essential field data collection.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Field measurements and equipment operation are physical tasks. However, data processing, map production, and GIS analysis are digital tasks increasingly automated by AI, creating a balanced exposure profile.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates data processing, map production, and calculations. However, physical fieldwork—operating survey instruments, collecting GPS data, and marking boundaries on-site—retains significant human roles.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Survey techs collect data using field equipment. Some fieldwork with physical equipment, but GPS and drone technology already assist. Variable outdoor conditions limit full robotic exposure.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Fieldwork increasingly supplemented by drones, GPS, and automated survey equipment. Routine topographic surveys in open areas can be partially automated. However, complex site surveys in variable terrain, urban environments, and detailed boundary work still require human technicians.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Field work with surveying equipment. By 2036, automated drones and GPS systems handle much routine surveying, but complex site conditions and urban environments still require human operators for some work.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large engineering firms and government agencies. GPS, LiDAR, and drone technology already transforming field work. AI for data processing and mapping advancing. Moderate regulatory requirements. Some fieldwork requires physical presence. Existing technology adoption patterns facilitate further automation.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Drones, LiDAR, and AI mapping tools automate much surveying data collection. GPS and satellite imagery reduce field time. The volume of surveys is tied to construction and land development.

title: Surveyors
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Significant fieldwork: operating precision instruments, measuring land boundaries, and collecting on-site data. Digital data processing and map preparation use GPS and GIS tools where AI assists. The essential physical field measurement work provides meaningful insulation.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Field surveying with physical instruments and site visits is core to the role. AI aids with data processing, calculations, and report generation, but on-site measurement and boundary determination require human presence.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates boundary calculations, legal description analysis, and map production. However, physical site measurement, equipment operation in the field, and professional certification requirements for legal surveys retain human roles.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Surveyors measure land using specialized equipment in variable outdoor settings. Drone surveying is advancing, but ground-level work in varied terrain limits full robotic replacement.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Professional surveying in variable field conditions. While technology (GPS, drones, LiDAR) automates data collection, interpretation of boundary disputes, complex property surveys, and work in variable terrain requires human judgment and professional licensure.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Field surveying in variable environments. By 2036, drone and automated surveying handle most routine work, but complex boundary disputes, difficult terrain, and legal precision requirements keep human surveyors involved.
adoption_friction_rationale: Mix of large engineering firms and independent practitioners. GPS and drone technology already transforming the field. State licensing requirements. Physical fieldwork in varied conditions. AI for boundary analysis and mapping advancing. Moderate employer fragmentation. Legal accountability for boundary determinations.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Licensed surveying requires human oversight for legal boundary determination. AI and drone tools improve productivity but legal requirements maintain human involvement. Demand tied to construction and development activity.

title: Tax examiners and collectors, and revenue agents
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Almost entirely screen-based: reviewing tax returns, conducting audits using software, analyzing financial records, and processing collections. AI significantly automates return review, anomaly detection, and compliance checking by 2028. Routine tax examination faces strong automation.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Tax return review, compliance checking, and assessment calculations are heavily digital tasks AI automates. Human agents focus on complex audits, fraud investigations, and taxpayer disputes requiring judgment.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Tax return review, compliance checking, and collection processing are structured digital tasks AI handles autonomously. Human agents remain for complex fraud investigations, taxpayer disputes requiring negotiation, and novel tax situations.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Tax examiners review tax returns and collect revenue. Desk-based analytical and administrative work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Desk-based analytical work reviewing tax returns and records. Entirely knowledge-based with some field visits.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Entirely analytical and administrative work. No physical component.
adoption_friction_rationale: Government employment with institutional inertia. Tax examination is highly data-driven and amenable to AI. IRS and state agencies are large employers. AI audit selection already used. Physical audits and taxpayer interactions require human judgment. Union presence. Some regulatory friction but efficiency pressure is strong.
demand_elasticity_rationale: AI automates tax return analysis, fraud detection, and collection processes. The volume of tax returns is fixed by the number of filers. Automated systems handle more returns without proportional headcount.

title: Taxi drivers, shuttle drivers, and chauffeurs
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Core work is physical: driving vehicles, navigating routes, and providing passenger service. Ride-hailing apps are digital platforms, but the fundamental task of safely transporting passengers requires physical presence. Autonomous vehicles remain limited by 2028.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Driving passengers in varied urban conditions remains primarily human at the 2031 horizon. Autonomous ride-hailing expands in limited geofenced areas, but most driving contexts still require human operators.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Driving is a physical task. While autonomous vehicle technology may transform this occupation, that represents physical automation rather than digital AI exposure. Digital AI exposure is limited to navigation and dispatch systems.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Autonomous ride-hailing (Waymo, Zoox) is commercially operational in 15-20 US cities by 2028 on geo-fenced routes, directly displacing taxi/chauffeur functions in those markets. Significant but not universal coverage.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Autonomous ride-hailing vehicles operational in many urban areas by 2031. Major cities have significant autonomous taxi fleets. However, complex urban environments, adverse weather, and luxury/personal chauffeur services still employ human drivers. The transition is well underway.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: By 2036, autonomous ride-hailing vehicles are ubiquitous on mapped urban routes. Human drivers remain for unmapped areas, extreme conditions, and premium chauffeur services where personal service is valued. The vast majority of rides are autonomous.
adoption_friction_rationale: Mix of large ride-hailing companies (Uber, Lyft with Waymo/Cruise partnerships) and small operators. Autonomous vehicle technology advancing but regulatory approval city-by-city is slow. Urban driving complexity. Insurance and liability frameworks need updating. Some labour shortages but regulatory path is fragmented.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Autonomous vehicle technology directly threatens taxi and ride-hail driving. Rideshare platforms already disrupted traditional taxis. Self-driving vehicles in controlled environments (airports, cities) will reduce driver demand.

title: Teacher assistants
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Predominantly interpersonal: working directly with students, reinforcing lessons, supervising activities, and maintaining classroom order. Some administrative and grading tasks have digital components, but the face-to-face student support and classroom assistance dominate.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: AI handles some tutoring, grading, and instructional support. However, teacher assistants provide physical supervision, hands-on student support, and behavioral management that require human presence, especially with younger students.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates instructional content delivery, grading, and documentation. However, teacher assistants provide direct physical support to students—supervising, managing behavior, assisting with special needs, and maintaining a supportive classroom presence.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Teaching assistance and tutoring involve interpersonal instruction and student support. This is cognitive and social work with no physical labor component for robots to automate.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Supporting teachers in classroom settings. Interpersonal work with students requiring patience and adaptation. The role is about human interaction and student support.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Supporting students with hands-on help, supervision, and physical classroom management. Requires human patience, adaptability, and interpersonal skills with children. By 2036, some educational technology assists, but the human support role for diverse student needs remains.
adoption_friction_rationale: Government employment in schools with institutional inertia. Support for students requires human interaction and patience. Union protections in some districts. State requirements vary. Working with children demands human presence for safety and social-emotional support. Low wages limit technology investment in schools.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Classroom support requires physical presence with students. AI tutoring may reduce some assistant tasks but the supervisory and hands-on help for young students persists. Budget constraints are the main limiting factor.

title: Technical writers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Almost entirely screen-based: writing manuals, how-to guides, and documentation using specialized tools. AI writing tools by 2028 can generate much of routine technical documentation from source code and specifications. Active headcount reduction in standard technical writing roles.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Documentation production, user guides, API references, and technical manuals are heavily digital tasks AI agents produce autonomously by 2031. Human technical writers focus on complex system documentation, editorial oversight, and information architecture.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Documentation, user manuals, API references, and technical content creation from source material are structured digital tasks AI handles end-to-end. The traditional technical writer role is fundamentally restructured, with remaining human work in strategic content architecture and complex product communication.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Technical writers create documentation. Desk-based knowledge work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Writing and documentation work that is entirely knowledge-based and digital.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Entirely writing and documentation work. No physical component.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large tech companies and enterprises are primary employers. AI text generation is already competitive for technical documentation. Clear ROI. Existing digital workflow. Minimal regulatory barriers. Some judgment needed for complex documentation but routine technical writing is highly amenable to AI. Market already being disrupted.
demand_elasticity_rationale: AI generates draft documentation, but every software product, API, and technical system needs clear documentation. Growing technology complexity creates more to document. Technical writers shift to editing AI output and creating strategic content.

title: Telecommunications technicians
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Predominantly hands-on: installing routers, running cables, configuring equipment, and troubleshooting network issues at customer sites. Diagnostic software assists with troubleshooting, but the physical installation and repair work dominates.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Installing and repairing telecommunications equipment—routers, switches, cabling—is hands-on physical work. AI aids with diagnostics and network configuration, but physical installation and repair remain human.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Installing and repairing telecommunications equipment is hands-on physical work. AI assists with diagnostics and network configuration, but the physical installation, cable routing, and hardware repair remain human tasks.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Telecom technicians install and repair equipment in varied residential and commercial buildings. The diverse environments and need for diagnostic troubleshooting limit robotic deployment by 2028.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Installation and repair of telecom equipment in variable buildings and facilities. Each site presents unique wiring and equipment configurations. While some standardized installations see limited automation, troubleshooting and repair in diverse environments requires human skill.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Installing and repairing telecom equipment in variable building environments. By 2036, standardized installations are automated, but troubleshooting complex systems in diverse environments requires human diagnostic skill and adaptability.
adoption_friction_rationale: Mix of large telecom companies and smaller contractors. Physical installation and repair in varied customer locations. FCC regulations. Some labour shortages provide pull. Each installation environment is different, challenging robotic standardization. Licensing requirements vary. Moderate capital availability in large firms.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Physical installation and repair of telecom equipment resists automation. 5G rollout and fiber expansion create demand. Remote diagnostics help but on-site work persists. Demand cycles with technology deployment.

title: Tellers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Predominantly screen-based transaction processing: cashing checks, depositing money, and managing account inquiries using banking software. ATMs and digital banking reduce demand, and AI chatbots handle routine queries. However, in-person customer service and complex transactions provide some continued need.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Processing deposits, withdrawals, and account inquiries are routine transactions increasingly handled by ATMs and digital banking. Remaining tellers handle complex transactions and in-person customer service, but the role shrinks dramatically.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Banking transactions, account inquiries, and routine financial services are handled by ATMs, online banking, and AI. The traditional teller role has been fundamentally restructured, with remaining human roles focused on complex transactions and relationship banking.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Bank tellers process transactions at counters. ATMs and digital banking have already automated much of this work; remaining teller work involves customer interaction, not physical labor.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: ATMs and digital banking handle the vast majority of routine transactions. Many bank branches reduced or eliminated teller positions. Remaining tellers focus on complex transactions and customer service. The trend toward automation is well-established.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: By 2036, ATMs, mobile banking, and automated branch services handle the vast majority of banking transactions. Human tellers remain primarily for complex transactions and customer relationship purposes. Most routine transactions are fully automated.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large banks are primary employers with massive investment in ATMs, mobile banking, and digital services. Role has been declining for decades. Clear ROI. Minimal regulatory barriers for automated transactions. Customer acceptance of self-service banking is well-established. Branch closures accelerating.
demand_elasticity_rationale: ATMs, online banking, and mobile banking have already drastically reduced teller positions. AI-powered banking further reduces branch traffic. The remaining in-branch transactions continue to decline as digital banking improves.

title: Top executives
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: A blend of digital strategic work (analyzing business data, reviewing reports, financial planning) and interpersonal leadership (managing teams, building stakeholder relationships, making high-stakes decisions). AI assists with data analysis and report generation by 2028, but strategic vision, organizational leadership, and human judgment remain irreplaceable.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: AI provides comprehensive analytics, report generation, and decision support. However, organizational leadership, stakeholder management, strategic vision, board relations, and navigating complex human dynamics are deeply human executive functions.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates data analysis, report generation, market intelligence, and strategic scenario modeling. However, executive leadership requires interpersonal influence, organizational vision, stakeholder relationship management, and making high-stakes decisions in ambiguous contexts where human accountability is essential.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Top executives make strategic business decisions. Entirely leadership and knowledge work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Leadership and strategic decision-making. Entirely about human judgment, vision, and organizational management.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Strategic leadership, decision-making, and organizational management. Entirely cognitive and interpersonal. No physical component.
adoption_friction_rationale: C-suite roles require strategic vision, leadership, stakeholder management, and organizational culture stewardship. Board accountability and fiduciary duty. AI tools augment decision-making but cannot replace human leadership. Large companies can adopt AI advisors. Governance structures and shareholder expectations require human executives.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Executive positions scale with the number of organizations, not individual productivity. AI provides better decision-support but the leadership, vision, and stakeholder management roles persist. C-suite headcount is relatively fixed.

title: Tour and travel guides
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Predominantly in-person and interpersonal: leading groups through attractions, providing live commentary, and managing logistics on-site. AI audio guides and virtual tours exist, but the personalized human experience of live guided tours remains valued.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Leading tours, providing live commentary, and managing group logistics in physical locations are interpersonal and embodied duties. AI-powered audio guides substitute in some contexts, but human guides retain value for interactive experiences.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates itinerary planning, information delivery, and travel recommendations. However, tour guiding is an in-person interpersonal experience—leading groups through physical locations, providing engaging storytelling, and adapting to real-time group dynamics.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Tour guides lead groups and provide commentary. Interpersonal communication work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Interpersonal work providing guided experiences. Each tour involves unique group dynamics and real-time adaptation. While audio guides and virtual tours exist, live human guides are valued for personality, knowledge, and interaction.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Tour guiding requires human personality, storytelling, cultural knowledge, and adaptive interaction with groups. Physical aspects include navigating varied environments. By 2036, some automated audio guides and robotic information kiosks exist, but the human experience and cultural interpretation remain central.
adoption_friction_rationale: Mix of large tour operators and many independent guides. AI audio guides and virtual tours already common. But live guided experiences valued for personal interaction and local expertise. Fragmented employer base. Tourism regulations vary. Cultural experiences and group management require human presence.
demand_elasticity_rationale: AI-powered audio guides handle basic information, but the experiential and interpersonal aspects of guided tours resist automation. Growing tourism and experiential travel demand. Local expertise and storytelling maintain human value.

title: Training and development managers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Predominantly digital: developing training programs, managing learning management systems, analyzing skills data, and coordinating development initiatives. AI assists with content creation, needs assessment, and program analytics by 2028. Team leadership and strategic talent development remain human.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: AI generates training content, conducts needs assessments, and tracks learning outcomes. Managers retain strategic workforce development planning, organizational change facilitation, and leadership development roles.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates training content creation, needs assessment, program evaluation, and learning analytics. Human managers remain for organizational learning strategy, facilitating executive development, and managing the interpersonal aspects of organizational change.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Training managers oversee employee development programs. Managerial work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Management of training programs. Entirely administrative and strategic.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Entirely management and educational design work. No physical component.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large corporations are primary employers. AI-powered learning platforms already widely adopted. Management role requires human judgment for organizational learning strategy. Moderate employer size. Some institutional inertia in training culture. Digital delivery facilitates AI but human facilitation valued for leadership development.
demand_elasticity_rationale: AI creates massive reskilling needs, expanding training demand. Every organization needs workforce development programs. AI tools enhance training delivery but program leadership and strategy require human managers.

title: Training and development specialists
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Significant digital work: creating training materials, developing e-learning content, and assessing training effectiveness. AI tools significantly assist with content creation and assessment design by 2028. In-person facilitation and interactive training delivery provide interpersonal balance.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: AI creates training materials, e-learning modules, and assessments autonomously. Human specialists focus on facilitation, executive coaching, and designing programs for complex organizational change.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Course design, content creation, assessment development, and delivery of standard training are automated by AI. Human specialists remain for facilitation of complex interpersonal skill development, executive coaching, and organizational development interventions requiring human facilitation.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Training specialists design and deliver training programs. Knowledge-based educational work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Designing and delivering training programs. Interpersonal and knowledge-based work.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Delivering training involves some physical demonstration but is primarily cognitive instruction and interpersonal facilitation. Minimal physical task content for robots.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large corporations are primary employers. E-learning and AI-powered training content already widely used. Content development amenable to AI tools. Some human facilitation valued for workshops. Moderate employer fragmentation. Professional certification (ATD) creates mild friction. Digital delivery infrastructure well-established.
demand_elasticity_rationale: AI creates enormous reskilling demand across all industries. Every worker needs continuous learning. AI tools make training more personalized and scalable, enabling specialists to serve more learners and develop more programs.

title: Transportation, storage, and distribution managers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Predominantly digital management: analyzing logistics data, optimizing routes, managing supply chain systems, and coordinating distribution. AI significantly enhances logistics optimization and demand forecasting by 2028. Physical warehouse oversight and staff management provide some balance.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Route optimization, inventory management, and logistics analytics are heavily automated by AI. Managers retain strategic planning, vendor relationships, and managing physical warehouse and transportation operations.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates route optimization, inventory management, demand forecasting, and logistics planning. Human managers remain for crisis response, labor management, regulatory navigation, and managing complex multi-modal transportation networks requiring interpersonal coordination.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Distribution managers oversee logistics operations. Managerial work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Management of logistics operations. Overseeing increasingly automated warehouses and transport, but the role is about planning, optimization, and human coordination.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Management and logistics planning role. Physical oversight of facilities but core work is cognitive planning and coordination.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large logistics companies are primary employers with strong technology adoption culture. Supply chain management is highly amenable to AI optimization. AI tools for routing, warehousing, and fleet management widely deployed. Clear ROI. Moderate regulatory requirements (DOT). Labour shortages provide pull.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Management positions scale with the number of facilities and operations. AI optimizes logistics but human oversight of physical operations persists. Growing e-commerce expands warehousing but automation improves efficiency.

title: Travel agents
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Almost entirely screen-based: researching travel options, booking reservations, preparing itineraries, and managing client accounts using online platforms. AI significantly automates trip planning, price comparison, and booking by 2028. Active displacement as AI tools handle routine travel arrangements.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Itinerary planning, booking, price comparison, and travel documentation are digital tasks AI handles autonomously. Human agents retain value for complex multi-destination trips, luxury travel consulting, and handling disruptions, but routine bookings are automated.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Itinerary planning, booking, price comparison, and travel logistics are fully automated by AI. The traditional travel agent role has been fundamentally restructured—human agents persist only for luxury and complex multi-destination travel where personalized advisory service commands a premium.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Travel agents plan trips for clients. Service-oriented desk work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Advisory and booking service work. Entirely interpersonal and knowledge-based.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Entirely service and advisory work. No physical component.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large travel agencies and online platforms (Expedia, Booking.com) have largely automated routine bookings. AI trip planning tools advancing. Fragmented independent agent segment shrinking. Minimal regulatory barriers. Complex luxury/corporate travel retains human value but market share is small. Economic pressure is strong.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Online booking platforms and AI travel assistants handle most routine travel planning. The role has already contracted dramatically since the internet era. Complex and luxury travel persist but standard bookings are self-service.

title: Tutors
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: A blend of interpersonal teaching (working one-on-one with students, adapting instruction, providing motivation) and digital content delivery. AI tutoring tools provide significant competition for basic subject matter tutoring by 2028, but personalized human tutoring for complex subjects and test preparation retains value.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: AI tutoring systems deliver personalized instruction, practice problems, and explanations effectively by 2031. Human tutors retain value for motivational coaching, complex conceptual breakthroughs, and test preparation for high-stakes exams.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI provides personalized instruction, practice problems, explanations, and progress tracking that replicate much of traditional tutoring. Human tutors remain for motivational coaching, working with students who need interpersonal connection, and high-stakes test preparation where human accountability is valued.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Teaching assistance and tutoring involve interpersonal instruction and student support. This is cognitive and social work with no physical labor component for robots to automate.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: One-on-one educational work requiring personalization and human connection. Each student has unique learning needs and styles.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: One-on-one educational support is fundamentally about the human learning relationship. Minimal physical component—the value is cognitive instruction and interpersonal mentoring.
adoption_friction_rationale: Extremely fragmented industry of independent tutors. AI tutoring systems (Khan Academy, ChatGPT) already widely used. Some parent/student preference for human tutors. No licensing requirements. Low capital barriers to AI tutoring adoption. Large tutoring companies can adopt AI tools. Online tutoring facilitates AI integration.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Maximum latent demand. Every student could benefit from personalized tutoring but almost none can afford it. AI tutoring tools are powerful but human tutors provide motivation, emotional support, and adaptive teaching that AI cannot match. Hybrid human+AI tutoring could serve vastly more students.

title: Umpires, referees, and other sports officials
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Predominantly physical and interpersonal: officiating games, making real-time judgment calls, managing player conduct, and maintaining game flow. Video replay technology assists with some decisions, but the on-field human presence and authority remain essential.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Officiating sporting events requires physical presence, real-time judgment, and game management. AI aids with video review and rule enforcement, but human officials remain essential for live competition.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Officiating sports is physical on-field work. While AI assists with instant replay and decision support, the human official remains for real-time game management, player interaction, and maintaining the human element that sports culture values.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Sports officials enforce rules during competitions. While technology assists with some calls, officiating requires human judgment in dynamic environments.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Officiating requires real-time human judgment in dynamic physical environments. While technology assists (instant replay, electronic line calling), human referees remain essential for game management, player interaction, and judgment calls in complex situations. Sports value the human element.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Officiating requires real-time judgment in dynamic physical environments. By 2036, automated officiating technology (video review, sensor-based calls) assists significantly, but the human authority and real-time judgment in complex, ambiguous situations preserve the human role. Cultural preference for human officials also persists.
adoption_friction_rationale: Strong institutional resistance from sports leagues and governing bodies. Officiating involves split-second human judgment and game management. Technology-assisted review exists (VAR, replay) but full replacement faces enormous cultural resistance. Fragmented across youth, amateur, and professional sports.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Demand tied to the number of sporting events, which grows modestly. AI-assisted officiating (video review, electronic line calling) changes the role but human officials persist for judgment calls and game management.

title: Urban and regional planners
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Predominantly digital: analyzing demographic data, using GIS tools, developing land use plans, writing reports, and preparing presentations. AI assists with data analysis, impact modeling, and plan drafting by 2028. Community meetings and site assessments provide interpersonal/physical balance.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Data analysis, GIS mapping, zoning review, and report writing are digital tasks AI handles well. Planners retain community engagement, public hearing facilitation, and complex policy balancing roles, but analytical productivity increases dramatically.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates demographic analysis, zoning code review, environmental impact modeling, and plan documentation. Human planners remain for community engagement, navigating political dynamics, creative placemaking vision, and balancing competing stakeholder interests in complex urban decisions.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Urban planners develop land use plans. Knowledge-based analytical and design work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Planning and analysis work that is entirely knowledge-based. No physical component.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Entirely analytical, design, and policy work. No physical component.
adoption_friction_rationale: Government employment with institutional inertia. Planning requires community engagement, political judgment, and public hearings. AI tools for data analysis and visualization emerging. AICP certification. Zoning and environmental decisions require human discretion. Moderate regulatory complexity. Stakeholder engagement is inherently human.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Climate adaptation, housing affordability, and sustainable development increase planning needs. AI tools enable better modeling and analysis. Every community needs planning but many lack resources for comprehensive planning.

title: Veterinarians
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: A blend of hands-on clinical work (examining animals, performing surgery, administering treatments) and digital tasks (maintaining records, interpreting diagnostics, researching treatments). AI assists with diagnostic imaging and record management by 2028, but the physical examination and treatment of animals remain human. Calibration anchor.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Examining animals, performing surgeries, and administering treatments are hands-on clinical tasks. AI aids with diagnostics, treatment protocols, and records, but physical veterinary medicine requires human skill and judgment.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates diagnostic imaging interpretation, treatment protocol recommendations, and medical records. However, veterinary medicine is hands-on—physical examinations, surgery, and direct animal care require manual skill. The client relationship with pet owners also retains human value.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Veterinarians perform examinations and procedures on diverse animal species in unpredictable clinical settings. The variability of animal patients and procedures limits robotic replacement by 2028.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Clinical care of diverse animal species in variable settings. Each animal and condition is unique. Surgery and examination require skilled dexterity with patients who can't communicate. Trust of pet owners essential. The variety of species and unpredictable animal behavior resists automation.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Treating diverse animal species with highly variable anatomy and behavior. By 2036, diagnostic equipment and surgical assistance are advanced, but the extreme variability of animal patients, physical examination requiring adaptive handling, and client relationships keep significant human involvement.
adoption_friction_rationale: State licensing, DEA registration, and veterinary board regulation. Mix of small animal practices (fragmented) and large animal/corporate chains. Physical examination and surgery require hands-on skill. Pet owner emotional bonds require human interaction. Malpractice liability. Labour shortages provide some pull.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Growing pet ownership and spending on pet care create expanding demand. AI diagnostic tools help veterinarians treat more animals. Significant unmet demand in rural areas and for exotic/specialty animal care.

title: Veterinary assistants and laboratory animal caretakers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Almost entirely physical: feeding and watering animals, cleaning cages, restraining animals for examination, and maintaining facilities. Record-keeping is a minor digital component. AI has negligible impact on hands-on animal care.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Feeding, cleaning, restraining, and caring for animals are entirely physical tasks. AI has negligible impact on these hands-on animal care duties.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Working with animals is physical—feeding, cleaning, restraining, and providing basic care. AI assists with documentation and scheduling, but the hands-on animal care remains entirely human.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Vet assistants and lab animal caretakers feed, clean, and handle animals in somewhat structured settings. Lab animal care is more structured than clinical vet work, but animal handling limits automation.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Animal care involving feeding, cleaning, restraining, and assisting with procedures. Animals are unpredictable. Each animal's needs differ. Some routine feeding and cleaning in lab settings automated, but handling live animals requires human adaptability and care.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Animal care involving feeding, cleaning, restraining, and assisting with procedures. By 2036, routine feeding and cleaning in structured facilities is automated, but handling diverse animals and assisting with clinical procedures requires human adaptability.
adoption_friction_rationale: Mix of large research institutions and small veterinary practices. Physical animal handling requires skill and patience. Regulatory requirements for animal welfare (USDA, IACUC). Moderate employer fragmentation. Some lab animal care in research settings is more standardized. Labour shortages provide moderate pull.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Hands-on animal care resists automation. Demand tied to veterinary practice volume and research facilities. Growing pet care spending supports demand.

title: Veterinary technologists and technicians
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Predominantly hands-on: performing medical tests on animals, assisting in surgery, collecting samples, and administering treatments. Lab results processing and records management have digital components, but the physical animal care and clinical work dominate.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Assisting with animal procedures, collecting samples, administering medications, and providing animal care are hands-on clinical tasks. AI assists with records and lab analysis, but physical work dominates.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Vet techs perform hands-on clinical work—drawing blood, administering medications, assisting in surgery, and monitoring anesthetized animals. AI assists with lab result interpretation, but the physical clinical work remains human.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Vet techs assist with animal procedures requiring handling of unpredictable animals. The variable animal behavior and diverse clinical tasks limit robotic exposure by 2028.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Clinical support for veterinarians including restraining animals, administering treatments, and lab work. Each animal is unpredictable. Requires trust and skilled handling. Some lab procedures automated but direct animal care resists automation.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Clinical work with diverse animals—restraining, sample collection, anesthesia monitoring. By 2036, automated monitoring and some sample collection assist, but the variability of animal patients and need for adaptive physical handling keeps significant human involvement.
adoption_friction_rationale: State licensing requirements. Mix of large veterinary hospitals and small practices. Physical animal handling for procedures requires skill. Pet owner expectations for compassionate care. Moderate employer fragmentation. Some diagnostic lab work amenable to automation. Labour shortages provide moderate pull.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Growing pet care spending and expanding veterinary services. Hands-on animal care resists automation. AI diagnostics may increase the scope of what vet techs can handle under supervision.

title: Waiters and waitresses
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Almost entirely physical and interpersonal: taking orders, serving food, managing tables, and providing customer service. POS systems are minor digital tools. AI has minimal impact on the in-person dining service that defines this role.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Taking orders, serving food, and attending to diners are physical and interpersonal tasks. AI ordering systems exist, but human table service remains the standard in most restaurants.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Table service is physical and interpersonal—taking orders, carrying food, and providing hospitality. Digital AI exposure is limited to ordering systems and POS technology.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Waiters navigate variable dining environments while carrying food and interacting with customers. Some restaurants use delivery robots, but the social interaction and varied environments limit robotic replacement by 2028.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Robotic serving systems in some chain restaurants. However, full-service dining emphasizes human interaction, knowledge of menu, and hospitality. Carrying plates through variable dining rooms and providing personalized service requires human servers in most restaurants. Fast-casual sees more automation.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: By 2036, robotic serving is common in many restaurants—automated ordering, food delivery robots, and self-service. However, fine dining and hospitality-focused venues retain human servers for the personal service experience. Mid-range restaurants are significantly automated.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large restaurant chains can deploy ordering tablets and serving robots. Severe labour shortages provide strong pull. But fine dining and full-service restaurants value human service as part of experience. Alcohol service requires human judgment. Mix of large chains (lower friction) and independent restaurants (higher friction).
demand_elasticity_rationale: Ordering kiosks and mobile ordering reduce some serving tasks. But table service in restaurants remains a human-interaction-driven experience. Demand tied to dining-out trends, which grow modestly.

title: Water and wastewater treatment plant and system operators
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: A blend of physical equipment operation (adjusting controls, collecting samples, maintaining equipment) and computerized system monitoring. AI assists with process optimization and predictive maintenance, but the safety-critical physical plant operations require human oversight and hands-on work.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Operating treatment equipment, monitoring chemical processes, and maintaining physical systems are hands-on tasks. AI aids with process monitoring and optimization, but physical plant operations require human operators.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates monitoring, process control optimization, and compliance reporting. However, physical plant operations—adjusting equipment, conducting inspections, and maintaining infrastructure—require human presence in regulated utility environments.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Water treatment operators monitor and adjust equipment in structured plant environments. Plant operations are increasingly automated with SCADA systems, and some physical monitoring tasks have robotic potential.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Treatment plant operations increasingly automated with SCADA systems and remote monitoring. Routine operations handled automatically. Human operators focus on monitoring, troubleshooting, regulatory compliance, and responding to anomalies. Some plants approach near-autonomous operation.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: By 2036, treatment plant operations are heavily automated with remote monitoring and control. Routine operations require minimal human presence. Humans remain for maintenance, emergency response, and system optimization.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large municipal utilities are primary employers. SCADA systems and automation already well-established. State licensing requirements for operators. EPA Clean Water Act and Safe Drinking Water Act compliance. Public health safety critical. AI for process optimization emerging. Union presence. Moderate institutional inertia.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Demand tied to the fixed number of water treatment facilities. AI and automation improve monitoring but human operators are required for safety. Growing water infrastructure needs provide modest growth.

title: Water transportation workers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Predominantly physical: operating vessels, maintaining equipment, managing cargo, and ensuring maritime safety. Navigation systems are digital tools, but the physical operation of ships and boats in variable conditions requires human presence.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Operating vessels, managing cargo, and navigating waterways are physical tasks. AI aids with navigation and logistics planning, but hands-on ship operation and safety management remain human.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Operating boats and ships is physical work in marine environments. AI assists with navigation and cargo management, but vessel operation, docking, and maritime safety require human crews.
