physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Water transportation workers operate vessels in variable maritime environments with physical tasks like mooring and cargo handling. Autonomous vessels are in early trials but the unpredictable marine environment limits 2028 deployment.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Some cargo vessel operations see increased automation (autonomous container ships on fixed routes). However, variable waterway conditions, port operations, and passenger vessel work require human judgment. Inland waterway work in diverse conditions particularly resistant to automation.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Vessel operation involves variable water conditions. By 2036, autonomous navigation handles many commercial routes, but variable weather, port operations, and emergency situations require human judgment. Regulatory requirements also mandate human crew.
adoption_friction_rationale: Coast Guard regulations and international maritime law. Large shipping companies have resources but maritime safety regulations are stringent. Union presence (maritime unions). Pilotage requirements for ports. Autonomous vessel technology advancing but regulatory approval for commercial shipping is very slow. International coordination required.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Autonomous vessel technology advancing for commercial shipping. AI navigation and remote monitoring reduce crew needs. Maritime regulations may slow adoption but the trajectory favors smaller crews.

title: Web developers and digital designers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Almost entirely screen-based: designing and coding websites, implementing user interfaces, and managing digital content. AI coding and design tools by 2028 handle much of routine web development—generating layouts, writing standard code, and testing. Active headcount reduction in basic web development roles.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: AI agents build, deploy, and maintain standard websites and web applications autonomously by 2031. Human developers focus on complex interactive applications, novel UX challenges, and system architecture, but routine web development is largely automated.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Website development, front-end coding, and digital interface design are fully automatable by AI. The traditional web developer role is restructured—remaining human roles focus on creative digital strategy, user experience vision, and complex interactive experiences where human design judgment adds value.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Web developers create websites. Entirely desk-based knowledge work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Entirely digital work designing and coding websites. No physical component.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Purely digital work. No physical component whatsoever.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large tech companies and agencies are primary employers. AI code generation tools already widely used for web development. No-code/low-code platforms advancing. Clear ROI. Existing technology culture. Minimal regulatory barriers. Competitive market drives rapid AI tool adoption.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Every business, organization, and individual could benefit from a better web presence. AI tools make development faster and cheaper, unlocking demand from millions of small businesses. Historical pattern: web development tools always led to more websites, not fewer developers.

title: Welders, cutters, solderers, and brazers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Almost entirely physical skilled trade work: joining metal parts using welding equipment, cutting materials, and inspecting welds. Blueprint reading is a minor digital component. AI has negligible impact on this hands-on manufacturing and construction trade.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Joining and cutting metals using welding equipment is hands-on skilled trade work. Robotic welding expands in factories, but field welding and custom fabrication remain human tasks.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Welding is physical skilled trade work—joining metals using heat and filler materials. Digital AI has essentially no exposure to this occupation, which requires hands-on manual skill and physical endurance.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Welding in manufacturing settings is highly structured and repetitive. Robotic welding is already widespread in automotive; by 2028 humanoid robots extend this to more welding tasks in controlled factory environments.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Robotic welding dominant in manufacturing and production environments—automotive, structural steel, pipe fabrication. Automated welding systems handle most standardized joints. Human welders focus on field welding in variable positions, repair work, and custom fabrication. Production welding largely automated.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: By 2036, robotic welding handles most production and structural welding. Automated systems manage standardized joints with high quality. Human welders remain for field repairs, complex custom work, and genuinely novel configurations. Volume welding is heavily automated.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large manufacturing employers already use robotic welding extensively. Labour shortages in welding are severe, creating strong pull. Factory welding is highly automated. Field welding in construction and repair is more challenging for robots. AWS certification and OSHA requirements. Mix of factory (lower friction) and field (higher friction) work.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Robotic welding handles much production welding. AI-guided systems improve automated welding quality. But field welding, maintenance, and custom work resist automation. Net gradual decline in production welding headcount.

title: Wholesale and manufacturing sales representatives
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Significant digital work: researching customers, preparing presentations, managing CRM systems, and processing orders. AI assists with lead scoring, proposal generation, and market analysis by 2028. In-person client relationships, product demonstrations, and negotiation provide meaningful interpersonal balance.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Product information, pricing analysis, order processing, and client communication are digital tasks AI handles efficiently. Human reps retain value in relationship-driven B2B sales, complex negotiations, and key account management.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates product configuration, pricing, order processing, and market analytics. Human sales representatives remain for complex B2B relationship management, consultative selling in technical domains, and navigating enterprise procurement processes.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Wholesale sales is primarily relationship-based selling and negotiation. This is knowledge and interpersonal work with no physical labor component for robots to automate.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Sales work involving client relationships and product knowledge. Entirely interpersonal and knowledge-based.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Entirely sales and relationship work. No physical component for robotic automation.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large manufacturers and distributors are primary employers. AI tools for customer analytics, pricing, and order management already used. B2B sales involves relationship management. Some employer fragmentation. Clear ROI for large operations. Minimal regulatory barriers. CRM automation well-established.
demand_elasticity_rationale: B2B e-commerce platforms and AI-powered procurement reduce the need for sales representatives. Relationship-based selling persists for complex products but commodity sales move to digital channels.

title: Wind turbine technicians
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Predominantly physical: climbing wind turbines, inspecting equipment, performing maintenance and repairs at height, and troubleshooting mechanical/electrical systems. Diagnostic monitoring systems are digital tools, but the dangerous physical fieldwork dominates.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Climbing turbines, inspecting components, and performing repairs at height are physical, hazardous tasks. AI aids with predictive maintenance scheduling, but hands-on repair remains entirely human.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Wind turbine maintenance is physical work performed at height in outdoor conditions. AI assists with predictive maintenance analytics and diagnostics, but the physical climb, inspection, and repair of turbine components remain human tasks.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Wind turbine technicians perform maintenance and repair at extreme heights in exposed, variable conditions. The hazardous and unpredictable work environment makes robotic replacement infeasible by 2028.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Maintenance and repair at extreme heights in variable weather conditions. Each turbine and failure mode is different. Working in confined nacelles requires human dexterity. Drone inspection assists but physical repair at height in wind remains challenging for robots.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Working at extreme heights on variable equipment in outdoor conditions. By 2036, drone inspection and some robotic maintenance assist, but the variable conditions, heights, and complex turbine systems still require significant human skill and judgment.
adoption_friction_rationale: Large wind energy companies are primary employers with resources. Physical work at extreme heights in remote locations. OSHA safety requirements. Specialized technical skills for varied conditions. Labour shortages in renewable energy provide pull. Some remote monitoring and AI diagnostics deployed but physical maintenance is challenging to automate.
demand_elasticity_rationale: Rapidly growing wind energy sector creates expanding demand. Physical maintenance of turbines at height resists automation. AI predictive maintenance helps prioritize but hands-on work persists. Strong growth trajectory.

title: Woodworkers
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Predominantly physical: operating saws, planers, and other woodworking machinery, and hand-crafting products. CNC programming has a minor digital component, but the physical cutting, shaping, and finishing of wood products dominates this manufacturing trade.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: Cutting, shaping, and assembling wood products using hand and power tools is physical skilled work. CNC programming aids some production, but manual woodworking remains human.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: Woodworking is physical production work—cutting, shaping, and assembling wood products using hand and power tools. AI assists with CNC design and production planning, but the hands-on craftsmanship remains human.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Woodworking in factory settings involves operating machines and handling materials in semi-structured environments. CNC automation handles much cutting, but assembly and finishing still require human dexterity for varied products.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: CNC routers and automated equipment handle most production woodworking—furniture manufacturing, cabinet production, millwork. Robotic finishing and assembly expanding. Custom and artisanal woodworking still requires human skill, but production volume is heavily automated.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: By 2036, CNC and robotic woodworking handle most production furniture and cabinet making. Custom, artistic, and restoration woodworking retains human craftsmanship, but volume production is heavily automated.
adoption_friction_rationale: Mix of large furniture manufacturers (automated CNC) and many small custom shops. CNC woodworking well-established in manufacturing. Custom and artisanal work valued. Fragmented small shop segment. Labour shortages in manufacturing provide pull. OSHA safety requirements. Large producers already highly automated.
demand_elasticity_rationale: CNC machines automate production woodworking but custom and artisanal work persists. Demand tied to construction and furniture markets. The craft aspect maintains a market niche even as mass production automates.

title: Writers and authors
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: Almost entirely screen-based: researching topics, drafting content, revising text, and managing publications. AI writing tools by 2028 can generate first drafts, suggest revisions, and handle routine content. Active restructuring in content writing, copywriting, and commercial writing, though distinctive voice and creative literary work retain human value.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: AI generates articles, marketing copy, reports, and even creative fiction by 2031. Human writers retain value for literary voice, investigative journalism, and deeply personal creative work, but commercial content production is heavily automated.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI generates articles, marketing copy, reports, and even long-form content. Routine writing is fully automated. Human writers persist where artistic voice, cultural commentary, investigative journalism, and human authorship are integral to the value proposition.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Writers create written content. Entirely desk-based creative knowledge work.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Creative writing work that is entirely knowledge-based. While AI writing tools assist, the creative and intellectual aspects are core. No physical component.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Entirely cognitive and creative work. No physical component.
adoption_friction_rationale: AI writing tools (ChatGPT, Claude) already competitive for many writing tasks. Large media and corporate employers adopt quickly. But literary authorship values human voice and creativity. Extremely fragmented freelance market. Some union protections (WGA for screenwriters). Copyright questions around AI writing unresolved.
demand_elasticity_rationale: AI generates content but creates more demand for human-quality writing with authentic voice and perspective. Every business needs content. The volume of content needed grows exponentially. Human writers shift to higher-value creative and editorial work.

title: Zoologists and wildlife biologists
digital_exposure_2028_rationale: A blend of physical fieldwork (observing animals in habitat, collecting specimens, tagging wildlife) and digital knowledge work (analyzing data, writing research papers, using GIS for habitat mapping). AI assists with data analysis and species identification by 2028, balanced by essential outdoor field research.
digital_exposure_2031_rationale: AI assists with data analysis, species identification, and literature review. However, fieldwork—observing wildlife, collecting specimens, and conducting ecological surveys in natural habitats—requires physical human presence.
digital_exposure_2036_rationale: AI automates data analysis, population modeling, literature review, and report writing. However, fieldwork—observing animals in natural habitats, collecting specimens, conducting wildlife surveys—requires physical presence and remains a substantial part of the role.
physical_exposure_2028_rationale: Zoologists study animal behavior. Knowledge-based scientific work with some fieldwork.
physical_exposure_2031_rationale: Research work with some fieldwork in natural environments. The role is primarily about scientific observation and analysis. Fieldwork involves variable environments but is secondary to analytical work.
physical_exposure_2036_rationale: Fieldwork in natural environments with unpredictable wildlife. By 2036, remote monitoring (drones, cameras) automates much data collection, but field research in unstructured environments with wild animals requires human judgment and physical presence.
adoption_friction_rationale: Government agencies and research institutions are primary employers. Fieldwork in remote natural environments requires physical presence. AI tools for species identification and ecological modeling advancing. Academic institutional inertia. Environmental regulations require human judgment. Moderate employer fragmentation.
demand_elasticity_rationale: AI tools (camera traps, satellite tracking, genomics) enable more comprehensive wildlife research. Climate change and biodiversity loss increase urgency. Conservation funding limits expansion more than productivity.
